545 Whampoa Prawn Noodles at Tekka Centre is a well-known hawker stall that has earned recognition in the Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand list, highlighting places that serve quality food at affordable prices. Despite its simple hawker setting, the stall has built a loyal following among locals who crave a comforting and flavourful bowl of prawn noodles.

The star of the dish is the broth. It is simmered for hours using prawn shells and pork bones, producing a rich, aromatic soup with natural sweetness and depth. Each bowl comes generously topped with fresh prawns, lean pork slices, crunchy bean sprouts, and fragrant crispy pork lard that adds texture and flavour. Diners can choose between soup or dry versions, both equally satisfying.

The noodles are cooked just right, maintaining a pleasant springy bite that pairs perfectly with the savoury broth or sauce. A spoonful of their homemade sambal chilli adds a spicy kick that enhances the sweetness of the prawns and the richness of the soup.

Even with its Michelin recognition, the stall remains humble and affordable, staying true to Singapore’s hawker culture. For anyone visiting Tekka Centre, a bowl of prawn noodles here is a hearty, satisfying meal worth queuing for. 🦐🍜

Soup no taste and diluted, noodle is oily with no flavors at all.
$7 for 2 small prawn as well

Very disappointed in myself for ordering this 😢

Restaurant Name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
Reviews: 18 dollars for a bowl of prawn noodles. Nothing else needs to be said.

Restaurant Name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
Reviews:
Ordered a Large pork ribs noodle soup at $10.

Soup is very tasty and rich with prawn flavour. I really like the taste of the soup but it made me slightly thirsty after drinking it. But the soup is still very tasty IMO.

Pork ribs are soft and tasty and portion wise is not bad.

Restaurant Name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
Reviews: The worst prawn noodles that I have ever eaten. Oily and the chilli is sweet?🙄 even beehoon texture was bad for the dry version. Ok to pay $7 which is above average price for hawker center basic prawn mee - but definitely not for this sub standard bowl of oily mushy stuff. How did that Michelin star even come about?

Restaurant Name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
Reviews: I had the soup version but I felt the soup could have a more prawny robust taste. Overall, it's a pass for me

Restaurant Name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
Reviews:
On 2025. Dry one iscalso good
On 2022 $10 for big prawn noodle.
Not the value for money but a good portion of ingredients and noodle.
Soup is good as it not salty.
Has a satisfactory feel.

Restaurant Name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
Reviews:
STANDARD DROPPED !!!! AVOID
I tried the Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle this morning. Very disappointed. The broth has NO taste prawn and is just very salty and saturated with MSG... The woman who cooked the noodle is extra rude. She gave so little broth and when you try to ask her for a little more she said "No! the bowl is already full"... such bad attitude. She thinks she is the only one who sell prawn noodles ?  The standard has dropped below any prawn noodle stall in any hawker center in neighbour food court ... Highly recommended to avoid... Don't spoil your appetite

Restaurant Name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
Reviews: Don’t know how they got this Michelin bib gourmand. Rude as… soup also so diluted. Gives a bad name to the Michelin establishment as to how they pick the recommendations. If you are ever served by the lady, pls don’t ask for more soup if yo don’t want to get shouted at!!

If you love old school braised duck in thick soya sauce , it’s here at hong lim.
The duck is tender and well marinated . The braised goodness went beyond the surface , it really penetrated into the meat .

Pig skin is springy and QQ
Tau Lok was good . I found the pork belly too fatty for my liking .

Intestines had some smell but masked by the thic Gravy.
For $20 its was a feast for 2 pax !!!
Damn this is even better than what my mum used to make.
Google mapsでクエイチャップ（Kway Chap）を探して此方を探しました。日曜日でも空いているのでありがたい。潮州料理が好きなので期待して訪問。お父さんが直ぐ提供してくれます。とても良かったです！
Food is great and very reasonable priced. The duck meat is tender and goes well with the chilli sauce. Worth a try!
不错，好吃好吃😋

Duck drumstick rice, add tau pok, pig skin and salted veg. $10.20. Decent price. Duck was tender and flavourful. However, everything is so oily. There was a shimmering layer of oil on the sauce, even the tau pok was soaked in oil like a sponge - no idea why they had to fry the tau pok before braising it which makes it super oily. Halfway thru the plate started to feel “jelat” liao coz it’s too oily. No soup was served too. Will prefer my usual braised duck stall just behind this stall, An Kee.
Ordered one plate of braised duck rice and Kway Chap for $9.50 Flavourful and no foul smell for the intestines. Duck meat is tender too.
I ordered the large duck rice, but I was quite disappointed cos it’s only white rice, meat and black sauce. I was expecting brown rice and pickles. Not something I would want to go back to try again.
They served me overnight braised egg.
I had the kway chap set and it was tasty overall. However, I do hope the large intestines can be prepared a little better.

Today’s comfort food fix – Kway Chap at Ah Heng Duck Rice (同济前阿兴鸭饭) 🍲🦆
Located at 531 Upper Cross Street Food Centre, this bowl is a real feast with everything inside – tender duck meat, braised eggs, duck liver, silky pig skin, crunchy salted veggies, and of course those chewy pig intestines. 🤤

Every bite is a mix of savory goodness and nostalgia – super shiok and fulfilling! 💯

#KwayChap #DuckRice #AhHeng #UpperCrossStreet #FoodieAdventure #ShiokAh #SingaporeEats #ComfortFood #BraisedGoodness
Excellent duck rice, nous nous sommes régalés (notre enfant aussi)
Nice , a tinge of herbal
Tasty duck rice that attracts a good following for their old school style version. Highly recommended.

Duck rice is delicious
Duck is tender and soft with delicious flavour

Staff are friendly and helpful

The kway chap and duck meat here taste really good — full of flavor and definitely worth trying! However, the environment is super hot, so be prepared. If you’re planning to visit, I’d suggest bringing a small fan with you to enjoy the delicious duck rice more comfortably.

An unassuming Braised Duck Rice / Kway Chap store that lives up to its Michelin recommendation (latest: 2024)!

The braised duck meat is done very well -  very little to no gaminess, not overly herbal and not salty at all! Very well balanced 👍🏼

They also sell Kway Chap (braised pork innards with rice noodles) and you can add on these side dishes with your duck rice as well. All these dishes are served with white rice only, a delight since heavy savoury stuff with sauce are best enjoyed with a hearty bowl of white rice.

Come early or you will have to queue.. and if you’d ask me, good food is worth the wait.

Ah Heng Duck Rice in Hong Lim truly lives up to its Michelin recommendation. From the moment you step inside the unpretentious, bustling eatery, you’re greeted with an aroma that hints at something exceptional—an experience that promises both comfort and a culinary adventure.

The star of the menu is undoubtedly the duck rice. Each bite of the tender, succulent duck is bursting with rich, savory flavors perfectly balanced by a subtle hint of spice. The accompanying intestines add an unexpected, delightful texture that contrasts well with the soft tofu, which is silky and absorbs the depth of the sauce beautifully. The harmonious blend of flavors makes the dish both comforting and sophisticated, exemplifying why this spot has earned high culinary accolades.

位於芳林巴剎(名稱源自19世紀一個名為「章芳林」的華人)與熟食中心的潮汕吃攤，一般以「阿興鴨飯」稱之，招牌上所寫的「同濟前」不知是否和汕頭的同濟善堂有關，而攤子的英文名稱Ah Heng或許表示了其和新加坡另一家同為米其林推薦的興記鵝鴨飯(Heng Gi)的關係。一早6點多就開始營業、適合透過來享用早餐的阿興招牌上雖寫鴨飯但若想在這個hawker center甚至左近多做其他嘗試的話也可以只點鴨肉，此次造訪還看到三五友朋的在地人點了一隻鴨共享以及粿汁(Kuay Chap)各一碗當作主食。此次所點的滷鴨肉的滷醬汁的存在感的確明顯，雖本身滋味不會太濃但對我來說依然和鴨肉本身的風味形成平衡，而鴨肉本身的滋味則也不太鮮明，需要細品才能嚐到肉的甜香，對我來說這鴨肉的口感表現更好，真的是鮮嫩。另點的乾豆腐的口感紮實，和醬汁的搭配很好，很值得點。

可考慮做為芳林巴剎一早享用潮汕風味鴨肉料理的選擇

IG: @melvineateat

7.5/10
$($8-12)

Ordered rice with braised duck, pig skin, pork belly, large intestine and egg.

Sauce is good, pig skin is tender and clean, intestine is tender. However felt duck is on the slightly tougher side.

Also probably goes better with kway chap or porridge rather than rice

Overall not wow but too bad
Bought a packet of braised duck rice as not much stall open today. Surprisingly leave it till 5pm still smell good, impressive!
The taste of duck meat blends with the spice marinade, each boasting a rich flavour. Snacks like duck liver and dried tofu are also offered.

Not sure why it got such low reviews, didn't justify the business. I ordered a dine in kway chap. Look at the portion and how big and generous the slices are. Taste also good. Plus the kway only $5. Where to find in Singapore nowadays where everything so expensive. Mai hiam la people, taste good price justifiable and portion is ok all that matters. Located at second floor near the lift area.
we're not local,but i and my hubby were surprise we receive mostly bones on duck rice,and we paid $6.50 for bone 😅
The food was cold including the rice. The portion was little. When I asked to remove the bone (she acknowledged it), but she gave me all the bone XD.

This is a popular Teochew styled braise duck stall originated from the former Tong Ji Hospital around Clark Quay back in the 70-80s. There's always a queue here. We were here on a Sunday morning around 11.30am, there was already a queue here.

The braised duck was well marinated and fragrant. The portion was fine and were nicely sliced. The gravy was nice too.

And there were two kinds of chillies, they were nice but were not spicy as I would expect them to be. And also they didn't provide soup, if not, it would be perfect, as most stalls would.

Service was quite prompt despite of the queue.

Overall, it was nice and so do give it a try if you are around the area looking for Teochew braised duck rice!
The best Lou Duck! Gravy is salty and dark. Super tender pig skin and intestine The salted vegetable is the legit salty kind, not the soggy sweet kind. Kway chup is also a good portion.
Best Duck Rice.

The stall’s meat is always nicely marinated, and I like the fact that they don’t  need additional sauces needed to bring out the soy braised flavor. Portions are perfectly cut, with every bite in the mouth full of satisfaction and shiokness. Pork belly also doesn’t have the porky smell.
$6 for this portion, a bit too little for the price. Other than that, the noodles are good but lack wok hey.

Long wait for the Chomp Chomp market reopen, today went down to buy my favorite Ah Hock Hokkien Noodle. Noodle became more dried compared to the usual but thought it’s most probably due to me tapao the food. While eating to and going to complete soon, i notice something black in the noodles… its a bloody fly inside the noodles.. 🤦🏻‍♀️🤦🏻‍♀️
What happened to your HKM? I actually thought I’d ordered from the wrong stall. The taste is so different now…. it tastes like home cooked noodles and is totally missing that wok hei.

Visited on a weekday with no queue. Ate this a couple of times already, weekday standards seem better. The noodles had good wok hei and flavour, BUT the dish could have been served hotter for a more satisfying bite and taste. The $5 portion was decent and filling. Overall, not bad..
Overly salty, undercooked noodles, prawns sliced so thinly I feeel robbed just by patonising this store. Just close shop if u can’t be bothered to cook properly.

I was disappointed with this plate of Hokkien mee probably I have a high hope knowing it’s in Michelin Guide selected 2025.

Can hardly taste any prawn flavour in the broth, so it came across quite bland. Even the chilli wasn’t shiok enough to save it. Definitely not the satisfying punch I usually look forward to in a good Hokkien mee.

Used to be one of my favs but that was more than ten years ago. Standard has since dropped to the point of almost no return.
Gave it a chance a couple of years ago, it was way too salty instead of proper brothy taste.
And gave it one last chance recently, it’s basically stir fried beehoon mee with some ingredients that are coincidental with hkm’s. No more wasting my time and money on a love that won’t return.

Had patronised Ah Hock Hokkien Mee since 35 years ago. Even though the founder retired and the son took over, it’s still upholding the same standard as the father. Kudos to you young man! The wife is helping out at the stalls and their service is impeccable. Keep it up!
I would recommend this as the best Hokkien Mee in Singapore. Always my favourite stall.

3/August/2025
Had fried hokkien mee ($5) for dinner, was quite good. Long queue, so be patient.

We tried this Hokkien mee the other day (cos it was the only Hokkien mee stall opened). Ordered $6, waited for almost 30 mins and when it came, we wished we’d ordered something else. It was dry and tasteless. We loved Hokkien mee and this is probably the worst of them all.
Very good plate of HKM. The auntie is very friendly too. Strongly recommend.

I ate this stall since I was a young boy. It's almost 20 years. I think now that the son took over the standard drop drastically. Very sad. First time I didn't eat finish... Every time I come chomp chomp this is a must eat and I'm willing to wait for one hour. I doubt I do it again

If this continues... All the regular will be gone soon... I hope they do something about it.
Nice
My favorite Hokkien mee!!! Dry style and soooo flavourful. Love it

Have been eating this regularly for the past 36 years. My parents only eat hokkien mee from this stall. When I was a kid, I didn't think much of it and thought it tasted normal until I tasted the typical hokkien mee elsewhere.

The hokkien mee itself tastes amazing cos of the rich stock they use. It is not too oily, salty or wet. If you are into strong tasting food or your tongue cannot really differentiate mild flavours, then this might not be for you. The ingredients (sotong and prawn) are decent quality (not that impt to me cos I'm really here for the noodles).

Service is alright. The helper (the one who takes order) has been working there for at least two decades by now and he is methodical in taking orders, and friendly enough. Wait time can be pretty insane, so go early or find something to entertain yourself while you wait an hour.

P/S: I saw many reviews swinging between 5 and 1. As a reader who is new to the stall, you must think the stall is inconsistent or something. That is not the case. I find that most of my friends who don't like this stall are used to the wet style hokkien mee (which is heavier) or their palette is very strong. Nothing wrong, just a case of "to each his own". Just know yourself and manage your expectations before trying.

Another store past its heyday.

In 2025, what does a $4 get you: 2 halves of a prawn (means 1 prawn), 2-3 pieces of sotong, noodles 🤣🤣 better not to order. cost of living increase + shrinkflation but then when you see other Hokkien mee stalls in Singapore, this is just…
Very nice hokkien mee. I always tried each time go chomp chomp

I went at 9.30am on a public holiday and waited 10min, the staff is courteous & the $5 portion is generous and competent. This is the HKM I grew up eating and have not visited for > a decade, so I am glad to come and savour the old school taste.

So many negative reviews and yet people kept ordering at chomp chomp.

It was quite good actually.
Taste below average and long waiting time. Beansprout not fully cooked. Still crunchy.
Dry type. Damn good. $6 very very worth it. I asked for no sotong in case anyone is wondering
Bad plate of HKM don't understand how the store still have customers.

one of the WORST hokkien mee i’ve ever eaten. travelled from woodlands to serangoon hoping to eat some goodaah hokkien mee. not sure how this stall is surviving. waited 15 minutes and it came with a free mosquito inside the hokkien mee too (:

I recently tried Ah Hock Fried Hokkien Noodles and, unfortunately, it was a disappointing experience. Despite its reputation, the noodles were lacking the essential wok hei, which is crucial for this dish. The flavor was bland and utterly tasteless, falling short of even basic expectations.

I ordered the $6 portion and paid an extra $2 for additional ingredients, but it felt like a waste. Even their chilli sauce, which is often the saving grace for mediocre dishes, failed to deliver. It lacked the kick and depth needed to elevate the noodles.

Overall, this was a letdown, and I wouldn’t recommend this stall. There are far better options out there for fried Hokkien noodles. Save your money and your appetite for somewhere else!

Food was okay, a tad drier than what I would prefer. Service was subpar. They made a mistake on my order. I wanted to film their store and food the $4 plate plus $2 worth of ingredients, but they gave me $4+$1 instead, and when I asked to add $1 more ingredients, they chose to refuse and refunded me $1 instead.

I came down to try the food and film it for social media and hence needed more ingredients so its more aesthetic, but I only had a total of 2 prawns and a small serving of squid.

When ordering, they had agreed to let me film, but after I had ordered, filmed the eating process and started filming the cooking process, they changed their mind and turned me away rather rudely.

I respect their decision to refuse the filming in order to preserve trade secrets. However, it could have been done up front, and also courteously.
Worst hokkien mee. Bought large. Hardly any squids , eggs . Pathetic 3 prawns-$8. Not good at all. Not a honest way to do business. Not recommended at all!

this is the $4 portion. cooked by the son, took 30mins. given his saltbae cooking performance, i thought it'd be good until i saw him pick the sotong one by one like gold.

1 prawn (cut in half, shown as 2)
4 little bits of sotong
basically no taugeh
very dry. i nvr eat hokkien mee alr mouth dry

i finished it in 11 bites. tried to stretch to 12 but cannot unless i eat 2 strands of noodle.

100% not recommended.
- Small portion.
- Had to wait a long time.
- 1 piece of prawn cut into half.
- Noodles were so dry.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: Noodle cooked al dente with a balanced savory sauce. Slightly too wet but doesn't affect taste. Meat slices are tender.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: This stall serves good Teochew fishball noodles. The noodles are well mixed with sauces and good to bite. I love the pork liver which is not over cooked so they’re just soft inside. Overall my $6 bowl of noodles is value for money

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews:
Had my bak chor mee fix at this stall on level 1 of Amoy Street FC. It had snaking long queues as always - I waited about 30 mins on a Tuesday at 1pm.

Tried their $8 minced meat noodles (dry), and honestly the soup was the highlight. Their soup was comforting and really umami, accompanied by a really fresh prawn and a variety of the usual ingredients like minced pork, sliced pork, fishballs and fishcake.

That said, the noodles were a tad too saucy and on the salty side, and I didn’t find the chilli very flavourful.

Overall, I'd rate this bowl of BCM a 7/10. It's worth trying once if you’re in the area and don’t mind queuing, but I've definitely had better. Prices start from $4.50, and goes all the way up till $10.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: Nice BCM. Generous ingredients and portion. Love the meatball and fishball.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews:
First of all this old man got a cute behavior. As though someone forced him out of retirement to come cook noodles. Like he just lighted his ciggy and i purposely come order type of attitude hahahaha.

Ok so taste wise is meh. Any ah tiongs can do better. The soup really tasted like soup. Portion is like a remake of a half finished bowl.
Overall I'm glad I tried. I'll take it I dropped $4.50 on floor and some random went to pick it.

1 star for old man cuteness 😊

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews:
First time patronizing this shop and tried their dry Bak Chor Mee, $6/-.
First looks, may seem a bit oily but the sauce coats all the noodles evenly and it's not 'lemak / gelat'. Noodles are cooked nicely and springy and the other ingredients are the usual suspects of bcm and a surprise guest, a pc of prawn. Star of the noodles is the fish balls.. imo. It's soft and bouncy and the soup was flavourful. Perhaps next time will try the fishball soup instead but overall good food, good taste. 😬

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews:
Came back to Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles at Amoy Street Food Centre on a Sunday and was delighted to see the first-generation uncle himself behind the stove!

There is a huge, noticeable improvement in the bowl recently. The 鳊鱼 pieces are much bigger and incredibly crispy now, adding a fantastic umami crunch. I also loved that there are more mushrooms visible and edible in the mix—it really elevates the flavor profile.

Special shoutout to the pork liver; the slices were generous, bigger than before, and cooked to a perfect, tender texture. Super satisfied with this visit. Definitely a happy tummy!

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: One of the best if not the best BCM I’ve had recently. Portion size is decent, good amount of sauce and flavour. Price is very very reasonable at $4.50 per bowl. Come early because the queues are long.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews:
The standout was definitely the soup. Clear but full of sweet umami from fresh ingredients, with juicy minced meat that doesn’t clump. The fishballs and thick fish cake slices were fresh and bouncy, the small-cut liver pieces had no smell, and the prawn was a good size. Overall, a refreshing, “healthy-but-flavourful” soup that I’d happily enjoy with a bowl of warm, fluffy rice on its own.

I paired it with thin beehoon, though in hindsight I should’ve stuck with mee kia—my usual go-to. The beehoon doesn’t cling well to the sauces, and the chilli was milder than expected despite the generous amount.

Another highlight was the freshly deep-fried tee poh. It’s huge, aromatic, and honestly could be a dish on its own. I came around 7:30am on a Sunday—no queue, and I even got to see the tee poh cooling on the table. It looked and smelled so good I’d gladly eat it just with rice.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: The Teochew fishball noodle tasted good but not something you will crave for another serving.. Price was slightly high for the serving size. Guess its typical CBD prices. Its crowded during lunchtime.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: nicee the sauce and ingredients savoury!

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: Noodles were al dente and just right. Sauce taste was bold. They were generous with the pork lard. The accompanying soup was flavorful. Wait was not too long. All in all a great first time.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews:
Nice bowl of noodle. Friend cook. Unfriendly helper (uncle and aunty)

Had the 8 dollar version, black n spicy. Taste good. Soup is good too. Prawn is large and fresh (^^)

**those prawn are not cheap even if you buy in market.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews:
Came at 915am and there was no queue but a few customers who ordered and were waiting. Got the $8 bowl and got served pretty quickly. Didn’t experience any bad customer treatment as some people have mentioned.

Taste wise I found it too saucy for my liking. Soup was fantastic though.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: The elderly man taking orders is extremely rude and arrogant. His attitude made the entire experience unpleasant, and I will never patronize this stall again.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: The $8.00 order was quite generous and the soup was delicious.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: Delicious meal on a rainy day. Nice soup broth. Highly recommended.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews:
Their signature bowl of dry mee kia reminds you why Fishball Noodles never go out of style. The mee kia noodles are perfectly springy, tossed in a good balanced chilli-vinegar mix, that packs a solid kick without overwhelming the palate. Every bite has that addictive balance of spice, tang, and umami lardiness.

Fishballs are bouncy and chewy with subtly sweetness, but not the best textured that i have eaten. Alongside, you get a mix of tender slices of fishcakes, minced pork, livers and crunchy shrimp, that add depth and texture.

The soup on the side, is light yet umami packed, good for refreshing your palate after the deep flavoured noodles.

Its rare to locate such good bowl of fishball noodles where the noodles, chilli, and broth work hand-in-hand: Bold, clean, and satisfying. No wonder they are one of the winners for Michellin Bib Gourmand.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews:
I decided to give this stall a try after seeing how thoughtful they were with the dabao set my colleague got from them last week. The noodles were drenched in extra sauce so they didn't dry up, even for a takeaway.
I dined in on a rainy Monday right before the lunch peak. There was only one customer ahead of me, and I went with the $6 dry mee pok. Right after I placed my order, a queue formed right behind me.

Despite the stall's name, I think it's a hybrid of fishball and bak chor mee, or what some might call a classic fishball noodle. I think they really stand out for being generous with their ingredients. There's even a medium size prawn While the fishballs weren't the handmade type I prefer, they were still springier than usual. The mee pok was cooked just right, and the liver was a perfect medium-rare. The broth is light, but it complements the dish well.
If I were to nitpick, it would be the chili, which had a sweeter note than expected and lacked a punch. Nevertheless, I think the free-flowing vinegar is a nice touch for those who prefer extra tangy mee pok.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: 这摊位老板做生意不厚道，打包干面薄带自己的容器去，要求老板把汤分开包，老板给说即使用自带的容器汤也要多付3毛钱，问他为什么，他给的借口(看清楚是借口不是理由)因为有些人带了大个容器会要求多汤，问他那多付3毛钱他会多给汤吗，他说他只能给一个人的分量，这是什么🐦话，在那堂食干面不都是附带一份汤吗?用他们的一次性容器收费2角是合理，但这汤3毛钱不是明抢?不是给不起3毛钱，而是这不合理给得不爽，还有那个摊位助手大姐如果是老板给的薪水不够也不用对顾客呼呼喝喝，我们是花钱消费不是等吃你免费施舍的乞丐!

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews:
Soup taste fantastic.
Fishball bouncy and fresh.
Portion is good for value.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: Average bak chor mee.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: The noodles were perfectly cooked, and the ingredients were generous. The taste was above average - definitely recommend.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: Highly recommend their $10 dry mee sua portion that comes with a generous amount of tee poh (Dried sole fish)

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews: 買10元，吃乾麵，份量足，料也多，大致上還不錯吃、只是覺得麵有點鹹。

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Reviews:
This is truly the spirit of hawker in Singapore,  it is never about the food..but the energy behind it and it's legacy..

The handsome guy spend his life taking over from his father,  truly maintaining it .

The pork of smooth tender texture is resturant grade... I cannot even describe..this is truly originally tasted of old days...

Fish ball, sauce perfectly blend into the noodles ..

I would say this is a heritage food, perfectly done into goodness with heart.

It beats any big fish ball chain hand down.

Keep it up. Will support again

Ammakase is a unique fine dining concept known as the world’s first Indian omakase, blending traditional Indian flavors with modern culinary artistry. Each course is thoughtfully curated and beautifully presented, offering a creative, immersive tasting experience. We recently visited Ammakase for their Valentine’s special and it turned out to be one of the most unique dining experiences we’ve had in Singapore. It’s described as the world’s first Indian omakase, which means you simply trust the chef and enjoy a carefully curated multi-course journey, and they truly delivered on that concept.

The 8 course menu was themed as a “romance along the coast of India,” and every dish felt creative, thoughtful, and beautifully plated. From the playful starters like banana blossom tart and avocado chaat to the richer mains like jackfruit with ghee rice, and ending with a stunning dessert spread, each course was a surprise and had its own story.

What made the evening extra special were the little details. A cupid came around asking couples to write notes for each other, they gave us a printed copy of the menu with our names on it as a keepsake, and they even took a photo of us and gifted it to us at the end. Such thoughtful touches made the whole experience feel personal and memorable, not just like a regular dinner.

If you enjoy Indian flavours presented in a modern, artistic way and love the idea of a chef-curated surprise meal, Ammakase is definitely worth trying, especially for special occasions or date nights.

Araya
The world’s first and only one-Michelin-star Chilean restaurant, Araya is as much about storytelling as it is about cooking. The experience is vibrant and deeply personal, with each course unfolding the narrative of Chile’s regions, produce, and culinary identity. It’s confident, immersive, and quietly impressive in how naturally it educates without ever feeling didactic.

Takeaways:
• Empanada is easily one of the most indulgent I’ve had—deeply savory, intensely flavored, and perfectly balanced in filling-to-dough ratio. Every bite lands with purpose.
• Picanha closes the savory courses on a high. Beautifully grilled, tender enough to cut with ease, and paired with sauces that enhance rather than overshadow the beef.
• Chocolate Trolley is pure temptation. Faced with an array of handcrafted chocolates, resistance is futile. The darker selections stood out for their depth and restraint.
• The experience feels intimate and engaging. Diners sit close to the action, with chefs serving and explaining dishes directly, often bringing out ingredients and examples as part of the narrative. They’re open, conversational, and genuinely keen to share the story behind the food.

The Damage (no drinks): S$450-900 for two

First time trying chile food, you can feel the warm reception once you enter the restaurant.

There’s only bar counter seats available, which makes interaction easier. Interesting, there will be a story told for each dish that is served.

Their madai fish taste exceptionally great, same for their scallop crudo. Empanada is the chef favourite snack, it’s worth a trying.

Overall it’s a great restaurant to experience South American food and their culture.

The pigeon breast was a real standout - cooked to perfection and accompanied by a smoky, umami packed molé inspired sauce. 1 major disappointment for this place came from the attention to detail, particularly dietary restrictions. Octopus was served even though it had been stated clearly “no mollusks” for that particularly guest. Similarly, a dessert made with rum was served to someone who had specified no alcohol! To their credit, the team recovered enough to whip up an alternative dish but this shouldn’t be happening in the first place, especially for this price point.

Overall a good place for a special occasion, and it might be much more enjoyable if one does not require any special dietary requests!

Came for the MILPA X ARAYA meal on our wedding anniversary.  The experience was exquisite, from the careful setting and decor to the service and well curated menu. The only disappointment was the empanada with clams inside and topped with caviar.  Something inside was tasting weird and felt a waste of caviar that did not balance the whole bite.

We were spoilt for choice with 3 types of bread, the nori bread with wagyu beef fat which was very dense, the Chilean bread which was like mini baguette, and the sour dough potato bread which was well fermented.  Loved the Chilean bread which paired better with the 2 artisanal butters, with less clashing flavours.

The starter was an interesting fish (I think it was yellowtail) in an interesting citrusy broth.  Had a strong coconut cream which would not suit some people.  Dish tasted very Thai but at least fish was super fresh.  The Coral was a pretty colorful dish and superbly constructed.

The sea bream was very fresh and well constructed but the heavy coconut cream flavour again could have been lightened to be less overwhelming.

The wagyu beef was ok on top of a complex mole that was too flavourful for me but loved by the rest at my table. It was served with a special made taco mixed with Japanese leaf and looked like a leaf.

Dessert was a lovely chocolate cake that was marvelous and they surprised us with an extra cake which was milky for dessert plus an anniversary cake which was like a a fruit cake with hint of almond.

All in all a wonderful experience so th every course having unique utensils and plates to bring in the story behind the dishes together.  We will be back for a pure ARAYA experience.

This was a very last-minute decision to surprise my wife for lunch, and Araya turned out to be the perfect choice. From start to finish, the experience was nothing short of outstanding.

We started with the ceviche, which was absolutely perfect, fresh, vibrant, and elevated by a sauce so amazing it genuinely made us dream. It was beautifully paired with a Chilean Chardonnay that complemented every bite.

Next came the little empanada, served with a wonderful wine from Mendoza. Once again, the pairing was spot on enhancing the flavours without overpowering them.

The highlight for us was the picaña, perfectly cooked and truly a joy to eat. Paired with the Purple Angel Chilean red wine, it became an unforgettable course. The meloso rice was excellent as rich, comforting, and deeply satisfying.

Dessert transported us straight to Chile for an afternoon, ending the meal on a beautifully nostalgic note. The chef plays masterfully with this Chile/Japan fusion, creating a menu that feels both refined and soulful.

Thank you, Araya team, for an exceptional experience. Everything was so close to perfection, and we will definitely be back for another visit!

I attended the Four Hands collaboration dinner featuring Chef Deepanker Khosla from Haoma in Bangkok. We arrived on time at 7 pm for our reservation, but noticed that the restaurant was only about half full and some tables had already started receiving their courses. Despite this, we sat for over 30 minutes without being served anything at all. Not even a starter or welcome course.

We were confused about the delay. It only became clear later that the kitchen was holding our courses until the guests next to us arrived. Perhaps, so they could prepare and serve both groups at the same time? The last couple showed up quite late, yet their dishes came out very quickly at the same time as ours. That’s when I realized we had been deliberately delayed just to sync with strangers at the next table and ease pressure on the kitchen. We didn’t book with them, we don’t know them, and no one informed us that we’d essentially be forced to dine on their schedule. Losing the first 30 minutes without any explanation felt disrespectful.

The chef’s table was fully booked, with two additional tables added for the evening—a good turnout for a Four Hands event. Taste-wise, the dishes from Haoma (the Indian-influenced side) were too intense for me: overly salty, sweet, and heavy-handed with extra sauces. The Chilean-inspired courses were more interesting, with many ingredients I was trying for the first time. The final dessert—a celebration of chocolates from around the world—was the clear highlight, though by that point I was already too full to properly enjoy it.

Overall, the dinner felt disorganized. There were long, unexplained waits between courses throughout the night, which suggests poor pacing and insufficient preparation. With only two waitstaff handling more than 25 guests, service was stretched thin and the whole experience suffered as a result.

My wife and I celebrated our birthday there. Service and ambience were impeccable. Food and wine pairing was done very well. The restaurant manager and staff were also very educational in sharing what ingredients goes into the dishes we were having. It was truly a gastronomical experience. Would highly recommend it to anyone. Our favourite dishes of the night were definitely the Moqueca and the Picanha! Ending the night with a huge selection of sweet treats from South America was also a pleasure. We will definitely be back again.

Let's try the joint performances of the two restaurants, the cuisine from South America and Italy. There are three places in the entire menu where white truffles can be upgraded - the signature pasta, the main course steak, and the dessert ice cream. Maybe there was a misunderstanding in communication, and only the pasta was added. The cocoa bean fruit served with pudding has a very South American flavor and is quite radical in seasoning. The brat cheese in a foamy form paired well with tomato broth, and it was my favorite snack. I really love the olive oil from Bombana. It has a fresh fragrance like freshly cut grass. The caviar and steamed egg were combined to make a cold dish, with an explosive acidity, and it was truly refreshing. The scallops were excellent, paired with celery juice, with a slightly sour and spicy flavor, and paired with the crisp and sweet fruits with South American characteristics, making the whole person feel healthier. The first pasta dish was extremely spicy, with a very firm texture. Being able to finish it all despite its spiciness shows great skill. The second pasta dish had a rich aroma of cheese, but the truffle aroma was average. The red mullet was cooked perfectly, with thick fish skin that couldn't be cut. This problem has always remained unsolved. Perhaps the grilled scales method is the best solution. The beef snack was not very impressive, a bit too salty. The beef main course was to my heart's content. The sauce and presentation were beautiful, the seasoning was balanced, and the beef was soft. The dessert was to my heart's content. The milk pudding with a rich milk flavor paired with ice cream, and the hazelnut quality was superb. The combination of the three was truly harmonious, and it was a very simple dessert.

I was pleasantly surprised by everything here, I did expect a great dinner but this was a very memorable evening! It was intimate, elegant, fun and absolutely every dish was perfectly executed.
The Chilean ingredients are displayed, and explained as I was sitting down. Biggest surprise on display was the skin, that actually was the dried Chilean seaweed, Cochayuyo. From start to end every dish had its own personality, and every time I thought that it couldn’t be better. I always get asked for my favourites, and it’s nearly impossible to say. The Picana, Wagyu with chimichurri was perfect, just like the Kinki fish.
The green ceviche Hokkaido scallops, botan ebi, leche de tigre sorbet with ginger jelly was another plated love that I felt like licking when I was done. There was so many dishes, and all equally scrumptious. And then the desserts, 3 of them where the main dessert Antártica was like a luxurious Ben & Jerry’s. Lost for words.
The interior reminds me about a private club, its dark and intimate and the guests are feeling at home directly. Perfect service. I wanna go back already. Araya was awarded with a star after eight months. I am sure more will come!

麥煎糕(粿)は麵煎粿、曼煎粿、麥仔煎などとも呼ばれる華南地区、台湾、マレーシアやシンガポール、インドネシアで食べられているトラディショナルなパンケーキで、この店ではピーナッツ入りに加えてココナッツや紅豆、チーズ入りのものも販売している。
お店の方によると、20年以上ここでご商売されているとのこと。
持ち帰っても良いが、近くのコーヒーストールで飲み物を買ってその場で食べるのも楽しい。
Good and ok.
Lovely pancakes served by a friendly uncle.
Nice oats pancake. The coconut filling one taste good, not sweet, and it is chewy.

Uncle and auntie’s stall is the epitome of what a hawker stall is to me.

They retain the old school taste of mjk with some new flavors. (Granted, I always go for redbean😂)
I love the buttery fluffy texture of the folded mjk, and having tried a few other stores that do it the same style, I find myself coming back to uncle and auntie’s stall.

Uncle is always smiling and so gentle, making notes on the mjk with the filling or on the bag as to which flavour is which, when you buy more than one.
Old school pancake with good ol’ fillings - love the ‘shell’ looking pancake, skin was soft and had a nice bite even after leaving it for some time. Red bean, pandan and cheese are my faves!

I've tried several of these pancakes over the years and they have always been really good! The pancake mix, in my opinion, is the perfect mix of savoury, chewy, and a hint of acid, always cooked just right; fillings are always fairly pleasant.

I do like the 'curry-puff' style, great with a cup of coffee or tea. My personal preference is the cheese one, but all of them are great! It always feels a bit nostalgic sitting down, eating one of these, and watching the world go by.

Highly recommended!

1.20 for a micro peanut pancake. Disappointed because a peanut pancake is supposed to be filling. Not to mention the peanut fillings are a little too loose and sparse. Saving grace was because it was fresh and hot.

Order the crescent shaped one. That one looks more normal sized.
The pandan one was freshly made!

Before we left the Food Centre, wifey felt like eating Oats Pancake (麦煎粿) from Aunty Oats Pancake Stall.

Those in the short queue were apparently regular customers, who seemed “like friends” to the elderly stall holder.

We bought the peanut filling pancakes @ $1.20 each. There were 8 others with interesting fillings - red bean, coconut, chocolate, cheese, lotus paste, pandan, salted bean and coffee.

When we reached home, the peanut pancake seemed a little damp, possibly because they were packed in plastic bag. Nevertheless, it was tasty although one (out of 4 pieces) was a little hollow inside; less crushed peanuts, had to be wifey’s piece🤣.

wish I took a photo of the misery that this MJK was but  have never seen one done so bad & so sad 🤯😥🤕
so UNGENEROUS it was almost nonexistent, but also just really badly done pancake.
V limpy, super thin (think McD’s hotcakes thickness & without its density), barely risen, but the rectangle slice was also cut extremely small, & bc of the super little peanuts/sugar stuffing, it was as good as eating a plain pancake & you’d think maybe random bits of peanut got in 😳
it was $1.20…… but hardly worth 1/4 of its price even 😣😞
Have never seen MJK done this badly agh
Can try

I only had the mutton meat soup. Got to say I taste a little richer than the usual ones and is noticeably less salty as well. The flavour is still there so many they did not add MSG or similar. Mutton meat wise, I would say the portion of meat within the soup is acceptable and they are all tender with even mix of lean and fatty meats. No strong mutton bad taste which is good.

We saw a video about this place and went last Saturday for lunch. We reached pretty early so there wasn't much queue. The mutton soup is super tasty! I would definitely go back for more. Went there for the first time with my friends for dinner after our event to experience an ordinary bowl of mutton soup. I was expecting something special since it has been much raved about. And what was unexpected was the service staff or the 'son' of the stall didn't even to spend a little of time to introduce the different options (upsell) he has when I later noticed that I could have ordered a mixed bowl with tripes and other innards which would be more expensive. Maybe because I'm a local Chinese and beside me was a native Chinese seemingly didn't know how to appreciate a bowl of mutton soup. The sheer lack of warm and passion was apparent in service.
Delicious mutton soup. Meat is tender and not gamey. Soup was really good but wasn't as thick and rich as I expected. Portion wise, ok for the price.

Travelled a fair bit to try the mutton soup after seeing the CNA show. Tried the meat, tendon and tongue ones. The soup was thick and flavourful, but tbh I still prefer my usual one at upper boon keng where I can taste more spices. A plus side is that they offer free refill of the soup, which a big plus since u get to end the meal with the steaming hot soup (otherwise not much is left for drinking after u finish dipping with bread). A good mutton soup if ur in the area, but i m not sure if its worth traveling a long way for.
Mutton leg soup only comes with bone. Please don’t try. Better to get other soup options. Soup tastes good.

I was looking forward to eating the famous mutton soup which apparently was the reason for the Michelin star award. There's a large variety of mutton parts some of which are not easy to find elsewhere and that's their advantage and the meat itself and portions are average. But the main downside is the taste of the soup itself. I'm sure this is not the original recipe that was passed down from the grandfather to the father and now the son. Or maybe it's the lack in experience and knowledge of how much the amount of ingredients or spices which goes into the soup which is not the special amount anymore.
Bottom line, if you are in the area and craving for mutton soup it's okay I guess. But definitely not worth going all the way here just to buy it.
Really good mutton soup, super tasty and the meat is so soft. Got to be one of the best in Singapore and the reason why i take statin.

Tried the super popular mutton soup, waited 45min in the queue at 2pm! its the longest queue in this place. the food was v good, strong mutton smell and taste but not as rich tasting as i expected. almost tasted too diluted. so it was a good dish but not a great one. however the meat is cook to perfection, thats a standout. Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: Bought tom yum ban mian with added fish. Wow, portion is so generous and soup is so flavourful! Will continue to support!!

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: My dad and II have been eating at this stall for many years, from beginning where there's not many customers to snaking queue, owners recognised me in the bus when I have no clue beginning (I haven't been going to market for years) eat while you still can, owner said he has no intention of passing down to his son

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews:
One of the best fish soup around, fresh and reasonably thick sliced toman fish 生鱼 (sheng yu) in tasty sweet broth.  Ordered 鸳鸯(yuan yang) S$7, combination of sliced fish and fried fish pieces with bee hoon in soup.  Otherwise, any one type would be just $5.50.
Waited in queue ~50 mins with roughly 8 other in front of me.  Reasons for the long wait due to several “regular” patrons known to the stall owner allowing express service without need for queuing.  That’s rather awful to all standing in the queue looking 👀 on… Plus this stall can be closed on their stipulated operating days too, so count your very best luck!

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: I wanted to gatekeep because the queue is getting longer but.... spread positivity! After all these years, still crowning as my BEST fried fish soup IN TOWN.

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews:
The queue was long, and everyone in line seemed to know exactly what they were waiting for. I joined the queue, and thanks to mobile data keeping me company, the hour-long wait flew by!

I ordered the fried fish with milk broth, and yuan yang with thick bee hoon (since the fish head was already sold out). The portion of fish was generous, and the soup… one of the best I’ve ever had. Rich, flavourful, and clearly a crowd favourite - every bowl I saw was completely emptied. Best of all, it seemed to have little or no MSG, as I didn’t feel thirsty afterwards.

The stall is run by an elderly couple, uncle does the cooking while aunty take the orders. She was warm and friendly, which made the experience even better.

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: I had the fried fish bee hoon soup with milk today, and it was exceptional. The broth was incredibly rich and umami-packed; probably the best fish soup I’ve had to date. The portion of fried fish was generous, crisp on the outside, and tender inside. This stall is a standout, and I’d strongly recommend it to anyone visiting Whampoa Food Center. Already looking forward to my next visit to try the sliced fish version.

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews:
Lady Owners becoming arrogant and favouring their friends over others in queue blatantly.
Her arrogance is typical behaviour of someone whose business flourished and thought people will have to tolerate her nonsense!
Her friends do not need to queue up when ordering for eating in or takeaways, which she condoned blatantly as if people in queue are insignificant to her.
Not worth to patronise this stall, slow and yet allowing queue jumping by her friends!!!

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews:
Best of the Best...
Every bowl was well balanced...
Choose fish head or fried fish or slices.
Choose rice or rice noodle
Choose milk or no milk added to soup.

All at $5.50. worth every single cent.

Please note:
Rest Day: Mon, Wednesday, Friday
Operating only in Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: One of our favourite fish soups in Singapore. Soup is deliciously rich and creamy especially if you asked to add some carnation milk. Fish tastes fresh and we keep on coming back. Stall provides free tabao container so don’t need to prepare own. Thank you uncle and auntie for your hard work.

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: Fried fish Tom yum bee hoon is nice. Fish is fresh n crispy

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: Delicious Sliced Fish Soup for just Sgd 5.50. I prefer this without Milk, so always say No Milk.

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews:
10th Nov 2024.
Ordered the fried sliced fish noodles & soup.
The soup is flavourful & slightly creamy with robust fish broth.
The soup compared to the same sliced fish noodles from The Ship, it's of different taste. But at $5.5, less than half the cost compared to The Ship, it's worth it.
Be prepared to queue for 45mins. The staff is patient & polite despite the never ending volume of customers.
The fried fish has a layer of batter, unlike The Ship's fried sliced toman.
Worth the queue & will come back for more 👍.

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: I ordered the fried fish bee hoon without the milk. The fried fish was delicious. It was tasty and fried to a golden perfection The fish was moist and the batter kept its texture in the soup right to the very end. It did not get soggy. The thick bee hoon had a good consistency. The soup in my opinion was a little bland. It had that “milky” look but also had a bitter after taste from burnt bits of fried fish. The wait in line was 30mins+ on the weekend.

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews:
Happen to chance upon this place at 1:30pm. Lucky to be their 2nd last customer and there was no other choices, only fish fish been hoon which I took up. Soup was heavenly , sweet, slightly salty due to the fried flatfish. Simple yet effective dish

Came back again at 12pm to try to Tom yam since they were sold out the first time. Waited for 1hr this time round!
Did not disappoint. Tom yam was pretty addictive although not the authentic Tom yam from Thailand that you would expect (it’s made from the premade paste)

Fish was fresh, huge chunks and very generous given the price, it’s great value for money too!

$5.50

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews:
I'm never someone to queue for food until I was introduced to this place. Imo, the fried fish tastes better than sliced fish, but fishhead is my fav. The bee hoon is too hard for my liking so I order the soup with rice, which comes with the added benefit of not having the delicious soup being soaked up by the bee hoon.
Tom yum is not as nice as the regular soup.

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: Decent fish soup. The fish was fried perfectly and not soggy like other stalls. However, felt that the milk was too overpowering and sweet. Couldn't taste much of the soup.

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: A soup so flavorful and fried fish still crispy despite being soaked in the soup. 5/5

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: Good portion size and rich broth. Be warned their Tom Yum soup is super sour but I love it. So addictive!

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: beehoon fish head soup, the taste of the soup is delicious and the fish heads are fresh, you can try it next time you are at the whampoa market 👍👍👍

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: My new favourite fish head bee hoon. I came at 9.02am when there was no Q to order but already had not wait 10 minutes for the food. I recommend ordering the limited fried fish neck IF it’s available. It cost more at $7 but It’s to die for! Those meat were extra thick and juicy. The soup was full-flavoured (mine was without the milk). The stall did not bother to display its Bib Gourmand badge. It’s that good :) I have tried 5 stalls with the awards in the past two weeks. Not all deserve the accolades. This one does.

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews:
It's a hawker center with lots of nice food like soya milk and prawn noodle.
This stall fish soup is superb, almost the best in singapore, they decided to cut down work day so they rest 135. Long queue daily, cheap at $5.50 - 6.00
Tips: order the soup with rice, you get more ingredients and fish.also, the fried fish taste good too.

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Reviews: A very good bowl of fish soup. Robust base , fresh fish with options of fish head chunks as well

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon

10/10 highly recommended. Impeccable interpretation and innovation of heritage dishes - elegant presentation but most importantly really delicious. Of course, some dishes were more outstanding than others hence I think it’s worth coming back for. I recommend you take this experience - elegant dishes with very relaxed and chill vibes - suitable for a date or family and friends’ gathering. Thanks to the attentive staff- we really enjoyed our evening!

Stopped by for the 3-course set lunch menu that reimagines local flavors with finesse. It's upscale dining without the pomp, where every ingredient tells a story. Highlights include the grilled Spanish Octopus with prawn paste and strawberries, and a chawanmushi makeover with clams and assam pedas.

Our mains featured seafood - Skate Wing with laksa mustard, pepper ketchup as well as Marble Goby with cashew nut curry, candlenut and seaweed laksa verde. The ingredients might sound wild and bold but the flavors were very approachable and harmonious.

We also had the corn salat add-on for $7, paired with warm corn tea sweetened with japanese black sugar. It's warm, soft and slightly custardy.
Very interesting 5 course menu with a good fusion of Southeast Asia ingredients to tease our palate. Overall an enjoyable dinner.

Food was great! Starters were delicious but mains were the highlights – loved the smokiness of the Kang Kong from the wagyu dish and the crispiness from both fish dishes. Flavours were on point too, would recommend! Only downside was that they ran out of kueh for dessert :(

Blown away by the Mod-Sin offerings here.

Chef Marcus Leow has outclassed himself. Loved most of the dishes we had over a 5-course dinner. Will return with family and friends.

Like their food menu, restaurant also kept their cocktails list tight — one concoction per choice of liquor. We enjoyed Sambal Marg(arita) $25 the most.

Such a wonderful dining experiences my first time here. Awesome food and such friendly service. Very creative with their menu amd their fusion cocktails/cocktails were delicious. Will definitely be back
Excellent food and service, and excellent value at this price point ($98++ for five courses).
Excellent food concept, excellent menu, excellent ingredients. Best lunch I had in a long time at any Singapore restaurant.
Impressive! 中餐的份量剛剛好，用餐環境舒適，不過廁所要特別走到一樓後門，有點麻煩。如果想拼摘星，可能環境舒適與方便度應該可以再大幅提升。服務人員介紹得很好👌🏻 不過口氣上比較沒什麼溫度😅 好像在背菜單而已。基本上餐點都算很棒！期待之後進化✨

Nice cosy atmosphere and I thought the slower pace of the servings was good if you want to chat with friends inbetween.

Some notable dishes include the Amela Tomato, Grilled Spanish Octopus, Clam Custard, Skate Wing Goreng, and Crispy Scale Marble Goby. Didn't feel that the other dishes were as outstanding, particularly the beef dishes and Claypot rice. Wine pairing portions can be described as measly but good nontheless.

Price is reasonable for the quality and overall quantity
Honestly, everything was soooooo GOOD! I love how quiet and slow pace (in a good way) the meal is. The coffee is really strong!

Honest the food was really good and well thought out, but our experience was marred by the long wait time in between the courses. For a five course meal with two supplements, the meal took more than 2.5 hours to conclude, keeping in mind it was the second seating.

The corn salat was delectable, and they really excel at desserts. I was happy with my marble goby main, though my friends said the wagyu main was average. The rest of the food was amazing but we were getting hangry before the mains came.
The claypot rice is the bomb
Modsin done right. Best I’ve had so far.  Beautiful cooking and delightful flavours.

From the moment I walked in, I was impressed by the ambience warm, inviting, and thoughtfully designed. The atmosphere feels calm yet elegant, making it a perfect place for both a relaxed meal and a special occasion. You immediately sense that a lot of care has gone into every detail, from the lighting to the overall vibe.

But the real star here is the food. What makes this restaurant truly special is how creatively they use starfruit across the menu. Almost every dish incorporates starfruit in some way, and it’s done so beautifully and intelligently that nothing feels repetitive. Instead, each dish highlights a different side of its flavour - sometimes fresh and tangy, sometimes subtle and balanced, sometimes surprisingly rich.

Every single dish was incredibly tasty and flavourful. Honestly, I licked the plates - that’s how good it was. Not a single item disappointed. The flavours were bold yet refined, unique yet comforting. You can really tell that the dishes are carefully crafted, not just to be different, but to taste amazing.

It’s rare to find a place that is both this unique and this delicious. The use of starfruit is not just a gimmick - it’s creative, thoughtful, and executed at a very high level. This is the kind of dining experience that stays with you long after the meal is over.

Highly recommended for anyone who loves great food, beautiful ambience, and trying something truly different. I’ll definitely be coming back and bringing more friends with me next time. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

As someone who has eaten the fresh fruit Belimbing before, I had higher expectations of how they would incorporate it into their dishes. I was hoping that they would bring out the original sweetness, sourness, and crunchiness of the fruit but also understand that they had to preserve the fruit since it spoils easily. Some notable dishes include the Amela Tomato, Grilled Spanish Octopus, Clam Custard, Skate Wing Goreng, and Crispy Scale Marble Goby. Didn't feel that the other dishes were that good though. On the overall, it's a nice place to pop by given that it's is also more affordable as compared to the other places with set menus and there's at least one good dish in each course.

Food and service was impeccable. Every dish was a delightful surprise, thoughtfully created and beautifully plated. The menu was creative experiential local cuisine, food portions are generous and definitely more than enough even on an empty stomach. Ambience with the daylight streaming in was cosy and warm. Perfect for brunch with friends, dinners with family, birthdays and hosting friends from other countries who might wanna try local food in a more interesting way. Will definitely be back!
可以把新加坡菜色加入一點西方元素，還可以把它作的很細緻，真的很難得。開放廚房，可看到廚師們忙著製作每一道菜，而且個個年輕就能料理這些食物，是蠻厲害的。菜色的搭配和口味都不錯，價格是一位98元，值得一試。

Had the tasting menu last night with my partner and have to say it was a delight! I had no expectations other than The Coconut Club makes awesome Nasi Lemak, but that was it. From the extremely sweet and KNOWLEDGEABLE staff (which is so hard to find these days), to the food just being really well-considered and DELICIOUS, it was absolutely lovely! My partner felt nostalgic most of the meal, even getting excited to hear dessert had a specific fruit he hadn’t eaten since he was a kid. Overall, a beautifully satisfying evening! PS try the Sambal Margarita!

creative, thoughtful food with an incredible attention to detail. Marcus Leow knocked it out of the park this time. the serving dishes were also so stunning. fine dining in every sense of the word. run, don't walk, before they get their first Michelin 😉
Went for lunch. Food was delicious and inventive. Lunch sets good value. Cocktails tasty. The corn salat was really nice too!
We had the 5 course meal that was so well balanced and honestly every single course was an explosion of great flavors! I would want to come back to relive some of the dishes we had!

Interesting twist to Asian food served western style.  We had the set lunch (48++, add $10 for beef main).  I liked the octopus appetizer, with a tint of rojak sauce, creative!  The main of ulam rice and fish with achar on the side wasn’t that great, the rice was presented in a bowl so it was very difficult to eat it with a fork and knife.  It would be better to incorporate the rice onto the plate, the experience would had been less awkward.

Drinks wise, we tried Bandung (not pink but white, fancy but tasted so so)  and Belimbing, (very sour!).  Non-alcoholic but priced the same as cocktails, so definitely overpriced.

The other thing worth noting is that there was just another couple throughout the entire lunch service, on a Friday, just wondering…..
Genuinely delighted with dinner at Belimbing. Creative and innovative use of ingredients, wonderful flavours, just the right amount of food, friendly staff.

Beautiful space and decent service but I felt the food was underwhelming for the price point. Attempt is made at imaginative Singaporean derivations but the landing feels lacking. Clam custard felt like it couldn’t figure out which side of the consistency spectrum it wanted to sit on. Octopus salad tasted promising but was finished in two small bites. Marble goby was good, especially with the crispy skin and probably the main redeeming dish. Corn salat was okay but again, price point was crazy. Normally not a stickler for value but this spot has a way of making you notice the disparity.
Surprised at how good the food was!!! Especially the nasi ulam claypot rice and the fish!!

Expect small pretty plates — not the sort that will fill you up, but enough to keep you satisfied. The food is decent with interesting concepts, though occasionally there are so many elements on a dish that it becomes a little confusing rather than cohesive.

Service, however, could be improved. The team feels perfunctory; no smiles, and while dishes are introduced, there’s little explanation beyond naming the components. When I asked about a particular ingredient, the server simply repeated its name without offering any context or story. For a place that highlights local cuisine, I hope the chef or management can better brief and inspire the staff so that their pride and knowledge shine through.

Practical note: the toilets are located downstairs at Coconut Club, so you’ll need to walk through the noisier sister restaurant. It’s a curious choice — why not have restrooms upstairs to match the otherwise polished ambience?
Amazing experience. The food was simply fabulous, very unique offering of Indian food usually not found in other restaurants. Great vegetarian options.
Both the food and service were amazing, we visited at noon on Sunday for lunch and the atmosphere was perfect too, not too loud nor too quiet.
Amazing hospitality.. shrishaa was best host.. we are very happy with him.

Excellent food and service. Would definitely come back. I think the palak paneer was the star of the night! It was a full house on Friday night so remember to make reservations
We went there to celebrate my spouse birthday and they make it very special at the end with a surprise carrot cake. Overall food was very delicious and great vibes.
The food was very good, with thoughtful elevation of humble, familiar dishes. I really appreciated the creative take on them. The ambience was lovely and made it a perfect spot for a date night.

Excellent mangalore fish curry

Wonderful spot - great authentic Indian food from different parts of India. Our favourites are all the lamb/meat dishes. The gwalawti and Lucknowi kebab AND the Lamb Chips were amazing!!!! Chandran was super helpful and made great recommendations - and very accommodating :) must come!
Went there for a family member's birthday party, it was amazing ♥️ Really nice place to host events with good ambience. The staff was really friendly as well and I really enjoyed their service.🙏😁

We celebrated our anniversary at Bhoomi Singapore, and it was truly a beautiful experience.

The starters were flavourful and thoughtfully presented, setting the tone for the evening. The main dishes were rich, comforting, and perfectly balanced, every bite felt special. The desserts were just the right touch of indulgence to end the night on a sweet note.

What made it even more memorable was the anniversary sweet they prepared for us, such a thoughtful and heartwarming gesture that made our celebration more intimate..

Thank you, Bhoomi, for giving us such a lovely and romantic evening🤍✨

Bismillah Biryani Restaurant -- this corner restaurant in Little India is a nine-time (and counting?) Michelin Bib Gourmand award winner for its excellent biryani; specifically, its dum biryani. I was here with my sister (who is a vegetarian) to enjoy its excellent vegetarian biryani (for my sister) and a chicken biryani (for me). We also shared a very good chickpea masala or channa masala. Service here was good - friendly and courteous. And the dining ambience here was nice enough and in air-conditioned comfort.

Bismillah Biryani is a hidden gem in Little India. The place is simple with limited seating, but the food is excellent. We tried the haleem, biryani, and kulfi, and all three were delicious. Definitely worth visiting if you’re in the area.

Food was great. But this is by far one of the worst services ever. The server are extremely rude and the delays on food for customers at the restaurant. For those who breaking fast for ramadan i strongly dont suggest this place they tend to delay on orders and are very disorganise with pre-orders as well.

I had a very unpleasant experience at this shop. Upon entering, none of the staff welcomed or assisted us, so we had to arrange the seats ourselves. We were then scolded for allegedly blocking the walkway, even though we were not obstructing anyone at all. There was ample space, and no customers were inconvenienced.

Throughout the entire time, the staff stayed behind the cashier counter, merely watching us without offering any help. Instead of guiding us, they only spoke up to reprimand us if they felt we did something wrong.

The overall attitude we received felt dismissive, almost as though our presence and patronage did not matter. It was a very disappointing and disheartening experience.

The Biryani meat was tender but the rice extremely spicy, taking away the fun from the taste. The portions are good. Sadly, I can't recommend the place.

Kulcha bread was microwaved and became hard and tough very quickly. Tandoori chicken portion is very small for the price. Mango lasso is very thin and milky without much mango.

Biryani taste was decent. But the size of the mutton was an absolute scam. For $12 I expected a decent piece of mutton, there were 2 pieces of mutton the size of 2 small dates. Absolutely unacceptable. Atmosphere was also bad, the whole shop looks worn down and dilapidated. Highly recommend trying neighbouring biryani stalls, much more value for money.

The highlight for me was the mutton, it was incredibly tender and literally fell off the bone with every bite. You can really taste the quality in every mouthful. For the portion size and overall flavour, it is truly worth the value and quality. Definitely a satisfying and memorable meal!

Amazing amazing amazing food. Escargots were mindblowingly good. Shoutout to our server Patrick, who was an absolute joy to talk to. Loveliest and most considerate server ever. Je reviendrai sans aucun doute dans cet établissement exceptionnel. Merci encore pour votre service attentionné. :)

We had croquet and some bacon on a wine sauce (forgor the name) and it blew our mind!
The mains which are the beef stew and fish stew is cooked to perfection. Not to mention the french bread that comes with every meal ♥️

I highly recommend this place!

📍: Bistro Gaston @ Keong Saik Road

It was my second visit (1st was 2-3years ago), went around 9 pm on a weekday and was really lucky that Gaston was still open and taking orders, especially when you are just looking for a proper meal later in the evening.

Everything we ordered turned out really good, tried Ricard, a traditional French pastis — an anise-flavored aperitif from the south of France with strong licorice and herbal notes. It’s definitely distinctive and not something everyone will love, but it was interesting to try something authentic and a bit niche. ￼

The steak and ravioli were both very good, especially the ravioli. I loved the sauce so much that I even dipped my baguette into it. The French-style beef dish was solid as well.

I also enjoy their French long beans it was well done and very tasty. If I had to compare just this dish, my personal favourite French long beans is still the one at Bonjour Ma Cuisine, but this version at GASTON was also good.
Tip top, staff are the best around. Food excellent too. Wine is sublime. Enjoy the atmosphere at this cracking spot.

We were very disappointed with the service at Gaston. We came for a birthday dinner and the staff member attending us seemed completely uninformed about the menu and lacked any sense of hospitality. He kept rushing to clear our plates and repeatedly asked if we were done, making us feel uncomfortable. When we asked about a special birthday dessert, he loudly suggested we just order an ice cream and put a candle on top, completely ruining the surprise. No tact, no professionalism. We were shocked. He clearly couldn’t be bothered to attend to us, which made what was supposed to be a happy occasion feel awkward and unpleasant. The food was fine, but the service really ruined the experience and we would not recommend this place.

I absolutely loved their escargot, rich, garlicky, and perfectly cooked. The steak was done just right, juicy and full of flavor. And the foie gras was simply unforgettable, smooth, buttery, and indulgent in all the best ways.

Nestled in the row of shop houses along keong Saik Road, one might just walk right by and not notice this quaint French bistro. Service is great throughout from welcome, through to after payment. Water topped up like 4/5 times in a span of 1.5 hours. Food was off the restaurant week lunch menu, starters were mostly hits especially the mushroom cepes soup, smoked salmon was on point with the seasoning and fennel.
On to the Mains, canard pekin was very generous in portion, just about right if you're really hungry. Well seasoned sauce and paired with roasted Brussel sprouts, mushrooms. Dessert was between chocolate banana cake with ice cream, profitoleros was generous also, with 2 big scoops of ice cream. French desserts never a let down. Overall great experience and will gladly return for more
Cozy bistro vibes, hearty Burgundy dishes, and great wine. Will definitely come back
Gaston offers a wonderful choice of amazing, staple as well as uncommon French dishes in a great friendly atmosphere. My favorite restaurant in SG!
Popped in for a quick lunch. Decided on the Beef bourguignon… it was sensational. Could not fault any part of the meal. Flavours were perfect. I used to try and cook this dish. Never again 😂
Excellent. Authentic french country fare made with quality ingredients at acceptable prices (considering the location). Wine list and service is especially good

There are moments when you crave familiar comfort fare. Tonight we found them in Bistro Gaston. Food was delicious and well-executed. We particularly enjoyed the heirloom tomatoes carpaccio and seasonal mussels.

A little corner of France in Singapore. Authentic French food and wines, always excellent. It’s the kind of place you want to come back to again and again (they also organize many regular events). A true dining experience with a proper menu in hand and attentive staff who are happy to engage and answer questions—no impersonal QR codes here. We’ll definitely be returning!

Great food (even if you're a vegetarian),  wine,  service. It only took 1 message in the morning,  and they remembered that I was there for my friend's birthday, candles were ready for dessert, no need to remind them, no need to double check,  smooth execution and nice surprise. Thank you.

This is a delicious French restaurant in Singapore. Probably one of the best in the city. Fantastic food, attentive service and great atmosphere. Try the rump, the snails, the terrine and frogs legs. Amazing wine too!
We came to Gaston for Friday lunch. The food was excellent! Hamachi appetiser was refreshing with lemonly zing. My seabass main course was nicely done

First impression: cozy is an understatement. It’s tiny and packed with tables, so we were basically elbow-to-elbow with our neighbors. We tried a few dishes — the cheese platter was great, especially with wine. The escargot came wrapped in some kind of pastry, so you could eat the whole thing, shell and all. I liked that twist! The steak? Super tasty.

One tip: don’t rely too much on the staff’s recommendations. I followed their pasta pick and totally regretted it 😅. Better to go in with a plan.

All in all, it’s a nice little traditional French spot. The food is tasty, but not rush-back-every-week tasty. Worth a visit, maybe not a regular.

Dropped by because I wanted to have some pâté en croûte and I heard they had it as a regular menu item, unlike some places that have it as an occasional special.

The pâté en croûte was served with a small side of salad with some vinaigrette and some cornichons. Overall, quite nice but I feel it was a little too cold when served, which to me, seems to lock up the flavour of pâté and rillettes a little bit. It just needs to warm up ever so slightly in order for us to be able to taste more. Just my opinion though.
Oh, and their sourdough was very good!
Will definitely come back to try more.

A Slice of Stockholm, Framed by Theatre and Heritage 🇸🇪🇸🇬

House inside Victoria Concert Hall, this restaurant delivers an experience that feels quietly theatrical in the best possible way. Set within one of Singapore’s most beautiful heritage buildings and just steps from the river, this is the kind of place where dinner naturally extends into a post-meal stroll along the Singapore River. A lovely touch, and one that completes the evening effortlessly.

The décor is elegant and atmospheric. High ceilings, dramatic lighting, rich textures, and a sense of restrained grandeur that feels intentional rather than showy. It’s not minimalist, but it’s not heavy either. The space balances old-world theatre charm with contemporary Nordic refinement, and the result is an ambiance that feels very much aligned with a Stockholm dining experience. Top tier, quietly confident, and beautifully executed.

On the food front, this is refined Swedish brasserie fare done properly. If you’re familiar with Swedish cuisine, you’ll recognise the emphasis on quality ingredients and clean flavours. A standout is the löjrom (Swedish vendace roe), which I didn’t photograph but is absolutely worth ordering.

The wine list deserves special mention, it’s very extensive. I was delighted to spot Orpheus & The Raven Blend, one of my favourite South African wines, an unexpected but welcome find. Pair that with a knowledgeable sommelier and you get an experience that encourages exploration without intimidation. To add to the authenticity, one of the servers spoke Swedish, which genuinely made the evening feel like a small pocket of Stockholm transplanted into Singapore.

Yes, it’s premium priced, but the experience matches the spend. From the food to the service to the setting, everything feels considered and elevated.

A practical note: the bathrooms are not in the restuarant but located within the theatre compound, which means navigating a few stairs. That said, it fits seamlessly with the overall aesthetic and sense of place and super clean. This is Singapore, after all.

Bottom line: Brasserie Astoria an elegant, immersive, and quietly impressive experience. Pair dinner with an after-dinner walk by the river, and you have a night that feels complete.

The Highlights
• Pasta with Caviar: Absolutely stunning and packed with flavor. It felt like a true indulgence.
• Signature Astoria Bread: This lived up to the hype and certainly did not disappoint!
• Wine Selection: Our server recommended a wine that was exceptionally tasty and paired beautifully with our starters.
• A Sweet Touch: A huge thank you to the team for the complimentary chocolate cake to mark our anniversary. It was a thoughtful gesture that made the night even more memorable.

The only slight letdown was the fried chicken. While it remained incredibly juicy on the inside, it was unfortunately very salty.

Overall, it was a glamorous and delicious evening. We highly recommend Brasserie Astoria for anyone looking to celebrate a special occasion!
