This is another omakase we visit each time we are in Singapore.Chef Hamamoto is great at what he does and you will have no regrets eating here.Strongly recommended
One of the best JP Omakase in Singapore : ) You can enjoy the fresh crab here 🦀

Among the exceptional omakase experiences I've enjoyed—from Kyoto and Tokyo to New York and San Francisco, where I reside—last night's meal at Hamamoto in Singapore ranks as one of the absolute best. It is rare to encounter a restaurant that so completely embodies its philosophy while delivering joy at every turn.

Chef Kazuhiro Hamamoto, hailing from Kyoto, personally sources ingredients throughout Japan, guided by seasonality and profound respect for each element. This ethos translates into dishes of remarkable clarity and flavor. If I were to design an omakase menu myself, this would be it—a thoughtful balance of classics and rarities, beautifully prepared with unique elements and cooking techniques woven throughout.

The meal unfolds with confidence. Appetizers—female snow crab, red shrimp, bonito, yellowfin tuna, daggerspike conger—establish the sushi masters' skill.  The Japanese spiny lobster with sea urchin and caviar, a signature, is utterly sublime. Wood-fired rockfish and unagi demonstrate mastery of texture and char, elevating traditional preparations.

The first nigiri, a beautiful piece of white jack, was lightly smoked and set the tone for what was to follow. After I was served, the sous chef ensured the level of wasabi and soy sauce was to my liking—a gesture that reflects the chefs' attention to detail and care for each diner's experience. The tuna progression, from a 206kg specimen featured that evening, includes impeccably cut chutoro, the less commonly encountered shimo-furi, and luxurious otoro. The final nigiri, nodoguro—grilled over wood—is extraordinary. Desserts were impeccable: melon shaved ice and chestnut ice cream with rum provided a thoughtful and delicious conclusion to my meal.

Chef Hamamoto and his sous chef are articulate, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate. They gracefully explained each dish's origins and flavor profiles to me in English, which I greatly appreciated. The sake program offers depth without pretension: hundreds of selections, most priced accessibly at S$35 per pour. The restaurant's format—12 seats, single seating, flexible arrival between 6:00 and 8:00 PM—allows guests to dine at their own rhythm, a luxury increasingly rare in fine dining. In a city rich with culinary excellence, Hamamoto distinguishes itself with purpose and polish. A second Michelin star would be well deserved.

Had a fabulous Omakase at Hamamoto . The dishes are simply divine, especially the Botan ebi & Uni, which are so sweet. Service was top notch and thanks Jason for his attentive service ..... will definitely be back again!
We celebrated my husband’s birthday today at Hamamoto. Everything was perfect! Food was very fresh and service was great. I just wish I had a bigger stomach!

It was more to my taste than the aged Ashino and Indian food Thevar I had the other two days! The skin of the mackerel was slightly grilled, introducing a hint of fruitwood aroma, and the subsequent sushi also had a trace of the charcoal and fruitwood scent, which could be considered a small core. There was a lot of tuna, but when I have omakase, I prefer white-fleshed fish, as it places a higher demand on the chef's skills. There were two kinds of sea urchin, one purple and one red. The purple one was very fat, but the more seasonal red one had a sweeter and fresher taste that was far superior. The dessert was yellow peach, which was not bad, but having only one dish left me feeling a bit unsatisfied.
Awesome!

I had a  wonderful dining experience at Hamamoto. The starters were absolutely delicious—I especially loved the kinki fish and lobster uni caviar, both incredibly fresh.

The sushi was impressive too. Hamamoto-san is generous with the uni, and the seaweed and gari (pickled ginger) were perfect complements to the meal. The Aka uni sushi was simply divine.

For dessert, you get to choose your own, and I went with the musk melon, which was a refreshing finish.

The ambience is cozy and casual, making it a lovely spot to relax and enjoy the food. I would definitely love to revisit!

The pinnacle of Japanese omakase and my new favourite omakase restaurant in SG. Every course and nigiri was exquisite, hard to decide which was my favourite. A few surprise courses not in the menu as well. Portion size is perfect; substantial but won't leave you uncomfortable. You'll get to try various kinds of unique ingredients like hairy crab, spiny lobster, abalone, and uni from different prefactures. Price point is high but absolutely worth it, from the food , to the impecable service to the entire experience. Already planning my next visit in a few months time!
Excellent kAppo-sushi meal with good customer service and friendly chefs.
This place has soul. From the decor to the dishes, you can feel the passion behind it all. Truly a special spot.
Flawless execution and culinary artistry. The service is beyond reproach, and this is our second visit. It was a total treat, and Kazu is a master at his craft.

In search of good sushi recently, I found myself at this fine omakase restaurant. Fortunately, it wasn’t as difficult to book as others had suggested, with a few simple clicks on their website and a decent lead time of a week for the next available dinner.

Arriving slightly early, we saw how two seasoned guests rang the doorbell, and all of us were promptly let in despite it still being early. A point to note if you plan to arrive ahead of time and avoid the wait outside.

Once inside, the modern Japanese counter seating made a strong impression. The bright lighting at the counter and the darker preparation area created a striking contrast.

Before the meal, we were presented with a drinks menu featuring a wide selection of sake, from accessible options to exclusive bottles. I opted for the sake tasting experience, which included twelve different sakes, each paired with the meal.

As the food arrived, it was clear that Chef Kazu and his team take immense pride in their craft. Every dish reflected their meticulous attention to detail, from the uniformity of the plating down to the final flower petal, to the superb knife work, all without unnecessary theatrics. The seafood, flown in directly from Japan, was fresh and of high quality. Each sake was introduced with its origin and brewing process, and the seafood (especially the uni) was accompanied by identification tags and a map of their prefecture of origin.

While all the sushi were great, we especially enjoyed the sushi that were well-smoked and delicately charcoal-grilled. The soup used to cook the hairy crab was rich and flavourful, with a tangy aftertaste that cuts out any fishiness. If only the portion were larger! That said, servings were intentionally sized to ensure that we could enjoy the entire menu without bursting. On top of that, we were surprised with a few additional items off the menu. From taste, portioning to colour coordination, we appreciated that everything was well-balanced.

Service was patient, warm, and impressively efficient. The moment that stood out was when I inquired about the washroom, a staff member instantly directed me, another pulled out my chair, and a third opened the washroom door, all seamlessly and coordinated. Such precision for something so mundane is a testament to the team’s professionalism.

A thoroughly enjoyable evening! Thank you to the lovely team for making this such a memorable dining experience.

The Hamamoto Experience omakase was pretty good: fresh sushi and great service. However, I’m not entirely sure it’s worth the price 🤔

Liked:
- Cocktails. Wasn't quite expecting it, but Hayop does their cocktails right. Each cocktail, named for their primary flavor component, is nicely balanced, and incorporates the requisite regional flavors one might expect in such a restaurant. Particular favorites: Alat, a salty margarita-like with salted watermelon notes, and Malinamnam, a refreshing, umami-forward clarified coconut drink. Pro tip: come early (before 7) for some ridiculously discounted HH cocktails.

- Manam's house crispy sisig. A relatively "safe" version of the dish that only features non-offal bits, but crunchy, savory and moreish with the garlic-flecked sinangag.

- Wagyu and watermelon sinigang. A flagship dish comprising a braised short rib and charred watermelon, doused in a piquant tamarind and watermelon sauce. Interestingly, the charred, maillard flavors are imparted unto the watermelon, not the shortrib - I didn't feel like the watermelon was that much elevated by the charring, but the shortrib was tender and flavorful despite lacking browning, and but the whole dish comes together nicely with the bracing acidity of the tamarind sauce.

- Ube shake. A bit of an irresponsible post-prandial indulgence, but pretty good. Strong but not overbearing ube flavor and the sago bits were a satisfying textural counterpoint to all that rich liquid.

No frills, black or white (or both) fried carrot cake. They are priced at S$5, $7, $9, with the mixed plate starting at $8. The chunks of carrot cake (steamed white rice cakes) vary in sizes when cooked, allowing you to taste the softness and lightness from the larger pieces, and enjoying the smaller ones coated with more egg and seasoning (such as garlic and pickled radish).

While the fragrance of egg is more prominent in the white version, the black one cooked with sweet dark soy sauce is a must-try. Left to caramelise in and develop a slight char on the wide pan, the dark sauce takes the classic carrot cake to another satisfying level of eating. The sambal chili on the side may be necessary for spice lovers, but is also negligible for those who appreciate the dish as it is.

Reviews:
Food quality is always high with the kway chap intestines tasting great. Some gamey taste but believe it gives an additional fragrance for those who understands.

Restaurant Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice
Reviews:
Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice is a Michelin Bib Gourmand hawker stall renowned for its expertly prepared braised duck rice, attracting long queues of loyal customers daily. The duck is braised slowly in a rich, aromatic soy-based herbal sauce, resulting in meat that is incredibly tender, moist, and deeply flavourful. Each slice has a smooth texture and absorbs the savoury braising liquid beautifully, making every bite satisfying without being overly salty.

The duck is served over a bed of fragrant rice, lightly drizzled with their signature gravy that enhances the overall taste while keeping the dish comforting and balanced. The accompanying chilli provides a gentle heat and tanginess, lifting the richness of the duck and adding another layer of flavour. The portion is generous, and the quality remains consistently high despite the stall’s popularity.

What makes Heng Gi stand out is its dedication to traditional preparation and attention to detail. The flavours are authentic, clean, and nostalgic, reflecting classic Singapore hawker heritage. Simple yet refined, Heng Gi delivers one of the most satisfying braised duck rice experiences in Maxwell Food Centre, fully deserving of its Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition.

Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice at Tekka Centre is a humble hawker stall recognised by the Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand for its comforting braised duck rice. The duck is tender and flavourful, braised in a fragrant soy-based herbal gravy that pairs perfectly with a bowl of steamed rice. Each plate is served with fresh cucumber slices that add a light and refreshing crunch to balance the richness of the meat.

One of the best parts is the value. For only about SGD 4, the meal comes with duck, rice, and even a small bowl of warm herbal soup, making it an affordable and satisfying hawker meal. Adding their braised soya egg is highly recommended, as it soaks up the savoury sauce and brings extra depth of flavour. Simple, hearty, and comforting, it is a classic dish that keeps regulars returning. 🦆🍚

Restaurant Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice
Reviews: So far this is one of the best braised duck we eaten for so many years. My whole family love it especially my 96 year old mum.

Restaurant Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice
Reviews: Very tasty and the chili is perfect too! Affordable and very worth it

Restaurant Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice
Reviews: This store braised its duck very uniquely and interesting compared to your typical duck store chains! Taste wise it’s more of gamey taste. Very affordable at $4 with decent meat portion! And comes with a big bowl of soup too

Restaurant Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice
Reviews: Tried Today , 10 / Oct . Rated 3/10 . Soup no good . Duck so so n vv salty ..!!!

Restaurant Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice
Reviews: This humble stall delivers a hearty portion of nostalgic duck rice that truly channels old-school charm. While the white rice may seem unassuming at first glance, it transforms into a flavor-packed delight when generously drenched in their signature gravy—a savory, aromatic broth that ties the dish together with its comforting depth. The meal is beautifully rounded out by a steaming bowl of soul-warming soup, reminiscent of the kind served in decades past. Every bite feels like a culinary time capsule, transporting diners back to the golden era of traditional hawker fare. For those craving authenticity and a taste of heritage, this plate doesn’t just satisfy hunger—it revives cherished memories.

Reviews: Enjoyed this savoury braised duck which always command long queue during mealtime. Ordered the drumstick, I believe the price was high for the part requested. Not sure why there wasn't any soup to come along. The chili was tangy & mildy spicy.

Reviews: Clean delicious and memorable braised duck! Made a special trip to get some meats from the store as my elderly dad had a sudden craving despite us having already cooked lunch. The stall is always busy and definitely worth the wait for the fantastic food and prices.

Restaurant Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice

Restaurant Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice

However, duck meat given was quite little and didn't seem like it was truly a quarter of a duck. Duck meat was moderately tender but a little dry. Restaurant Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice
Reviews: Fabulous food, genuinely an insanely tasty duck and rice dish. Also came with a bowl of soup/broth which was DELICIOUS. The stall only takes cash but there is a cash machine about 1 min away from it. It was $8 Singaporean dollars for 2x duck and rice with the broth. That's about £4.50 GBP. Cannot recommend enough, insanely good especially for the price, I've paid so much more for such worse food 😫 it's so good. And the staff were super friendly and helpful. 5***** for everything. Also came with a chilli sauce which I can safely say was one of the best chilli sauces I've ever tried. Perfect combination of heat and tasty-ness!!

The duck was tender, with a thick, well-balanced sauce that wasn’t overly salty. The rice was of good quality, nice and grainy. The accompanying soup was flavorful and not just plain, colored water.

We also ordered pork and egg, but I still prefer duck.

Reviews: A very tasty braised duck, teochew style. Tried the duck rice with braised tofu. Duck meat was flavorful and tender 😋😋. Rice was top up with braised gravy - this was very nice. Chilli sauce was a nice complement with duck meat and rice. Herbal soup was good. Next time I'll try with added pork or egg. Reasonable hawker price. Queue during peak hours. Restaurant Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice
Reviews:
Quite a basic bowl of duck rice - tried the $4 bowl once, felt that the portion was too small. Went back a second time for the $6 portion, but still, it didn’t satisfy me.

Restaurant Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice
Reviews:
Having been underwhelmed by the Bukit Panjang branch, I decided to give OG another chance. Despite the lunch crowd, the queue moved swiftly. I went for the standard duck rice set and added pork for a total of $6.

The price tag seems reasonable considering current inflation, but the portion size left me wanting more, especially on a particularly hungry day. The braised egg and tofu, which could have made the meal more filling, were unfortunately sold out.

While the duck meat was decent, lacking any unpleasant gamey smell, it wasn't as tender as I had hoped. The herbal soup also tastes quite flat. The chili sauce, too, was too acidic for my taste.

Perhaps I visited on a bad day but it is unlikely I will revisit them again.

Heng Heng Cooked Food Stall has rightfully earned its Michelin recommendation in 2024, standing out as a noteworthy destination for Singaporean street food enthusiasts.
Their laksa is deeply aromatic and bursting with rich, flavourful broth, complemented by generously portioned fresh ham and prawns. While the dish excels in quality and generosity, diners who seek the nostalgic taste of traditional laksa might notice a subtle difference from the original essence. However, one unique touch is the availability of laksa leaves, allowing customers to enhance their bowls according to personal preference—an appreciated gesture that elevates the experience.
Equally impressive is their prawn mee, which strikes a perfect balance between a robust, umami-rich broth and well-cooked noodles, harmonizing beautifully with the freshness of the prawns. It’s a dish that resonates well with all ages, particularly children, making it a fantastic option for families.
Overall, Heng Heng Cooked Food Stall is undoubtedly worth a visit. The food is well-executed, portions are generous, and the pricing remains reasonable, making it an accessible spot to enjoy high-quality local flavours. Whether you're craving a comforting bowl of laksa or a delightful serving of prawn mee, this stall promises a satisfying culinary experience.
Strong prawn taste laksa if you like prawn taste. The soup is tasty but not thick enough for my liking. A lot of cockles though the size is small

The prawn noodles exhibit a delightful balance. The dry version, when combined with the stall’s distinctive chili paste, creates a harmonious flavor profile.  The broth, meanwhile, achieves the perfect consistency—neither overly thick nor opaque, showcasing a refined culinary technique.

The lady owner is really nice & friendly but be warned that the service is a bit slow, resulting in a pretty long queue … but then again, why rush? It’s worthwhile to wait some time for something good 😊

The prawn noodle soup with sweetness from prawns.

This is the most popular Laksa stall in the West. It is hot (high temperature) and spicy hot. Very delicious. Usually there is a long queue. The cockles are very fresh.

这是西部最受欢迎的叻沙摊位。 热，辣。 非常美味。 排队通常都会很长。蛤很新鲜。

Laksa was good but not prawn noodles is average

Not sure how they got their Michelin. Not sure why is high rating as there’s no prawn broth taste. I ordered the medium size for 2 bowls of laksa and 1 prawn soup noodle.

Laksa gravy just plain sweetness, fish cake, cockles, tau pok. Laksa leaves also cannot save this dish.

Delicious and appetizing laksa. No pork no lard. Usual ingredients of laksa, with prawn.
Laksa very yummy, love the fresh cockles inside the laksa. Very cheap and worth it. Tq.

A hearty breakfast at Heng Heng Cooked Food, my first attempt ordering their signature laksa. The stall owner was kind and generous, the serving of laksa priced at $4 topped with huge cockles, these days, such palatable local hawker food is rare to come by, overall, I enjoyed this weekend breakfast indeed and recommend you give it a try too! One of the few better stores in Yuhua Market with Michelin Bib Gourmand. Get your Laksa 🍜 or Prawn Noodles 🦐 for $4, $5, or $6.

The store owners are nice and friendly, allowing you to customise your dish if you don't want some ingredients.

The Laksa soup broth isn't very spicy or thick, which is suitable for my taste. I find that the prawns size varied on different days of ordering though.
First experience here and loved it. Ordered prawn mee . Broth so flavourful. Uncle is very friendly and nice. Can use Paylah. Can recommend.

Have not eaten this in awhile so decided to have a dose as I was passing by this way.
This stall has kept its taste, rich prawn broth but not over powering. Chilli matches well with the noodles. For $4, I would say the serving is generous.

This old school prawn noodle ticked a lot of right boxes - robust soup, sliced prawns, generous portion, hae bee infused chilli paste and even still got kang kong, yet the end result did not quite matches the sum of its parts. The lack of pork lard is definitely obvious here.

It's no wonder most who patronize the stall came for their Laksa instead.
8 ppl q .. she had add lots of water to the laksa kua pot. By the time get served it tastes of nothing. Also if you get bigger portions they only increase noodles but not kua/fish cake etc

A bowl of very good laksa, full of flavours and decent portion, unlike other laksa stalls. I noticed that this stall blanches the noodles first before adding the laksa gravy whereas other blanch their noodles using the laksa gravy. Apparent there is no loss in flavours using the former process.

Cockles and prawns were fresh and the tau pok fully soaks up the laksa gravy.

Well deserving their Bib Gourmand.
$4 for this laksa, with 3 tau pok and 2 half prawns. Taste is good. Noodle portion is also ok.
Tried their laksa which looks good.  It is reasonably priced.  A very Traditional laksa.  Would prefer more aroma and taste.
排很久，但不會讓你想回訪

Truly michelin food. Smooth curry, juicy chicken, awesome sambal, huge fish cake and huge chunk of potato are really makes a complete set.
.
#sgfoodies #sgfood #michelinguidesg #hengkee #currychicken

Delicious curry mee! Fragrant, flavourful broth and generous ingredients.
Friendly staff and great service!

This stall opens at 10:30 am, and I arrived at 10:35 am to queue. Ended up waiting about an hour just to try the drumstick Curry Chicken Rice Noodles at $9.50. Unfortunately, the taste was very average.

I’ll probably try some other better food around this area next time.
Best curry chicken noodles in Singapore.

Heng Kee Curry Chicken Noodles,  comfort in a bowl 🍜❤️

Their curry is rich but not jelak, with that old-school, slightly grainy spice paste that tells you it’s been simmered patiently. The gravy clings to the noodles, spicy but rounded, and somehow always hits harder on a hungry day.

For the $9.50 portion, the chicken is generous and tender, tofu puffs soak up all that curry goodness, and the potatoes are soft enough to break apart with a spoon. I love how messy it gets halfway through oil on the surface, curry splashes on the bowl, zero regrets.

It’s not fancy. It’s not trying to be trendy. Just a solid, deeply satisfying bowl that feels familiar, comforting, and reliably shiok every single time.

Queued about 1.5 hours during weekend lunch but is totally worth it. The curry gravy is rich and full of flavour and the chicken is super tender. After all these years, the standard is still there. Always satisfying!
Perfect place for lunch. So good! Cash only.
Fantastic yummy curry with tender chicken. Simply delicious comfort food.

Very flavourful bowl of curry chicken noodles. The gravy is thick, rich, and robust—adding chili takes it to another level. The chicken is tender and delicious. Two sizes available at $7 and $9.50 (I had the $7 bowl).Went around 11am and queued for about 30 minutes, but it was absolutely worth the wait. Thumbs up! 👍 Will definitely be back again.

总体一般，三星评价。
来芳林办事顺便想吃下基记面家可是转了几圈找到后发现没营业，路过楼下的时候看到这家排队索性下来试试……
排了接近半小时，前面也就是七、八、十来个人，询问后我要了一碗大份；鸡腿米粉面价格9.5新币。
米粉面就是一半米粉一半黄面，加个鸡腿切段。
份量是大份，实际没有多少米粉和面，一块豆腐切开，一条鱼条，四分一的土豆一块，一根鸡腿切段。
制作方式就是先煮熟米粉面然后像西安羊肉泡馍一样用大锅里的咖喱汤来冒（汤装进去再倒出来反复几次）配料和粉面，几次下来再装上同一口大锅里的咖喱汤就成了，直观看卖相很好。
找地方落座试了一下味道，说实话咖喱汤汁很一般般没那么浓郁，撇开汤面浮的黄咖喱，发现汤色有点发黑，这是我不喜欢的，尝了几口给鸡块肉还可以，豆腐和土豆算是陪衬，面和粉的融合也没有吃出多么出彩，9.5新币的价格属实有点对不起出品，尤其黑的汤底，我担心嘌呤应该超标不知道多少。
潦草几口吃完了粉面和豆腐配菜起身离开。
店家虽然挂着米芝莲的招牌，但是在我看来是有差距的。
卫生情况；食阁卫生就别太讲究了，但是我是看不惯一手收完钱又去翻动食物都不戴手套习惯。
就这样吧，服务还是不错的。

Another Michelin hawker.

The queue moved quite slowly, despite only 5 pax in front of me. I guess it’s the way the owner preps the dish. He would cut the chicken, then drench it with scoops from the huge curry pot, rinse it before filling it up with curry sauce again, on top of cooking the noodles/ bee hook.

I ordered the bigger bowl which cost $9.50. The curry broth is flavourful and not too spicy and the chicken is tender and soaks well with the curry. It came with tau pok and fish cakes as well. Thought it would be better if there’s an egg to go with it.

After tasting it, I understand the hype and it’s well worth the wait. Go try this if you are nearby.

Heng Kee Curry Chicken Bee Hoon Mee is definitely worth the hype, but come prepared. Cash only, so be aware! The stall is extremely popular and there’s usually a long queue around 30 minutes at about 1pm, so patience is required.

The wait pays off though. The chicken is wonderfully tender, cooked just right without being dry, and the curry soup is rich, fragrant, and full of depth, soaking beautifully into the bee hoon and yellow noodles. Every spoonful feels comforting and satisfying, especially if you enjoy bold curry flavours.

Overall, a solid bowl of curry mee that lives up to its reputation just remember to bring cash and expect a queue.

The original curry chicken noodle that I have had for more than 20 years! The young chap must be the 3rd generation running the stall. The tender flavourful chicken is soul food!
Heng Kee’s chicken curry noodles should be designated one of our national dishes.
The queue can be quite long especially during weekdays with the office crowd.. so I prefer to go around 1.30pm where you then queue about 15 - 20 minutes ‘only’.
Really loved their Curry Chicken Noodles. I waited in line for 20 mins for the food.

Chicken meat is bloody. Man used bare hand to pull noodle for a takeaway before my turn. I wanted to take chilli but old lady snatched away and said she will take for me. Taste so so, not as nice anymore. Used to eat there often but today was really unhappy and will be the last time.
Be ready to be scold by aunty if u scooped more chilli. Bought 2 bowls and one came with a strain of hair. Serving is small and not cheap for a hawker centre… they pay low rent… first n last time.

Reviews:
Naturally, the visit was motivated by the expectation of experiencing Michelin recognized street food, a promise that carries a certain intrigue precisely because excellence is achieved within simplicity. Fortuitously, a heavy downpour combined with an unconventional dining hour allowed immediate access without the queues often associated with such establishments, making the ordering process effortless and direct.

Unfortunately, the top selling dish had already sold out, leaving the noodle soup as the secondary choice. While entirely respectable in execution, the dish ultimately settled into the territory of adequacy rather than distinction. The flavors were balanced and competently prepared, yet lacked the depth, memorability, or technical nuance one anticipates when Michelin recognition enters the conversation. Considering the elevated price point for the region, expectations naturally rise, and here the experience remained firmly within the bounds of “good,” but never approached exceptional.

This is where a certain skepticism emerges. Across Asia and equally throughout parts of South America, street food exists that delivers astonishing intensity, personality, and craftsmanship capable of redefining expectations in a single bite. In comparison, the reasoning behind awarding a Michelin star here feels somewhat difficult to reconcile from a purely culinary standpoint.

Service, however, deserves clear acknowledgment. The team was notably friendly, attentive, and accommodating throughout, contributing positively to the overall impression. The setting itself aligns fully with authentic street food culture: plastic chairs, practical tables, visible utensils, and the unmistakable sensation of dining somewhere between kitchen storage and open workspace. Far from being a flaw, this authenticity forms part of the experience and should be understood exactly as such. Street food is not the Four Seasons, nor should it attempt to be.

In conclusion, the experience remains honest and competently delivered but ultimately falls short of the anticipation created by its reputation. Pleasant, authentic, and well intentioned, yet from a culinary perspective it settles at a measured three points rather than a moment of genuine astonishment.

Restaurant Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle
Reviews:
If you're looking for a "hug in a bowl" at Bedok Interchange Hawker Centre, Hock Hai is the definitive choice. This Michelin Bib Gourmand recipient is famous for a version of curry noodles that prioritizes fragrance and balance over sheer heat.
​
​The Broth: Unlike thick, viscous gravies, this is a "drinkable" curry soup—rich with coconut milk (lemak) and aromatic spices, yet light enough to finish the whole bowl without feeling overly stuffed.

​The Chicken: They use poached chicken that is remarkably tender and succulent, served in generous chunks.

​The "Flavor Sponges": The tau pok (beancurd puffs) and large wedges of potato are the stars, having spent enough time in the pot to fully absorb the savory broth.

Ordering the "Bee Hoon Mee" mix is the local pro-tip; the thin rice vermicelli clings to the soup while the yellow noodles provide a satisfying chew. It’s a mild, comforting meal, though spice lovers should definitely stir in a spoonful of their signature sambal for an extra punch.

​Quick Verdict: At roughly $4–$6, it remains one of the best value-for-money meals in the East. Expect a queue during peak hours, but the efficient service keeps things moving fast

All meat given was chicken breast.

Restaurant Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle
Reviews: Ordered the medium size $6 portion. Gravy is rich and creamy. Meat is also nice and juicy. They give good portion of ingredients too. Highly recommended. Will definitely come eat again.

Reviews:

Unfortunately got to face the worst attitude of the both lady,especially the older/senior lady staff who will shout around even to her own male colleague !
HORRIBLE SERVICE at Bedok Hawker !

Restaurant Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle
Reviews:
What do we have when we add steam chicken into a nice pot of curry with tau pok and kantang?

Of course, we have curry chicken! Put it into a bowl of kway tiao or noodles, we have the legendary curry chicken noodles.

Sounds easy huh? Obviously not.

Skip the hardwork to the stall owners and we as consumers will just share how nice they are.

This stall at bedok interchange hawker serve one of the best curry chicken kway tiao in Singapore. The pricing are priced differently due to the chicken parts you are requesting for. If you have no preference for the parts, good news. Just buy the cheapest portion and you will be happy. If you want the drum, be prepared to pay more. However you wont regret your decision since this is so worth it.

The drum is tender and nice. Sip abit of the curry while you tear the meat off the chicken. Ah. Nice. Eat the kway tiao or noodles with a bit of the curry, hmm delicious.

This one really must try. It is super good.

Location: bedok interchange hawker

Restaurant Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle
Reviews:
I patronize this stall quite often. Have always enjoyed their curry noodles. However on this day , I had the worst experience. I ordered 1 small($5) thigh noodles, added 1 dollar of gizzard. She said 7 bucks so I asked why .. then realised she gave me medium($6) instead. I said nvm and paid for it. Sat down , ate with son and realised it wasn’t thigh that was given. Went back told her she messed up the entire order. She just said she didn’t hear thigh, only heard $6. Not a word of apology.
Went back to seat feeling dam frustrated. Took another mouth and returned the whole bowl to her and walked away. Totally lost my appetite after this. I am trying to find their web page or their boss contact . Any help will be appreciated.
I hope others don’t have go thru such frustration like me

Restaurant Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle
Reviews: I like it. Curry is not too thick. Will repeat. High volume hawker center, so can’t expect too much on atmosphere.

Restaurant Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle
Reviews: This outlet is so far one of the best stall as the curry is served pipping hot with the fresh white steam chicken n noodles. I find the gravy here thicker n richer in flavour. To fully enjoy the meal , one can add more ingredients  like chicken or potatoes to satisfy ones craving.  Afterall the waiting queue is always long, so like the chinese saying, make it worth eat until shiok.

Restaurant Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle
Reviews: Long Qs during peak hours. Curry noodles were good and one of the better ones I had.

Restaurant Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle

Restaurant Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle
Reviews: Perennial favorite. Can't remember how many times i was here.  Silky chicken, robust curry soup, its hard to go wrong. For those unwilling to travel to Hong lim, this is your best choice.

Potatoes undercooked and no curry taste.

Even the curry itself is not fantastic.

Reviews: Curry wasn't superb, like it's always quite bland for these noodles stall. I mean flavour is there.

Reviews: My personal favourite of curry chicken noodle across Singapore. Visit off peak hours to avoid longer waiting time.

Restaurant Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle
Reviews:
I recently had the chance to try this curry noodle stall based on recommendations from my friend. Here’s my experience:

First, the tofu was absolutely delightful—soft, flavorful. The chicken was another highlight, incredibly tender and juicy. While the curry had a slight hint of spiciness, it was very mild overall, making it enjoyable even for those with a low spice tolerance.

Paired nicely with the noodles that were decent but not extraordinary. The portion size and price felt fair, offering good value for the experience.

I made my visit in the late afternoon and was thrilled to find no queue at the stall—a rarity for a place with such a strong reputation.

Now, I understand why this stall is so popular. While some might find the flavors not to their liking—taste is, after all, deeply personal and subjective—for me, this was absolutely worth it.

Restaurant Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle
Reviews: This curry chicken noodle is sibeh tasty, especially the curry soup. Taste same as Sarawak curry. Singapore food always no taste for Malaysian, but this one very great!

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews:
Fish balls definitely made in house.
The fish balls are soft and spongy compared to the commercial ones. When cut open it reveals pink texture.

Noodles are rather clumpy and some are not fully cooked.

My $ 5 dollars bowl came with a big bowl of noodles but only 8 fish balls. That works out to about 50 cents a fish ball.

Chilli sauce was spicy and a little tangy. Quite appetising.

Cost on the higher side.

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: Great bowl of fishball noodles. Loving it. 👍🏽

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: Ordered a bowl of fishball and fish dumpling soup $5. Fishball is the soft version, no bounciness  as compared to others, thus it depends on your preference. But I love their fish dumplings, really really good. Just something hot and yummy to go with my  CKT when in this hawker Center.

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: Used to be very good fishball standard but seems to be overly soft and noodle not that q as previous.

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: Ordered fishball soup and i enjoyed it

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: I asked for no chilli but both packets came with chilli. I can't eat spicy food. 2 bags down the bin. Ordering system is bad cause uncle probably couldn't hear properly.

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews:
Standard has dropped tremendously, there’s another newer stall there selling better fishballs noodles, probably explaining why there’s no more queue here. The fishballs here are overly soft.
Customers also probably not coming back due to their “money face” requirements of wanting additional 10 cents just for a small empty bowl … highly NOT recommended … just look at the photo, decided not to continue eating it and buy something else to eat …

Reviews: Cocky rude owners who don't bother when their apparent friend cuts into long queue and the stall people still serve her. Food wasn't that good and compounded with the service, had to give a 1 star. Would be zero if possible.

Reviews:
Bad cocky stall owner. Asked for spring onion on noodle, female owner refused, said "nobody put spring onion on noodle"?? Asked to borrow a small bowl must pay 10 ct.
Fishball mediocre, cut chilli was miserable, soup extremely salty. Only saving grace is noodle portion is large.

Reviews: 魚蛋有點彈性，麵條有點硬，也是有點甜

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: I disagree with the stall being on the Michelin list. Sampled again today & found the fishballs to be overly soft (suggesting too much water used), lacking in fish flavour, & unnecessarily salty. Their “her giao” (fish dumpling) was not velvety at all; perhaps overcooked

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: I wouldn't say it's the best fishball noodles in that area, however the cook deserves  a 2 star review. Ordered a takeaway large dry meepok without chilli. Ended up with dry meepok with "super generous" amount of chilli. In the end struggled to finish the whole food.

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews:
No standard ... ordered large (takeaway) ... was charged 5.50$ .
It was pack in plastic not container.  They Actually charge $0.50 for plastic! The way they pack the chilli made the soup spicy for my kid. ..and for $5.00 u will expect more .

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: Love their fishballs

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews:
Price has gone up by $1 but understandable due to inflation. The dried version is really spicy so beware even if you ask for less spicy!
Definitely like it more than the non spicy dried version which is ketchup based.

The fishball and fish dumplings are my fave and the noodles are al dente and taste sooo nice with the chilli even if you can’t take spicy! Haha. I got the old uncle to do my order and I feel so honoured that we got such a legend!

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: Nice fresh fishball made by stallholder. Like their soup and dry versions. A must try for fishball lovers.

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews:
How do you know that the fishballs are legit? When I poured out my takeaway Mee Pok, the fishballs bounced off my plate and bounced even more onto my table. Can you imagine if the fishball can bounce more than an amateur basketball player can dribble, how good is it?

Hock Seng Choon is the kind of stalls where they do not focus on variety and its just a few things, but these few things are done to perfection; very Japanese way of perfecting things. Needless to emphasize, the fishballs and all are super legit; if you don't trust random Singaporean's review and only trust people with certs and all that fancy titles, you can see the newly obtained Michelin Bib sticker that uncle has just received in Dec 2024. Congrats Hock Seng Choon!

If you happen to have the luck to stay in the East, please drop by and give them some love; this place deserves it. By the way the servings are bigger than what you might usually see, and its the kind of generosity that big, growing adults really can appreciate; value-for-money 100%. Let's go!

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: Very disappointed.. I used to love the mee pok there.. I don’t know is it changed stall.. the taste is totally different from what I remembered having many years ago. And guess what?! I saw a cockroach crawling at the noodles area.. 😣 I just touched down from the airport so I’m too tired to make a big fuss.. but I will not go back anymore.. eekkss.. oh yes! Forgot to mention the Xiao di’s service was bad too.. like I owe him some money.. 😅

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: Been a patron of the fish ball noodles stall since the early 80s. Serving good Old School fish ball noodles with no frills. Each bowl is served with your choice of noodles (soup/dry) with five handmade fish balls and one fish dumpling. A dine in or takeaway serving currently costs SGD 4.00 Takeaway soup costs an additional SGD 0.50 My usual choice is the dry version with either Mee Pok or Mee Kia. The noodles texture are done just right and the accompanying chili paste mixed in has a good spicy "kick" which may be overwhelming for some. The texture and taste of the fish balls are good. There is usually a queue at this stall during peak meal times. Overall good consistency of the noodles served here if it is prepared by the elderly gentleman (boss), but only slightly diminished if prepared by the younger man (assistant).

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: Just average taste..only fish balls.... stingy in ingredients....no minced pork in soup or anything..... compared to other fishball stall.....won't come back...

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: Amazing noodle with added chilli

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: Noodles just a mess of oil, sauce and chilli paste. Soup full of msg and to give credit to the fish balls, it’s a personal taste. There are better ones all over.

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: Very tasty soup. Fishball is soft and nice, portion is enough for me. Overall is recommended.

Reviews: Noodles. Feels overcooked . Fishball is soft. Only one fish dumpling. Will not queue for this.

Chicken rice 🫲

Char siew 👎

The stall holders don’t like it if you ask for additional chicken rice. Maybe they are worried the rice will sell out before the chicken.

It is always a challenge to eat the chicken rice from this stall as the queue is always long. Finally the queue for today is considerably short with 4 customers in front of me, however the wait is still long which took approximately 20ish mins. As I observed how the stall owner prep the food, he literally don’t chop the meat but slice cut the meat and remove every single bone. That’s probably why the wait is long and the queue is formed. TLC - tender loving cut!
Aside the long queue, the taste of the chicken rice is nostalgia! Simple yet full of flavour and reminds me of my childhood days. The various condiment and chilli sauce elevated the overall flavour of the chicken rice.

Indeed the chicken ia succulent and tasty! And the chilli is spicy with lots of ginger, i quite like it too. HOWEVER Expect always long Q, BUT the long Q is simply due to V Slow service turnaround by the stall owner and not so much large crowd trying the buy and try the food.

If u wish to try, make sure u come during very off peak hour or u just have to cater at least 30 to 45 mins wait just for a 10paxs Q ahead of u. Otherwise do give this stall a miss the slow service is v turnoff.

Also do note usually by 1330H-ish it will b almost sold out. Price starts from $3 per portion.
The queue is ridiculous long, very bad attitude especially the auntie, not recommended stall. They are better chicken rice stall at this hawker centre. Do not visit this outlet.

S$3.50 (excluding kopi) 🙇🏻‍♂️👍❤️
Hoe Kee Kitchen (和記雞飯小厨) at Jurong West is a gem. The chicken is tender, the rice is fragrant, and the garlic chili packs a punch - all at prices that remain affordable for the local community.

It’s no surprise there’s often a long queue, but the hearty portions and wallet-friendly prices make it worth the wait.

Good old stall and food and cheapest! Had their chicken rice since young. Traditional taste feels nostalgia. Expect queue daily and go early before sell out. Sometimes 1pm already sold out.
Be respectful. Most stall owners there have been around for decades. They look after each other and community. Don't complaint about waiting or anything.
I ordered the drumstick chicken rice which cost $5.50 now. There some small bones in it as it was not debone . Must becareful when giving it to little kids.

Chicken rice ($5) - Tender, boneless. Good rice and clear soup.

Started selling out at about 1pm.

Best chicken rice but terrible experience queuing for it. They allow their regulars to cut queue which makes the people queuing look like idiots.

If you are a regular of this shop, please stop cutting queue. You are making everyone's life terrible.

Queuing began at 9:00 a.m. on a Saturday Monday. It took roughly 20 minutes to get to my turn. I asked Auntie what time they opened and closed. She added that they open at 8.15 a.m. and close when it's sold out. Their chicken rice starts from $2.50 or $3. I ordered 鸡尾 for SGD 4. To be honest, I believe it is adequate and reasonably priced. But I wouldn't line for it.
Taste is awesome but quantity of chicken is paltry. Knowing this I ordered for $5, not a big difference. So order smart.

Rice was ok, not much taste but was fluffy. Black Soya sauce was diluted. Soup ok. Overall ok
$2.50 Chicken Rice....VFM.

This chicken rice has been one of the absolute favourite for a few decades now, and it’s still cementing its place as one of the best in the west (if not sg!) with their $2 offering/plate.

🍗 the chicken is tender across all portions, even down to the breast meat!
🍚 fragrant rice with light soy sauce, could easily down 2 plates of this any day, by itself hehe
🌶 one of the best chicken rice chilli to date, always chase down a saucer of this with my meal
⏰ Queue can easily stretch up to 30 mins - 45 mins during peak hour and they are normally sold out after 130-2pm.

🏆 kudos to them for keeping prices affordable whilst maintaining the standards 👍🏻

Always a comforting meal to have 👍🏻🍚👌🏻🐔💰
