Google reviews says 4.8 but Gg says 3.5.

@ingleside.sg boasts fermentation but Gg didn't get any punchy hits of flavour. There are a myriad of "exploitations" that could have enhanced the flavour of their dishes which I found rather bland, but the three appetisers, three mains plus one side and a dessert we had did not entirely showcase the "power of fermentation".

I'm not saying the food is bad, it's nice enough, especially when I added salt to it. The food however isn't amazing, it isn't 4.8 ⭐️. Good execution by the chef with earrings who was very skilled, interactive and generous, but way too simple (after all the hype), and the portion sizes were small for the price - I was still hungry after dessert.

With all the talk about miso, koji, vinegar, etc, I would have thought my small 35 day dry-aged A5 Kagoshima wagyu sirloin ($153.47) would feature a taste elevation with a marinade or a sauce but nope.

I will have to say though that the smoked sea salt brownie dessert (did not pick up on the smoked sea salt flavour though) made our night. The brownie looked hard and stodgy but was light, moist, soft and intensely chocolatey. The accompanying pineapple bits were also good but they should have fermented the accompanying pineapples, or if they did, I could not tell.

Anyway, we had a great evening and adjourned to Tsujiri for ice cream because I was still hungry.

Went to Ingleside to try their famous dry aged meats and woodfire cooking. The Tajima Wagyu Picanha certainly did not disappoint. It was tastefully prepared, marinated in shio koji and finished over a wood fire.
Beyond the already awesome mains, I was pleasantly surprised by how good the sides were too. The sourdough bread with their homemade miso butter was super unique and full of flavour. We also tried the scallops, which were fresh, delicate, and beautifully prepared. Simple, well executed dishes that made the meal really enjoyable.
We ended the meal with a deconstructed lemon meringue tart. Dare I say it might be the best dessert I have ever tasted, especially because it was not too sweet, which is the highest compliment by Asian standards. The combination of a buttery crust with tangy lemon curd was unique and absolutely delicious.

Had the pleasure of trying out Ingleside last week, and we got a few items to share between me and my partner.

The sourdough and miso butter was a simple yet delicious pairing, with the umami of miso cutting through the richness of the butter!

We also tried the rockfish and steak. It was my first time trying rockfish, and it was delectable as well. The aging help to bring out more complex flavours in the rockfish and is definitely a must try!

Lastly, we also got the deconstructed lemon tart, which was balanced with just the right amount of tartness. Me and my partner wolfed it down so quickly!

Definitely a restaurant to go for special occasions, or if you just want to have some great food!

Last visited in Dec 2025

I’ve visited Ingleside 3 times this year to try their 3 seasonal tasting menus - Ignition, Embers and Inferno. This restaurant’s motto is to follow three core cooking/preparation principles - dry aging, fermentation, and woodfire cooking. All these 3 preparation methods were evident across the 3 tasting menus they’ve had this year. If you don’t want to try their tasting menu, they always have an a-la-carte menu too.

In each tasting menu, the meal started with a bunch of bite-sized starter courses, which across the 3 seasonal menus were brilliant. This was followed by their signature Truffle toast. The taste of the Truffle toast evolved across the 3 seasonal menus but remained an absolutely fantastic umami item. The truffle toast course was followed by 2 other courses before the main course which is always a Wagyu dish. The Wagyu of the ongoing Inferno menu was the best in my view. That main course is followed by a pre dessert and a dessert course. My favourite dessert was that of the Embers menu which was a chocolate and berries dessert dish.

Service is fantastic. I always get a counter seat which I prefer as I like to see the kitchen in action. The staff are very jovial and kind in their interactions. They explain every course in detail and the head chef also himself comes out to serve & explain some of the courses.

Overall, this is a very good restaurant and it’s not a surprise that they were included in the 2025 Singapore Michelin guide. A 100% recommendation

We ordered the Lampino Iberico Chuletero, Tajima MBS 6-7 Wagyu Picanha, a lemon-ginger spritz, and sourdough. Both meats were cooked medium rare, with the Wagyu standing out for its intense beef flavor and melt-in-your-mouth texture. The Iberico was slightly firmer but still flavorful, complemented by charred corn, Marsala sauce, and mushrooms that balanced its richness. The sourdough was delicious, especially with the exceptional seasonal fermented butter that should definitely be sold separately. The ginger-lemon spritz, though refreshing with a salted rim, could have used a stronger ginger kick. The staff’s informative tour of the dry-aging and fermentation process added a personal touch. A great experience overall!

Items we got: Lampino Iberico Chuletero, Tajima MBS 6-7 Wagyu Picanha, lemon ginger spritz and 1 sourdough

We ordered medium rare for both meats. The highlight was definitely the Wagyu – it had a really, really deep and intense beef flavour and also quite literally melted in your mouth.

The Iberico was not as soft as the Wagyu but still really flavourful. It was served with a lot of supporting elements (charred corn, a marsala sauce and mushrooms) that also perfectly balanced the Iberico's rich flavours and made it less heavy and "jelat".

Quite liked the sourdough, but the star has to be the seasonal fermented butter that came with it – they really need to start selling it in a jar!

The ginger lemon spritz came in a glass rimmed with salt and was refreshing! Perhaps a minor nitpick would be that I wish the ginger flavour could be a bit stronger, but anyone ordering it would definitely like it nonetheless.

Lastly, really appreciated the staff's tour of the dry-ageing and fermentation processes that Ingleside clearly is proud of. Also thought that the concept of using wood as just another ingredient was really unique.

Definitely would be coming back again during special occasions!

Ingleside is a great experience. The staff paid great attention to us, catering to our needs well by bringing us a bag hook when they noticed I had trouble with my bag.

We had the Wagyu Piranha and the Lumina Lamb Loin, which were both marinated with their house-made shio koji marinade. It brought a unique flavour to both the beef and the lamb, elevating both dishes well.

The food was absolutely delicious, clear to see why the picanha was a best seller, preference for the meats. Not particularly fond of ginger but the lemon ginger spritz was very refreshing and helps with the richness of the foods. Would love to try more of their butters in the future. Service was wonderful, very attentive, very professional. The atmosphere was good, very warm and pleasant to sit in though voices from other tables do carry especially if guests are being loud since the space is compact.
Had a wonderful experience in Ingleside! Love the food and service here! My personal favourite is the wagyu picanha, super tender and soft!

Dry ageing and woodfire, two elements combined to elevate the taste of the protein served by them. The wagyu and pork was perfectly tender and the lemon meringue tart was sweet, mildy sour and so refreshing ☺️ what an experience!

We've just returned to our hotel room after one of the best dinners we've ever experienced. Iru Den managed to strike the balance between relaxed yet professional service. The staff offered a comprehensive explanation of the food and drink. We particularly enjoyed the 6 glass beverage flight,  some outstanding choices. The food was delicious and just exceeded our expectations. It was a delight to watch the chef and kitchen staff prepare the courses with such dedication. This is a very special restaurant and one to put on your list to visit! Thank you Iru Den for such an excellent evening!

Interesting food .... Location is a bit of a hunt ..... I am not a fan of counter seating but thery don't seem to have much other options even though I mention to staff of my preference.....service is pleasant but there is room for improvement
Fully embracing taiwanese flavours..
It tasted like elevated Taiwanese cuisine and the service was warm and welcoming. I highly recommend the beef which was super tender and melted in my mouth.
Fresh produce from Taiwan transformed into amazing cuisine. Familiar flavours prepared perfectly
One of the best fusion omakase concept out there - with a touch of home yet fine dining experience. Highly recommend anyone out there to give it a shot.

Best Fine dining experience I experienced so far. Got to know them from the YouTube channel "Get Fed".

I didn't put any picture, because no photos are needed.

All I can say is just when U thought that the carbs is just to fill your stomach, think again. Your word will be "wow".

Worth the money too if you think it's expensive.

Iru Den’s omakase felt like a heartfelt tribute—especially with the loving touch of Chef’s MIL Cai Po woven into the experience. Each dish told a story: the Uni Mee Sua and Amberjack were crowd favorites at our table, but for me, the standout was the Wagyu Striploin—so tender it practically melted on the tongue. The honeycomb in the dessert leaned a bit sweet for my taste, but it didn’t overshadow the overall balance and creativity of the meal. Excellent service, thoughtful pacing, and a menu that delivers value without compromising quality. A memorable evening worth revisiting.

I had the chance to dine at Iru Den with my date, and it was an amazing experience. The ambience felt like having dinner at home—warm and inviting—yet with the polish of a thoughtfully curated meal.

One of the dishes that stood out for me was the ciabatta served with 菜脯 compound butter—such a unique and delicious touch. Every dish was well-executed, but the appetizer, Kueh Pie Ti, really surprised me with its burst of flavour. The duck was also a highlight, carrying a gentle smokiness that was perfectly balanced—not too strong, just right. And the 卤肉 Donabe was simply amazing, with little charred bits that added depth to the sweetness of the braised pork.

Overall, it was a memorable evening with excellent food, cozy vibes, and a sense of comfort that made the dinner truly special.

We would like to sincerely thank you for the warm welcome and excellent service during our recent visit. Everything was handled with such care and professionalism, which made our dining experience truly enjoyable.

Our Japanese friends especially appreciated the food, and they thoroughly enjoyed every dish. The quality, presentation, and hospitality exceeded our expectations.

用台灣食材做的法式餐廳每一道都蠻用心蠻好吃的，特別是最後一道的費南雪超級好吃，是全新加坡吃過最好吃的費南雪，其他每一道都非常好吃，只有炒飯比較遜色一點

I was quite excited to try this restaurant but unfortunately something didn't quite connect with me. I think sometimes when trying to develop deep complex flavors they instead get muddled and feel flat... or perhaps my palate was off that night. But for example, amuses bouches usually have pointedly contrasting textures and flavors. The beginning bites here, while tasty, all had a similar thick crusty base which: first, weighed down each individual snack and second, blurred all the flavor profiles together. I missed the peaks and bursts of flavor I've come to expect.

Everything was well-prepared and I appreciated the effort to visually highlight the produce from Taiwan with pictures and maps presented on an ipad. However I was surprised that the only tea on the menu was a japanese hojicha. The beverage offerings were a bit disappointing in general. I don't like the taste of Evian (the only still and sparkling option) and tap water was not offered as an alternative.  Also no real non-alcoholic beverages were available.

Excellent food remarkable service/hospitality period! Love their Caipu Butter, so glad it’s free flow  I couldn’t stop having it so addictive.

Congrats to Iru Den for being listed in the Michelin Guide Singapore 2025!
Taiwan influenced cuisine. Chef husband and sommelier wife working hard together. Flavourful food. Ample free parking.

Fantastic modern Taiwanese fusion meal. Chef’s menu had a good variety of dishes with premium ingredients. My favourites include the uni somen, pork cheek, and seasonal clay pot rice. Good selection of sakes and wines with 1 for 1 corkage. Would love to dine here again!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Iruden = absolute gem.

From start to finish, this place just gets it. The space is beautifully done:  minimalist modern, warm, with just the right amount of buzz in the air. But let’s talk about the food: every single dish felt thoughtful, fresh, and totally unforgettable.

We had the bigger menu, and special shoutout to the carabinero prawn chawanmushi, Uni somen, mini abalones claypot rice, they were unreal. You can tell they’re serious about quality ingredients and flavor. Everything was super balanced, nothing overdone, and it all just worked.

Service? On point. Friendly, knowledgeable, and totally dialed into the vibe, helpful without hovering.

Honestly, it’s one of those rare spots where you walk out thinking: “When can I come back?”

Highly recommend, whether it’s date night, a special celebration, or just because you want a damn good meal.

First time having Taiwanese inspired omakase and it was very impressive. Special shout out to chef Javier and his team for the wonderful creations and memorable experience. Looking forward to the next season’s menu!

Is an interesting place, in the black and white houses in between Orchard and Newton MRT. You can see the owner takes great pains in designing the place but a waste the staff he employs are not very enthusiastic. Our server is either her English is poor, I couldn't hear her at all. I've to keep asking her if she can speak up until I give up. Wine pairing is nice but the pour is very small. Food is not bad, but is not great. It feels like a hit and miss place. We're the only 2 pax at lunch. I can't see this resto lasting for too long unless some major changes will take place.

A hidden gem worth every detour.
Tucked inside a restored black-and-white bungalow on Scotts Road, Iru Den delivered one of the most memorable Spring 2025 menus we’ve tasted. Dinner opened with a bright Guava Fizz, then moved through a flawless parade of dishes: ten-year “black-gold” radish broth that warmed the soul, 7-day dry-aged marlin over cool cucumber “snow,” uni-slicked somen laced with wild mountain herbs, and a maqaw-pepper short rib that proved charcoal and perfume can coexist. The clincher was the clay-pot taro rice—socarrat crackle, milk-fish belly umami, pure comfort.

Service is gentle yet intuitive; staff introduce every ingredient without a hint of script. The dining room glows under binchōtan sparks and moonlit windows, making you forget Orchard Road is metres away. Prices sit in fine-dining territory, but the craftsmanship, storytelling, and ever-changing seasonal produce justify the splurge.

Already counting down to the Summer menu—book early or miss out. Highly recommended.
Detailed + well curated taiwanese omakase! Every dish was creative and their ciabatta + cai po butter was to die for!!! Highly recommended!
Superb Taiwanese cuisine fine dining , everything you order are all delicious, especially “Clay pot rice “

Our first time at Iru Den but 2nd time we’ve had Chef Low’s creations. The last time was back at Il Den and we remembered that dinner fondly, esp the donabe. This time, hubby wanted Asian for his 50th and I was pleasantly surprised to discover that Il Den has evolved into Iru Den with a Taiwanese focus. It was wonderful to see how the restaurant and the chef have evolved.

Lovely restaurant tucked inside a garden, we enjoyed the interesting ingredients that’s seldom seen locally. Service was good, with servers taking the effort to explain the ingredients used. Wine pairing hit the spot as well thanks to Emily, the sommelier. We also liked watching the kitchen action from our counter seats. Some dishes were better than others. I wasn’t a huge fan of the marlin dish, but we really enjoyed the UFO, somen, langoustine and clay pot rice. Hubby really liked the caipu butter!

It’s not easy running a fine-dining restaurant in Singapore esp for chef-owners. So glad to see Iru Den holding its own over the years, we’ll be happy to return!

Was there for a birthday lunch.
The concept of Taiwanese omakase is rather refreshing as it is pretty uncommon.
The mapo chawanmushi is one of the silkiest egg I ever had, but sadly it was too salty for my tastes. Perhaps some rice was missed
The oyster fry amuse Bouche is a nice nostalgic treat
Short rib was delicious, I definitely choose it over the fish…

Chai po butter is a genius combo but I think some grilled mantou will make a better fit
Trout was pleasing especially with the cherry tomato halves. But the accompanying salad is hmm 🤨
Sesame ice cream, velvety smooth, glid down like a creamy snow ski
Service was enthusiastic & friendly.
They were especially kind & thoughtful to umbrella us in the rainy weather
Lovely dinner experience with Iru Den. Served great food, dined in great Ambience and hosted by a set of lovely service crew

This was my second visit to IRU DEN, and I was thoroughly impressed by their updated menu featuring Taiwanese influences. Almost every dish was a standout, but I was particularly blown away by the UFO oyster, uni somen, and donabe. Each dish was thoughtfully crafted and bursting with flavor. I can't wait for my next visit to try more of what they have to offer!

Had a fantastic experience here. Took a grab and did the 6 course & extras. So personal. Owner there cooking. All explained and lovely interesting food. Highly Recommended
Damian & Matthew from London

Been having Ishizawa san's food since his Shinji days. Never disappoints. He has set up his own establishment at a cosy place that was vacated by another Japanese restaurant that was helmed by a less than friendly chef then. The vibe is so different now. I skipped taking photos of the sushi and only took the omakase dishes. All great! 👍🏻

A friend took me to Ishizawa for a weekday lunch as a pre wedding celebration and it was such a lovely choice. We went for one of the sushi omakase lunch sets and everything was done with care and precision. Nothing flashy, just quietly excellent sushi that lets the ingredients speak for themselves.

The chefs communicated with us in limited Japanese, which somehow made the whole experience feel even warmer and more personal. There was a lot of smiling, nodding, and gentle explanation. The staff were also very attentive, always topping up tea and making sure everything was just right without being intrusive.

We were recommended a seasonal sake to go with the meal and it paired beautifully with the sushi. It elevated the whole experience and was well worth it.

I also learnt that this is a place you need to book quite far in advance, so planning ahead is definitely recommended. Once you step inside, it genuinely feels like you have been transported to Japan. Calm, refined, and a very memorable meal overall.

This is easily one of the best omakase experiences I've had in Singapore. It flies under the radar with minimal social media hype and surprisingly few Google reviews, which makes it feel like a hidden gem. A friend recommended it, and I'm so glad they did, it's outstanding!

The service is genuinely premium, the dishes are beautifully presented, and both the sashimi and sushi were exceptionally fresh. When I gave some gentle feedback about one of the cooked fish dishes, the chef immediately responded by preparing an extra course of fried fugu as compensation. That level of care for customer satisfaction really stood out.

The location inside Raffles Hotel adds to the special feel. The chef Inoue himself was warm and welcoming, with a constant smile throughout the meal.

Highly recommended if you're looking for authentic, high quality omakase without the usual crowds or over the top marketing.
Ishisan is ichiban
Amazing! Ishi-san has embraced his own techniques post-Shinji, expect more courses and lighter tasting sushi pieces - leave feeling balanced and refreshed BUT not hungry :”)
Outstanding experience on all accounts! Big love from Perth, Australia.
Small 10 seater sushi restaurant located in Raffles Hotel. Amazing food.
Amazing service and the food was fresh and delicious.

Incredibly great dining experience with melt in my mouth fresh quality of sushi piece! Definitely a hidden gem! Thank you Chef Takahiro Ishizawa for his welcoming and friendly hospitality, will definitely return again!

We first got to know Chef Ishi-san when he was the head chef at Shinji, which has been our favorite sushi restaurant for nearly a decade. Now with his own restaurant Ishizawa at Raffles Hotel, he has maintained the same exceptional standard. The interior exudes a warm, elegant Japanese aesthetic, and the service is attentive and thoughtful, making the dining experience truly delightful.

Ishizawa is a true gem. A joy to experience... refined yet relaxed, masterful yet warmly inviting.

Chef Takahiro Ishizawa, formerly Head Chef at Shinji by Kanesaka, brings all the elegance and precision we’ve long admired, but here, he’s created something more personal and intimate. Every course is crafted with incredible attention to detail, balancing flavour, texture, and beauty in perfect harmony.

As long-time fans of Oshino and Shinji, we immediately recognised that same integrity and high standard we love, now infused with Chef Ishizawa’s generous spirit. The seasonal seafood, flown in from Japan several times a week, was impeccable…. and even the rice was memorable on its own, carrying a quiet depth and subtlety that lingered with each bite.

What stood out most, beyond the technical mastery, was his presence and generosity - in portion, in spirit, and in the way Chef Ishizawa made us feel seen and genuinely cared for. It never felt stiff or formal; instead, it was beautifully refined dining with a light, friendly, and engaging atmosphere.

Ishizawa is the kind of place you leave feeling both impressed and deeply nourished - not only by the food, but by the whole experience. A place to savour slowly, exceptional in every way.

We’re so grateful for the recommendation, and we can’t wait to return. A standout in Singapore’s Japanese dining scene.
Luxurious sushi, lovely service from all the staff and a fabulous skillful smiley chef! Lunch was perfect!

Absolutely unforgettable omakase experience at Sushi Ishizawa, Raffles Singapore.
The craftsmanship here is Michelin‑level – every piece of sushi, uni, and sashimi is prepared with such precision and respect for the ingredients. Chef Ishizawa is incredibly kind and communicative, making the evening feel personal and welcoming.

The photos I took won’t do justice at all. You really have to come and experience this yourself. Highly recommended for anyone looking for an intimate, top‑tier sushi experience in Singapore!
Authentic delicious edomae sushi from ex shinji master with impeccable service.

One of the best omakase lunch ever!!  The ingredients were very fresh and every dish was so well curated in terms of flavor and textures, making the entire  lunch very memorable.
Will definitely be back for more. Oishi 👍🏻

The sushi here is exquisite. Each sushi piece comes with interesting yet delicate layering of seasoning and fresh Japanese herbs, which enhance the flavors of seasonal fish. The rice was airy and tangy. The sushi melts in your mouth while you try to savor it. I'd strongly recommend pairing the meal with champagne or sake so it doesn't overpower the delicate flavors of sushi but that's just me being very Japanese. Anyways it's a great deal for what it is.
Delicious, authentic, restrained and elegant. Thank you for a memorable meal!

Ishi san was the former head chef of Shinji Carlton (1 Michelin star), joining Shinji when it first opened at Raffles Hotel years ago. He now has his own space in what was previously Oshino.

At Shinji he was known for his clean, precise, sushi - in the Kanazawa house style. Sushi there was always about the delicate balance between neta and shari. You might get better quality of fish / more luxe ingredients (at higher prices) elsewhere,  but no other chef I tried got the balance just so.

Now that Ishi san is no longer part of the Kanazawa group, he does not need to stick to the house style. He can pick and choose from his fishermen contacts, and the neta quality is a 1/2 to 1 step up. His shari is warmer, cleaner mouth-feel, a touch more umami. The sushi still held in that delicate balance of restraint and yummy.

Always a good time with Ishi-san.
Friendly, dedicated, delicious!
amazing sushi with the most talented chef (ishi), 10/10 recommend for omakase in sg<3
好吃，但是后怕。我怕以后吃其他地方的寿司，吃不下嘴了。
Food, service and ambience were fantastic! The attention to detail and preferences makes the overall dining experience great! Great value for money! Highly recommended!

Food is amazing. We were always huge fans of Shinji at Carlton and this place is run by the same folks. They actually remembered us from the Shinji days. We had the Ten Omakase which was a lot of food but well worth it. The quality is really amazing and the set up of the restaurant is cozy and welcoming.

Absolutely incredible experience from start to finish. This newly opened Japanese fine dining spot is a hidden gem! The ambiance is elegant yet welcoming, and every detail feels thoughtfully curated. What truly sets this place apart is the chef—clearly a master of the craft. Each dish was a work of art, both visually and in flavor. The sushi was melt-in-your-mouth fresh, and the tasting menu was a perfect balance of traditional techniques with modern creativity. Hands down some of the best Japanese cuisine I’ve ever had. Highly recommend for anyone looking to be wowed.
Still top notch !!!

Mutton Soup And Sup Kambing (SGD $17) @ Ivy's Hainanese Herbal Mutton Soup.
.
Established sometime in the year 2000 by Max Ng and named after his wife, this beloved stall continually draws long queues, and on occasion, sells out within 1 hour of opening for the day.
.
They source mutton from New Zealand, and are known to omit ginger in their hot soup / broth served in bubbling clay pots, which is stewed with about 20 different herbs including nam yue / red fermented bean curd paste. Their thin and light soup / broth has deep meaty savoury sweet bitter herbal flavour.
.
The tender boneless mutton meat has meaty savoury flavour, the succulent bone-in mutton ribs slide easily off the bone, the juicy goji berries / wolfberries lend herbal sweet bitter flavour, the crunchy black fungus / wood ear fungus has vegetal earthy savoury flavour, the bouncy button mushrooms carry vegetal earthy sweet flavour, the spongy tofu puffs have grainy savoury flavour, and the crisp fried bean curd sheets have grainy savoury salty flavour. Pairs so well with white rice.
Soup so taste less 😓😓😓
Very yummy mutton soup with herb flavour that is not overpowering and very nice to drink. Meat is tender and side ingredients used are fresh. Can try.

Ivy's hainanese herbal mutton soup. My favourite mutton soup of all time. Not gamey at all and not overcooked, every piece melts in the mouth. Served in a Chinese clay pot. Choices include mix of mutton meat, shanks, leg meat or tendons. Prices start from $12 for their small portion. But it's a filling portion and worth every cent, rich flavours of their secret blend of Chinese herbs, goji berries, tau pok, and beancurd sheets and black fungus mushrooms and spring onions. Served with their fermented beancurd garlic chilli sauce.

We were lucky going on Wed and it closes at 7.30pm. We arrived at 6.15pm and everything was sold out except meat. Ordered the $14 small portion. The soup was so flavourful and didn't have the mutton smell that puts you off. I drank finished the soup. The meat was tender and generous. Everything was quality and to perfection. Really hard to find nice mutton soup and this did not disappoint. 10/10.
I love mutton soup, this stall serves delicious Chinese - Hainanese Herbal mutton soup!
The soup is very flavourful and hearty. They close whenever they sell out, or by 19:30hrs.

If you are a lamb soup lover, you must make the trip to Ivy Hainanese Herbal Mutton Soup in Pasir Panjang. This place serves what is, in my opinion, the best Hainanese lamb soup I have ever tasted—a true hidden gem.

What sets this soup apart is the broth quality. It's incredibly flavourful, deeply herbal, and tastes rich without being greasy. The lamb itself is tender and fresh, with absolutely none of the gamey smell that sometimes plagues mutton dishes.

The real proof of quality? I didn't feel thirsty at all after finishing the bowl! This confirms that the broth is genuinely slow-boiled and relies on natural ingredients and herbs, not cheap MSG, for its depth of flavour.

Beyond the taste, the value for money is superb. For the quality and generous portion size, the pricing here is incredibly reasonable, especially for Singapore. It feels like you're getting a premium, home-cooked meal for a hawker price.

This is a mandatory visit for anyone who appreciates authentic, nourishing, and expertly prepared lamb soup!

This shop has an almost cult like following and consider me a convert. Strong, pungent, herbal and decadent. Soup wakes you right up with it's herbal and meaty aroma, then suddenly sweet when the goji berries burst. It's on the pricier end but if you're going to have something as rich as this you want the good stuff and they serve the good stuff. Very good value as a heavy meal. Uncle serving sometimes get a little sassy but consider it part of the experience

Kinda disappointed today.
The soup taste less thick with my mutton look reddish (look bloody on the outside n inside). Moreover, it is pricey for such quality today.
Not a wonderful makan today. Maybe other days will be better.
Delicious soup. I ordered a small portion of mutton/tendon ($16) and expected a light one person meal, but I struggled to finish.

This store serve some of the most authentic Hainanese mutton herbal soup I’ve ever tasted. I think the Michelin inspection team should come pay a visit to this store and see if they stand a chance to get the Bib Gourmand Michelin Award next year. Try to believe !

The Best herbal mutton Soup todate.
Very traditional and flavorful. Mutton Meat simply got good bite and fungus and other ingredients are sufficiently given and balance. Price for money. Good value. Store was formally from Tao Payoh Lor 7. Standard just as good if not Better. Highly recommended.

July25, this is the 1st time after a long time to try a mutton soup; moreover a claypot one. I always worry about the soup being over night but after tasting today especially Ivys’ just simply love it, hot on a raining day, meat was chewy, for me it was good. Recommend.
I go for the $14 mutton meat soup. The soup is nice, the meat ok but too little meat. Too little meat for $14. too much other stuff.

Best of the best!

I came from Oklahoma just for the soup and it did not disappoint. It is very flavorful and refreshing.
mutton a bit less but overall is one of the best in sg.

The chilli stood out for me the most. Garlicky, with bright tangy notes to complement the soup.
It’s in the hawker centre.  I always take away.  The mutton soup is really rich in herbal taste n the mutton taste good n tender.

IMO the best curry puffs in Singapore. The auntie is always nice and the taste is fantastic. Always get several when I visit Singapore. Amoy food centre is also very central to everything.
Delicious puffs. We tried both the chicken ones.

Loved the people - they were so lovely and kind &  then combine with the taste of the curry puff! 🤯Best chicken curry puff across our travels. Go before they are sold out and enjoy- we wished we could have had one every morning. ( we tried them all & our fave was the classic chicken curry puff)
Ordered 50 curry puffs for my office party. The original curry puff is really good.

Banging puffs. Black pepper is supreme.
Very tasty, affordable, curry puffs!
Gotta catch em all crispy puff. I tried them all but I don't know anymore which one is the best. It doesn't matter, they all taste good!

Unreal puffs! We tried all 3 savory versions. Common to all is the golden, flaky, flavourful crust, which honestly barely needs filling to be worth eating. Of the fillings, they are all excellent and worth trying, but my unexpected fave was the sardine - it tastes like the best possible version of a prepackaged spicy sardine snack, with big chunks instead of tiny shavings of fish. Amazing spot.
ミシュラン獲得カレーパフのお店。月曜日の朝の8時30分頃に来店したら誰も並んでいなかたのですぐに買うことができました。パフはサクサクほろほろで食感がいいです。カレーはピリ辛でジャガイモと鶏肉が入っていたが卵の塊は無し。とてもおいしかったです。
Wow how can something so deceptively simple be so amazing. Loved the sardine and black pepper puffs, just bursting at the seams with flavor.

Flaky, buttery, and thin dough encase fillings of various types (curry potato and chicken, black pepper chicken, sardine, yam) and fried to a golden perfection. The pastry has a gentle crunch and then melts in your mouth as you continue to chew on it with the succulent chicken cubes or soft curried potatoes.

Batches of these addictive puffs are prepared and cooked freshly at the stall, which makes them incredibly enjoyable with their warm and moist fillings.

I like the crispy flaky curry puff and yam puff, but the size is smaller. Curry puff is not too spicy, and yam puff is sweet enough as I personally don't like less sugar, less oil and less salt for any desserts. Will come back again.

The quest to try Michelin Bib Gourmand stalls continues. Went in the morning where the stall owners were still busy making the day’s worth of curry puffs. Got the original and sardine versions for $2 each. Not the cheapest curry puffs around but it’s a bang for your buck.

The curry puffs have an incredibly thin, flaky crust that gives way to a soft, flavorful curry filling.

The sardine flavor packs a punch as well but loses out to the OG curry flavour.

Definitely a must try! And eat it when’s it piping hot. Well worth the calories!
Friendly staff - they have 4 flavours and I tried the chicken and potato ($2). The skin was nice and light, the fillings were tasty as well. The only issue for me was the puff was kinda small...
Very friendly owner and I tried the Curry Puff and Black Pepper Puff, both amazing and not expensive at all!
No.1 Curry Puff for their Black Pepper Chicken ($2.20 each)!!! It's so delicious and worth to try it!!! The skin is so crispy even have passed 30mins after the delivery!!!

Very nice curry puff. The skin is perfect. Melts in the mouth with the curry potato chicken paste. Like the sardine too but sold out earlier. Curry puff is smaller in size. $2.20 a piece. Overall still a nice eat.
Best curry puff in town. Fresh, hot and that black pepper is so good....homer good.

The crust is super flaky, while the filling is fragrant, well-seasoned, and packed with flavour. Whether it’s curry chicken, sardine, or yam, every bite is satisfying. 😋👍

Perfect as a snack or a quick grab-and-go treat. Be careful… once you start, you can’t stop at one! 😂

Highly recommended if you’re in the area — Jin Ho Jiak! 😋😋😋
So good, tried the yam puff & the curried chicken with potato. Both really yummy, perfect pastry and delicious fillings. You gotta try it.

Dinner at Jaan by Kirk Westaway was very good. The room is elegant without being over the top, the service team was excellent, and sitting seventy floors above Singapore certainly adds a little drama to the evening. The food was clearly Michelin quality and thoughtfully presented. Service may have been the best part of the night. We grabbed a Grab over and it was easy.

That said, it felt like we were paying for the views and the Michelin aura as much as the food. Everything was good, but the pricing felt about 20–30% too high for what actually landed on the plate. The pacing also felt a bit rushed for a tasting menu. When you’re dropping that kind of money, it’s nice to let the evening breathe a little.

If you’re celebrating something big and don’t mind paying for the full Michelin experience, you’ll likely enjoy it. Try to get a table right by the window if possible. We were seated more toward the middle, which had some advantages, but the skyline views were partially blocked.

Overall I’d call it a 4.5 that carefully rolls up to five stars on Google, though this isn’t truly a five star experience in my book. It is a Michelin two star restaurant and you can see that in the technique and presentation. I probably wouldn’t return. The cost is simply too high for the overall experience, which can run about $700–$1,000 per person depending on how enthusiastic you are with the wine list.

Had a very pleasant dining experience at Jaan by Kirk Westaway. The food felt elegant and thoughtful, with each dish perfectly balanced and beautifully presented. Nothing felt excessive or overworked, there was a quiet confidence in the cooking, where everything was refined and composed without trying too hard to impress.

The flavours were clean and precise, allowing the ingredients to speak for themselves. There’s a certain restraint that makes the experience feel very intentional.

The ambience and view are also wonderful, creating a calm and intimate setting that complements the food well. Service was impeccable, attentive, warm and seamless throughout the afternoon.

Loved the view from Jaan and the food was excellent. It was a great lunch — we truly appreciated the outstanding cuisine and the fact that Chef Kirk came to greet all the guests. A memorable experience.

Jaan by Kirk Westaway gerçekten harika bir deneyimdi. Manzara muhteşem, yemekler özenli ve lezzetli, servis ise son derece profesyonel. Singapur’da özel bir akşam için gönül rahatlığıyla tavsiye ederim.

Jaan by Kirk Westaway offers an elegant fine dining experience with stunning skyline views. The British-inspired tasting menu is refined, seasonal, and beautifully plated. Flavors are delicate yet memorable. Service is polished and attentive throughout. It’s expensive, but perfect for special occasions and a sophisticated culinary treat.

This was my third time coming to JAAN, but the first time as a 2 michelin star restaurant. The decor has become more elegant and minimalistic somewhat.

The tasting menu was very tasty, with standouts such as the goose moose tart topped with fried celeriac. The old hen’s dish was very delicious too with the umami of the yolk really coming through and accentuated by the buttery mushroom brioche. The line caught seabass was perfectly flaky and flavored by a touch of seaweed, the scallops were so sweet and the fish reduction sauce was really intense.

The waygu steak wrapped by crispy chicken skin was very innovative but felt a little oily and heavy, with the accompanying foie and jus.

The breads were delicious especially with the devonshire butter with lemon thyme. And the cheese board was outstanding, especially accompanied by the 2004 port that they offer with the cheeses.

We had a bottle of 2011 austrian vetliner which was just fantastic.

The desserts were delicious as well, especially the caramel pear, such delicate pastry with a beautiful caramel flavor coming through.

A nice place to visit for a special occasion.

The tasting menu is thoughtfully curated, highlighting seasonal ingredients with elegant flavors. Service is polished and attentive, making the overall experience feel special. While it is pricey, the ambiance, creativity, and consistency make it a memorable choice for a celebratory or upscale dining occasion.

Had an absolutely exceptional dining experience at JAAN last week. Was here for a birthday celebration and took the lunch set. Every dish was beautifully crafted, thoughtful, and full of refined flavours. The menu was well-paced and memorable, with each course telling its own story.

The service was impeccable — warm, attentive, and without ever feeling intrusive. The ambiance is elegant yet intimate, making it perfect for a special occasion or a meaningful night out.

JAAN is more than just a meal; it’s a complete experience. Truly deserving of its accolades, and I would happily return again. Highly recommended.
Had the most amazing evening! Great food and very professional service. Ambience is romantic with a great view !

Had a really nice experience at Jaan by Kirk Westaway. The food was great - refined and seasonal, but still very approachable. Each course felt thoughtful without being overly complicated, and everything tasted clean and well balanced. It’s the kind of fine dining that feels effortless rather than stiff.

We were lucky to have a table with a view of Marina Bay Sands; watching it change from daytime into nighttime while we ate was honestly a highlight.

Service was relaxed, friendly, and on point, which really added to the overall vibe. A great spot for a long, enjoyable meal where the food and the view both really shine.

Extremely awesome fine dining experience!

The appetizers were the best appetizers I have ever had among ten-ish 1-3 stars Michelin restaurants. Very fresh flavor with clear characteristics of each ingredient. The main dishes (seabass and venison) were very satisfying that the sauce brought out the freshness and flavor of the meat. The mini pancake with caviar was a great combination that we asked for more 😆

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐is not enough to the server! I don't remember her name but she is a Taiwanese and she did very well and clear introduction to each dish. The great service was definitely a critical factor for us to have an unforgivable fine dining experience.

In total it cost around 450 SGD per person with 5 course lunch plus pre-order caviar, no wine pairing. It was expensive but it was worthy.

JAAN was our second Michelin star experience in Singapore (after dining at Les Amis in March 2023) and boasts a modern British cuisine.

We enjoyed a beautiful dinner the week after the F1 Singapore Grand Prix and the view from JAAN alone was incredible - you could see the whole track lit up at night. We chose JAAN for an early wedding anniversary celebration.

The restaurant itself is an absolutely exquisite space with breathtaking views of Singapore, being on the 70th floor of the Swissotel Hotel. You get views out to sea as well as Marina Bay Sands. The standout in the interior is the stunning glass installation that hangs overhead.

We had the 8 course degustation with standard wine match; as we drink primarily New Zealand wine back home the standard wine pairing was more than sufficient as it was all international wines we had not tried before.

A precursor to starting the main menu were a tomato tart, ‘goose mousse’ tart, ‘fish & chips’ (caviar atop a delicate potato base) and ‘cheddar pancake’ (deep fried pancake ball with molten cheese centre).

We were served breads with butter prepared right at the table, along with fresh lemon thyme.

Next we had charred leek & potato soup, ‘English garden’ which consisted of 32 different ingredients which was just tremendous in its detail, violet artichoke which had a cured egg and was rich and delicious and paired with crunchy mushroom toasts to dip, red mullet, a hand dived scallop for myself (my husband requested an alternative to shellfish prior to booking and received a gorgeous poultry tart), Kagoshima wagyu, ‘gin & tonic’ (which you could choose to have alcoholic or non-alcoholic gin with as a palate cleanser), then two dessert options of which we both went for one each; a rich chocolate hazelnut medley or a strawberry peach creation.

We also opted for some cheese prior to the Gin & Tonic course; generous portions provided along with myriad accompaniments.

We were served a beautiful little cheesecake to finish as an anniversary gift, before petit fours.

All of the food was delicious, refined and creative, and served on some beautiful plate ware.

The wines were fabulous and added that extra ‘wow’ to the food, as any good pairing should.

The staff were attentive without being obtrusive and chef Kirk Westaway also came out and made the rounds of all tables which was a lovely touch.

We were there around 3 1/2 hours but it never once felt like it dragged.

We were also given a small loaf of the bread, butter and more lemon thyme to leave with.

This restaurant was definitely at the upper end of our budget ($388SGD pp for dinner and $268SGD pp standard wine pairing - all prior to taxes) of which we were partially to blame for forgetting tax on top in our conversion! but it was an incredible experience nonetheless. Highly, highly recommend for a special occasion.

Lots of interesting and flavourful food creations. Small morsels but very filling as there were many items on the menu. Service was impeccable n we were constantly asked if we were fine. They were open to changes in menu in accordance to our dietary needs.

2019:
Excellent! Service was tip top, food was superb, love every single dish in the signature menu. And, the stunning table view on the 70th floor made dining here incredible.

It's worth every penny. Will be back again.

The best way to describe JAAN is the emperor with no clothes. You are paying S$300 per person for a dinner with dainty little bits that doesn't fill. Part of the meal include handmade flavoured butter with a very hard stale bread and a thumb sized cut of meat with hand crafted sauce. Only one can pretend that such a meal is luxurious. That’s why they call it a “tasting” menu, to bring you away from the fact that the whole point of eating is to replenish hunger. The taste is satisfactory but just not worth the price. Some of their other offerings include truffles and pigeon meat 🐦 The view from the 70th floor is less than expected because of thick and dirty windows. Our lady receptionist who greeted us had a very upper lip attitude, like we were not welcome, because only guests who made a reservation (only possible via paid deposit 💸 with credit card confirmation) are welcomed in. Impossible to dine here without reservation. The restaurant has only 12 tables. It’s challenging to make a reservation, because the restaurant is supposedly always full until you go in and see all the vacant tables. It was another obstacle to find the restaurant, as the lift to the 70th floor was hidden in some obscure corridor. Overrated, over complicated British cuisine. I’m sure they tried their best anyway. 🙈

Wanted to highlight that there was this China woman who was serving my table on the night of 16 Dec who was extremely unprofessional and rude. Here's what was wrong with the service that ruined the whole meal: (1) Kept sweeping crumbs on me when sweeping the table. (2) Talked in a rude tone and wasn't speaking English - has to improve her English as she was mumbling ingredients. It was unclear and showed a lack of understanding of the dishes presented. (3) Kept moving my personal belongings around. I had my phone lying at the side and she kept moving it right in front of me as if I'm about to eat my phone for the next course. (4) Most importantly, spilled water on me. Not just a splash but a glass full of water. How this happened was she lined 5 glasses right in front of me as she was cleaning the table (yes, at the edge of the table). Then she proceeds to elbow sweep the table causing one of the 5 glasses to completely spill on me (some are not even mine but she decided to line them up in front of me for some strange reason). I was drenched and was not able to enjoy the meal from then on. She did not apologise or remedy the situation. She just slid away silently. My table then looked like a construction site with cloths lying around to soak up the mess she made.

Maître d handled the situation well, but a level of service should be expected. People shouldn't be whispering in Chinese when explaining the food. If a villager from a non-English speaking country is hired, then she should be properly trained. Proper English with understandable pronunciation should be a given, especially so when a restaurant is 2 star Michelin. As a result of sloppy service, I lost my appetite, was drenched and I was unfortunately unable to enjoy the meal despite the food being quite good. Have some pictures as well of the mess made, happy to share.

Perfect experience as usual. Shout out to Joseph who accomodated our request for a customisation of the menu. Bella was the epitome of professionalism and warmth- it's no wonder she was recognized by the Michelin guide, and rightfully so! And also kudos to Kirk for always checking on his guests. And of course the food today. Next level. The langoustine dish and scallops were out of this world. And somehow the Berkshire pork was improved compared to our previous visits. Also the generosity for the cheese platter. We will be back in a couple months!
Great fine dining with a wonderful view of Singapore, towards both the south and towards the city.

Food was excellent, but the service was disappointing. After the first course, I waited for the staff to clear the crumbs and replace the utensils, but it never happened. When the birthday cake was served, no one offered to help take a photo — I had to ask. The waitress said she would return, yet I saw her attending to another table with the cheese trolley instead. I eventually approached another server, and by then the candle was already close to melting. To top it off, no one saw us out as we were leaving. Having dined at many Michelin and fine-dining establishments, this experience really fell short. That said, kudos to the sommelier and chef — they were wonderful.

So happy to be back to Jaan, our favourite 😍 restaurant 😋... Food is sooooooooo YUMMY as usual !! Service is EXCELLENT! Sylvia is gentle & cheerful, serves with a positive vibe. 😄 keep up the great work, Jaan Team ❤️
Incredible moment. Food is marvelous and very kind service. Can't wait to visit again.

Overall a splendid lunch at Jaan, and I would highly recommend this experience.

Wished:
Would be fantastic if the crab stood out more than the pancake in the crab pancake. Langoustine with caviar was nice and light but wish for more sweetness from the langoustine. The lime fruit pieces in the salsa of the pork dish was too much/big and overpowered some bites of the dish.

Everything else was perfect. Particularly enjoyed the cheddar straw, leek & potato soup (this is a master piece), scallop, and chocolate hazelnut dessert. Rye bread with butter was spectacular, so it was a truly pleasant surprise when they packed us a complimentary box of bread and butter to go.

Thanks team Jaan!

Outstanding on all counts. Low key and understated; the food is very, very good and elevated with an excellent wine collection guided by an enthusiastic and knowlegeable sommelier. The dim sum, roasted pork (not to be missed) and everything else is tops here. Frequented by many regulars. Place has been around for decades and has a loyal following. Highly recommended.

No attention to detail, inconsistent in each servings.

金湖海鲜酒家是新加坡知名港式粤菜馆，招牌煲仔饭堪称一绝，鹅肝腊肠的独特搭配香气四溢，米饭粒粒入味，值得专程品尝。海鲜类菜品如胡椒蟹、豆豉蒸贵妃蚌都保持了高水准，食材新鲜度可圈可点。点心方面虾饺、炸虾等出品稳定，能尝出海虾的鲜甜。不过价格确实偏高，人均消费100新币以上，部分菜品如炸虾表现不够稳定，有时依赖厨师状态。服务专业周到，环境适合商务宴请或家庭聚餐。午市套餐性价比相对较好。整体而言，适合重要场合或港式粤菜爱好者，但若追求性价比需谨慎选择。建议避开高峰时段以获得更稳定的出品，总体而言是体验正宗港式风味的好选择。
Food always good! Clay pot rice was excellent. Beef brisket delicious!

This Michelin-recommended Cantonese restaurant, situated in the basement of Forum Mall, was my choice for my birthday celebration this year, marking my second or third visit. Previous experiences here were unremarkable, leaving little memory of the dishes. However, this visit changed our perception, with their superb Cantonese cooking and the freshness of the ingredients.  However, the food was rather pricey.

Our meal comprised a selection of dim sum and other dishes. The dim sum was delicious, and the salt and pepper squid was authentic, being well-fried and not overly chewy. The white pepper claypot crab with glass noodles and the deep-fried prawns with crispy garlic were both fresh and flavorful, with a natural crustacean sweetness. The claypot beancurd with fish paste was exceptional, featuring an umami-rich gravy that made the dish very delectable. Desserts were satisfactory but not out of the ordinary

The only disappointment was the steamed egg with lobster meat, as it was rather bland and unexciting. Service was somewhat lukewarm, possibly because we aren't their regular customers, which was a slight letdown. Despite this, we plan to return to explore more of the menu, as the cooking is excellent.
Nice foods all staffs very nice and friendly.

Tried the dim sum at Jade Palace and was really impressed. Everything tasted fresh and well-crafted, especially the har gow and siew mai, which were juicy and full of flavour, though the portions were a little on the small side. It’s a cosy spot with attentive service, and I’d definitely come back just for the dim sum alone.

Our go to place for cantonese steam fish. Always fresh, always good. Atmosphere is a little noisy but that what makes a good Chinese restaurant.
Wow, what a wine selection. One of the best cellars in Singapore. I'm coming back with my wife for a date night :)

Very bad experience in this restaurant which caters with many caucasian tourists who obviously don’t know the food quality is poor and extremely expensive compared even to the more prestigious restaurants in Orchard road. More concerning is the hygiene. During our visit, birds were seen freely feasting on uncollected bowls at diners’ tables, which is unacceptable for any food establishment.

A very unpleasant dinning experience.

Broth was okay but nothing outstanding. Chili for the noodles was mediocre, it lacks character. Prawns were not fresh, the flesh was soggy and tasted like a freezer, large prawns were just mid-sized taking into account of industry standards.

Michelin worthy? Definitely not.

Closing hour according to Google was 3:30 p.m. however certain food items were sold out by 3:00 p.m., they started cleaning the shop splashing soap water onto my face and clothes, they also began to shut the metal shutter making the most annoying and deafening noise thru the process while I was still eating.

Today marks my last visit.

You need to beef up your standards, seriously.

No crowd when I came on Sunday morning before 10am, it’s like 10% occupied. Ordered the local recommended pork rib prawn noodle, I selected soup version. Inside the restaurant it’s clean and considered comfortable. On the table a container is provided for pran shell and bones, I found this very well organized. For tourist, beware that it’s not a common practice that the restaurant provide tissue paper or napkin so bring your own especially when you come to this kind of food place where potentially you use your finger to unshell the prawn. Outside the shop at the front entrance there is a big garbage bin when I walked passed i can smell the odor. I came from the back and left from the front, if I came from the front with this smell, it would probably affect my appetite. But from the back was much better as I saw crows bitting dead rat just right in front of me on the pedestrian path. The noodle taste average for me (for malaysian please don’t expect the same taste like our prawn noodle), the broth has some umami but can taste the sweetness was not from the bone or prawn but rather sugar or rock sugar. The broth is lacking the “spices kick” if to compare with prawn noodle from different countries in the region. The prawn texture was good, probably it’s boiled before putting into the noodle. The pork rib was tasteless and texture a bit too lean in my opinion, not recommended. Afterall if you haven’t tried Singapore prawn noodle, it’s ok to experience it but my suggestion just take the prawn noodle, pork rib is not necessary it’s not adding any positive element to the dish.
Delicious prawn noodle. Fast service. Delicious ngioh hiang too. Yummy ! Crowded during peak hours. May need to wait for seats
The gravy is similar to Penang prawn noodle
The good and service have birth improved. One of the best prawn noodles in Singapore

Before and after michelin ... tried their Penang laksa prior to the award and was pleasantly surprised. Returned some months after and noticed they have the michelin sticker. Seems they have maintained their standard with their Penang pork rib prawn noodles. Nice tender lean meat and hard boiled egg cooked just nice together with rich and robust broth. Lip smacking.

Food is great and worth the trip down! Best ckt in sg, i prefer this than the local black ckt, im a picky eater, so hard to find a gem like this, if in doubt, always visit the main stall in ABC Brickswork to get the best taste from the chef himself!

The pork ribs were really tender and tasty so that made the prawn noodles pretty worth it (though the soup was slightly spicy for me and I asked for no chilli) but I was disappointed with the ckt as it lacked flavour, considering that it was the dish that most people recommended.
ミシュラン獲得店。日曜日の18時30分ごろに来たが、注文客がいなかったのですぐに注文することができました。クエッティオ（焼きそば）を注文。味が染み込んでいてとってもおいしかったです。

Authentic Penang comfort street food. The fried Penang kway tiao is popular among customers, which may take a while to cook depending on the number of orders. With each motion, uncle works the flames to impart a smoky aroma that binds the soft flat rice noodles, Chinese sausage slices, beansprouts, beaten egg, fresh prawns, chili paste, and crispy pork lard together.

The prawn noodles with pork ribs are not bad. The assam laksa is packed with flavour in a rich sardine-based broth, with hints of floral and minty notes from the garnishes. The sweet prawn paste and chili padi add even more punch to the tangy gravy and chewy rice noodles. More ingredients such as prawns and pork ribs can be added at an extra cost to complete your meal.
Laksa is good. Fried kway teow so so, ordinary but good ingredients. I like the way where fried kway teow isnt too salty. Arrived on 1:20. Stall closed after us, we were the last

Hands down the worst Char kuey teow I have tried in Singapore. Horribly oily with zero wok hei. The Chinese sausages were tasteless. Nice sized prawns is the one thing good about it. Uggh. I couldn't finish it. Left 90% for the crows to eat.
Ate delicious prawn bee hoon soup. Bought Penang fried kway teow home,l it has 2 medium sized prawns, some lap Cheong, bean sprouts. Ate it the next day, still taste good.

Was at ABC market to try a Hokkien mee stall, but they were unexpectedly closed. Walked around and saw that this stall which I had saved on my list of places to try previously was open.

I got their large char kway teow ($6 as at Apr 2025). There was a slight wait as it was only cooked upon ordering. It was full of wok hei but I realised how much I enjoyed the Singapore style with dark soy sauce. The prawns were unfortunately frozen prawns, which didn't have taste and a poor texture, but at this pricing, one cannot be expecting them to use fresh prawns?

Came on a weekday lunch time and thankfully there’s no queue. I got the prawn noodles soup and the soup was flavourful yet not too overpowering nor salty. I think the portion is really good as it’s just $5 with lots of pork ribs.

Unfortunately, I found the Penang prawn noodle and asam laksa to be quite disappointing. They did not reflect the authentic flavors I was hoping for, and I felt that they may not do justice to the original Penang cuisine.

I also considered ordering the fried Koay Teow, but when I saw another diner's dish looking soggy and wet, I decided to pass on it.

Overall, I left feeling quite disappointed and would not recommend making a special trip to your restaurant based on my experience. I hope you can take this feedback into consideration as you continue to serve your customers.

We dined here on Saturday, 21 February at 8pm, booked by friends visiting from the US who were staying at the Four Seasons. Unfortunately, one of our friends fell seriously ill and was unable to attend the dinner.
The service was the main disappointment of the evening. One of the waitresses — possibly the manager — appeared visibly impatient while taking our order and gave the impression that she could not wait to be done with us. She also commented that we had ordered “too little,” which felt unnecessary and came across as condescending, leaving us uncomfortable as diners.
In addition, when we asked about credit card promotions, we were given a flat “no” without any explanation. After later noticing promotions advertised on the DBS website and probing further, the response shifted to a vague verbal comment that “maybe Chinese New Year, no promotions,” with no clarity on terms or conditions. The lack of a clear, courteous explanation — and the dismissive manner in which the query was handled — suggested either unfamiliarity with the promotions or a lack of willingness to explain. A more informed and polite response would have been appreciated.
The food, however, was excellent and ultimately the saving grace of the experience. The dishes were refined, well-executed, and fully deserving of the restaurant’s strong reputation. The kitchen clearly operates at a very high level.
For a restaurant of this calibre, service should match the quality of the food. While the cuisine was outstanding, the service fell short of expectations, resulting in a mixed overall experience.

Overall disappointing experience. The first course of the peking duck with pancakes was delicious but that was the only positive thing about the dinner. The coursing of the meal was off. No dim sum at dinner so you go straight to the main course of peking duck.  That's ok but then there's nothing to follow it up.  The fried rice was not edible...we ordered both styles and no one ate more than a bite.  Super salty and it felt like they were trying too hard. Staples like har gao and siew mai were decent but rather pedestrian. Where they really excelled was with the unorthodox, like a pan-fried yam cake (instead of the usual turnip), a puffy seared beef bun and a surprisingly crisp and gorgeous flaky layered pastry with moist shredded radish within.

This Chinese restaurant impresses diners with its lavish opulent interiors , Instagram worthy views of the Marina Bay Area and polite hospitable service . Food flavours of some dishes have a light subtle delicate texture that is refreshing on the palate but doesn’t leave one with a lasting impression . The restrooms on the contrary are in a class of its own , probably a cut above the rest with additional amenities provided such as lens wipes, dental floss etc . In brief, this restaurant wins hands down on its bespoke fine dining ambience ,curated with soothing instrumental Chinese music to induce a relaxing atmosphere for the culinary  journey ahead which leaves much to be desired .

With so many recent Google views garnered of the food images displayed recently ,  has prompted me to give an Updated more  detailed feedback  of the dishes  that I found mediocre:

A)The prawn dumpling - succulent but upon one bite , the entire dumpling fell out from the rubbery supple translucent skin , leaving me no choice but to consume them separately. This is the most uncommon experience I ever had with dozens of Har Gow I have tried from chefs of different culinary skill levels . Usually the skin is delicate but crafted in such a manner that it wraps and encompasses the moist prawn meat and is to be eaten together as one for its wholesome goodness .

B) Secondly , the spring roll on a fancy glass pebble plate that screams much visual attention . Alas , one’s transfixed gaze upon it soon ebbs away the moment the spring roll is consumed. Taste wise It is so ordinary that i found its presentation on the glass pebble plate absolutely necessary to compensate for the chef’s inadequate culinary skill in elevating this dish up.

C) The crispy Free range soy sauce chicken dish I had was a real dampener unworthy of any photo image capture . Portions were not substantial and  the meat clearly lacked marinate and flavour .

D) Lastly , I ordered the red bean with the 15 year aged tangerine peel dessert and instantly regretted my decision . With just one spoonful intake, the dessert tasted totally weird , alittle bitter with herbal hints .A matter of fact the concoction felt more experimental than the norm . It had no hints of the fragrant citrus tangy orangey taste  nor the subtle sweetness of the red bean .

On the contrary the complimentary dessert which consisted of the petite pandan and strawberry milk custard was more outstanding and well made . It was full of flavour packed in such a minute bite size piece .

Fortunately ,Items that saved  the day were the beef ball dim  sum and the bean curd skin with spinach broth.

Diners with essentially deep pockets should indulge in the chef’s much publicised key signatures like the Pipa duck etc .., and perhaps only then would one be able to leave with a Déjà vu feeling of having tasted the  crème Ala crème of the chef’s extraordinary epicurean creations .
For diners in search of more wallet friendly options to enjoy both the cuisine amidst panoramic skyline views , then opting for the Dim Sum leaves one with a calculated risk , second guessing which food items would measure up to one’s expectations .

With breathless anticipation and a reservation secured weeks in advance, we embarked on our gastronomic pilgrimage to the newly opened Chinese restaurant at Marina Bay Sands. Such was our fervour that we were, quite literally, the first guests to cross the threshold that day, an honour we wore with pride and the naïveté of those yet to be disillusioned.

Let it be said: the service was impeccable, the panoramic views of Singapore’s skyline utterly mesmerising, and the ambiance curated with meticulous attention to aesthetic pleasure. One must also applaud the lavatory experience, which was chef’s kiss. And as a devoted disciple of beautiful dinnerware, I tip my hat to the tableware, it delivered nothing short of a visual symphony.

Alas, the food. ohhhh maaaan, the food.

It was the culinary equivalent of a siren song luring us in with promise, only to dash our hopes against the rocks of mediocrity. Each dish arrived with passable presentation, but none rose to the occasion.

THE suckling pig, fine, if entirely unremarkable. A single sesame-seed-sized gold flake rested atop it, perhaps justifying half the dish’s price tag. Its vehicle: a pillowy mantou reminiscent of a blini, yet lacking the charm or depth of either. The accompanying sauce were forgettable at best🫩

Our selected fish dish, tragically unavailable (despite us being the first patrons present at le time), was substituted with a recommendation that I would charitably describe as… baffling. The battered crust was so unforgiving. Crispy? yes.. because of how hard and thick it was, and the sauce, a saccharine-sour enigma, obliterated the fish’s presence entirely. Shuckity shucks.

Then came the fancy-fied 乾炒牛河. Devoid of XO flavour, or frankly, any flavour. Perhaps they were taking a stand against sodium but it was a nostalgic throwback to the early days of covid, when taste was but a memory. Greasy, as one would expect, it clung to the strands but without wok hei or seasoning, the dish felt like an act of culinary gaslighting. My Cantonese ancestors stirred in their graves😔

The venison, commendably tender, still suffered from the muted flavours. But the one saving grace would be our vegetable dish. Silky luffa, pleasantly firm mushrooms, and a well-rounded broth that finally offered a whisper of satisfaction.

Oddly enough none of our dishes was served hot, maybe the tepid temperature of our dishes can be attributed to our seating clearly situated at a diplomatic distance from the kitchen. One can only assume the food embarked on a leisurely cross-country expedition en route to our table, cooling with every scenic detour. Naturally we declined dessert, out of self-preservation rather than restraint.

In sum: stunning service, dazzling surroundings, and food that can only be described as aesthetically ambitious, gustatorily apathetic. A masterclass in form over flavour.

But special mention to the drinks, while the individual ingredients didn’t exactly announce themselves with fanfare, the flavours were delightfully harmonious. The kind of libation one could get dangerously drunk on without realising😌

Would not personally come running back, considering quality of food with it’s price point, but nonetheless, we thank the lovely staff and raise our glasses to our beautiful city✨

Kelantan Kway Chap 吉蘭丹粿汁 – Berseh Food Centre (Michelin Bib Gourmand)

Kelantan Kway Chap at Berseh Food Centre is a long-standing Michelin Bib Gourmand hawker favourite, celebrated for its honest, well-executed Teochew-style kway chap. The dish features smooth, wide rice sheets that are soft yet resilient, soaking up the flavours of the braising sauce beautifully. A generous assortment of soy-braised pork cuts is offered, including belly, skin, trotters and intestines, each prepared with care and braised until tender without losing texture.

The braising sauce is the heart of the dish — dark, aromatic and well-balanced, carrying notes of soy, spices and gentle sweetness without being overpowering. Every component feels thoughtfully cooked, allowing the natural flavours of the pork to shine while remaining deeply comforting. Portions are satisfying, and prices remain accessible, reflecting why the stall continues to earn Michelin recognition for quality and value.

What truly elevates the experience is their amazing homemade chilli. Fragrant, punchy and layered with heat, it adds an addictive kick that cuts through the richness of the braised meats and transforms each mouthful. A small spoonful goes a long way, but many regulars find themselves going back for more. Unpretentious yet full of character, Kelantan Kway Chap is a must-try for lovers of classic Singapore hawker fare. Look

Reviews:
Paid $5.20 for a person kway chap set and was pleasantly surprised by the quality and value.

The kway itself was a standout – tender, silky-smooth, and served in a light, clear broth that wasn’t overly salty. It had a comforting, balanced flavor that didn’t overpower the rest of the dish – excellent in both taste and texture.

The kway chap set came with a generous and well-balanced mix of ingredients: slices of pork, pig intestines, pig skin, tau hu (beancurd), and a braised egg. Each component was well-prepared – the meats were flavorful without being gamey, and the braising sauce soaked in nicely. Everything complemented the broth and kway perfectly, making for a satisfying and hearty meal.

On top of that, the service was great – staff were friendly and accommodating, which made the dining experience even better.

Overall, for just $5.20, this kway chap set delivers great taste, good variety, and warm service. A definite go-to for a comforting, traditional meal.

Thoroughly enjoyed my dinner experience at Ki Su!

Service: The chefs explained each dish, the waiters always wore a smile, and the owner Yen Kun mingled with patrons, checking in to get our feedback on the dishes. Could definitely feel the sincerity!

Ki Su Shoujin Omakase is a high-end meatless vegetarian omakase that delivers beautifully on cuisine, service and ambience. The space feels elegant and calm with a truly fine-dining atmosphere. Service is attentive and professional and the food is delightful, each course is thoughtfully crafted, with presentation so refined that every dish feels like a piece of art. The visual impact alone creates a real “wow” moment, even before tasting.

Despite the refined setting, three female diners held loud Mandarin conversations throughout the service, overpowering the dining room and detracting from what should have been an intimate, immersive experience. We could barely hear the chef explaining the dishes, which is a key part of the experience. For a restaurant of this calibre, the dining room atmosphere matters just as much as the food.

The restaurant may want to consider informing guests beforehand that speaking loudly is not respectful in such a refined setting, similar to how some fine-dining establishments enforce dress codes. Once the group left, the space immediately became calm again, highlighting how much the noise had affected the experience.

At $168+++ per pax, guests expect an immersive and premium dining journey. Unfortunately, the disruption significantly discounted the overall experience, making it feel far less special than it should have been, almost like dining in a fast food outlet rather than a fine-dining omakase. A stronger approach to preserving the dining atmosphere would greatly enhance an otherwise exceptional restaurant.

The dinner at Ki Su Shoujin Omakase was a true fusion of artistry and exquisite flavor—an unforgettable feast for the senses. Highly recommended! Loved the service from chef to staff, all very welcoming and sweet, especially Alex in particular.

The red pepper nigiri was very similar in mouthfeel to chutoro. I love eggplant, so I was very delighted with their take on it.

I was not satisfied with the amount of food (big eaters beware), but I eat a lot more than average, so not a complaint at all.

Very, very minor quibble: I think asking patrons how the food was after almost every course is a bit much. I understand and appreciate the attention to detail, but I prefer less intrusive customer service; so I would rather have discussions like this only after the whole meal is done.

When my friend told me he was treating me to a birthday dinner at a rather pricey vegetarian omakase restaurant, my first reaction was honestly to wonder if he was trying to be funny. I’m not a vegetarian, nothing against it, but on my birthday? Still, since it was a treat, I thought there was no harm in giving it a try.

The moment I stepped into the restaurant, my impression immediately began to change. The service team was genuinely warm and welcoming. We were seated at the counter, as expected for an omakase experience. A beautifully presented box with a welcome note arrived first, followed by a hot towel and a selection of chopsticks for us to choose from, small touches that immediately elevated the experience.

When I saw the menu, my initial thought was, “There’s definitely going to be mock meat,” especially with nigiri sushi listed. Again, nothing against mock meat, but I usually lean more towards vegan-style dishes. My assumptions disappeared the moment the meal began.

From the first course to the dessert, every dish was fully vegan, and truly impressive. Red pepper transformed into a convincing “tuna,” pumpkin purée stood in for sea urchin, and mushrooms took the place of meat. Yet nothing tasted like a simple “vegetable substitute.” Each dish was creative, elegant, and genuinely delicious. It opened my mind to how extraordinary plant-based cuisine can be. Throughout the meal, I found myself repeatedly going “wow,” eagerly anticipating the next surprise from the chefs.

One dish I must highlight is the truffle mashed potato. Even though it wasn’t a main dish, it completely stole the spotlight for me. I’m usually not a fan of truffle, but they achieved the perfect balance, you can taste the truffle aroma without it being overpowering, and the mashed potato itself was incredibly smooth and comforting. If I hadn’t been so full, I would absolutely have asked for a second serving.

The entire omakase took about 1.5 to 2 hours, and it was one of the most fantastic dining experiences I’ve had to date. My heartfelt thanks to the service team and the chefs for making my birthday dinner so memorable.

I was also told that the menu changes every few months and depending on seasonal ingredients. If you ask whether I would return, my answer is definitely yes, especially when the menu refreshes.

The meat and innards are cleaned and prepared meticulously each day, served in a clear, peppery broth that retains the natural sweetness of pork. If you are lucky, try the elusive pork and glutinous rice roll in pig’s intestine while it is available for a short window of time each day. This indulgent, umami-rich dish is a rare culinary gem and is hardly found anywhere else, due to the amount of time and effort it takes to get it right.

We placed an advance order several days ahead for a 6.30–7.00 pm delivery, as we were hosting guests on New Year’s Eve (yesterday). The restaurant informed us that direct delivery was unavailable and that Grab was the only option, which we accepted in good faith.

Despite ordering early, no Grab driver was secured. At 7pm, the restaurant called to say the food had already been cooked earlier at 5.30pm and commented to me that I wouldn’t want to receive cold food. This comment was baffling and unhelpful as I expected a responsible solution, not a careless remark. Shortly after, a staff called and asked whether I could go down to collect the food myself, which completely defeats the purpose of using a delivery service in the first place. Either delivery is offered, or not.

After repeated follow-ups past 7 pm, I was finally informed that the order had to be cancelled because no driver was available. Shockingly, no delivery service had been pre-booked despite this being an advance order. The service was deeply unsatisfactory, and the staff’s attitude made matters worse. When I asked about the refund, I was met with a dismissive tone and told that it was “between you and Grab,” as though the restaurant bore no responsibility at all.

This level of indifference was unexpected and unacceptable from a restaurant of this standing. The poor handling of the situation left my guests disappointed on New Year’s Eve, and we had no choice but to fall back on McDonald’s ironically which provided a far more reliable service on one of the busiest nights of the year.

I sincerely hope the owner takes this feedback seriously, although based on how the staff handled the situation, I am doubtful. This experience raises serious concerns about service standards in the F&B industry today. One has to question how reliable such services truly are, and whether greater oversight of F&B and hospitality operations is needed.

Great place, excellent food.  Enjoyed the atmosphere inside.

Had an enjoyable dinner for 2.  Opted for the a la carte menu although there was an autumn seasonal menu available.  Service was excellent. Ambience of the restaurant is intimate and cosy.
