Visited on 18Sep and had the set lunch. Food is value for money and delicious. Extremely clean restaurant with good ambience. Service is friendly and prompt. Will visit again!

The food here is great and is extremely value for money. The service was impeccable with the attentive service staff. Ambience is top notch too. A fantastic experience overall and I'd definitely visit again.

My husband and I popped in without any knowledge of the restaurant and left the place feeling superbly contented. It lives up to its promise of small bites, big flavors.

The portions were just right and the well-seasoned food complemented one dish to another. While the restaurant carries a modest wine list on their happy hour selection, they were delectable.

We would enthusiastically return and can be assured to be attended by their attentive and personable staff.

I definitely recommend and will be back

I have been visiting and eating in 4 different Da Michele pizzarias, including Napoli, Modena, and Paris, and this one was the worst experience for me. Unprofessional waiters. And when you pointing at them the problem they confirmed that they are serving their own pint, not european pint. What ?! Pint is a worldwide metric system. I am not so sure that the weights and measures regulation would be very agree with that.

Ein sehr gutes typisch italienisches Restaurant, mit einem wahnsinnig freundlich und perfekt geschultem Personal, besonders Paola meine Kellnerin an dem Abend.

From the nice atmosphere to the friendly staff and terrific pizzas.

Amazing pizza with fresh, flavorful toppings and a cozy atmosphere. Special thanks to Paola for her friendly, attentive service — she made our visit even better! Highly recommended.
Friendly and warm service from Dempy!

Food is mediocre at best, we ordered truffle porcini and lasagna.

This 150-year-old Neapolitan pizza chain opened its first Asian outlet here in Singapore in 2024.  It is known for its authentic "wagon wheel" pizzas with very thin, chewy crusts and quality Italian ingredients. All its pizzas are made to order and come in one size – 15 inches (8 slices).

While the pizza arrived rather quickly within 10 minutes, it was a little cold. Despite this gripe, the food was generally good. But then that bar was surpassed by the mutton curry with yoghurt rice - truly astoundingly good. The Halwa to finish was just a continuation of this 10/10 meal. It definitely didn’t stand out in the way I thought it would. The portion sizes were also not that large. My friend and I got a platter for 2, and if he was still quite hungry after having his half.

I also got the chili challenge, which is S$33 and what they’re known for. You can choose up to a 6/10 spice level, with 7 and up being accessible at the full moon chili party they have. To get an invite to the party, you have to finish a full 6. Before you select your spice level, they ask if you want a sampler of the different levels. This costs S$25 dollars, which is not on the menu and not told to you.

The service otherwise was excellent though. The waitstaff were kind and polite, and very prompt with the service. The main chef was very involved with our dinner and was very kind and supportive. It was nice that he was still a part of the face of the restaurant, and he had the charisma to back it up.

Reviews:
I liked it, liked it very much! This is the drier version of Char Kway Teow, but it has its own aroma and right burnt sweetness. I'm used to Apollo Char Kway Teow, but they have retired. And their style is SUPER WET, and it's so goood!
I want to state clearly, this is a very good Drier style of Char Kway Teow. I enjoyed it's blackness aroma, just the right amount of sweetness, and it is not loaded with fried pork lard (creepy!). Compare to Outram CKTeow (Hong Lim Food Centre), I very much prefer this one--51 Old Airport Road Food Centre, #01-12. It has crunchy Chye Sim and Beansprouts, skilfully done. By the way, it is has good moisture, not completely dry.
I ordered mine without cockles and preserved sausages. I know that many people loved it, but trust me, without it--it's still very good. In fact you taste more of the noodle and sauce.
Some people comment about how good the prawn is, how delicious the cockle is, how good the sausages is. Well for me, it's the noodle, the black sauce, the blending of the egg, noodles and kway teow. And most of all the frying skill that gelled everything together. The rest are just bells and whistles.
I highly recommend this place for an awesome plate of char kway teow--i.e. the drier style. Just to be clear, it has moisture and smoothness.

Reviews:
Had a craving for char kway teow and was reminded of my younger days, when I used to head down to Old Changi Airport Food Centre for it. Today, I was lured by Lao Fu Zi Char Kway Teow, a Michelin-listed stall from 2019–2025 that I’ve heard so much about.

I queued for about half an hour and ordered a small portion $6 sgd. The serving was rather small for the price, and the taste was reminiscent of my neighbourhood Teochew-style CKT. I wouldn’t say it’s exceptionally delicious, though the wok hei does make it stand out slightly. Still, I don’t think I’ll be coming back for this again.

Reviews: Solid plate of char kway teow. All the flavours came together so well and the wok hei is excellent

Reviews:

The fried kway teow is leaning more to a dry savoury type. Wok hei was quite evident in the dish. I also do think there’s the proportion of kway teow to yellow noodles is a bit off as well. But nevertheless, still a very formidable plate of food in Old Airport Road hawker centre.

Restaurant Name: Lao Fu Zi Fried Kway Teow

Reviews: this was 5-star all the way...  Michelin got this spot-on

One of those rare times that michelin actually got it right. Noodles are crunchy, beef brisket braised till tender. Sauce also hits the spot, aside from being too watery. Soup is, errh well, just soup.

Noodle...2/5... Beef....3.5/5.... Noodle not cook properly, sticking together, sauce a bit oily but the cooking is traditional Cantonese style....$8... So not really worth it.... Can eat but won't queue for it

A very satisfying bowl of beef brisket and tendon noodles. The brisket is tender and well-braised, while the tendon is beautifully gelatinous, both infused with a deep, savoury richness.

The noodles are well-cooked and coated evenly in the aromatic sauce, complemented by fresh greens that balance the dish nicely. Straightforward hawker fare done very well—comforting, flavourful, and certainly worth returning for.

Michilin guide beef noodle. Beef is well stewed and tender, without any part being too dry， hard  or overcook. Meaning he choose the brisket very very carefully and is of very good balance of tendon, fats and meat.
One of the best beef tendon noodles in Singapore. Old school taste, the beef tendons were cooked super tender and melts in your mouth.
Old school 古早味 style. Tender brisket, deep-soaked in flavours from the rich gravy. Definitely 2 thumbs up!

Pork Trotters sold out due to limited quantities, so ordered their Por Ribs Noodles.
Surprisingly it did not disappoint me. Noodles are quality thin noodles that makes a bowl of noodles taste good and al dente. Their sauce are well balanced with some chilli added that make the noodle so flavorful. With well blanched vegetables added. To top it off, the pork ribs are well braised that its almost fell off the soft rib bones type. Much to my liking of pork ribs noodles.

Old school beef brisket noodle done in  traditional Cantonese way. Braised 3 hours with herbs like Star anise ,bay leaves &  cinnamon.Meat is soft & tender. Tendon will melt in your mouth comes together with springy noodle .
This was a common dish in the 70s & 80s and any wanton noodle stall will offer this dish as well as pork ribs noodle & chicken feet noodle. However it is a rare item nowadays. Probably because it is a very tedious process.
However over here they still offer these 2 items plus pork trotter noodle too !
Highly recommended  !

价钱公道 ! 来啦！走过,经过,千万不要错过哦 !

绝对不走捷径，也不会偷工减料！
就连法国人都认同 !
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Super nice, enough for me to take my phone out to leave a review

Beef is tender, tendons are melt-in-your-mouth, very flavourful and well-balanced
Even the veggie is cooked to just the right texture with a bit of nice crunch on the stem and soft leaves
Boss is very quirky and funny

I’ve seen this stall before and what intrigued me was the years it was on Michelin recommended list. Today I managed to get a bowl of $8 braised beef and tendon. Overall the noodles are QQ in bite but the braised beef and tendons were a bit disappointing. The beef was not too tender just good to bite and some tendons are not as expected. It’s a bit chewy. Really cannot trust Michelin list. I had better braised beef and tendons in Chinatown and those stalls are not on the list. Disappointing.

I cant believe this michelin bib gourmand only has 4 reviews? Plus it is not even listed on the directory in the meiling hawker centre pin. So underrated.

Firstly, food.. ingredients were very fresh, you can feel the choysum are truly the farm to table kind, crisps, natural veggie freshness and all sifu did was just dip it in for 45 seconds and thats it you get 1 to 1.5 stalk of natural goodness.

The beef was tender, almost melting like a good rendang, lacking the raw beef meaty taste yet you know it is fresh because a slab of unfresh beef will be pretty old and stiff no matter how well done, or if you try to mask the taste. The noodles are your typical yellow egg strands at average shops, factory made , alkaline lye water laced but they manage to perfect the texture. Thats some craft hello!

If anything to make me take away one star would be , why so heavy on the sauce and taste? Making it quite gelat after eating..

The soup broth is quite good too, i was thinking must be sone radish msg concoction, nah not very true. Some earthly hints of soybeans and meat bone broth. All is good, no queue underrated, i just wonder if boss willl do a rendition of 3 treasures, ribs, trotters , brisket and if yes, how much??

Traditional beef brisket noodle (牛腩面). My go-to place when I have a craving. Slow cooked brisket and tendon in spices and sauce. Soft but not disintegrating. Served with noodles cooked to QQ style. They have pork rib noodles (排骨面) too.
Rich and savory beef noodles, slow-cooked to perfection, with tender slices of beef, springy noodles, and a flavorful broth that's sure to warm your heart and satisfy your cravings!

my boyfriend and I have dined here twice in the last couple months and had fantastic meals on both occasions! The Bocados de Tiradito is excellent, I preferred it over the Ceviche y Arandanos but my boyfriend loved both. The Pincho de Cordero was perfectly cooked and we couldn't get enough of the sauce - will definitely be ordering this again in the future. On our first visit, we enjoyed the Lechonsita which was as scrumptious as it was beautifully plated, and on our second visit, there was a pork shoulder special served taco style, which we initially intended to split, but enjoyed so much that we ordered a second portion... still dreaming about the flavors this morning. Latido is a unique concept and it's great to try new flavors, looking forward to future visits!
Colombian cuisine. Great food and friendly service.
Bread is cute but eh it’s alright I guess, I am not mind blown. Nothing spectacular.
Enjoyed the set lunch menu. Kalai did an excellent job explaining the menu items and provided impeccable service. Thank you Kalai!
Food and cocktails were delicious. Service is real and good, better than at other establishments. Ambience is luxurious. Expensive but worth it.

I’m rather disappointed with my experience with Latido this Valentine’s Day, though I share this in the spirit of fairness.

I made my reservation in advance, genuinely looking forward to celebrating somewhere nice. However, only on the day itself — when I checked the menu online — did I realise the restaurant was serving exclusively a fixed Valentine’s set menu with no à la carte options. This was not clearly highlighted during the booking process (not via the main website). For an occasion as significant as Valentine’s Day, where pricing and format differ substantially, such information should be made unmistakably prominent so customers can make an informed decision upfront.

In hindsight, I acknowledge that I could have double checked earlier, before the cancellation deadline — that part is on me. At the same time, the set-only arrangement was not obvious when I made the reservation. When I saw the Valentine’s menu on the day itself, I was honestly at a loss. The set menu was beyond my budget and, frankly, more than my stomach capacity. I simply wanted a comfortable place to celebrate, but faced with an expensive fixed menu and no alternatives, I didn’t quite know what my options were.

I immediately called to explain the situation and requested to postpone the reservation to another date. I was not attempting to cancel outright — I fully intended to dine there on another occasion. Unfortunately, I was informed that postponement would still be treated as a cancellation with a fee exceeding 50%, and that this is standard practice across restaurants in Singapore.

While I understand the need to protect revenue on peak occasions, what made the experience particularly difficult was the rigidity and tone of the response. The interaction felt transactional, with little room for understanding despite my willingness to continue supporting the restaurant. It left me feeling more dismissed than valued.

To be clear, the staff on the ground were extremely amicable and professional, and the food itself was enjoyable. My disappointment lies with the communication and handling of the reservation, not with the service team.

I respect the operational challenges restaurants face on high-demand days. However, clearer upfront disclosure and a more empathetic approach would have made a meaningful difference to what was meant to be a special evening.

Want to say a big thank you to Chef Fernando Arevalo really welcoming us into his heartwarming restaurant.

By great fortune, we were seated just in front of his chef's table and despite his busyness, through our conversations, we could truly feel his heart to bring Columbian food at its best, to us.

Every dish was excellent. We loved it. Not the usual ( and if i might say overdone) kind of high-class pretentious cooking, but the rare find of heartwarming, unpretentious, passionate cooking that brings such delicious flavours that warms the heart. Yet, each dish was perfectly balanced.
- we truly did not know how lobster, chorizo and ribs could go so well together. But Chef Arevalo could.
- the rabbit taco wrap was SO good. I was glad I took his recommendation. Thought he handled the gamey-ness of the rabbit really well! But my favourite was the wrap itself- his unique creation that was so unique in texture and yet goes perfectly with the wrap' ingredients
- their signature rye bread and onion butter. Very well done. And the onion butter is so unique and yet perfect for the bread. Yummy...
- glazed lamb skewer. The glaze was so tasty, texture so good. And balanced the juicy, tender, perfectly cooked lamb.

I would also like to thank the restaurant for making a personalised cocktail for me based on my tastes, which was clearly generous in their alcohol and very delicious, because the lightweight me was very pleased after the meal.
- after which they were really kind to offer me hot drinks

Thank you for not just the good food, but also the really warm and kind welcome to your restaurant. Great team there. Thank you for bringing back top grade food that is yet unpretentious, hearty and joyful to the Singapore scene that has become far too sterile, uninnovate and mercenary.
Was really great for a date. Food was amazing, especially the Lamb. Book a seat by the bar if you like a good view of food prep!

We ordered 3 starters but the only 1 that really stood out was the bread, which was nice and enjoyable. The other 2 were average. For the mains, both dishes were generally good and nicely presented. However, the steak wasn’t quite to my liking.
The service was a highlight. The staff were friendly, warm, and attentive throughout our meal. The ambiance was also lovely, comfortable and inviting, making it a pleasant place to dine.

Food was decent, a little over priced, but nothing stands out :(

Had the
- bread
- lamb pincho starter
- kue pie tee cevice starter
- seabass
- beef short rib

Latido is Singapore’s very first Colombian restaurant. In fact, it is also my first time having Colombian cuisine, so I decided to give it a go as part of my culinary journey.

I am utterly amazed by the interior design and decoration featuring the tribal art and masks from South American indigenous communities.

Flavours of all dishes are bold and vibrant. These are the dishes I ordered for my lunch :

1. Pan de la Casa (Signature Homemade Rye Bread)
2. Bocados de Tiradito (Sawara Ceviche)
3. Ceviche y Arandanos (Hamachi, Patacon, Suero, Cranberry, Tiger’s Milk)
4. Arepa de Choclo y Huevo (Sweet Corn Cake, Pork Jewel, Egg)

I will be back with my friends / family next time to try their main dishes. Latido has successfully left me a positive impression of the Colombian cuisine. Keep it up
The service was good. Also the food!!

Very pleasurable experience with some minor qualifications to my five stars. The atmosphere was excellent, and some of the dishes we had were quite incredible - the arepas were really nice and chicken hearts were sublime, both are starters. They had ceviche but I did not have it. As mains we had their variety of lechon, it was very good though perhaps not unheard-of-good. The wine... the first 2 attempts at wine, thankfully they let us taste it liberally, were clearly from bottles that had been left open too long. So, perhaps not a sommelier's paradise. The third one we tried was then outstanding and we had the whole (freshly opened) bottle. Why does it matter, well wines are sensitive to how they're treated. Independently from whether you like the type of wine. That often is the real difference in whether you like the wine in a restaurant. Or not. So, summary: great service, overall enjoyable food, and the final wine bottle was very good. Price level... Well. They're in Guide Michelin.

One of the best restaurants we’ve been to in a while. Ras the bartender laid out everything so well and nailed our food and drink - really enjoyed it across the board. The rest of the staff were super attentive especially Kalai and we felt very well taken care of. Latido has quickly become one of our favorites in Singapore. Well done.

I had a really fantastic experience at Latido. The food was amazing and very authentic Colombian, you can really feel the quality and the care in every dish.

It’s true that Latido is one of the very few Colombian restaurants in Singapore, but what makes it special is that it feels like the only one with such particular care for the customer, the food quality, and the whole experience. The ambience is warm and comfortable, and it’s a place where you can really enjoy the food slowly and share different dishes together.

It’s located in the heart of Tanjong Pagar, and honestly it makes a real difference compared to many other places. I will definitely come back and I strongly recommend it.

If you love Latin culture and Colombian food, this place is a paradise 🇨🇴✨

Below average food for the price.
Do note that if part of the table wants the set meal, the entire table has to order the set meal. Even though 2/4 pax wanted the set meal, they couldn’t make an exception as it’s their policy. I stated to the waiter with facial piercings that they could’ve made this policy clear on their website but he proceeded to ignore my suggestion.

Other than that encounter, the rest of the service was good and they were able to replace some of the set menu dishes to accommodate diet restrictions. Food wise was less than average though I did enjoy the lobster dish. However the wait time between some of the dishes was just too long. Total damage was $700+ for 4 pax. I personally do not think it is worth it and won’t be coming back.
Wonderful to see Colombian-inspired cuisine showcased in Singapore. The food was delicious, with the cordero and ceviche kue pie tee being standouts. Volveremos pronto!

The food was excellent, worth every penny, the experience was out of this world! I’ve tried many cuisines around the world (i.e Paraguayan, Ecuadorian, Venezuelan) and the food tried here at Latido is superb. I wish to commend the service from Ras, Jeffrey, and Kalai — each of them served our dishes with grace and explained everything to us patiently. 100% recommended. Bring your friends and family.
Food was really well presented and cooked to perfection! Service by Kalai in particular was meticulous and warm. My family and I had a great joint birthday celebration here :)

The food at Latido is amazing and beautifully prepared and full of flavour. The service is superb and made the whole dining experience even more enjoyable. Special thanks to Kalai for the warm, attentive, and professional service. It was the perfect place to celebrate my birthday, and everything was just perfect. Truly a wonderful experience, highly recommended!

Honestly a very underwhelming meal because of how hyped up this restaurant was.

The rabbit meat didn’t taste good and there was a bone inside which was quite unpleasant. Upon feedback, there wasn’t any action taken at all, not sure what kind of service recovery that is

The lobster & beef short rib dish was also super expensive and mid at best. The lobster is only 60% cooked and the texture is jelly-like, which was quite off putting - did not eat
An enjoyable meal. Pity that its popular steak was not available when we’re there.
Awesome meal, great wines and amazing service!

Finally checked out Latido, and the flavours were totally up my alley!

Sweet, fluffy carbs. Smoky, charred proteins. And plenty of acidity to keep every bite fresh and balanced.

Highlights for me : lamb saddle, crab meat plantain, stuffed sea bass, tropical salad

The ambience was lovely, though it did get quite noisy after 7:30pm once the crowds rolled in.

Just finished a meal here. Food was alright not sure it is Michelin worthy. Restaurant was boiling hot asked them to adjust the ac and I wasn't the only one complaining about the temperature.. They didn't adjust. Asked for a jug of water after two bottles of Aqua Panna, it never came to the table. Mediocre experience.

Great food, attentive staff and nice ambience.
Kudos to the chef and kitchen staff for accommodating my restricted diet and still presenting dishes that looked the same as the rest of our group.

Love the food and impeccable service. Went back second time last week and have been recommending to friends since months ago!! The only disappointed part is .. it doesn’t open for lunch on weekends hah!

First time trying Colombian food and we were blown away by how good everything was! The fish was exceptional :) Service was friendly and knowledgeable as well. Highly recommended!

Mais là, franchement pas au niveau d un étoilé : ni de la cuisine style street food  plat mal présenté , le service froid et peu sympathique, le personnel ne sait même pas que le restaurant est une étoile à part le manager !! : pas de mise en bouche , un seul vin à la carte au verre en blanc , ensuite ils oublient un plat de crabe commandé …. 9 of us had lunch here on 30 Jan. We started with Lou Hei, followed by mostly tim sum with half a roast duck, vegetables and fried noodles. The food is tasty and prices are reasonable. The staffs are also friendly and quick in service. Nice Chinese restaurant to visit if you’re in Chimjes.
Sit here since 7 pm. Now it it’s 739, no food is served !
CHUMESにある広東料理の店。一皿が大体３〜４人前で結構量がある。

Had a birthday dinner celebration here. Came here with high expectations as Lei Gardens is known to be a known restaurant that serves very good food. However, the entire meal we had at Lei was a total let down.

First let's start with the appetisers..... the roughly cut pickled cucumber appetiser served was the same as those served in low cost chinese hot pot restaurant. The char siew and the bland tofu balls had no decoration and were plonked on a white plate like what they served in zhi char stores.

The roast duck was tough, dry and had a bad gamey smell. We have much better ducks from some top Singapore's hawker center.  The conpoy fried rice was bland and dry and so was the grouper fish
The fish fillets tasted frozen and the mushroom served was not wild mushroom but the common and cheap japanese enoki mushroom from the supermarket. How can Lei blatantly mislead their diners like that ??

Overall, the food served was bland in taste and just medicore. The entire meal was a total letdown. We ordered the $1688++dinner menu (final price tag was $2000 including tea for a meal that tasted worse than a neighbour zhi char restaurant) and every one at the dining table felt that we could have a much more satisfying and delicious meal at standard casual restaurants like CRYSTAL JADE or CANTON PARADISE.

It really came as a total shock to us that Lei Garden's food quality is so medicore and poor.

The only saving grace was the friendly and very attentive staff members who were very helpful. They rendered excellent customer service. We also appreciate their heartwarming Cantonese rendition of the happy birthday song.

People like us were misled by the "Michelin label". After the meal i found out that Lei Gardens had only been award the "MICHELIN GUIDE" and not "MICHELIN STAR" !! ...... and some 3 years back too in 2022.

We will certainly never return to Lei Gardens nor recommend friends to dine here.  Just totally disappointed that we selected the wrong restaurant to celebrate my mother's milestone birthday. A total letdown. Once bitten twice very shy.

An outstanding dining experience.

Had a wonderful evening at Lei Garden located at Chijmes, and it more than lived up to its reputation. The Peking duck was superb — perfectly crisp skin and beautifully balanced flavours — and the crispy pork was equally exceptional.

What truly elevates the experience, however, is the service: attentive, polished, and genuinely welcoming without ever feeling intrusive.

Ideal for a special occasion or celebratory night out. Highly recommended.

Leaving a comment here to remind myself never to come here ever again. Honestly you are better off getting tze char food in neighborhood for better food quality, pricing and experience.

Ng Qi Hao was polite, quick to respond and anticipated our requests without us even having to ask. He made the dining experience so much more enjoyable! Felt like a cha chaan teng at dinner and not a restaurant. Noisy environment. Seemed understaffed at times.

Also mentioned it was a birthday celebration, needed birthday mantous. Not prepared. Had to wait for them to prepare it on the spot.

Been coming here for ages, never felt like I needed to leave a review until now.

Being a non-Chinese speaker myself wasn't a problem and we were nicely helped through the wide menu selection and found some of our favorite dishes and some new ones too. If you are after some special dishes it's best to advise them when booking to ensure it can be prepared for your visit. Each dish was amazing and so well prepared, we ordered many dishes and still had food left at the end of the evening which was packed for us to take home and enjoy later. Really good restaurant.
Service and attentiveness is impeccable. Food is fresh and good. Wonderful experience.

Tricky to price the meal but I appreciate the quality of the food.

Restaurant Name: Leon Kee Claypot Pork Rib Soup
Reviews:
Leon Kee Claypot Pork Rib Soup is one of those rare food stalls that truly feels timeless. I first ate here more than 20 years ago, back when it was still the old uncle personally cooking behind the stove. Returning now brings back many memories, and it’s heartening to see that the legacy has clearly been carried on. The lady running the stall today appears to be his daughter, who I remember used to help serve customers back then — a beautiful continuation of a family craft.

Seeing Leon Kee recognised in the Michelin Guide 2025 feels well deserved. This isn’t trendy food — it’s honest, traditional cooking done right, and consistently so over decades. A bowl of history, care, and comfort in every serving.

This modern French restaurant truly satisfied my endless curiosity for new ingredients and flavour combinations while staying firmly rooted in French technique, even after trying many highly regarded French restaurants in Singapore and abroad.

A few standout moments:

- oyster as an appetiser was an amazing opening, fresh, fragrant and rich flavour, that I ordered extra 2 pieces.
- The sweetbread (veal throat) was unlike any I’ve had before. Creamy, almost melting, with a delicate richness that reminded me of the fatty part of premium toro.
- Scallop flown in from Switzerland was so naturally sweet and pure that I initially thought the chef had glazed it with sugar and butter. Easily an 11/10. the best piece of shellfish I’ve eaten in recent memory.
- Smoked baby duck fillet served with pickled melon was a revelation. Throughout the menu, the chef shows a masterful hand with acidity, whether from fermentation, vinegar, or the brightness of fresh fruit and vegetables, ringing perfect balance to every plate.
- Unlike classic French desserts that can feel heavy with butter and sugar, the desserts here are remarkably light and refined, allowing the true flavours of the ingredients to shine.
- The chocolate course, made with Valrhona (widely regarded as one of France’s finest chocolate makers), was the perfect luxurious finish.

Creative, precise, and delicious. An outstanding modern French dining experience.

If there is one thing that defines a truly great French meal, it is the sauces, and my recent dinner at Lerouy was an absolute masterclass in exactly that.
From the moment we sat down at the counter—which offers a mesmerizing view of the open kitchen—the execution was flawless. Chef Christophe Lerouy and his team move with a silent, synchronized precision that is a joy to watch. The menu is "carte blanche," meaning you don't know what you are getting until it arrives, but trust me, you are in safe hands.
The highlight of the evening, without a doubt, was the sauce work. Every single dish was tied together by a sauce or emulsion that was incredibly complex, glossy, and packed with flavor. Whether it was a rich, foam-capped bisque or a sharp, citrus-laced reduction, the sauces were so good we were practically using our bread just to wipe the plates clean. It’s rare to see this level of classic French technique melded so effortlessly with modern, sometimes Asian, influences.
I must also give a special mention to the sommelier. Wine pairings can sometimes feel stiff or routine, but the service here was fantastic. She was knowledgeable and passionate, steering us toward some really interesting, unconventional pairings that elevated the food rather than just complementing it.

If you appreciate technical perfection and sauces that you’ll be dreaming about for days, Lerouy is unmissable. Highly recommended for a special occasion.

I went in expecting a three-Michelin-star standard, but it was an utter disappointment. Service was mediocre, and the food was simply bad.

The first dish: pasta with caviar and truffle was overwhelmingly sour. The acidity drowned out every other flavor I could barely detect any truffle at all. The sourness lingered unpleasantly after each bite.

Then came another caviar dish. It felt like they were just sprinkling caviar on everything and calling it fine dining. Adding caviar to every plate doesn’t automatically make it Michelin-worthy.

The mushroom with cream was no better. The first thing I tasted was pure oil, followed by a faint mushroom chew. The cream in the middle was overpowering and clashed badly with the mushroom.

Overall, I can’t fathom how this place earned three Michelin stars. The taste was poor, and the menu seemed to revolve entirely around truffle and caviar without any real finesse or balance.

I had a truly fulfilling dinner here. The delicious dishes, made with the freshest ingredients, were prepared in a creative and well-balanced way. I also really enjoyed the atmosphere and the elegant setting of the restaurant. The portions were a little generous for me. I love their caviar.

Sometimes, Perfection doesn’t need to be over-the-top, pompous, or shockingly extraordinary. Sometimes, it is about lovingly crafting a meal using the experience of more than 30 years and the finest ingredients Mother Nature has to offer on this planet. Cooked cleanly and purely, every course incorporates balanced seasoning and more importantly, is thoughtfully served with authentic smiles. Ms. Catherine, Mr. Murugan, Chef and the Les Amis team created an experience for us that couldn’t be a better way to conclude the year of 2025, and to look forward to a happier, brighter one in 2026. Our heartfelt thanks to the Team for taking us on this journey of French culinary excellence that we will never forget.

I had heard quite a fair bit about Long Kee Wanton Noodle, often recommended as one of the must-try stalls at 505 Jurong West Market & Food Centre. With a day off on hand, we decided to head over to Jurong West for a comforting bowl of Wanton Mee for breakfast.

As expected on a weekday morning, the hawker centre was mostly filled with retirees. Long Kee, however, stood out immediately with its snaking queue, which I assumed was the norm whenever they are in operation. Despite the long line, the lady taking orders was friendly, and to my surprise, the queue moved along at a decent pace.

I ordered the Wanton Mee with chilli, and lo and behold, this plate checked every box on my personal Wanton Mee checklist. It was a bowl full of nostalgia, the kind of noodles I would yearn for from my childhood. The slices of char siew were lean, not the glossy, oil-laden kind, but more of a steamed-style preparation. While the dish may look simple at first glance, the noodles were well tossed in seasoning and paired beautifully with their fiery chilli sauce, making each bite deeply satisfying.

The wantons were pleasant too, with two pieces served per bowl, simple, comforting, and well done.

Given the long queue, I figured it would be a waste not to try more, so I went ahead and ordered an additional bowl of dumpling soup.

The dumplings were plump and generously filled with well-seasoned minced meat. What stood out were the chunks of chestnut, which added a refreshing texture and an appetising bite, rounding off the experience nicely.

If I ever return to Long Kee Wanton Noodle, I would definitely order their chicken feet and mushroom noodles as well, alongside their classic wanton noodles, this time without chilli, to better savour the flavours.

Tried, was not as good as last time nor like the original stall in town.  这家的云吞面口味与弛名的国记云吞面非常相似，但不是在这里同一个小贩中心的国记，因为他们也换了招牌名字，现在已改名为 伟记云吞面，而其味道也大不如前。

This stall noodle texture is the main unique selling point, it was not usual very thin noodle, or yellow rubbery like some. In fact, It was slightly thicker that usual yet chewy n tender, very well absorb the soup sauce base. Savory yet sweet and slight spiciness. Loved it.  隆记云吞面主要特点的他的面品，不像一般的细条面，或是沉黄色碱水味过重，吃起来口感会有如胶带。而这家的面质感就比较厚重带点粗矿但有弹性，且没有难吃的碱水味。它能很好的吸收汤汁酱料，味道咸中带甜又微辣。非常不错。

The main ingredient CharSiew also play a important part, not like those HongKong heavy dark Char-grilled style, it just like the usual CharSiew but they slided it thick and yet juicy. Taste so good eating with the noodles.  这家的叉烧也很不错，虽然不是像香港炭黑烧烤那一类，但其叉烧够厚且带汁水，和面一起吃进口中，味道很是享受。

Overall, I liked their WantanMee. If you are my followers, I recommend this stall to you.  整体而言，我喜欢这家的云吞面，如果你喜欢我的审查推荐，你可以去试一试。

So often wine is something of an afterthought to a Restaurant where, despite having a seemingly long list of wines, there is little thought behind it other than to have a range of types and prices. Ma Cuisine is the exception here, and in a fantastic way. Not only do they have a wide range of wine types and prices, but their understanding and research behind each is second to none. Talking to their staff and selecting your wine is an experience which is thrilling and creates excitement. Thankfully, the wines match that anticipation.
But what of the ambience of the restaurant and the food, as this is a restaurant and not a trendy wine bar. Well, the place itself is a very welcoming and well-styled, with plenty of character, making you feel relaxed and comfortable. Lighting is a combination of subdued lighting with selected spots at the tables, which creates a nice feeling of intimacy and privacy in what otherwise would be another open-plan restaurant. Each table has a combination of individual chairs or leather-clad soft seating spanning the side of the restaurant.  But we came to eat, and that is where you again will be smiling and taste buds jumping for joy. The only problem is what not to choose, as each dish is so wonderfully prepared and satisfying. The food has all the right characteristics, look, textures and taste. Each is not only expertly cooked but is equally well presented, with each dish being explained in a tantalizing way as it is placed on the table. We went for a shared approach so we could all experience the culinary delights that the kitchen so expertly prepared.
Staff are welcoming, helpful, very efficient and serve with a smile, understanding exactly what a customer is looking for and what level of discussion or discretion is required.
This is an experience to savor and not just another restaurant or meal that you will quickly forget. Oh no, this one you will remember and no doubt keep on your to-do list.

Second, food. Here are failures in both substance and thought. First, the likes:

Liked:
- Chicken liver parfait. Not quite sure why it's called a parfait, which brings up a wholly different kind of food in my mind, but it is pretty delicious, though maybe the volume of shiso could be dialed down a little to display the...pate.

Needs improvement:
- Grilled white corn. Don't get me wrong, this was delicious - probably the best dish on the menu, but given that it's a sharing plate it would have been a good move to allow for the plate to be sized to the number of diners. We were provided 3, which, given the nature of corns-on-cob, was a little hard to share between two people. I've seen this allowed in other tapas-style restaurants, so it surely must be a thing.

- Sate mochi. Interesting textural and flavor contrast, like a cross between those fried sesame balls you get at dim sum and sheperd's pie. Definitely interesting, though, once again - this is a sharing plate place, right? Why is there only one ball? Why not make it two and increase the price, or make the balls smaller, or something?

- Roasted Padron peppers. A huge pile of them topped with a generous dusting of bottarga, or grated salted fish roe. The peppers were a little too watery and the bottarga didn't add too much dimension to the overall flavor profile beyond some required saltiness.

- Iberico Pork neck. This was a misfire. I understand the intention to present this medium rare, which I'm totally on board with in principle - it's great to dispel the myth that high quality pork can't be cooked like beef - but in this case, the cooking time seems to have been inadequate to render out the fat, causing the dish to be full of blubbery bits of fat and a fair amount of gristle. Not really what I would have expected for a dish at this price point. The meat had a steak-like chew, which, given the intention to present it medium rare, was fine, but the blubberiness was the main issue.

Service was good, if basic. The server was helpful in suggesting what to get and not to get, though it would have been good for the dishes to be explained a bit more thoroughly, given their eclectic nature - or maybe I missed the explanations over the din. Also, I find it odd that there's tandoor bread on the menu given the paucity of suitable dips to go with it in the list of main offerings. I get that the menu is constantly changing, but when the only option on the main menu that could go with the bread is burrata (notwithstanding the taramasalata etc. on the weekly menu), one questions the prominence of the bread, or the lack of native accoutrements to make it a worthwhile order on its own. Put it another way, if you're going to offer bread as a standalone, full priced menu item, it should be able to stand on its own without relying on any other dish. Alternatively, offer bread to go with the dishes that require it.

Restaurant Name: Margaret Drive Sin Kee Chicken Rice
Reviews:
One of my core memories is eating the chicken rice on the second floor of the old Margaret Drive hawker centre after a meet the parents session with my Dad when I was in secondary four. That was twenty years ago. So when the various stalls opened across Singapore, I wanted to see if the taste is any better than the other chicken rice which have made their name across Singapore since.

I ordered half a chicken for sharing, and also got some beansprouts to go along. In recent times, the first thing I look out for when eating a rice dish is to taste the rice on its own via the first bite. This was hot and fragrant, a good start.

The chicken was rather tender, but it was cut in chunks rather than how most other places do it. The chilli in the bean sprouts added some kick to the dish, but the sauce in both elevated them. The chilli and ginger were pretty nice too.

I honestly can't remember the taste from 20 years ago, but this was a decent chicken rice that's worth trying.

Restaurant Name: Margaret Drive Sin Kee Chicken Rice
Reviews:
For a reasonable price, an honest plate of Margaret Drive Sin Kee chicken rice comes with generous, thick chunks of steamed chicken over slick, fragrant oil rice. The chicken is velvety, moist, and tender, even for the breast meat. I also like that it is not slapped flat with a cleaver knife and chopped into thin slices, allowing the plumpness of the meat to be savoured with each chew. The well-seasoned rice with notes of chicken, ginger, garlic and scallion has to be one of the most flavourful ones in town.

Topped with crisp and refreshing cucumber slices and drizzled lightly with soy and sesame oil, this classic dish is good enough to enjoy by itself. For those who like to jazz up their meal with the trio of spice, pungency, and sweetness, chilli, ginger, and dark soy sauces are available on the side for self-service.

Marguerite offers a refined dining experience in a stunning botanical setting. The menu features creative, seasonal dishes with elegant presentation and balanced flavors. Service is attentive and professional. Prices are on the higher side, but the serene ambience and high-quality cuisine make it perfect for special occasions or leisurely meals.

Marguerite offers a refined dining experience in a beautiful garden setting inside the Flower Dome. The modern European dishes are creative, seasonal, and elegantly presented. Service is attentive and professional. It’s on the pricier side, but perfect for special occasions and a peaceful, memorable meal.

Marguerite is a bit of a contradiction. The food is visually stunning—true edible art—and the service was absolutely fantastic; the staff are attentive and professional. However, for the high price point, the meal was ultimately forgettable. Not a single dish or even an amuse-bouche stood out as truly delicious or memorable. Strangely, when booking, we were told only 6:30 PM was available, yet the restaurant was deserted with only three tables occupied all Thursday night. It’s a beautiful space, but the atmosphere and flavors don’t justify the cost
Interesting lunch menu, thoughtful choice of ingredients and each bite had a clean after taste. Appreciate the service for our birthday celebration.

An enchanting French garden escape with a world-class dessert trolley

My close friend and I enjoyed a lovely lunch here today. The atmosphere is absolutely charming—cozy, elegant, and set in a breathtaking indoor garden filled with lush plants and thoughtful botanical touches. Every detail, from the table settings to the plate presentations, felt delicate and refined.

The food was beautifully presented. The starters were subtle and sophisticated. The main course was good—well-composed and skillful—though I felt it lacked a tiny bit of depth compared to the exceptional starters and desserts.

Ah, the desserts—this is where the experience truly shined. The restaurant offers what might be one of the best dessert trolley services I’ve ever seen. A elegant cart is wheeled to your table, filled with an array of exquisitely crafted sweet treats. Each dessert is plated individually for you, with careful attention to detail. The portions are small, allowing you to taste several without overindulging, and the variety is impressive. This alone is worth a visit.

The coffee afterward was also a delightful surprise—far better than expected and a perfect finish.

What makes the visit truly worthwhile is the complimentary access to the gardens after your meal. Strolling through the landscape felt like a natural extension of the dining experience. If you leave right after eating, the price may feel a bit high, but including the garden walk makes it excellent value.

Other practical highlights: the golf cart shuttle to and from the entrance is a nice touch, and SMS reminders are sent if you have a reservation.

Just a note: when booking online, you must confirm via email after submitting your card details. I forgot this step and my link expired, but a phone call resolved it kindly.

Overall, this is a wonderful spot for a leisurely lunch, especially with visitors. A beautiful French meal, a world-class dessert trolley, and a peaceful walk in the gardens make for a truly memorable outing. Highly recommended for a special yet relaxed experience.

A wonderful dining experience in a very unique setting - inside the Flower Dome. Dining here include free access to the Dome and ideal for visitors to explore the garden and then have a delightful meal from their seasonal menu (4 or 7 course). Or you could be driven (which we chose) in a buggy from the main entrance to the entrance. We had a nice 4-course blend of the unique (kangaroo tail pho) to the more traditional lamb / duck dishes. The freshly baked sourdough was perfect for the food menu. Food was impeccably prepared and delicious and will cater to dietary preferences. The spacious restaurant in a garden (of course!) setting is ideal for families and fine casual dining. The service staff were attentive, informative but not intrusive, total descriptive of our server Henry, who was cheerful and passionate about his duties. We rounded the experience with a delightful walk around the themed (it was the Spring Festival) garden.
Very impressive service and food!

Had a wonderful 6th-anniversary dinner here.

This place is one of those Michelin starred places that serves you food you actually want to come back for. I love the snacks to start - the beef pocky was excellent. Each course was interesting yet thoughtful. The beef Wellington for Christmas was a thing of beauty and delicious. The other really special feature of dining here is the mignardises. When you have the full menu, you end your meal with a selection that looks like jewels. Outstanding service too. We felt so well taken care of.

A good lunch menu. Added a supplementary eel course, it is superb. Love the kangaroo tail pho consommé and pate en croute. The lamb pastry of the main course is a nod to a very good curry puff homage. The apple pie with Martel caramel ended the course perfectly. The walk in the flower dome at the end of the meal is a good experience. You can get complementary entry to the flower dome. Loves how it aligns to the theme of the restaurant.
Other than the delicious food, the very attentive staff, Henry and Max, elevated the entire experience. It was an enjoyable night.

Walked up to Maxwell Fuzhou Oyster Cake (Maxwell Food Centre) with zero queue — already winning. Grabbed two oyster cakes and, oh wow, the fillings pleasantly surprised me: juicy oysters, prawns, minced pork and coriander all tucked inside that golden, crispy outside shell. Hint: eat it while warm, because the crisp edges + warm, flavorful core combo hits differently.
The batter outside snaps just enough; inside is moist and savory without being overly oily (though I’ll admit, there’s a bit of grease if it cools down).
Price is (kindly) wallet-friendly too... around S$2.50 per piece.
Would I go back? Absolutely. It's scary since this is on the way home for me, so I pass it daily... 😮

The crust is crispy and filled with a mix of minced meat, oysters bits and coriander. I even found a small prawn in the fillings. I wish it could be less salty though.

While these are best enjoyed fresh and piping hot, they hold up surprisingly well. I bought the snack home and a quick heat-up in the toast revived the crispness.

Update Sep 2025: Among the few oyster cake stalls I've tried, this one is the best. The cakes are consistently fresh and generously filled. Despite the price increases over the years ($2.50 now), I think they are still worth it.

I've eaten their oyster cake for twenty years. Having been stationed abroad since 3 years ago, I recently came back on a home visit, and popped by to buy their oyster cakes again.  I was shocked and miffed!

This is not the way to ride the "fame" to make a killing just because they had received some gourmet recommendation, which I don't know how they got it.

There are FAR better Oyster Cakes in Geylang, Jln Besar, Fengshan... just to name a few.

Don't waste your money and calories on this.

P/s I was so appalled I forgot to take pictures of the oyster cakes.

Came for a birthday celebration, and this was the best dining experience we had experienced in Singapore so far. Service was both attentative and energetic - staffs were all very friendly and attentive from start to finish. Ambiance is very neat and clean. Fully enjoyed the lunch tasting menu!!

Here came Seroja and Thevar, both of which are restaurants that I really like. They made me want to try this Huangpu Military Academy. The decoration is very elegant, and the flavors are similar to theirs. It's balanced but doesn't overpower the flavors.
The first appetizer was figs with fermented skin. The flavors were well balanced, and the sweet figs complemented the citrus sauce perfectly. The squid sushi with grape was refreshing, but the texture was not too糯. The scallop tartare was very flavorful， but the mustard flavor was a bit too strong. The first piece of bonito fish was paired with cucumber seaweed， which was very refreshing. The ice cream and cold noodle soup had the same flavoring， full of Korean style. The bonito itself didn't show its flavor， but the smoky flavor gave the same depth of texture. This dish helped enhance the taste of the fish. This dish was very typical of Japanese cuisine， with more Korean elements incorporated into it. The Arctic clam steamed egg started to flavor itself and finally began to exert its power. The Arctic clam was fresh， sweet， crispy and springy， and the soup was rich and salty. The first seafood dish was the signature abalone， a very skillful dish. The base sauce was very rich， and the abalone was cooked perfectly. The two complemented each other very well. The grilled fish and Thevar's dish were the same. The skin was very crispy， but I preferred Meta because his fish was more heavily seasoned， with a slightly higher saltiness， which was just what was needed to capture the aroma of the fish. The cold noodles were the highlight， having a very good synergy with Seroja's herbal noodles. The cold noodles were sour and sweet， with a refreshing aroma. The texture was firm， and the bottom was flavored with perilla oil， with a strong Korean flavor. However， the oil was a little too heavy. The wagyu beef was nothing special， a standardized main dish. The first pickled grapes were paired with ice cream and jelly. The ice cream was of柚子茶 flavor， and the grape ice cream was a little astringent， which actually made me like it. The second dish was corn paste + popcorn + corn ice cream + crispy corn. The ice cream was more salty， and I thought it would have the same corn explosion aroma， but it was a bit disappointing. But overall， it was great， with a constant balance of sour and sweet.
I really liked the several small desserts at the end. The banana puffs were especially delicious. If they were mass-produced， it would be great.

[Meta (**)] has evolved. Old [Meta] was very good, but new [Meta] has gotten more refined. Is it better than the old [Meta]? Hmmm... Depends, but it is a lot pricier than the old [Meta], which begs to question, is the value proposition better or worse?

Frankly, the only real issue in the old place was the acoustics in the dining area. This new place just tries too hard, while scoring some truly remarkable hits, but floundered in others.

For a start, I will say, FOH service was excellent. Friendly, helpful and attentive, getting the highest I've ever scored for service in any of my restaurant reviews this far. Only issue is, on occasion, the ladies can be a little too soft when describing the dishes, making it impossible to hear them.

Foodwise, the various starters were very competent, with the absolutely delicious Cuttlefish Gimbap, along with the Scallop & Caviar Tart being textural and mouthfeel superstars! That said, while the tuna sandwich was texturally sound, it ate far too fishy.

Their Signature Jeju Abalone Juk was incredible! Layers upon layers of textures, depth of flavours and simply perfect technical execution. The skin and scales of the Amadai were crispy but the cuisson of the fish was unfortunately over. The noodles of the Milmyeon was a textural masterpiece, and the sauce was perfectly paired, but the pickled celtuce was oddly misplaced.  Sadly, the BBQ Wagyu was a little too tense and overall ate a little, dare I say, boring.

The unfortunate happenstance of the dinner was the "not great" dessert courses. Overly bitter champagne jelly that ruined the otherwise palatable palate cleanser, a grainy custard that marred an otherwise great corn dessert with fantastic components, and a lacklustre showing of petite fours with a "juksik donut" that was so tough, I thought I was a dog biting a chew toy.

So back to my initial question, is this evolution better or worse? Well, the Michelin guide says better, promoting them from 1* to 2* and if I was an inspector, I would whole-heartedly agree. It has traded some of the liveliness it had in the past, but the ambient noise used to be so loud, it could at times be unbearable. The technical execution is much more refined, also a little more mature but with that, sterility becomes a little more present. Not a question of "for better or worst" in this aspect, but more upon qualities expected for rising to 2 and 3 stars.

But as a diner, where we view through a different lens, I think it's scores marginally worse on the value proposition scale. For example, the non-alcoholic pairing is extremely pricey, considering it's a straight juice mix with no fermentation. Yes, the drinks were tasty, but as a diner, it felt like they could have done a little more on this aspect.

Objectively, still a great restaurant and dining experience and I still rate them extremely highly.

The opening act at Meta unfolded as a series of jewel-like morsels, each one a study in restraint and refinement. A Fig Salad paired ruby fig with delicate beancurd skin and citrus soy, its sweetness and earthiness brightened by edible petals scattered like a midsummer garden. The Tuna Sandwich, crisp and precise, layered a silken yolk centre with a lush tuna tartare beneath a crown of ikura, each bite rich yet refreshing. The Scallop Tart dazzled with translucent scallop lifted by wasabi and finger lime, while the Prawn Toast, grounded by a kelp base, carried a lightly blanched prawn and a glistening mound of caviar — a decadent interplay of oceanic richness and umami depth.

The seafood progression began with the Bonito, revealed in layers — hay-smoked fish with a gentle rustic note, accented with thinly sliced ginger and crowned with a cool cucumber granita. A tangle of cucumber and seaweed added crunch and brine, turning each mouthful into a play of smoke, freshness, and ocean clarity. A surprise clam dish followed, tender and briny, resting over a quivering egg custard that married ocean and earth in hushed tones. The Tilefish completed the course, its skin crisped to a golden lattice and paired with turnip in a broth crowned by vivid carrot foam, bringing earthy warmth to the seafood sequence.

The Jeju Abalone stood apart as a true showpiece, its cross-hatched surface charred to a caramelised intensity that gave way to tender flesh beneath. Resting on a bed of kamtae juk and lily bulb, it was layered, soulful, and deeply satisfying — a signature for good reason, and the undisputed highlight of the evening thus far.

The BBQ Lamb was served with a lacquered char, tender within and flanked by jangajji pickles and mole, a thoughtful interplay of Korean spice and smoky depth. Yet it was the Corn Rice — fragrant, buttery, and layered with quiet complexity — that stole the show, transforming a humble side into a dish of its own distinction.

The Melon was a study in restraint: a delicate makgeolli sorbet resting on coconut snow, concealing beneath it sweet, juicy cubes of melon. Light and refreshing, it balanced lactic tang with natural fruitiness, a palate-cleansing prelude to the closing sweets. The Sweet Corn followed, playful and nostalgic, weaving roasted kernels, caramelised popcorn, and silken corn ice cream into a composition that danced between sweet and savoury, crunch and cream — a humble staple elevated into something truly memorable.

The evening drew to a close with an array of Petit Fours, each crafted with finesse. A chewy Juak, a sweet Geotgam, and a playful Banana Cream Puff formed the trio, presented with a handwritten “Happy 16th Anniversary” — an elegant, personal finale to a meal that was as heartfelt as it was refined.

My wife and I randomly walked into this restaurant, not realising it’s listed in the Michelin Guide for both 2023 and 2024.

It wasn’t lunch hour anymore, yet there were still many customers, which was a good sign.

We ordered a seafood glass vermicelli salad, a pad thai, and a Thai-style fish soup. The salad was freshly prepared with crisp, quality ingredients and had a well-balanced, refreshing flavour. The pad thai was slightly on the sweet side for our taste, but overall still quite enjoyable.

The fish in the soup was large—more than enough to make the two of us feel full. The soup itself was outstanding; even the aroma alone was mouthwatering. The fish was soft (not exactly tender), but it absorbed the flavours of the broth nicely. The soup wasn’t overly oily or salty, and you could drink it without feeling overly thirsty or heavy afterwards.

It was a very pleasant surprise and we truly enjoyed our meal here.

I had the pleasure of dining at Mustard Seed twice, first in September and again just last week, and I’m happy to share that the food remained wonderfully consistent across both visits. That level of consistency is truly the mark of a great restaurant.

I’ve heard about Mustard Seed long ago, since pre-Covid days and always knew how hard it was to secure a seat. Finally dining here feels like a real privilege. On both occasions, the restaurant was full, which is always a happy sight and speaks to its well-deserved popularity.

Now, onto the stars of the show: the food. I genuinely appreciate the thoughtful elements behind each dish - the layers of flavour, the intricate concepts, and the meticulous execution. Every course feels deeply considered and beautifully balanced. I’m already looking forward to the next season’s menu.

Fingers crossed I manage to get a seat again… it’s honestly harder than camping for my university modules!

PS: Bonus clip of the cat who greeted us after our first dinner 🐈‍⬛

Getting a chance to eat here is a privilege. This is a culinary gem. And one that does not rely on international culinary big wigs but grounded on good sincere cooking by young local talents. Getting a table here was itself an ordeal. Priced at $188 ++ , it was full house on a Wednesday evening that I was there. And no wonder, considering the delectable course after course of culinary gems that was served. You can’t quite put a label on that food that was served. I can only say it’s beautifully new-Asian: a culmination of the essence of Asian flavors. This is a must try; if you ever got the privilege to.
Amazing! Mustard Seed is just lovely, consistently both comforting and surprising, with complex flavours & textures and warm hospitality. A perfect restaurant in Singapore!
Food was Delicious and left us yearning for more. Staff was friendly and attentive to needs too. Will definitely recommend and will revisit! Thanks for a wonderful experience!

I went to that restaurant with super high hopes, especially since it was so not cheap. I was a little letdown.  They clearly tried hard, but their take on certain dishes wasn't all that special. The whole dinner was also kind of rushed. Honestly, the food and ingredients weren't worth the price we paid. I didn't like the dessert. They might try to create their versions, but the original version seemed much nicer.

I do understand how negative reviews can affect livelihoods - but was honestly surprised by how mediocre the experience has been, given how difficult it was to book or reserve the slots.

Too much salt in Chawamushi, and Scallop Otah, too little corn taste in Somen. The best dish was the last main dish threadfin white curry - very decent flavour but not a wow.

It is not a matter of personal taste but look at A) the ingredients used - non sashimi-grade seafood including the (probably) frozen shrimp in the Chawanmushi and the Otah Scallop - I could not pick out any expensive ingredients in the entire menu and
B) 9 course meal without any amuse bouche or petit 4s -

I was half thinking the margins earned must be quite high by the restaurant.

Perhaps this is why this place has not even gotten a Michelin bib gourmand let alone a star even though the price point is that of a star.

The fact that they change menus every 2 months could be both a good and bad thing - good for loyal customers and perhaps bad for wanting to perfect a dish that should take longer than 2 months (?)

That said, I enjoyed the Honey Yuzu cooler made with Singha soda water - which I thought was well made. I also think there was effort made to introduce the dishes by each of the staff and did not feel that they were arrogant unlike what other reviews suggest.

The team does a great job of elevating a lot of local and Japanese flavors for a unique experience. I really enjoyed it. However, I felt that the menu was pretty small for the price. Also, a feedback for their $10 tea. They don’t even give you a full glass. Which is pretty disappointing.
Great food

We had the Jan/ Feb menu and thoroughly enjoyed the experience. It’s a simple and no-frills set-up which we liked, and the team’s ability to create new flavours from old classics which meld so well together was really impressive.

We especially enjoyed the beef tartare and the shiso leaf courses - please keep them on the menu or have them on heavy rotation!

4 stars because of price point though. At $250ish per pax in a neighbourhood near YCK, it’s honestly steep.

Managed to get a lunch spot after a cancellation. Really worthwhile visit as the dishes are exquisite. Enjoyed the second dish which was a tartar with Chye Poh. The taste was familiar yet different. The scallop with curry sauce was also memorable. It is great that they explain all the dishes when they come out so you can recognise the different ingredients used. Very imaginative blend of different types of food and superbly executed. The service was also very professional and thoughtful with small wet tissues for each course. They change their menu every two months so great to come back to try different things.

If they were to open a standalone restaurant just for their Nasi Padang they’d make a killing!

Its a great place for an excellent taste of home when you have the hankering for it! A tiny quaint restaurant on Race course rd in little India area- a 10 min walk from Raffles hospital on Victoria Street, Bugis junction etc. Bugis exit Metro station B..

Excellent hospitality- Very good warm service by crew- - I had no reservation- Got no indoor tables even at 6.45 pm !!!Jeez! So  I agreed to wait outside at the road side table over some cold downers, and in about 24 mins was ushered in as assured!

I saw most of the diners- Europeans and orientals alike were going all hog like desi Pros on the daab chingris( mildly spiced prawns baked inside a green coconut with cream for infused flavour) Biriyanis, tikka masalas, butter gravies and naans- the aroma told me they were spot on in the best possible way. Cudos to the chef from Kolkata. Man! if it wasn't 6.45 pm!! Grrr

Its AC inside, well decorated but kinda small for sure- 7-8 tables maybe? . There's a drink list with beers on with other sodas and lassis etc. They have Bengali sweets too. The menu is awesome for someone like me-  a well curated collection of finger food and main dishes of West Bengal and North Indian origin. You want desi khana jamake??  Dabake khana hai? This is the place to run riot hehehe :)

We took finger food-  7 pm is to early for us for dinner. The fish cutlet with kasundi is a triple century superhit ! and I personally don't really go for fish or even effing T20 cricket. So that tells you all. Don;t miss this for what you're worth sucker!

The matarshooti kachori ( Green Pea stuffed poori) - was just perfect with the aloo dum ( Potato curry)  true Bangali style- as a Bong with UK heritage and an expert amateur chef of 38 yrs I couldn't ask for more. Boy you fellas scored here too!

The meat chop was great-- maybe not a 100% but still a great choice with the beer.

MY regret -It was too early for us--- odd time just walked in to experience it. I wanted hog out with the samosas and rolls then meat dishes and naans and desserts... Maybe next time.  My soul tells me you guys are doing it just right! Mustard in all was a great experience. A must visit for apnaa dildaar khanaa- or jolkhabar!!

I had a really good meal at Nana Curry in Vivocity. Their curry rice was rich, creamy and packed with flavour. The portion was generous and the curry had the right balance of spice and fragrance that made it really comforting. It’s the kind of dish that makes you want to come back again.

We also tried the truffle curry noodle, which honestly surprised me. At first I was a bit unsure about mixing truffle with curry, but it turned out to be a great choice. The noodles were springy, the curry base was still strong, and the truffle gave it a nice twist without being too overpowering. It felt different but in a good way, and I’m glad we gave it a try.

Overall, it’s a nice spot if you’re craving a good bowl of curry with something a little unique on the side.

Traditional curry with rice or bread, it packs a spicy kick and comes with different choices of meat (chicken, lamb, or fish) and vegetables. Tau pok and vegetables can be added that soaks up the aromatic curry gravy. Great on rainy day, cool day.

This is one spicy curry I can find in Singapore, especially this outlet in the hawker centre setting. The sauce is outrageously spicy, simply love it to go with rice or toasted bread.

Hideaway's concept, at least as I understand it, is to marry comfort and warmth in a living room setting. Lounge, dining and kitchen meld into one, as fragrances from the kitchen mingle with laughter from the dining room. That is the canvas for a meal.

On that canvas, the base coat is excellent service. Mili and Monica set about making extensive preparations for our ROM. It was a small affair (family only) but they made it feel grand. We were received at pre-event site visits with open smiles, examples of custom-made menus they had prepared in the past, and attentive suggestions about everything from makgeoli pairings to lighting angles for photos. Communication was quick and helpful - solution-oriented without being overbearing. And most importantly, we were floored by the warmth at every turn.

Then there was the artistry of the food. The word "elevated" is sometimes casually bandied around when describing unnecessary tinkering of timeless traditional recipes. But when I say that Korean cuisine - the food that I had grown up with, and which I helped prepare with my grandma at her farm - was elevated, I say so without subtext or caveat. Consider the core of korean cooking: jaang. Consider also, traditional korean condiment ratios and flavor profiles. The food respects that, even as it experiments with the form or adapts to local palettes. And the makgeoli selection, new age as it is, was enough to impress my father who continues to believe that getting sloshed in Hongdae with ₩3000 soju is "real drinking".

To my mind, we are blessed to have Naeum in the Singaporean culinary scene. They're a proud and inspirational flagbearer for Korean cuisine, and innovation. Naturally, this is not the sort of meal one casually indulges in on alternate Tuesdays. But if you were hoping to be intentional about a special occasion, and were looking for a safe pair of hands to cradle your event into happiness, this would assuredly be my recommendation. One of my standout dining experiences of 2025! Nae:Um, a Korean-Western fusion restaurant that’s a must-visit for people seeking healthy yet indulgent flavors. Cant miss it if you are fermented food lover.

some highlights of the meal:
- we began with a tomato soup infused with kimchi, offering a unique twist on traditional kimchi brine. Unlike the usual sharp, pungent bite, this soup is velvety, with a balanced, mild sour-sweet profile that gently awakens the palate for the courses to come.
- some of my favorite dishes include The domi (red snapper), memilmyeon  & mandu (buckwheat noodles and dumplings), are nothing short of exceptional, each dish showcasing a harmonious blend of textures and bold, authentic flavors.
- The main course, featuring Iberico pork, is a revelation. Cooked to a perfect pink hue, it’s as tender and succulent as premium hanwoo beef. The accompanying onions, caramelized to a fruit-like sweetness, elevate the dish to another level.

I had an incredible experience at Naeum. The space is cozy, the course was cohesive, and both the wine and non-alcoholic pairings were excellent and highly recommended. Plating was clean, precise, and visually striking. Price is reasonable and hospitality was satisfactory.

Starters:
The dongchimi tomato looked simple but had complex flavours. Fresh, tangy, and a brilliant way to start the course. Easily, my favourite starter.

The gwanja seaweed rosette offered unique textures, complementing the first starter.

The toran black bean contrasted crisp and soft elements beautifully.

The sokkori oxtail was elegant and prepared the palate perfectly for the mains.
Starters were strong and memorable.

Subsequent courses:
Domi seabream lemon, and daikon was light, delicate, and harmonious, elevating the meal and making it playful and memorable. One of the highlights of my meal, love the fish.

The memilmyeon and mandu paired earthy morel dumplings with noodles and tangy kimchi. There was also subtle floral turnip slices which added charm to the dish.

The jeonbok which was jeju abalone, seaweed vinaigrette, and caviar was intricate and luxurious. The drops of flavours were also precisely placed without a single smudge. Amazing.

The nobchi with squash, and maeuntang was flavorful with its rich butter sauce. Squash presentation was good.

The Iberico ribeye was satisfying with the onion and perilla layers though I feel the layering was not necessary, I appreciate the touch of details in making it look more presentable. Personally felt that if the onion was infused into the dish and not visible, it would have been more palatable.

The hansang with deodeok, mushroom gomtang, and banchan felt comforting and homely. As an asian myself, I connected with it.

Desserts
The darae changmyeon was refreshing and bright. Lively contrast to the richer courses and worked well as a palate cleanser.

The daechu, truffle, and white chocolate was indulgent, sinful and sweet. Love the charcoal biscuit base, it was a good touch.

The petit four ended the meal playfully with a mix of traditionally elevated flavours. Absolutely love the rice cake. Mugwort flavour and the rice puff base was something new and interesting to me.

The meal was thoughtful, harmonious, and thoroughly enjoyable. The only minor note is the cake. The base was slightly soggy and tough to bite, but everything else more than made up for it. The inventive play of textures and complementary flavors made each dish engaging. It is a great story.

I will definitely return. Thank you, Naeum.

Restaurant Name: No.18 Zion Road Fried Kway Teow
Reviews:
If you like the dry type of Char Kway Teow, with the right amount of moisture, YOU WILL LOVE THIS!!!
I personally prefer the watery type, my favourite now closed is Apollo CKT in Marine Parade. They are unbeaten in my books. But for a dry and savoury with the right amount wateryness, this is fantastic!!!
The most outstanding thing about this CKT is the WOK HEI! Oh my God, it fumes up your nostrils, and it is so smoky and fume fragrant. It is unmatched, tasted many places, but this is so memorable.
The service is pretty fast, even though there is a long long queue. YOu have to go before 12pm to avoid the cue. BTW people start queuing up as early as 11.30am, when they only open at 12.30pm! Yeah, I'm dead serious!
I ordered mine without the cockles (filthy animal!) and without the preserved sausages (larp cheonh). And asked for more bean sprouts and it taste amazing!! Next time I'll ask them to leave out the Pork Lard (likely impossible), because it is loaded with lots of it. All these things are just CONCENTRATED SATURATED FATS. I don't want to squeeze my chest when I wake up in the morning. That's the most common time that people have an heart attack.
The point is, you can still enjoy the CKT fully without the concentrated saturated fat of preserved sausages and pork lard.
Go before 12pm, and thank me later.

If you’re looking for a fine meal, you’ll find many places in 🇸🇬. But if you’re looking to have a memorable experience, to feel, think, and reimagine through delicious food that surprises you, then you’ll find yourself at Nouri - the older sister of Appetite (where we visited a couple times now.)

Crossroads cooking is the ethos at Nouri, rooted in the belief that cultures do not exist in isolation, and neither should food. It’s an idea born not just of creativity, but of research, anthropology, and compassion. Behind each dish is a long process of inquiry, sourcing, and deep listening. Chef Ivan and his team approach food as part anthropology, part philosophy, and part art, translating centuries of migration, memory, and meaning into dishes

It’s rare for every single dish in a tasting menu to be on point. Nouri did that well - some dishes hit harder than expected, both in flavour and feeling. It’s the first time I’ve come close to tearing up during a meal, in the best possible way. 🥹 Each dish seemingly asks: “What does this mean in your culture? What does this mean in mine?” The meal never feels intellectual for the sake of it. Instead, it feels intimate, like someone has mapped the world and found a way to serve it to you.

Special shoutout to Dominique for the book recommendations and Wyman who takes hospitality to the next level - I’ve never met such an attentive and curious host! What a legend.

Easily one of the top 5 meals of my life. From the incredible, warm greeting ritual at the front to each meticulously and beautifully crafted course, I was in awe the entire meal. I will be coming back here as often as I can.

Focused on something he calls "Crossroads Cooking" Nouri Restaurant sees Chef Ivan Brehm investigating the interconnectedness of various food histories across five continents, the results part traditional and part innovative but undeniably interesting.

Open for lunch as well as dinner in Chinatown, the entrance understated for a Michelin-starred eatery, guests are greeted in a foyer by friendly staff before being led to a room with tables lined up around a marble countertop and what is at least half of Nouri’s kitchen.

Offering a truncated afternoon tasting, four courses for S$168, lunch begins with an offer of Bubbles, Wine or bottled Tea from Muri whose “Fade to Black” blend pairs well to Snacks eaten with Bread and  Hamachi on Bread with lots of acidity.

Petite in terms of portions, Bass let to age deftly balanced by Vanilla and Pepper, it was after Brehm loudly dressed-down one of his Sous that “Chicken & Dumpling” arrived with restrained heat and a “dumpling” of Rice wrapped by Cabbage.

Stretching to India for preserved Rose Petals at Dessert, “Things That Go Well Together” including Strawberry Sorbet and cracked Peppercorns, Petits Fours span globally such that Black Sesame,  Osmanthus, Tempeh and Coffee all get a moment but nothing really to connect them.
