Pitifully small portions! Had to stop for satay on the way home. Even my small 80 yr old grandmother was hungry on leaving. Look at the size of the main course🤨. How is it possible to spend hundreds of dollars for miserable portions. FINE DINING IS NOT SMALL DINING!!!!! If they don’t fix this major issue they will not survive
student tuning Bhalo Zara Zara station first time Khabar hone ki
Spent New Year's Eve here, absolutely loved it. Service and food were amazing, highly recommend it if you want a culinary experience in Singapore.
Food was well prepared, amazing wine pairing. Having my dinner at Born during my short visit to Singapore, amazed with the quality of the food. Good job Born!!

We had a wonderful fine dining experience at Born. From the moment we arrived, the team made us feel genuinely welcomed with a very warm and personalised touch. Every detail was thoughtfully considered, and the service felt attentive yet comfortable. The overall experience was refined, intimate, and memorable — truly a place where hospitality and passion shine. We left feeling well taken care of and already looking forward to our next visit.

We were so excited to visit here but unfortunately it’s just a trend restaurant for people who haven’t experienced a true European Michelin restaurant. The ingredients are too experimental to be enjoyable for most people’s pallets. The price to value ratio is terrible. Possibly the worst star I’ve ever collected and I’ve got more than 100. The whole experience was cold and the stories behind the food seemed contrived and for show. The pigeon dish was so unimaginative and forgettable. The best dish by far was the bread course. Save your money and most importantly your time. They also made a mistake with our dietary requirements and tried to sit us at a table that is not even in the restaurant.
Simply Delicious!

I wanted to visit Born for so long already. And it was really worth the wait and the trip. Excellent, just excellent compilation of flavours. Every plate. Very professional service, great wine and lovely ambiance. A lot of extra points for the tea selection and service. Bravo!
First time been was when it newly opened in 2022, the concert of “Home” made me feel warm. Amazing food and service, no doubt that it ranked in star from the following year!

Absolutely exceptional experience from start to finish. The chef is friendly, and the staff are well trained. The restaurant concept is impressive, with thoughtful balance between ingredients and flavors. One of the best parts is that the pacing of the meal adjusts to the diner, unlike many fine dining experiences that drag on for hours. Their dessert is especially delicious. Simply a 10 out of 10.

Simply wonderful.  From the dishes that teased our palettes to the amazing service and attention to detail.

All the staff were practically on standby every step of the way.  We were served by different staff throughout and everyone of them delivered.  Wine connoisseur Leslie made sure the wine we chose was of the utmost quality.

Definitely will return.

Nothing short of amazing. Beautiful ambience, each dish curated with such purpose and precision. The chef who told a story through his dishes. Service was great and food was not only so aesthetic, but so delicious. Thank you to this wonderful team, it’s rare for me to wish to come back to restaurant but I would definitely come back again.
Good Google reviews. But at $228++ for its lunch set (Fridays only), it is rather expensive considering that it only has 1 Michelin star. That price range is more appropriate to 2 Michelin stars.
The employees at the Born were extremely friendly and supportive. The food was excellent!

After the restaurant Born, everything is a little different

Flavors of Asia with a small touch of Europe
Pure hedonism for the palate
Thank you Chef Terry Chee

Though Chef Zor was on leave, I had a very enjoyable meal thanks to Natalie’s impeccable service, precision, and attention to detail. Really appreciated how she was always super speedy to assist, provide proactive service recovery, and mindful of the guests’ experience.
Muy buena

Highly recommended for great flavors and flawless execution!
Cozy place with an open kitchen view. Love their pigeon Wellington and tomato soup with uni.

Very nice lunch at this Japanese French fusion Michelin star resto

Esp liked monkfish and duck consommé signature

Chaleur beautifully blends French finesse with Japanese precision. Chef Masahiko Kawano crafts each dish with balance, seasonality, and soul. The standout is the duck consommé, simmered for eight hours into pure depth and elegance. Every course feels thoughtful and refined.

Service is attentive without being intrusive, and the intimate counter setting lets you enjoy the artistry up close. Only small note: the placemats could use a refresh. Otherwise, exceptional experience.

Came here for my birthday and had such a wonderful experience. The food was spot on but what stood out most was the service. The team was warm, attentive, and made the evening feel really special. Definitely a place I’d recommend for any celebration.
Buen ambiente

Nestled along a row of charming shophouses lies Chaleur, started by chef Masa who hails from the now defunct Beni at mandarin gallery.
The place got their Michelin star 9 months into its operations which is pretty cool. Chef masa’s faire is heavily French inspired, however utilising Japanese ingredients. The use of fish is apparent which is very Japanese, but cooked in a very French manner, for example, the flounder which was seared to perfection. One of the starters which was a medley of raw fish and eggplant came in a edamame sauce. Light and delightful. The duck consommé was my favourite. Think duck Bak Kut teh soup. Prices are reasonable and if you’re feeling a little more peckish than usual, supplement your meal with lobster and abalone with a slight top up. What’s also great is their wine and champagne selection. Super extensive so you don’t run out of choices.
It’s really nice and well deserved Michilin restaurant✨ Both chef and staffs are very nice and I will visit again🎉 Highly recommend!

Had my birthday dinner here and I am impressed. EVERYTHING was so good!!! From the snacks to the bread to the desserts, it was so good. I will be back when the menu changes and will bring my friends to try!! 10/10

Wierd seating arrangements of a big U-table, and hard for conversations.  Food is ok, delicate but not particularly memorable.  Breads are underwhelming for a French restaurant,  feels like frozen ones. Petit fours also look under sized and from frozen.

Exquisite experience, very attentive service, the food (and drink) is beautiful and tasted heavenly - it must come from the heart caring for every ingredients as well as the  presentation of the dishes.

Five Takeaways:
•Always have doubts about Lobster but the Blue Lobster add-on was the most memorable part of the meal
•Chef Signature Duck Consomme was rich and full of Duck essence, the dish was warm and comforting
•Challans Duck served had a perfect sear and the Pedro Xemenez sauce was dark and rich adding some earthiness to the dish

•Compact dining area and even more compact kitchen with an open concept and a lot of Japanese tones. Service is very friendly and professional

Exceptional experience at Restaurant Chaleur. Chef Masa’s food is delicate and fragrant yet rich in taste and texture. Wonderful and original combinations of flavours. Great wine list. Great service from Ms Rainbow.  Also the most amazing bread!

Dining at Chaleur was nothing short of extraordinary. The Blue Lobster supplement was a true indulgence—succulent, delicate, and expertly prepared to bring out its natural sweetness. The Wagyu Tenderloin was impeccably executed, with deep, smoky notes from the charcoal and bone marrow elevating its richness. And the Chef’s Signature duck consommé with wholegrain noodle was a masterpiece—comforting yet sophisticated, with layers of umami that lingered beautifully.

Beyond the impeccable dishes, Chaleur also strikes the perfect balance with its portions, ensuring a satisfying experience without excess. Their homemade bread, served in small, thoughtful quantities, is a refreshing change from the typical overabundance elsewhere—where baskets overflow, only to lead to unnecessary waste. Here, every element is curated with intention, enhancing the meal without overwhelming it.

From the ambiance to the precision in every dish, Chaleur delivers a Michelin-starred experience that is both refined and deeply satisfying. Highly recommended for those seeking an unforgettable culinary journey! Thank you Chef!

Chaleur isn’t just a restaurant—it’s an experience. For those who appreciate fine cuisine, exceptional champagne, and a setting that whispers luxury without ever shouting, this Michelin-starred destination is a must. The meal started strong with piping warm bread paired with silky butter—a small but powerful testament to the precision and care you’d expect from a top-tier French kitchen. Every dish was a delight—expertly prepared with a beautiful mix of Japanese and French techniques that made each course mouthwatering. The setting is refined yet cozy, tucked away on the second floor of a charming shophouse near Neil Road.

One of the highlights was their stunning glass wine cellar, showcasing an impressive selection of wines and champagnes. Chaleur partners with Dom Pérignon, so you’ll find some of their finest (and rarest) bottles on the list—including special editions like the Lady Gaga one we had at a spectacular LVMH-hosted event.

The intimate space makes it ideal for both elegant social gatherings and relaxed business conversations. A real gem for anyone who loves great food, great bubbles, and a touch of understated luxury.

Visited in March 2025 for lunch.

We were the only party at the restaurant so it was an extremely intimate and cosy affair. Service was good and food was excellent!

The fattiness of the kanpachi paired with the zesty mikan was super refreshing. The guinea fowl was also cooked to perfection.

Their menu and price is definitely a good starting point for those who want to try a Michelin restaurant for the first time!

My friends made a dinner reservation in this restaurant, I was invited to dine with him. I am impressed with the service which the crew has been very attentive to details which I am left handed and was offered with the table setting based on my preference. I will definitely coming back to try their lunch.Consomme is very rich & yummy too.Thank you to Tony for being attentive to details.
I had an excellent experience. Very good dishes. The Boston blue lobster was perfectly cooked. The service was outstanding. Tony was exceptional.

好吃，是吃过最清爽，且酱汁搭配与调味都很均衡的fusion。

甜点水平还有进步空间，日本主厨很用心。

A personalized and delightful experience end to end. Worthy of its 1 Michelin Star and more. While all the courses were excellent,  the bread and butter pairing was particularly delightful to the senses

My husband and I had the pleasure of dining at this warm, home-like restaurant.

The thoughtful curation of the menu was evident, with each dish showcasing care and attention to detail.

The staff created an atmosphere where you felt like more than just a guest.

Had another great lunch today of the winter dinner menu featuring quail as the main dish. It was well cooked like the pigeon pie in the style of beef wellington with the quail breast wrapped with foie gras, minced pork and cabbage. As usual, the snacks and appetisers were thoughtfully selected and skilfully executed. We love the the 3 seafood dishes of chutoro, scallops & Japanese garoupa...they were truly taste sensations. As a beautiful ending to the meal we had a refreshing strawberry dessert. My gourmet friend and I will certainly be back to taste Chef's spring menu which will be launched next week.
A lovely restaurant, excellent chef, service and food. Had second helpings of the bread, butter, duck consomme. Great explanations by Zean and Rainbow! Kudos to the team.
Simply delicious.

We had an unforgettable dinner at CHALEUR last night while celebrating my wife's birthday! From the moment we arrived, Mr. Kawano, the owner, made us feel incredibly welcome. The ambiance was warm and inviting, perfect for a special occasion.
The dinner offered a fantastic selection of dishes, and each one was beautifully presented and bursting with flavor. We particularly enjoyed the noodles in special duck consumme and the Yonezawa beef, which was a delightful surprise for my wife's birthday. The attention to detail and the quality of the ingredients truly stood out.
The service was impeccable; the staff was attentive without being intrusive, ensuring we had everything we needed to enjoy our evening. Mr. Kawano even stopped by our table to wish my wife a happy birthday, which made the experience even more special.
If you're looking for a restaurant that combines amazing food, a charming atmosphere, and exceptional service, look no further than CHALEUR. We will definitely be returning for more wonderful meals in the future! Thank you for making my wife's birthday celebration so memorable!
Incredible experience!

Restaurant Fiz offers an intimate fine dining experience with beautifully crafted, seasonal dishes. Flavors are delicate and well-balanced, and presentation is elegant. Service is attentive and personalized, enhancing the overall experience. It’s premium-priced, but ideal for special occasions or diners seeking a refined and memorable culinary journey.

It was our first time dining at Fiz and it was a memorable one. The food was utterly delicious and opened our eyes (and tastebuds) to Malaysian fine dining. Never would we have imagined that Malaysian dishes could be interpreted in such a unique and satisfactory way. Chef Hafizzul was attentive and friendly which made the dining experience more meaningful. We were very happy with Fiz and will definitely be returning.

Fiz is doing something truly special for the local dining scene with their EP 3.0 Sajian Warisan menu. A massive highlight of the night was Chef Hafizzul himself. He is incredibly humble and took the time to share his heritage, skills, and cooking journey with us. It was a completely eye opening experience, and his passion really shines through in the food.

The meal kicked off on a high note with the Fiz Kaya Toast, delivering a brilliantly rich and decadent bite. The Ang Kar Prawn followed, bringing a serious, sweat inducing heat with its white curry custard. The flavours were massive, though I do wish they provided a knife, as eating the large prawns with just a fork and spoon was cumbersome. The salad gave it a great crunch, but the the delicate uni got a little lost in the spice. Next was the Shima Aji. It had a very sharp, sour kick similar to a celok sauce. The finely diced fish and creamy avocado base were nice, but overall the dish leaned a bit too salty overall and had me reaching for my water. It was also slightly repetitive to see caviar used again so soon in the tasting.

The absolute star of the show was the Blackmore Short Ribs Percik. Chef Hafizzul uses a traditional slow basting method over 38 hours, and I have never seen anyone pull off this level of effort in a commercial kitchen. The beef was unbelievably marbled, pulling apart over a thick, cashew heavy Massaman curry gulai sauce. It was a total masterpiece. The Sotong Sumbat Sambal Hitam was decent but felt a bit safe, and the lightweight plate it was served on kept sliding around the table while I tried to cut the squid. The sides, however, were spot on. The Nasi Dagang made with rare rice had flawless grain texture, and the Chef Special Gudeg hit right at the heart. Chef Fiz explained it replicates the flavours of Gudeg Yu Nap, which had a pop-up in Raffles Hotel some time ago, albeit less sweet than the usual fare from Jogjakarta.

A quirky frozen papaya palate cleanser with popping candy reset our taste buds. The sweets brought everything home perfectly. The Permata Rimba offered a deep chocolate hit with a great nutty crunch, and the Signature Bahulu was addictively crispy, blending Gula Apong and santan for a very clever savoury and sweet finish.

I am happily giving Fiz 5 stars because the culinary vision is just that good, but the front of house experience does need a bit of polish to match the kitchen. The greeting at the door felt a little disorganised, making us feel slightly unwelcomed. Our server also seemed quite tired and unkempt, and missed the refined introductions you expect at this level of dining. However, minor service hiccups aside, the incredible flavours and Chef Hafizzul's dedication make this a must visit spot for any serious food lover.

We visited Restaurant Fiz in January 2026 to celebrate a friend’s birthday.  A huge thank you to the team for a memorable evening!  The food was excellent and the immaculate service made us feel incredibly welcome.  We were particularly impressed by how attentive the chef was, it was such a treat to have him personally attend to us and even surprised us with a delicious, complimentary dish.  We also really appreciated the close attention they paid to the birthday dessert 'cake', which made the celebration feel extra special.  Between the great flavors and the nice ambience, it was a perfect evening.  Highly recommended!
The chef is a genius! He made even tomatoes taste good (I normally HATE tomatoes). The lunch was great and I’ll definitely come back.

Dining at Fiz was the culinary highlight of our stay in Singapore. The chef and entire staff were enormously kind and explained the nuances of each dish. We can recommend Fiz to anyone visiting Singapore in search of superb cuisine and a memorable evening.
Best Malay fusion in CBD area. Helpful guide by chef himself on making of each dish.

It has always been a pleasant experience in this restaurant. Chef Hafizzul is so warmth to welcome us, talk to us about his preparation and sourcing of the food. Every mouthful is tasteful and always leave us in awe. His combination of flavours and colors are remarkable. Highly recommended.

Restaurant Fiz is a contemporary Southeast Asian restaurant in Tanjong Pagar. It is not very common to use Halal-certified produce in fine dining restaurants.

I tried their Episode 2.0 Salian Warisan (Full Experience). It is an 11+ course tasting menu exploring regional flavors and ancient preservation techniques like fermentation and smoking.

All dishes were executed and presented very well. It was an eye-opening experience. I will be back when their new episode is released in the future.

Our second time here. Came for EP2.0 and now 3.0. Chef Hafizzul’s work at Fiz is a beautiful conversation between heritage and imagination. Each dish feels deeply rooted in traditional Malay cooking, yet reinterpreted with a finesse that belongs confidently in fine dining. The flavours are familiar, almost nostalgic, but they arrive with new textures, thoughtful presentation, and a quiet sense of innovation that never feels forced.

What stands out most is the respect for tradition. Instead of diluting Malay cuisine to fit a modern mould, Chef Hafizzul elevates it, allowing time-honoured techniques, spices, and stories to shine in a refined setting. Every course reflects intention, balance, and an understanding of how to let bold flavours speak without overwhelming the palate.

Dining at Fiz is more than a meal. It is an experience that honours culture, craftsmanship, and creativity. Chef Hafizzul has created something rare: a space where traditional Malay cuisine is not only preserved, but celebrated at the highest level of culinary artistry. 10/10 would recommend and definitely would return for 4.0 and beyond. Kudos Chef and team for making the experience extremely pleasurable.

I loved Restaurant Fiz and what it represents. For too long “fine dining” has been pretty dominated by Western concepts, so new players that are bold and bring SEA regional focus is really cool to see. I think Fiz is a vibe, and judging from the reviews you clearly like it or you clearly don’t. I personally left as a fan, and very satisfied!

Execution by the kitchen is top notch. Ingredients, gorgeous. Such a beautiful showcase of Malay flavours which for so long has been overlooked at this price band even though the work behind it is intensive and requires such knowledge of flavour, and cooking skill. Also tbh sometimes with fine dining you might leave feeling underfed or unsatisfied — this is NOT the case here, it is refinement and thought, but also a hearty meal! Think familiar flavours, executed with interesting new angles. I particularly enjoyed the cleaver touches of citrus and lightness (vegetables were a standout for me) used throughout to keep everything balanced.

I’ll be thinking about this meal for a while. My pictures do not do it justice, you need to try it for yourself.

Come with an open mind and support this venture!

The food was exceptional.  Each dish drew on cooking and flavor traditions from Malaysia, but I don’t ever recall Malaysian food being this good.  My personal favorites were the Masaman oxtail and the grilled fern, but every dish had someone who thought it was the best.

I am not one to write reviews but this restaurant really blew me away. We went for a couples dinner and got à la carte. Expectedly we ordered a lot as everything sounded wonderful. What I wasn’t prepared for was the depth and complexity of flavours - we ordered mostly vegetarian and I was so pleased that it wasn’t an afterthought and dish after dish was masterful in its treatment of components and how it came together.

The service (specially for Singapore where we have come to expect poor to average service) was exceptional. I was a little cold from the aircon - the server noticed and offered to get me a scarf, the manager introduced the dishes with special emphasis on the provenance of the ingredients (like the rice harvested once a year) and the chef- owner who came to chat with us and then bid us goodbye after the meal.

I will definitely be back - this has been one of the most special and unusual meals in a while for me.

Delicious across the board. Fantastic people too.

Food was refined but not pretentious and still maintained the authentic flavours you’d expect from Southeast Asian cuisine. A must try in Singapore
The atmosphere is superb, The food is out of this world,  The chef is friendly and generous with knowledge, The staff is helpful and full of initiative.

Wagyu is an absolute must-try at this restaurant. The meat is incredibly tender, rich, and full of flavor, cooked perfectly to bring out its natural juiciness.

With only one night in Singapore, I wanted to be sure of having a truly memorable meal. As a French chef travelling through Asia, I asked an international food critic where I absolutely had to eat. She didn’t hesitate for a second: FIZ. She was completely right.

From the moment we arrived, the experience felt calm, confident, and generous. Although Chef Hafizul Hashim was not in the restaurant that evening, it quickly became clear that the place runs at a very high level regardless. The restaurant manager, chef de cuisine, and sommelier looked after us exceptionally well — present, precise, warm, and fully in control.

The chef de cuisine guided us through a generous selection of dishes, and from the first plates the quality of the products stood out. This is ingredient-driven cooking of the highest level. Details matter here: house-made shrimp paste with extraordinary depth, dry-aged fish from their own fish ager, and confident use of the Josper wood-fired oven and grill.

The flavours are bold and expressive — sambals with real punch, a melting Thai crab curry full of aroma, and heirloom rices cooked gently in fresh coconut water. Simple in appearance, deeply complex in execution.

One moment stayed with me. After dinner, close to midnight, the entire kitchen team was still there, peeling shallots for the next day. In Asia, peeled shallots are available everywhere and are an easy shortcut. When I mentioned how impressive it was, the response was simple: every small detail makes the difference — and you can taste it. That philosophy says everything about this kitchen.

The sommelier deserves real credit. The wine selection is thoughtful and precise, with rare bottles that pair beautifully with the food — clearly curated with intention rather than trend.

The dining room is elegant and calm: large banquette seating, generous tables, beautiful glassware and cutlery, refined tableware, and an open kitchen that reinforces confidence and transparency.

FIZ holds a Michelin Green Star, and it shows — respect for produce, sourcing, and flavour integrity is unmistakable. At the same time, the experience delivers the refinement and polish of top-level fine dining. For me, it naturally sits between both worlds.

A restaurant that performs at this level in the chef’s absence is the sign of true leadership. An exceptional experience, and one I will return to without hesitation.

Thanks to all of the team, you guys rock!

Good dishes, but the overall experience fell short.

nice location and ambience but overall experience felt overpriced for what was delivered, especially at around SGD 230++ per person (plus SGD 88 for two glasses of wine pairing).

Service was friendly but below what I’d expect from a Michelin-star restaurant. Water refills were often missed, menu explanations only came when asked, and the pacing felt rushed. The welcome also felt quite technical rather than warm, and it was sometimes hard to get staff’s attention.

The biggest letdown was the ending — the bill was dropped without us asking and we were told the next seating was waiting. Spending about SGD 660 in total to be rushed out - this really took away from the experience.

Quick update from my last review. Went back for dinner recently for the 3.0 Sajian Warisan. It did not disappoint! And everything I said before remains. Here’s hoping 2026 will be a great year for the restaurant.

If you’re looking for a modern interpretation of Malay cuisine, I think this would be a delicious place to start. Yes, admittedly not cheap at $228 but if you want to give yourself a treat, or if you want to take someone to impress them with Nusantara cuisine, this place would be it.
The amount of labour that goes into the dishes is nothing short of amazing. And you don’t feel cheated because you really do get fed properly as the photos will testify.

I'm glad I visited Restaurant Ibid before they shut their doors near end March 2026. This is one of the best meals I have had since the start of 2026, and it reminded me of how good food could taste if you put effort and passion into it. The service by the team was great, and I really enjoyed the wine pairings, especially the tonkatsu with the red that they served.

The boss will be taking a 6 months break and Ibid will likely be reopening as a private dining. I will definitely make another reservation there when it opens.

This is a shout out that if you want to try this place, better do so ASAP as it is closing in March.
We all know that Chef Woo Wai Leong is a winner from the Masterchef and his skills as been improving leaps and bounds to his Michelin Guide title today. He has an eye for details and flavours and the food here is really good I must say.
One of the more decently priced fine dining experience here. The number of courses are pretty decent too and didn't left me hungry after the meal.
Felt very well taken care of by the staff here and pretty attentive. The dishes here are really good with interesting combination of flavours.
All the dishes were good but there were a few which stood out for me, especially the starters the Devilled Egg, the main was definitely the wagyu and the sweets the gula melaka ice cream.

We had such a wonderful dining experience at Restaurant Ibid. My parents and I truly enjoyed every part of the meal, from the beautifully crafted dishes to the warm and thoughtful service.

What made the evening especially memorable was the opportunity to have meaningful conversations with Chef, which made the experience feel so personal and genuine. The team also went the extra mile to celebrate my mum’s birthday, which meant so much to our family and made the night even more special.

Thank you for the heartfelt hospitality, beautiful food and unforgettable experience.❤️

first time come travel can try this restaurant，this palce is very nice and the food yummy😋😋

We did our Christmas Eve dinner this year at Ibid! What pleasant surprise and an experience! Unlike other restaurants, this was an interactive experience with the chef team, with the food and the stories behind it. Very impressed with the team work of the five of them. They communicate briefly, quietly and efficiently. Really enjoying watching them work together and delivering high quality dishes to diff groups of customers! Highly recommend for a relaxed and engaging dining experience.

I had done some research ahead of my trip to Singapore and came across Ibid. While I would have liked to echo the many positive reviews, the experience unfortunately didn’t quite impress me. Like some of the more critical reviews mention, the chef clearly has interesting ideas, but for us the flavors felt a bit off and occasionally strange in a way that didn’t really resonate.

I was dining with my girlfriend and we both agreed that nothing truly stood out during the meal. That said, the staff were genuinely warm and very friendly, which we appreciated. Perhaps we were unlucky with the menu that evening, but overall it didn’t feel memorable. Personally, I would save my money and explore other options in this incredible food destination.

My husband and I first came to Ibid in May 2019 the night we got married - we’re both vegetarian and loved the food. We still talk about some of the dishes.

We’ve since moved overseas but came back to Ibid for another meal Dec 2025 and it was equally as magical. Sander literally licked some of the plates - his favourite was the gula melaka ice cream, mine was the egg custard.

We both enjoy sitting at the seats with a view of the kitchen and getting to interact with the staff, it’s so cool to watch the plating of the food. Highly recommended meal, you won’t regret this one.
"Great location, easy to find."
You could tell the passion chef and his team had for their food. Amazing creations with just the right amount of local flair to it. A pity that they’re closing next year :”(
So impressed with the menu! Deviled egg and Soy egg custard were to die for 🤤 Great service.

We picked Restaurant IBID for a milestone birthday and couldn’t be happier with our decision. Everything about the experience was fantastic.
The food was sophisticated and delicately prepared. Every bite was delicious, and you could tell how much care went into each dish.
The atmosphere is intimate, which made for a really special evening. The service was fun and friendly, never stuffy or pretentious. The Chef took his time to explain the dishes, answer questions, and you could see how meticulous he is about his craft, produce and process. That personal interaction made the night memorable.
If you’re looking for outstanding food, genuine hospitality, and a place where the chef actually cares about your experience, Restaurant IBID is it!
Delicious duck!!!

I've known Chef Woo for many years and have been to Restaurant Ibid several times, bring my wife as well as close friends to celebrate birthdays. Each time, the food was amazing and the service was excellent. I highly recommend this restaurant and will continue to return and support in the future.
Like MPW, Chef Woo understands that dining out is first and foremost an experience and on that note they definitely deliver. The food doesn't disappoint either.

I’ve dined at Restaurant Ibid several times, and will continue to try their seasonal menus as long as they’re around. It’s one of my favourite restaurants in Singapore for obvious reasons - food is super delicious, service is great, unpretentious and very friendly chefs. 5 stars for everything!

I've been to Ibid multiple times and it's been a stellar experience each time. For our first date night since having a kid, we went back to Ibid and the warmth of the team and the well-executed dishes were a welcome respite from parenting duties.   This season's menu is another hit and we can't wait to see what's next. Don't forget the killer wine list too!

Showing support to our SMEs and down to scammers.

This review is from my visit in Nov 2021, celebrating my ex-gf (now wife) birthday. It was covid then and there were tight controls around the no.of pax and alc consumption after 10.30. Great food, and extremely hospitable team.

Such an experience and joy to dine here.  This is food with a heart and service with a soul.

Service: The service staff were very attentive, taking their time to explain each dish to us slowly and carefully, ensuring that our warm water are constantly refilled without us asking. What we found wonderful was how the service staff noticed that the drink we ordered was not to our liking as we didn’t finish it and offered to make a new drink for us to ensure we have a good time. We thoroughly enjoyed ourselves here and even received a hand written menu and note from the staff which gave the service just that little bit more personal touch.

Food: The food was unique, where true to the philosophy of the restaurant, puts seasonal vegetables at the centre of each piece. we we able to enjoy what the chef wanted to convey to us through the food. We especially enjoyed the pigeon and snow crab dish. Serving was prompt and we did not feel rushed, nor did we feel like we waited very long for each dish. Atmosphere: it was clean with nice background music that was not too loud. The chair seems to have some cushioning which makes pull and pushing the chair easy, with not much dragging sound.

Overall a very unique take to fine dining, serving seasonal dishes every time ensuring that each visit is unique and different. Will recommend.

Been here several times, experience and food are always excellent. Seasonal menu with a focus on vegetables. Local flavours and spices are subtly woven into the dishes and never ceases to amaze me how good it tastes.

While the evening didn’t start well with some poor communication, overall the service was a highlight — warm, attentive, and genuinely friendly without feeling formal or overbearing. The staff offered thoughtful recommendations and timed each course perfectly, which made the meal feel smooth and unhurried.

The food was beautifully presented and delicious. Flavors were balanced and refined, showing real care in both the ingredients and preparation without being overly complicated.

Overall, it’s a fine dining experience that feels welcoming rather than intimidating. Great food, excellent service, and a wonderful atmosphere came together for a memorable night, and it’s definitely a place I’d happily return to.

It’s a great choice for celebrating special moments or enjoying high-end European gastronomy.
Not the best service for a Michelin star. Food wise was also a hit and miss in my opinion. Certain dishes were good, some were just pretty mediocre.

On our first trip to Singapore, we discovered this restaurant through the Michelin Guide and decided to book a lunch.

You can truly feel that every dish is thoughtfully designed. The flavors are layered, and you can experience different nuances within a single plate. A standout highlight for us was the exceptional freshness of the fruits and vegetables—their flavors were pure and concentrated, which clearly reflects the chef's meticulous sourcing and refined culinary techniques.

The plating of each course was artistic and visually stunning, making it a joy to capture through photos and videos. I also particularly enjoyed discussing the details of the meal with my companion; it made the whole dining experience much more engaging.

The restaurant's atmosphere is bright and comfortable. The staff were friendly and polite—not only did they provide detailed explanations of each dish, but they also proactively asked for our feedback, which made us feel well-regarded. The pacing was spot on, and the portion sizes were just right for lunch.

A great dining experience requires everything to come together perfectly, and I am so glad we had such an enjoyable afternoon here. I look forward to trying a new menu on our next visit to Singapore.

Unique restaurant for unique moment. We came in Automne menu, as the menu changes at each season.
The cuisine is delicious, as a vegetarian, I felt truly considered through the whole food experience. Every vegetal ingredient is sublimed. You can (re)discover what season can mean in your plate and all the taste harmony that the Earth can offer. If you are a meat eater, you can definitely enjoy incredible plates with animal products, perfectly paired with amazing vegetables. As French, we want to give a special mention to the cheese tray. Felt like home, amazing quality.
Regarding the service, we deeply thank Jag team for making this dinner memorable.
We are eager to come again, to taste the Winter menu!

We chose JAG to celebrate our anniversary, and it was an experience we will remember with so much fondness.
From the moment we arrived, everything felt intentional, warm, and quietly elegant. The service was attentive without ever being intrusive, allowing us to truly relax into the evening and each other’s company.

The food was exquisite. The Sanchoku Wagyu Beef Tartare was beautifully balanced and refined, delicate yet deeply satisfying. The Pink GuavaFoie Gras was rich, silky, and indulgent in the most graceful way. And the highlight of the evening was the Pan-Seared Sanchoku Wagyu Striploin, simply sublime. Perfectly cooked, tender, and bursting with flavour, it felt like a celebration in every bite.

More than just a meal, the evening felt intimate, thoughtful, and lovingly crafted, the kind of dining experience that elevates a special occasion into something truly memorable. Thank you to the JAG team for creating such a beautiful space for us to celebrate love, connection, and time together.

We left with full hearts, grateful smiles, and the certainty that we will return again.

Me and my husband had a wonderful experience! A menu with attention to detail! From the first interaction, the attention and concern the costumer was outstanding! Strongly recommended!
A peixão thank to Lawrence Tan and M.Lin for the kindness, attention and dedication to us .🙏🏻

Had the pleasure of dining here to celebrate our wedding anniversary, back in Dec. The food taste was awesome, but felt that the presentation didn't have that wow factor.

Service was impeccable. Shout-out to the service staff and the attentive Mr YS, who was very professional and knowledgeable.

Overall value for money. Definitely thinking about going back to try out their winter menu early this year.

Also, probably the best bread I've ever had. Realised didn't take photo of it. Would go so far as to say, tastes better than the croissants in France.
Very disappointed with the vegan menu. The beans and courgette for the main were both undercooked, and the service was inattentive. Will not come back.

We had our 12-pax solemnisation and wedding lunch at JAG, and it honestly couldn’t have been better. Maryjoy and the team were amazing to work with—super friendly, flexible, and happy to accommodate all our requests, from curated menus and wines to blasting our own playlist and having the whole space to ourselves.

The restaurant is beautiful and filled with natural light; our photographer barely needed extra lighting and the photos turned out amazing. My only regret is that the day went by way too fast, because everyone was having such a good time!

Not every day you come across a Michelin-starred restaurant that strikes the perfect balance between being professional and proper, yet warm and genuinely personal and Restaurant JAG does this beautifully.

The concept itself is very unique, with a strong focus on vegetables (worth looking up their philosophy online), and it really sets JAG apart from the usual fine-dining experience. From the moment we stepped in until the time we left, we truly felt at home.

The team was friendly and attentive, with just the right amount of small talk; never awkward, never intrusive. The food was excellent; loved the salmon and the mignardises in particular.

A very sweet touch was the attention to small details. They offered us with a complimentary cake for our anniversary, which we really appreciated. The ambience was lovely too, especially with the view overlooking the Singapore River. Staff were always checking in to make sure everything was going well.

The final little brown little envelope surprise was something we didn’t expect and it shows how much passion the team had put in to ensure all the guest have a memorable experience.

Big thanks to Chef Lawrence, Maryjoy, and the rest of the team (sorry we didn’t manage to catch everyone’s names) for such a wonderful experience. Keep up the amazing work. We’ll definitely be back.

“A delightful vegetarian tasting menu with refined flavours, seasonal produce, and stunning presentation throughout.
My fav was chestnut,coffee,winter truffle as my main…Proof that vegetarian cuisine can be both soulful and sophisticated.”

平日ランチ利用。予約して行きましたが、満席ではなかったです。

シンガポールでは一つ星から三つ星まで行きましたが、どこも値段が見合うと思えず、足が遠のいてました。
気を取り直して、数年ぶりにシンガポールで星付きレストランに行ってみることに。

こじんまりとしてあたたかみのあるお店の雰囲気と、サービスは良かったです。

席についてすぐ、This is autumn と書かれたメニューに違和感。クリスマス目前ですよ。
秋の食材って9月10月、11月に入ると冬の食材も出てくるのに12月で秋とは、四季のないシンガポールの感覚なのか、よく分からず。

幸せな一年を祝っての食事だったので、シャンパン頼みました！グラスで55ドル。これにサービス代と税金が加算され、高額な一杯ですね。今年は日本に半年居たので日本の価格感覚が抜けておらず、この値段には驚かされました。でも美味しかったです。

お料理は、何で星がついているのか分かりませんでした。辛口でごめんなさい。

私はごく普通の日本の郊外出身ですが、その日にとれた野菜や果物を食べる機会がありました。決して特別なことではなく、日本では普通のこと。なので、なんでこの食材にこんなにお金を払うのかって思ってしまうのです。

また、人生で初めてcoravin でワイン注がれました。ワインが長持ちしてお店の方にとってコスト的にとても良いのでしょう。
でも注がれる時の音も、見た目も、注がれた後にグラスにワインが飛び散ってる感じも、全然美しくない。ワインを注がれる時のわくわくも無ければ、飲みたい気持ちも半減。悲しい。

食材の鮮度や温度、焼き加減、食感、香りなどなど、色々と気になってしまい、なのに高額なので、やはりシンガポールの星付きレストランには行くのやめようと心に決めました。
ヨーロッパや日本と、星の基準が全然違うと改めて感じた体験でした。

One of the best French restaurants with an organic, healthy concept. To be honest, its vegetable dishes are much better than the protein ones. We were surprised by the flavors and ingredients they use. The full set menu is light, fresh, and delightful in flavor. it is quite different from other French restaurants we've tried before. They incorporate luxurious ingredients in a low-key way, such as hidden abalone in a nut-based soup or finger lime in a radish and tuna salad.

The restaurant is run by a millennial generation team trained all over the world. They put more effort and time into the dishes and plating rather than interior design or branding. When I walked into the dining area, I found it quite understated. In contrast, the dishes are full of surprises, including the desserts. I thought it would be purely vegetable focused courses, but they actually include a variety of proteins. Somehow, their concept reminds me of life in Silicon Valley. the organic foods from Whole Foods and healthy preparation methods for longevity.

The restaurant relocated to Robertson Quay two years ago. Diners can enjoy river views from the window side seats. Unfortunately, the night I visited, it was raining and gloomy, so I couldn't see much outside.

At the end of the dinner, they gave me souvenirs, including a cash coupon for my next visit (and for referrals) plus perfumes made from that day's vegetables.

The service team was very patient, answering every single question from a curious person like me.

Had an amazing birthday celebration at Restaurant JAG. The food was outstanding, thoughtfully crafted and absolutely delicious. Special thanks to Maryjoy and Lawrence for the warm, attentive service that made the evening feel extra special. Great food and excellent service all around. Highly recommended.

We celebrated my fiancé’s birthday here last night, and it turned out to be one of the most memorable dinners we’ve had in Singapore. What truly sets this restaurant apart is its philosophy: vegetables take centre stage, and the proteins are designed to complement them, not the other way around. Every dish was beautiful and showcased how creative and flavourful vegetables can be.

Service was warm and attentive without being intrusive, and the atmosphere made it perfect for a quiet and intimate celebration. Special thanks to Mary-Joy, YS, Kai and of course Chef Laurence! Would definitely recommend.

Superb food introduction by Kai and all
Food was really delicious from start to end. Thanks for the recommendation and surprise for the birthday cake

Still as great and amazing as ever even though it was previously at Duxton Hill under Chef Jeremy. The restaurant is still focused on the use of seasonal and European regional vegetables, fruits and herbs. Well worth its Michelin star even under a young local team! Will return and hubby will host his corporate event here. The service is friendly and warm and staff are professional and knowledgeable. Grab the window seats for a good view of the Singapore riverside. The atmosphere is romantic as sun sets into the evening.

Thoughtful menu and impeccable service.

Kai and the front of house team were wonderfully attentive, confirming dietary requirements ahead of time. Every dish on the Autumn Light experience was brilliant and brought out the best in each ingredient. The chef’s personal check-ins were a lovely touch, would give 6 stars if I could.

We had a fantastic evening at Restaurant Jag. From the moment we booked, the team were incredibly attentive — reaching out in advance to tailor the menu for one of our guests’ dietary needs so she could enjoy the same style of dishes as the rest of us. We chose the Light Tasting Menu, which was beautifully balanced: inventive vegetable-forward courses, incredible flavours, and just the right amount of food.

The service was warm and attentive, and the staff’s passion really shone through. They even shared great recommendations for other restaurants to try during our trip. An intimate, elegant experience and easily one of the best meals we had in Singapore.
Food is good, service is amazing. Each dishes have their own story. Very unique!

Chef Han has successfully used local produce and provided  local hawker fare a Michelin star worthy makeover .

The Chili crab ice cream was off to great start, followed by the pork belly satay and other starters.  Only comment , felt the uni should not be grilled with the otah, Uni is meant to be consumed cold.

Restaurant Labyrinth offers a creative reinterpretation of Singaporean cuisine through a refined tasting menu. Dishes are nostalgic yet innovative, with playful presentation and strong local flavors. Service is attentive and knowledgeable, guiding diners through each course. It’s pricey, but ideal for those seeking a modern, thoughtful take on heritage food.

From the moment we stepped into Labyrinth, we were captivated by the warm, sophisticated atmosphere and attentive, friendly staff.

The food was exceptional. Every dish we tried was beautifully presented and bursting with flavour!

Restaurant Labyrinth is a creative fine dining restaurant at Esplanade Mall that reinterprets Singaporean cuisine with modern, avant-garde techniques. The menu features innovative seafood and meat dishes paired with carefully curated cocktails and wines. The ambiance is elegant and intimate, perfect for special occasions or culinary adventures. Service is attentive and knowledgeable, ensuring a memorable dining experience that highlights both local flavors and contemporary gastronomy.

Restaurant Labyrinth is a creative fine dining restaurant that reimagines Singaporean cuisine with modern techniques and artistic presentation. The tasting menu is innovative, showcasing local flavors in a unique and refined way. The ambiance is elegant and intimate, while service is attentive and knowledgeable, making it a memorable destination for contemporary Singaporean gastronomy.

When we first arrived slightly before our reservation time, instead of being offered a seat or even a welcome drink while we waited, as is common in many European restaurants, we were told to either stand around or take a walk around the rather underwhelming Esplanade and return later. It was not the most gracious start, especially for a Michelin-starred establishment.

With the second course that was served, a strand of hair came out with the dish. The response was limited to a brief apology and a replacement. There was no further effort to recover the situation or reassure us. From that point onward, the service noticeably declined. Explanations became minimal, the warmth faded, and the server appeared tired. Before we even asked for the bill, the card machine and check were brought over automatically, as if we were being subtly ushered out.

Although the menu includes a wide variety of dishes, the overall narrative feels unfocused. Several courses overlap in concept, and none were particularly surprising or outstanding. There was no defining moment that justified the price.

Considering the creative elements, the food quality might make sense at around $80–100 per person. At the actual price point, however, and given the level of hospitality, it is difficult to understand how this qualifies as a Michelin-level experience.

It is expensive. Once was enough. Had we known, we would not have chosen to dine here.

The presentation was creative and "witty," but the taste didn't live up to the visual hype. The flavors lacked the "wow" factor or emotional depth one expects at this price point. I found a hair in my second dish. The staff apologized and replaced it, but finding a hair in a fine dining meal is a serious oversight that ruined the mood.

The crab in the chili crab pie was not warm entirely. The middle was coldish, definitely not warm.

The bowl for the prawn mee was too deep and it was difficult to eat the noodles.

The humourous bespectacled  bald waiter/ manager's service was excellent.

Rice from the chicken rice could have been more fragant/ flavorful. Thought the sg chinese waitress who spoke fantastic mandarin was quite defensive when feedback (questions were asked and i answered truthfully to help them) was given about the food to another waiter.

Kaya toast and the artichoke dishes were fantastic.

Kudos to the filippino waiter who noticed a left-hander. This is the 2nd restaurant that I've visited tt noticed it.

I am glad that the owner decided to pay homage to Singaporean food and make it his main selling point since inception as sg food is fantastic. Unfortunately he'll have to put up with people comparing hawker food and his. Jia you. Hope he'll continue to prosper.

Paid about 550 for 2 pax with 1 drink each (and water).

Fantastic!  We were so very fortunate to be able to make it for lunch on January 18th. The staff was super in their communications with us beforehand. Love the unique versions of Singapore classics. Dinner menu was subpar, very poor fusion singaporean cuisine its embarrassing to have this with friends from other countries.

Restaurant Labyrinth delivered one of the most exceptional dining experiences I’ve had in Singapore. Every course was beautifully executed, showcasing creativity, precision, and a deep sense of Singaporean heritage. The flavours were familiar yet elevated in ways that surprised and delighted us throughout the meal.

The service was warm, attentive, and genuinely thoughtful. The team took the time to explain each dish in detail, adding so much meaning to the experience. You can truly feel the passion and dedication behind every element!
Labyrinth transforms local classics into unforgettable moments. Loved every dish, loved the people even more. This is a must-try if you enjoy being happily surprised.

Labyrinth continues to set the benchmark for what modern Singaporean cuisine can be. The food is en pointe — brilliantly reimagining local dishes and elevating them into 5-star creations without losing their soul. Just when you think something might be chilli crab, it arrives looking nothing like what you’d expect… and then proceeds to challenge your taste buds and your visual expectations in the best possible way. Every course is a conversation starter.

Service here is always outstanding. None of the stuffiness you get at many fine-dining establishments — the team is warm, attentive, genuinely passionate, and makes you feel completely at ease from start to finish.

A must-visit for anyone who loves Singapore flavours told through a world-class lens.

Really enjoyed my experience here! The dishes were unique and tasty and the staffs made us feel very welcomed!

Highly recommend if you are looking for something different.

It has been >5 years since I’ve been back at Labrinyth and I must say it was great to be back to have the taste of local flavours in the most unexpected ways! The “congee” and the “pink guava dessert” was my favourite dishes!

Dining at Labyrinth is nothing short of a revelation—a journey through Singapore’s culinary soul, reimagined with breathtaking creativity and emotional depth. Chef LG Han continues to prove why this Michelin-starred restaurant stands in a league of its own: each dish isn’t just beautifully crafted, but deeply personal, rooted in memory while boldly pushing boundaries.

The standout of the evening was Chef Han’s interpretation of Bak Kut Teh. It’s rare for a dish to feel both familiar and completely new, but this one did exactly that. The moment it arrived, it radiated warmth—comforting, aromatic, almost nostalgic. The first spoonful felt like a warm hug, capturing everything I love about the traditional dish while elevating it with finesse and clarity of flavour. It was soulful, refined, and unexpectedly moving.

Then came the kabu congee, which may very well be the best congee I’ve ever had. Silky, delicate, and impossibly layered, it struck that perfect balance between simplicity and sophistication. Every bite was soothing yet complex, showcasing Chef Han’s ability to transform humble ingredients into something transcendent.

Labyrinth isn’t just a restaurant—it’s a love letter to Singapore, told through dishes that surprise, comfort, and delight in equal measure. If you’re looking for a dining experience that lingers with you long after the last bite, this is the place.

Had a great meal here where dishes are extremely well executed, while maintaining that creativeness to it to keep the entire dining experience fun, surprising and most importantly delicious. Kudos to the service staff as well who were attentive but not intrusive.

Definitely worth many visits!

Restaurant Labyrinth is highlighting the Singaporean cuisine in a brand new way. Chef Han and his team creates the most stunning dishes when recreating the local street food and I have discovered so many new dishes here! Every dish has a story and it’s with great joy I was dining here. If you have tried Hawker food in Singapore you will recognize some of the dishes, except it’s the best version of every dish. (If you ask me) i really appreciate the love, and research behind every dish on the menu. I’m impressed, and it takes a lot to impress on me. Labyrinth is both Michelin starred and also one of Asia’s 50 Best restaurants, and I understand why.
As there is not so many tables, I would recommend you to book beforehand.

With all the fantastic places in Singapore to dine for dinner, Labyrinth, unfortunately, fall short of the mark, especially for being a Michelin star restaurant. From my experiences at dining at Michelin star establishments labyrinth was trying exceptionally hard to meet the status quo rather than to lean in to what made them special.

Had lunch with a client. Good was excellent as was the service. The corn and pomegranate started and the sakura chicken main were excellent. The chickpea with rice wasn't as outstanding though. Great service throughout but place was a little noisy. The lunch set was good value for money.

I went to Revolver Singapore for their vegetarian business lunch. The paneer dish was quite good, but unfortunately the rest of the items didn’t really stand out for me.

We were seated directly opposite the hot tandoor oven, which made the area quite uncomfortable as it was very warm. The service was also a bit disappointing — basic cutlery like a knife wasn’t provided initially and we had to ask for it.

The restaurant was also extremely loud, making it difficult to have a conversation during lunch. Overall, apart from the paneer, the experience didn’t live up to expectations and I personally didn’t enjoy the meal much. I found myself wanting to leave quite quickly.

The ambience is extremely small, dark, and claustrophobic, and it felt uncomfortably warm—almost like sitting in an oven. It was surprisingly crowded even on a weekday. On top of that, the food is very expensive and simply not worth the price in my opinion.

What a letdown - this place disappointed on every front. Most dishes tasted of stale oil, and the flavour lingered unpleasantly long after the meal. Service made things worse -  the main hostess was rude and unwelcoming. The seating setup is also baffling - right in front of open-fire tandoors, which on a hot afternoon turned lunch into a sweaty endurance test. Hours later, I still feel uncomfortable and unwell - not something you’d expect from any food establishment, let alone one that boasts of being a Michelin star.

Would absolutely not recommend.

Once again thanks to Khairil, we had an awesome evening! We will be visiting again for sure.
Very good food, modern fusion.
Good food and service. Slightly expensive compared to similar restauranta.

Dinner for four, very dark as we entered. Food was good except for tiny portions. Ordered to share to taste more. Sat at table opposite the two burning wood fires. Very hot and smoky and inefficient exhaust system which gave me a terrible splitting headache after 2.5 hours.
Slightly under seasoned overall. Liked the spices but more fusion than North Indian. Fine dining portions and plating.

An underwhelming experience at Revolver or perhaps I walked in with very high expectations.
We ordered the Fresh Delhi Paneer, Charred Chicken, Kulchette with Mysore Pulled Lamb and Butter Chicken and finished with the Revolver Sundae.
Let me share why it felt underwhelming.
The Delhi Paneer was essentially palak and paneer served separately. As an Indian who has dined at some of the finest restaurants in India and across the world, I found this dish rather average. It lacked the distinctiveness or elevation one would expect at this level.
The Charred Chicken, unfortunately, had a slightly old-stock flavour. I understand that these things can occasionally happen, but my palate is quite sensitive, especially when it comes to the freshness of ingredients and this note stood out.
The Kulchette with Mysore Pulled Lamb was the highlight for me. The masala leaned close to a Gowda-style preparation, and I genuinely enjoyed it more than anything else we had that afternoon.
The Revolver Sundae reminded me strongly of Daulat ki Chaat from Indian Accent. India offers such a vast and diverse dessert repertoire that there is immense scope for drawing inspiration beyond what felt familiar here.
We also encountered a hygiene concern during our visit, which I am choosing not to elaborate on publicly. However, for a Michelin-starred restaurant, consistency and impeccable standards are paramount, and one hopes those benchmarks are upheld at all times.
Perhaps it was a case of expectations versus experience, but I do believe there is potential to surprise and delight more.

If you’re looking for a place that delivers on the "special" in a Valentine’s special, keep walking. To name a few points.

- 20 minute gap for each dish to arrive (3 hrs for 7 courses?)
- Staff handing me our stuff and telling they're about to go home? (what do I do with that info)
- Arrived early but no decent seat options given (had to specifically request for this)
- Bill is handed over to the lady (Do you expect girls to pay during valentine's?)

While the restaurant clearly aimed for "modern," the execution felt more like a dated gimmick than true innovation.

The service fell well below expectations and the food was disappointing. The staff were unable to explain the dishes properly, and several items were excessively greasy, with an unpleasant taste of stale oil.
Additional charges were applied for the beef selection without any prior explanation, and multiple bottles of water were opened and charged without informing us.
Overall, the experience did not justify the price point and was very poor value for money.

I wanted to send it back but my husband is a very fast eater and he kind of started eating it before I could stop him.  lt must have been stored very cold I guess. But the chef didn't realise that ? We have visited Revolver many times but during our recent visit, it fell short of our expectations.

Firstly, the warm and friendly service was missing, apart from the very nice lady who remembered me from my last visit. Service was prompt but lacking the service touch.
Secondly, the food service was too slow. We had to chase the servers twice to check on our orders. And food standards have also fallen short. Our truffle kulchette was served at room temp, previously it was served nice and warm. The Lobster Manchurian was also smaller in serving size though price remained the same. Thankfully, the flavours for the Caviar Paratini, Grilled Hamachi collar and the Paneer with winter spinach were great so overall, the meal was still decent. They were also very thoughtful to provide a complimentary dessert for our birthday celebration.

We booked the 6.15pm seating and were seated at the long counter top, away from the direct flames so it was a good seat. It was nice to watch the chef busy at work with the wooden flames and tandoor. We selected the Signature course at $199.
For starters, we had the Revolver Trio which was served with and avocado smash, burrata tart and duck chettinad. I really enjoyed the burrata tart which exploded in my mouth and the crispiness of the tart blends in so well.

In my POV, the restaurant fell short of expectations, with overly intense spicing that overwhelmed rather than enhanced the dishes. The pulled duck and butter chicken were drowning in heavy sauces, masking any nuance in the proteins. While the cheese-filled kulchette offered a pleasant surprise on its own, it stood no chance when paired with the overpowering butter chicken.
The truffle mushroom was competent but unremarkable—exactly what you’d expect, nothing more. The dessert kulchette was similarly underwhelming. The kulfi gelato melted far too quickly to appreciate its pistachio fragrance, turning into a puddle before I could properly enjoy it.
Perhaps this style of modern Indian fine dining simply doesn’t align with my preferences. I was hoping for cleaner flavors that showcased quality ingredients and skilled grilling techniques, but instead found dishes weighed down by excessive spices and sauces.

The open kitchen concept, while visually appealing, ironically prevents meaningful chef-guest interaction at the counter seats. More concerning was the intense heat radiating from the charcoal grill—I felt uncomfortably warm throughout my entire meal. I would have appreciated being mentioned about this before being seated, or at least being asked if the heat was bothering me. I’d strongly advise against seating guests in that area.
The service team was friendly, approachable, and genuinely hospitable, but I was hoping for more menu pairing guidance to diners effectively.

What truly ruined the experience was the service. A middle‑aged Chinese male server was extremely disrespectful and made us feel like a burden.
For a dish that costs $20++ for 1 cube of paneer, I expect to be able to enjoy it properly — instead, he kept hovering over us and even touched my plate while insisting on clearing it before I was done. His attitude was unwelcoming, rude, and far from hospitable.
I was so put off by the experience that I walked out after the starters and continued my dinner elsewhere, where we were happily accepted even without a reservation.
Overall, a deeply disappointing experience. I would not return.

For our wedding anniversary we booked a waterfront window table, so we would make the most of the view over Marina Bay. The restaurant is located on the first floor of the Fullerton One building and I must admit we had a little difficulty locating the lift and the restaurant entrance.

The restaurant is small (seats about 24) and very intimate. The decor is fairly minimalist - white marble walls, red carpet and white leather seats (with floor to ceiling windows overlooking the water). The wine list is very extensive and well curated.  Sommelier, Warren Estrop, certainly knows his wines - I'm not a wine expert but I appreciated when they gave me a choice of red wine (different vintages) and asked which one I preferred - both we perfect but could tell which was the more exclusive.

We went with the Grand Opulence Tasting Menu, a 7-course degustation dinner, with a cheese supplement (I'm a sucker for good cheese).  Even though it is a tasting menu we still needed over three hours to get through it all.  It's hard to pick a highlight, as each individual dish was a unique culinary creation. From the very first dish, where Chef Stoobant delicately sliced Scottish salmon and quenelled french caviar on top. To discussing the habitats of marron, small freshwater crayfish. Then the simple delight of the Shizuoka King Crab, edamame, and green curry (brought back memories of our trip to Japan). The simplicity of the Japanese momotaro tomato, marinated in vanilla oil. The succulent Omi Beef with sand carrot and mala. I particularly enjoyed my discussion with Chef Stroobant about their selection of cheeses and the difference between cow, sheep and goat - though I noted his disappointment that they had consumed the Yak's curd, that one of their chefs had brought back from Mongolia. The fine marbling and velvety texture of the Ōmi beef. From there to our heavenly deserts, a rainbow of petits-fours, alongside yuzu-brown butter financiers.

You can sense the high level of perfection that Chef Stroobant is creating here but it is the knowledge and enthusiasm about the food and wine that lifts this restaurant to a Michelin star standard.

**What was excellent:**

The signature pig stomach chicken soup was a masterclass in patience, rich and deeply flavorful from hours of boiling. **What missed the mark:**
Unfortunately, several signature dishes fell short. The fried kway teo, while having great wok hei, left a bitter aftertaste (possibly from the vegetable stems). The oyster omelette was overly gooey from too much starch, lacking enough egg texture. The steamed fish, though fresh, was let down by a salty soy sauce.

五个人，加茶（猪婆参五位）加服务费加GST，总共490新币。看每道菜价钱都还是很合理的。等我周五去吃其他菜再来一篇

极爱生腌蟹，特别新鲜，上面一层全是蟹黄，吃得特别满足。在国内也经常买生腌蟹，但没有这么品质这么好的。希望回国之后能去潮汕地区试试看。鱼饭并不是带米饭的，是一整条鱼，只是早期渔民用这种鱼当饭吃，所以留下了这个名字。鱼皮很亮，一看就知道很新鲜，特别好吃，也没有什么刺。帝王鸡仪式感挺强，我开始以为是盐焗鸡，但其实是带汤的，配以很多蘑菇。味道还不错，这道菜真的需要四个人以上来吃才行。但不会是我top选择。

San Xiang Rou Cuo Mian (叁香肉脞面), also known as San Xiang Bak Chor Mee, is a well-known hawker stall in Singapore recognized for its rich and aromatic minced pork noodles. Located at ABC Brickworks Market & Food Centre, the stall has gained a strong following among locals who enjoy hearty and flavorful hawker dishes.

The name “San Xiang,” which means “three fragrances” in Chinese, reflects the stall’s focus on creating a dish that combines several layers of aroma and taste. A typical bowl features springy noodles tossed in a savory sauce made with chili, soy sauce, and aromatic oil. The noodles are topped with minced pork, slices of pork, pork liver, meatballs, braised mushrooms, and crispy pork lard. The combination of textures—from tender meat to crunchy lard—adds depth to the dish.

Unlike some traditional bak chor mee that rely heavily on black vinegar for tanginess, San Xiang’s version leans toward a sambal-based flavor profile, giving the noodles a spicy and slightly sweet taste. Customers can usually choose their preferred noodle type and spice level.

The stall’s popularity has led to recognition in the Michelin Guide under the “Michelin Selected” category, highlighting it as a recommended spot for quality hawker food in Singapore. San Xiang Bak Chor Mee represents the vibrant and diverse culinary culture of Singapore’s hawker scene. 🍜

If you're a fan of a traditional, vinegar-forward bowl, San Xiang is a good choice. The balance of the sauce is excellent, but the real standout is the generous amount of ingredients you get for the price.
The Highlights
The Pig Liver: Often the "make or break" for Bak Chor Mee, the liver here is cooked just right—tender and creamy without being tough or powdery.
The Surprises: It’s rare to find such variety in one bowl; having two fish balls alongside the minced meat and pork slices made for a very satisfying meal.
The Noodles: They hold the sauce well, ensuring every bite has that signature savory-tangy kick.

Seroja
A quick riser on the fine-dining circuit, Seroja has already collected a Michelin star and a young chef award, and it’s easy to see why. The kitchen showcases Malaysian archipelago cuisine with confidence and finesse, translating familiar regional flavors into a thoughtful, modern tasting menu. It’s polished without losing soul, and ambitious without feeling forced.

Five Takeaways
• The opening bites set the tone beautifully. The Tuna Ginger Kerabu and Octopus Sambal Kueh Pie impress, but it’s the Fish Floss with Raita that truly stands out—layered, unexpected, and deeply satisfying.
• Lobster Laksa is a quiet flex in luxury. The laksa leans more sauce than soup, not the richest version out there, but it forms an elegant base for a thick, perfectly chargrilled lobster.
• Duck Percik is expertly executed—charcoal-grilled duck with a beautiful meat-to-fat-to-skin ratio. The percik sauce brings heat and character, while crispy rice on the side adds welcome texture.
• Roti Paung with Johorean Butter is a nod to heritage done right. Soft, simple bread elevated by rich, salty butter that steals the show.
• The vibe and service are impeccable. Sleek, modern, and calm, with an open kitchen and bar seating that puts you right next to the action. Service is attentive, gracious, and effortlessly polished—always present, never intrusive.

The Damage (no drinks): S$550-680 for two

For over five decades, Shang Palace has set the benchmark for Cantonese fine dining in Singapore. As the sole dining concept to endure from Shangri-La’s inaugural Singapore hotel since 1971 (and the global flagship of the Shang Palace brand) it stands as a testament to heritage, precision and enduring relevance.

Now entering a new chapter under Executive Chinese Chef Daniel Cheung, the refreshed menu reflects a confident evolution rather than reinvention. Drawing on Chef Daniel’s four decades of experience, the cuisine honours tradition while embracing modern expression, elevated by contemporary presentation, refined storytelling and subtle tableside touches.

The Braised Boneless Duck with Eight Treasures is a centrepiece of heritage and technique. Crisped through deep-frying before slow braising, the duck is infused with a rich abalone-based broth, then crowned with an opulent arrangement of seafood and delicacies.

Equally compelling is the Double-boiled An Xin Chicken Broth with Fish Maw, Sea Conch and Honeydew. This patiently crafted soup is pure, nourishing and resonant with layered flavour after three hours of careful simmering.

Nods to nostalgia appear in dishes such as the Baked Assorted Diced Seafood, Sea Conch and Chicken in Cream Sauce, a refined reinterpretation of a beloved Hong Kong classic, while bold modernity shines through the Baked Iberico Pork Rib with Osmanthus Honey and Black Pepper Sauce, flambéed tableside for a final flourish of aroma and drama.

The refreshed menu also introduces a renewed dim sum repertoire, blending nostalgia with innovation. Highlights include Steamed Crystal Dumplings with Black Truffle, Traditional Deep-fried Hokkaido Scallop Dumplings served with Supreme Broth and the much-loved Steamed Chicken Roll with Ham, Black Mushroom and Fried Fish Maw, a classic that recalls early 20th-century Guangzhou tea houses.

Shi Le Yuan Kway Chap is a popular spot for traditional Teochew-style kway chap, known for its comforting flavours and well-braised ingredients. The stall serves a generous platter of braised items such as pork belly, pig intestines, tofu, tau pok, braised egg and preserved mustard greens, all simmered in a fragrant soy-based gravy. The sauce is rich and aromatic with a subtle herbal depth, coating each ingredient beautifully without being overly salty.

The pork belly is tender with a good balance of meat and fat, while the intestines are cleaned well and braised until soft and flavourful. Each item absorbs the savoury braising liquid, making every bite satisfying. The kway, which are broad rice sheets served in a light broth, are smooth and silky. The mild broth complements the richer braised platter, helping to balance the overall meal.

Portions are generous and prices remain reasonable, which explains the steady crowd during peak meal hours. Despite the simple presentation, the quality and consistency keep customers returning. For those craving a hearty and traditional kway chap in Singapore, Shi Le Yuan delivers a comforting bowl that highlights the beauty of this classic hawker dish.

Perched on the 35th floor of the Hilton Singapore Orchard Road, is the Shisen Hanten, a Michelin-starred restaurant that delivers not just exceptional Sichuan cuisine, but also a dining experience that feels refined from the moment you step out of the lift.
The restaurant has a classy, modern elegance - understated yet luxurious.   Service throughout the evening was excellent: the staff were attentive, polite and efficient without being intrusive, striking just the right balance for a fine-dining setting.

Almost every dish we ordered impressed, but a few truly stood out.  The Foie Gras Chawanmushi with Crab Roe Soup was one of the most memorable dishes of the night.  Rich, creamy and deeply flavourful, the foie gras was incorporated almost like delicate tofu pieces in the soup. It's not a combination you would immediately imagine, but it worked beautifully, giving the dish a luxurious depth.

The Szechuan-style Stir-fried Hokkaido
Mangalica Pork with Cabbage and Piman was also very well executed. The pork was a little too fatty for my personal preference, but there's no denying the technique - perfectly charred with excellent flavour and wok aroma.

The absolute must-order here is Chen's Mapo Tofu.
I've had my fair share of Sichuan food across China and Singapore, and this is easily one the best versions I've tasted. The balance of mala spice, silky tofu and savoury depth was simply outstanding.  After the bold flavours of the mapo tofu, the restaurant served a refreshing cold tea to cleanse the palate - a thoughtful blend of Yunnan Pu Er, Taiwanese oolong, Hangzhou chrysanthemum and rose petals. Light, aromatic and very soothing.

Another pleasant surprise was the Dang Gui Duck.
The duck skin was beautifully crisp while the meat remained tender and juicy. The dang gui sauce was an absolute flavour bomb, adding a fragrant herbal richness that elevated the dish beyond expectations.

Overall, Shisen Hanten delivers a refined yet deeply satisfying Sichuan dining experience. Between the elegant setting, polished service and some truly exceptional dishes, it's easy to see why it is a Michelin star restaurant.  Definitely a place worth returning to to try more dishes !!
