I had the pleasure of experiencing an unforgettable omakase dinner at Shoukouwa, and it absolutely lived up to its two Michelin stars. Every course was a masterclass in precision, balance, and depth of flavor.

The meal began with mozuku, a refreshing seaweed appetizer that gently awakened the palate. Kegani (hairy crab) followed, its delicate sweetness a true indulgence. Then came sakana no kunsei, a beautifully smoked fish that added a savory, aromatic layer to the experience.

From there, the sushi course unfolded like poetry. The kinki (rockfish) was tender and nuanced, kasugo (young sea bream) had an elegant sweetness, and both shimaaji (striped jack) and buri (yellowtail) showcased impeccable freshness and skillful slicing. The botan ebi (sweet shrimp) was succulent and creamy, while the toro maki was pure decadence. The star for me was the nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch)—buttery, rich, and deeply satisfying.

The warm misowan served near the end was comforting and umami-rich, a perfect palate cleanser before dessert. The meal closed with a delicate mizugashi. Simple, seasonal fruits, and thoughtfully restrained. A beautiful, gentle ending to a luxurious evening.

Shoukouwa’s intimate counter setting allows for personal interaction with the chefs, whose quiet mastery and hospitality make the experience even more special. The staff was warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding me through each dish with care.

This was not just a meal, it was a deeply immersive culinary journey. I’ll be thinking about it for a long time.

Very pricey, but you get what you pay for. The seafood is fresh and varies according to what was available that day, so the menu is always different, the (flavouring?) to the sushi is unique, eg yuzu used instead of the usual wasabi to enhance the taste of the fish. The waiter will explain what each of the seafood is before it is served. Bar seating only but its part of the authentic experience to see the chef's skills as he prepare the food in front of you and place the sushi in your hand directly. Worth every cent. Highly recommended

Very nice and cozy setting loved the last tuna hand roll and great service the staff was friendly. Price is expensive but was very worth it. Try to book before hand though. Also like the crab and soup the appetizer

Having been to both dinner and lunch, I have to say this is the best sushi in Singapore. Cannot think of anything negative to say about this place except maybe the price, but they are flying fresh ingredients from Japan couple times a week.
Excellent, even if pricey, Omakase. Service was pretty good.

Impeccable in all areas. Our go-to for top notch dining experience & food quality since we discover Shoukouwa few years back. The hard part is that there is no turning back as Chef Nishida & team's dedication to palates simply raises the bar & made us look past others.

Absolutely divine, the delicious sushi and imaginative appetitisers where worth the $1900 we paid for an excellent dinner. The taste profile and sake pairing that can only be compared with the best Sushi in Ginza on Corporate account.  Not experienced this level of cuisine in Singapore for sushi ever. Only in Japan. Strongly recommended for a special birthday or anniversary.

Really good quality ingredients. Sadly, his shari was so inconsistent. Some nigiris’ shari was too hot…. Staff handling the shari is not well trained and chef was also rushing to serve the nigiris out .
Can’t find somewhere better than shoukouwa. Returning whenever they change menu. Manager and chef are quite nice persons. I learned sake and Japanese food and cultures from them.

Das Shoukouwa ist eine Pilgerreise für Sushi-Puristen. Vom ersten Bissen an ist jedes Gericht ein Meisterwerk der Edomae-Tradition. Der Chefkoch, ein echter Handwerker, kreiert Omakase-Menüs mit Fisch, der täglich per Luftfracht vom japanischen Toyosu-Markt geliefert wird, während die Sake-Paarungen das Erlebnis zur Poesie erheben. Das ist pure kulinarische Alchemie.

Best sushi place in Singapore imo. Each sushi was sliced perfectly and had amazing melt-in-your-mouth feeling.

Front of the house gave very clear explanation of how each fish is sliced, marinated, seared, etc.

However, since I went for 6pm service, the pacing felt a little fast since they had to clear the table for the second seating.

I must Say Excellent food - Sadly the "newbie " server told us our option was not available for lunch and couldn't even provide a menu e and when we questioned the manager, he arranged the menu we wanted. It seems the waiter wanted to "upsell" us - what was surprising the 2 gentlemen across had the same menu as us.

the manager was a nice guy but strangely they billed us incorrectly with the higher priced menu! which  i had to get corrected.

Very unbecoming of Michelin star restaurant .Pity i liked the food
but this style of business/service is unacceptable

this spot is hands down one of THE GOAT of omakase in sg. been gg for close to 3.5 years and be it lunch or dinner, it always delivers🕺

ingredients are super fresh and its totally worth the price you’re paying for! to my fellow small eaters: the lunch KAI set ($260++) is literally perfect. its q filling and trust me you wont be leaving hungry de😆

A supremely special evening.  The dining experience is remarkable without trying too hard.  The curation of courses worked so well and unique dishes were punctuated by traditional flavors highlighted by surprising twists.   The setting is incredibly peaceful from start to finish.

Outstanding experience from start to finish!
The staff at Shunsui was extremely attentive and entertaining throughout our meal. They checked in on us several times and even took note of our special requests, which really elevated the dining experience.

The food quality was exceptional, and the atmosphere made for a memorable evening. Everything came together perfectly – from the service to the ambiance to what was on our plates.
Highly recommend Shunsui for anyone looking for great Japanese cuisine with top-notch hospitality. We’ll definitely be back!
디너 이용했습니다.오마카세 코스 중 다른식당과 차이점,특이한 점은 코스 시작부터 이나니와 냉우동이 나오는데 맛있었습니다. 한국에는 거의 없는 킨키도 보이고,와이프는 다른코스라 킨메다이가 나왔습니다.무난했습니다. 코스 후반에 이꾸라 원하는 만큼 주는데 맛있습니다. 전반적으로 퍼포먼스도 괜찮고, 식사도 맛있습니다. 단점은 주변이 너무 시끄러웠습니다.

Truly outstanding!
Great experience - excellent service, delicious food and outstanding, beautiful food presentation.

It was a casual dinner during a working day and my time at Shunsui was a lovely one.
Each dish was served freshly to us and everyone is seated at the bar counter. Presentation of the food was on point and the price was affordable as well.
The only downside is that I was seated next to a group of chatty ladies and it really disrupted my inner peace having a dinner. It was tough having chats with my partner because the noise was simply another level.I felt like the waitress could have evenly spaced us out so there will be more privacy for each customer group.
One of the dish was never ending flowing ikura mini rice bowl and that was fun HAHA. The chefs were all enthusiastic.
I would definitely head back to Shunsui again at a non peak hour.
Surprised my husband for his birthday and he loved it here! Food is  of course great, but the entertainment brings it to next level.

So far, this has been the most enjoyable meal I’ve had. Both the service and the dishes were outstanding. The atmosphere truly made us feel like we were in Japan, especially with the staff speaking Japanese. The 8 course menu was fun, interesting, and full of surprises. I especially loved the part where we could decide how much ikura we wanted, which was definitely the highlight of the meal.

The chef explained every item clearly and with so much passion. You can really see his charisma and dedication, which added a lot of character to the food. Everything was fresh, and the rice was perfectly done. The service from the lady in kimono and the gentleman in the black shirt was excellent as they were very attentive and accommodating to all my sudden requests.

One small suggestion would be to have better ventilation when there is smoke, as a bit more airflow would make the experience even more comfortable.

Overall, I genuinely enjoyed this meal the most and it left a long lasting impression. Kudos to the team !! ✨💕

Lovely 10 course omakase, FUGA.

It was on promotion, so $149++ per pax instead of $179++.

For $20 more (comparing to the Kacho 8-course), you get wagyu & urchi.

We went for Sunday dinner, there were only us and 1 other group throughout the whole evening, so it was almost like our own private room and chef.

Reservation is required as you would have to inform on your menu choice beforehand.

counter seats only, noisy  and the staff like to put on a show, food is ok but not impressive and I'm not a fan of staff having too much interaction with guests while drinking with them
and it's time restaurants start to talk about the provenance of their ingredients

Went for the lunch set meal and was surprised, albeit pleasantly, to be one of only two couples in the establishment. That made for a very intimate experience. The food was very rich and tasty, whilst watching the chef work his magic was an experience all on its own.
Highly recommend if you like sushi and fine dining experiences.

We used to frequently patronise their city gate branch but sadly it was closed. We went to the Hong Kong street branch and always love their good quality omakase dishes and great service and warm hospitality.

Pricing is reasonable and serving pace is on point.

Fantastic omakase experience. Every course is delicious, the presentation is beautiful, the chefs make it great to watch and the value is the best I've had in Singapore for this exceptional quality of food. This place will be on my list to visit whenever I'm in Singapore.
The omakase lunch menu was excellent, and I thoroughly enjoyed each dish.

The place was comfortable with warm lighting. The food was amazing. The sashimi was one of the freshest I've ever had in Singapore. I've tried their sake and it was so easy to drink. The chef was very patient in explaining every dishes and how best to eat them.

The only downside was that there was a group of customers celebrating birthday and it became too noisy after awhile. What supposed to be a quiet enjoyment of food became pasar malam.

Good service

Very fresh ingredients

But at the price point, a bit lacking in soul. A bit meh

Good effort

Second visit to Shunsui for omakase and always enjoyed the food quality, chef’s hospitality, innovation and service level. We chose the Kacho course which is $129++ per pax and of cos a good bottle of sake for pairing. Highly recommend if you are looking for good and value for $ omakase!

Jason and his team were great, food is excellent, service was thoughtful and it’s clear the team love working with each other.

Was there with wife for our anniversary, will definitely be back.

Came in for my birthday and it was a fantastic experience of Omakase. Staff was very professional from the start to finish. Restaurant is very clean and tidy, great atmosphere and vibe. Music choice is also very pleasant. At every point of our experience, we were always greeted with a smile and authentic Japanese etiquette. 5 star service and experience overall, would return again.

Jason the lead chef and his staff truly made this an experience to remember.
Food was amazing for the price, but the service was what was truly worth visiting for. The chefs are so passionate and friendly that the entire room was always filled with laughter
Amazing omakase experience, fuga was excellent value at SGD179+++
Great food and service 👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻
Out of surprise,it will become one of my favourite omakase places to go . They delivery the fresh food and good services.Must try

Had a great time at Shunsui Japanese Fine Dining. The vibe is relaxed yet refined — perfect for a treat-yourself evening or a special occasion. The food was both fun and delicious. I especially loved the abalone, which was tender and full of flavour, and the homemade dessert - crispy mochi red bean roll, which was delicate and thoughtfully crafted. The non-stop serving of fish roe added a playful and indulgent touch to the meal. The freshly churned ice cream made on-site was another highlight - simple, creamy, and memorable.

Service was warm and attentive from start to finish. The staff were friendly and made us feel genuinely welcome throughout the evening. As with many omakase places in Japan, the chef personally walked us to the door to say goodbye - a thoughtful gesture that adds a personal note to the experience.

Highly recommend for anyone looking for a quality Japanese dining experience with a bit of flair. Looking forward to my next visit.
amazing food and the chef was nice enough to make replacements for me as I'm allergic to shellfish. they explained all the dishes well and made it a fun and interactive experience!

Amazing Omakase Experience!

Had an incredible dining experience at Kappo Shunsui . Every dish was fresh, beautifully presented, and packed with flavor. The chef’s skill and attention to detail were outstanding. Service was friendly and attentive, making the whole meal even more enjoyable. Definitely a must-visit for Omakase!
A special thank you for preparing a lovely birthday dessert for my husband—it made the night even more special.
Wonderful meal; beautifully presented dishes and of such high quality.
Had a really amazing meal! Thanks for the wonderful food and service!

Used to eat there.. went bk today for lunch but the food so so only.. ordered the sweet n sour pork for $33 😕.. the pork is so dry n hard..cannot even bite.. with this price.. I can go many other restaurants to eat.. also ordered a plain vegetables without any pork for $15.. that's not cheap also.. the rest of the dishes very normal.. won't go bk again..

Food standard dropped so much especially the Sambal kangkong, it’s oily, tasteless and overcooked. Sweet sour pork is very hard and fried with rancid oil that had been re used many times. Very disappointed.
Yummy heartwarming food..it feels like home everytime i eat there! It's so hard to find a place like this in Singapore nowadays.
Avoid, super long wait, take incorrect order not apologetic, taste just average
I hate this place so much. Food is terrible. I would rather eat trash. 0 choices. DO NOT come to this place.

Queue for 1 hour and was finally our turn. We were told that out of 13 dishes only 3 main dishes is available. Service didn’t update us on the dishes left and what was sold out. Restaurant open at 5.45pm and was told when it was our turn at 7pm only 3 dishes left?! SERVICE WAS HORRIBLE.

Must try👍🏼

Been eating here for many years, food is still excellent. Tofu prawns, beef kailan, steamed song fish head etc. Small menu of evergreen favourites.

First time patronise this homely eating house, the lady boss and staff were friendly. The menu is simple and the dishes we ordered were well executed and served piping hot. We had black chicken soup, sweet and sour pork, steamed pork salted fish and stir-fried kailan. All dishes shone but the star dish would be black chicken herbal soup. Very hearty and black chicken was tender. Sweet and sour pork was meaty and ratio of batter to meat was just right. Definitely so much better than most zi char stalls we had. Stir-fried kailan was beyond my expectations because this type of vegetable is usually bitter but this restaurant did justice to the vegetables. Very crisp and wasn't bitter at all. The steamed pork salted fish was cooked to perfection and not overly salty. We will definitely go back to try other dishes! Kudos!

千万别来吃！😡😡😡
AVOID THIS RESTAURANT AT ALL COSTS. The food is ridiculously salty, and you'll wait at least half an hour for your meal. The entire place is filled with elderly customers, and it's CASH ONLY! Don't be fooled by the Michelin stickers on the door—it's all a marketing gimmick. The fish had a disgusting, muddy taste, like eating dirt, and the fishy smell was overwhelming. I hope no one else has to suffer through this!

Been wanting to visit this place for some time and a friend from overseas visited and we decided to head to the place.
There is no reservations just walk in, had to call and check and was told most likely would not have to queue but there is an hour dining limit.
Visited on the day the restaurant was partially filled we were able to get a table immediately.  Ordered a few dishes and have to say the wait for the first dish was a little longer than expected. The table next to us came later but got their dish first, and we realized they seem to cook in batches so generally the same dish would come out serving a few tables at one go.
Ordered 5 dishes. Would say we enjoyed the food. Everything was good, but if I have to say the weakest among the 5 dishes probably had to be the ginger chicken. There wasn't any ginger taste, but there was a surprise when we saw cubes in the dish which we thought was potatoes and it turned out to be the ginger! It was quite soft and the taste was quite mild hence the reason why there wasn't much ginger flavor.
Of course for me the star was the sweet and sour pork and the tofu prawn. Even the foreigner commented the dishes had the wokhei and it was good. Our foreign friend loves the beef on the kailan the most as the beef was so juicy and tender.
We ate slightly more than an hour and no one chased us away. I believe though its a "rule" they have leeway if the dishes take longer to be served or we still have food on the table.
Now to the issue of cash payment only. It caught us by surprise as well we only saw it on a note on the wall.
However the auntie mentioned it was their tradition and there is totally no issue with it because there are a few ATM machines just a minute walk away. Very pleasant and nice lady had some small talk with us.
Pretty good food, one of the places with good wokhei and definitely need to bring a group to try out more dishes.

This place has gone downhill over the years — prices have shot up while portions have shrunk and quality has tanked. It’s honestly ridiculous what they’re charging for what you get. To make things worse, they still only accept cash — no PayNow, PayLah, or any form of digital payment in this day and age. For the kind of money they’re asking, you’d be far better off eating literally anywhere else nearby. You’ll get a much better meal, bigger portions, and way more value for your money.

Update:

I’m quite shocked at the owner’s AI generated response for this review.

Downgrading to 1 star experience because:

1. The owner listed the exact time periods my friend and I were in the restaurant. It’s quite petty. What does that have to do with any of the feedback I provided? The restaurant was hardly full when we were there.

2. The owner completely misses the point with the cash payment feedback. It’s not about whether this is a legal requirement under the law. They can set the rules, but to disregard customer feedback in this defensive manner is a clear sign they don’t really care.

3. And yes, as the owner pointed out we also did order one bottle of mineral water. That is totally the item that justifies the $76 price tag. 😂

The portions are tiny and it’s not worth the price. At this price point, they shouldn’t be taking cash only. I was a bit disappointed. It was 76 sgd for a 2 person lunch….

Waited 40 minutes for the first dish to come, and this is only served after reminders. 🤷🏻‍♂️

Two nearby tables who came later than us, ordered later than us, have their food served and almost done, yet our food order seems forgotten and ignored. Our food order are similar to the other later diners. 🤷🏻‍♂️🤷🏻‍♂️

No apologies, no explanation, nothing but just hand gesture to ask to wait. 🤷🏻‍♂️🤷🏻‍♂️🤷🏻‍♂️

While it is normal/service to remove cleared plate(s), the service crew come and take a plate with unfinished food, while muttering apologies. Unclear and unsure if the sorry is for the tardiness or taking the plate away 🤷🏻‍♂️🤷🏻‍♂️🤷🏻‍♂️🤷🏻‍♂️🤷🏻‍♂️
Very delicious Cantonese meal in the heart of Geylang!

The food is okay but they are way too expensive. Even 5 star hotel restaurants don’t charge so much.

If u eat the same thing in other sze cha stalls, easily 50% cheaper.

Not value for money imo.

Please improve your pricing

It's time Michelin review their food from 2018 to 2025, the standards is not even close.
The taste of the food is only average and salty but the service is extremely terrible.
After ordering and waiting for 40min, we saw other tables that came later than us by 10min and 20min and ordered the same food as us getting the dishes but our table remains empty. The excuses the supervisor gave was the dishes are cooked in sizes and ours is coming up soon as these are M size and ours is S size.
After another 20min, we see other tables that came 30min later than us getting the same dish we ordered (S size) and it is still not for us.
Even the table (can tell is friends with the supervisor) beside us topped up the same dish as us gotten their top up dish.
Subsequent excuse from supervisor is that the staff are new.
The service is extremely bad and they are just riding on their "fame". To ones own risk to go
Typical good old Singaporean Chinese Home Cooked Foods.

Limited food choices on the menu, was made to order first at the entrance before we could sit at the allocated table. Water cress soup was bland, steamed fish was rather fresh but came with a river taste, beancurd was overly salty, sambal kang kong didn't had any sambal taste. The only saving grace was the sweet and sour pork, but it was served the last when we had already finished the rest of the dishes and rice.  We were hurriedly called to foot our bill once we finished our food cos was told there was a queue outside the restaurant?!? Too pricey and overall it was a disappointed experience and will not return.
6 prawns for $90. Here I thought Pokemon cards are expensive.
The foods were great and the owners were very kind and helpful both on tourists and locals. They deserve the michelin star not only for the foods but also on their great service and gesture.

overpriced for the quality, quantity, and overall experience here. standard has dropped drastically over the years, and pricing of food is quite ridiculous for the smaller portion sizes and quality. only cash, no paynow, paylah, or any form of qr or digital payments. for their pricing, there are other places nearby that offer better value for money.

you're better off going to any other restaurant near this for a better meal at a much lower price and you will probably get better bang for your buck.

My hubby was recommended by my foodie friend to try their sweet and sour pork and told me to do takeaway for him but he did not know they have a limited menu. Was msging my husband what he wanted for his takeaway but was kept being pushed away to go somewhere else since I asked if they have fried rice. I told her I needed to wait for response but she kept making rude comments and even made judgement on me that the person ordering is my son. Not coming back again. Had to park faraway to hobble to this shop with my swollen knee and get this kind of attitude. Rubbish.

Fixed menu with their speciality dishes. Having tried most of the items, my all time fav is the steam pork patty with salted fish. Price is on the more expensive side, and they only accept cash. Food is superb but some dishes are quite “heavy” so need to eat with rice if not will be too salty.

The place is so noisy that we cannot hear each other at the same table. Very pricey in my opinion without gst. Not sure what the per pax charge is for, 2 dollars each pax even if we didn't use the napkin or drink the tea. Menu is very limited, and prices not shown.  $33 for sweet and sour pork. Have not fully finished our meal and was told the group was waiting for our table. Not a good experience. Won't be back.
A bit expensive
Really well prepared dishes. Fresh and delicious! Gives a home cooked feel.

The food quality was not bad, and there was no waiting time, which was a plus. Service was generally okay — nothing exceptional but decent. However, I was quite surprised to find there were no prices listed on the menu. This made it hard to gauge what to expect, and unfortunately, the final bill felt overpriced. For example, 6 pieces of prawn cost $90, which seemed excessive. A bit more transparency on pricing would go a long way in improving the overall dining experience.
Attracted due to michelin star awards. No service charge and no GST. Cash payment only. They charged $2/pax without informing ahead.

肉質鮮美

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh

The pork ribs are very tender. The soup is flavourful.

Didn't encounter the bad service in the reviews. The service was ok during the lunch hour on Sunday.

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews:
had the non herbal version
not bad...taste is not too overwhelming

had the beansprouts and liver/kidney soup as well

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews: One of the best Bak Koot Teh in Singapore with black soup. The pork ribs are so fresh that it just simply felt off the bone. The soup was superb with the mee suan together with the fried fritter. Will be back to try other dishes

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews: Michelin? Must be a joke. Just a salty black soup.

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews: Soup was excellent with slight herbal taste.  Other cooked food ordered was very nice too.

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews: BKT is good and consistent, not sure about the other dishes. Soup is refillable.

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews: This is the first place I ever had Bah Kut Teh and it used to be one of my favorites. However, this last trip left me wanting. The soup was less flavorful, the dishes were par for the course, and the service just alright. I don't think I will go back considering the many other options that are available.

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews:
This is in my opinion superior quality fall off the bone tender bak kut in dark herbal broth. I enjoy this near-Klang variety as much as I enjoy those good white peppery kind. We ordered a small regular and a small special with mixed liver, button mushrooms and veggies. Their turnip egg and preserved veggie was also not too salty. Perfect to go with rice.  Super shiok.

Tried prawn vermicelli (tang hoon) and pigs trotter another day. Love their premium chunky meaty big prawns and there’s four in the pot. Shiok.

The Clay Pot Noodles is not bad on its own but I’d skip the “Special Bak Kut Teh” as the broth is too herbal for my liking. In future I will stick to the normal Bak Kut Teh and just order white rice.

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews: Food is good, especially the soup, and service, atmosphere is normal

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews:
It has a bib gourmand and an awesome reputation.  Here’s our rating
5* for the herbal soup and the sauce on the pork liver/kidney
5* Kai Lan - just cooked well balanced flavour- the chef can cook
3* pork ribs pre-cooked and I liver cooked when served in very hot claypot
2* liver and kidney kidney sliced very thin (delicious if eaten immediately)  was overcooked rubbery in claypot. The liver was far too thick to be served with kidney ended up raw or terribly overcooked and graining by being in claypot

Why a 1% service charge. Enough to piss people off insufficient to

The chef can cook but fails to understand impact of claypot on his dishes

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews:
I’ve dined at this restaurant several times and have always had decent experiences, but my recent visit was disappointing. It was my first time trying to place a takeaway order, and I was told to join the dine-in queue. I went inside to clarify with a staff member (the bald male server) that I only wanted a takeaway, but he redirected me back to the dine-in queue again. His tone was quite harsh, even though I had been polite throughout, and he mentioned that he “knew” I wanted takeaway but still continued serving dine-in customers who were waiting for seats.

I’m not sure if this is the correct process for takeaway orders, but the interaction felt unnecessarily rude and left a bad impression. It ruined my mood and I decided to leave without ordering. I rarely leave negative reviews, but I hope this feedback helps improve the experience for future customers.

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews:
Was there on a Saturday after 1.30pm and was able to get in immediately. No Q but not alot of tables inside and many were occupied.

Ordered the signature bkt and the one w intestines, pig Trotter, salted veg and 2 yam rice.

Signature BKT has some peppery taste but the intestines one one was surprisingly diluted (although u can request to add soup later). Pig Trotter taste was ok but not as tender as I hope.

Overall it's ok, but not so good that I would purposely come back again.

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews: I ordered the Bak Kut Teh. It was good, but not perfect; the herbal flavor was a little too weak. I also feel like it was missing something, but overall, it was fine.

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews:
We ordered one small claypot bkt..
We don't like it..
We ordered hot kopi... what we were served with was lukewarm kopi.. errrrr
The BKT quite tasteless.. Ya the pork ribs are big..

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews: Disappointed with the taste and overall food quality. The Bak Kut Teh tasted no different from an instant ready-made packet, one vegetable dish was undercooked while the other was over-fried, and the remaining two dishes were only of average standard. Unfortunately, I won’t be returning.

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews:
Pretty good herbal bak kut teh that is also very wallet friendly. 10 bucks will net you 4?! ribs.
The soup is decent, herbalicious, constant tingling at the back of your throat. Not sure if its MSG or just the herbs. The broth initally has the taste of coriander, similar to turtle soup. The ribs, tender  flavourful. The giam chye, tangy, soft, very good.
The youtiao however, have the oil taste and was not meaty enough to soak up the broth. The refill lacks the coriander taste, but otherwise did not taste watered down.
I think is pretty decent spot and would come back to try the pepper version.

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Reviews:
Claypot pork rib BKT.

Apparently it’s Michelin Bib Gourmand and I can see why - affordable big portion and yummy.

Must have it with the fluffy yam rice!

7.5/10

The food tasted just ok, but not valuable for the quality and portion size. Small portions and bad service, also rushing everything right from the beginning.
They asked us to order dessert before dinner, charge for each tissue, pushing us to order food. Not a great dinning experience unfortunately and disappointed 😞
Good local seafood place open till 3am! Old establishment over 45years in business. Delicious seafood!
Very mediocre chilli crab. Not authentic SG style.
喜欢它们的螃蟹粗米粉，虽然螃蟹也好吃但米粉和汤更是一绝！每次去必点！！！带朋友过去都赞不绝口：）以前是因为追星过去现在是自己很馋这口
Food was a little underwhelming but had a great time here for my friend’s farewell

Singapore Famous Rojak is rightfully recognized for mastering the art of this quintessential local fruit and vegetable salad. In my opinion, I feel this to be a disadvantage. Yet, its the strength of their food that easily pushes this worry away.

Porridge - was piping hot and had a nice fragrance to it. Nice salty taste and loved the touch of long spring onions dashed on - spring onion is a key ingredient they use smartly for elevating their dish.

Chicken - Wow. A mix of both breast meat and thigh meat, portion was decent. Dipped in the delicious sauce, albeit a little salty; the chicken texture and taste was spot on. Silky gelatinous skin was top notch.

Chilli - A sourish bite of spice which worked very well, loved how it complemented the chicken especially the breast meat.

Towards the end, I poured the remaining sauce into the porridge for an even greater kick. Overall, this is a great Chicken shop. Their only carbs serving of porridge further proves the high standard for their protein. While I was not particularly craving porridge that day, the grainy wet porridge mixed wuth the smoothness of the chicken provided a highly interesting eating experience: Essence of a great Chicken rice but providing novel textures.

They made chicken porridge so sexy and palatable!

Silky smooth tender and flavourful chicken. More than worth for the Bib Gourmand. The tangy chilli goes well dripping the chicken.

Even the porridge (with sesame oil and white pepper) itself is not any other plain porridge but infused with the chicken broth, exactly how it should be.

Oh yes. Please order the abalone salad 捞生 to go with it.
-Half spoonful of the porridge with a bit of the salad 捞生 and add a piece of chicken after it. What a spoon. How satisfying. Full of flavour.

Ordered the half chicken set with the small abalone salad.

The only downside side is that there are some tiny bit of bones. Just be careful when eating it will do. Hawker atmosphere so 4 star for it.

Poached chicken with porridge ($4.50) - Good except for the bones.

From an earlier visit:
1 person chicken breast set ($4.50 + $0.50 for egg in porridge) - The chicken was tender, had bulk, was meaty, and was a large portion. The porridge with egg was fine.

Amazing chicken and porridge to die for!!

Must try must eat must come!

好喜欢这家米其林推荐的意大利餐厅啊！环境温馨服务好，很多老顾客会变吃边跟主厨聊天，点的每一道菜都超满意，和牛、鹅肝、意面、闭眼点就是了。建议预约，工作日中午去的都坐满了，他家生意好一点不奇怪！

Service was great. Food was served aesthetically pleasing but tasted really empty and bland. Surpringly quite dissapointing for the price I paid. Focaccia dish with the gorgonzola tasted really funny and immediately after eating it, my stomach felt greasy and unwell. This continued past 24 hours. nice place, quality food and very good service. I love the foie gras and the pasta.

服務很棒、團隊很棒，沒了。

點三分熟和牛，實際上大概七分熟。

說是和牛，但瘦到不行，完全沒有肉汁，吃起來像是巴拉圭草飼牛，牛肉乾一樣的口感。醬很死鹹，又稀，跟牛排搭不起來。鵝肝可以。

外場女性跑來問晚餐怎樣，跟他說肉超級乾，他說了這是澳洲和牛，跟日本和牛不同，然後就飄走了。沒了，那幹嘛問？你只想聽好聽的結果嗎？沒有對這塊熟到不行、瘦到不行的三分熟和牛有任何改善意見。

外場胖胖的先生很友善，也很認真推薦，今天在餐廳唯一的亮點。謝謝你補救了今晚。

—

義大利麵的話，不難吃，但這趟新加坡之旅吃了Fico跟Gotti都更好吃，不太能理解米其林推薦是根據哪道菜色來評鑒的。

—

提拉米蘇，馬司卡彭的風味做的非常好，但下面的蛋糕體，失敗，與其要用意義不明的巧克力還咖啡深色蛋糕體搞成搭不起來的風味，不如好好用手指餅乾。

—

佛卡夏不錯，兩個人吃份量微多，但就真的停留在還不錯，亮點是松露醬跟佛卡夏的搭配，選擇不太鹹的火腿跟Burrata搭配，都蠻不錯的。

—

路過有位子可以吃，價格說貴真的也還好（以米其林推薦來說），但餐的水準真的不太行，吃過亞洲很多這等級的義大利餐廳，今天點的餐都沒有到平均水平。

The food was outstanding, the service warm and attentive, and the overall vibes made it perfect for a group celebration. Our favourite dishes were definitely the uni pasta and the Florentine steak. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, and the service made us feel truly welcome. We will definitely be coming back and highly recommend this place to anyone who loves authentic Italian cuisine!

I loveee the food. It has always been on my list of food to try and after 2 yrs I finally came to try on my bday.

We got the off menu special (focaccia with truffle and parma ham), prawn pasta and the meat sharing plate.

Somma has totally a different vibe - fine dining but make it chill. There are so many little thoughtful touches that set it apart from the usual Singapore fine dining scene.
Okay, gotta be real- when the entire team came out to greet us, I was like 😳 lowkey shy. But once they started chatting with us, the mood shifted. It felt warm, easy, and, like we could just be ourselves-like we were hanging out at a friend’s place, not some fancy restaurant.
The food? Not trying too hard, not confusing- just beautiful in its simplicity. The dishes look simple, sure, but you can tell there’s a lot of heart (and brainpower) behind each one. And the taste? Straight-up amazing. No fluff, just flavor.
We also went for the cocktail pairing -drinks by Bar Somma. Cold, strong, exactly how we like them.
We did the 8-course meal, and honestly? I’d say it’s the perfect way to experience Somma, especially if it’s your first time. Just go for it!

(Typed a long review but it got removed before publishing so here are a few main points)

Celebrated my husband’s birthday here recently and we loved it!

Like others have said, dining here is very refreshing and not stifling, unlike other fine dining establishments.

The team’s service was great, very warm yet professional. Appreciated their small personal touches too.

The dining experience was quiet and intimate, warm and homely, yet exciting as well. Unique experience which allowed us to focus on the food and experience instead of unnecessary distractions.

Food was great - not overcomplicated and not repetitive of other restaurants. It was very good.

Chef Mirko is so genuine and passionate about his craft, he is truly an inspiration especially in a world where it’s getting harder to thrive on these things.

Would return again!
Great food and a beautiful place

really great night at Somma. felt like we were transported out of sg for a few hours. its rare to find a place that does high end food but keeps the vibe so chill and welcoming. highly recomend if your looking for a proper dining experience without the formality.
Kai the best!

One of our best gastronomic experience so far. The restaurant is a serene and peaceful space (compared to the very loud and busy Somma bar) where waiters seem to evolve like in a choreography. All movements are precise and neat while keeping a very friendly and natural touch. The food is highly creative and tasteful. We took the 8-course menu including 1 in its vegetarian version. It was excellent. The pasta with caramelized carrot juice was a real heaven. And the mandarine millefeuille a pure delight. We chose a Condrieux white wine which paired perfectly well with all the dishes. Somma is one of the most exciting Italian fine dining restaurant I tried recently.
Chef Mirko Febbrile is doing something very interesting. It is Italian cuisine but not traditional style only. There is strong personality and modern approach.
Many dishes use very high quality ingredients and presentation is beautiful but not over complicated. Flavor is clear and powerful.
One dish using seafood was especially impressive. Very delicate but also deep umami.
Service was also excellent. Staff explain every dish with passion and knowledge.
Restaurant interior is elegant but comfortable. Not too formal atmosphere.
Overall Somma is very strong restaurant and I think it will become even more famous soon.
おすすめです。

I recently had the 6-course winter menu and it was an amazing experience from start to finish. Every dish was rich in flavour and beautifully balanced, with thoughtful ingredients that really highlighted the season. You can tell a lot of care went into selecting and pairing each component.

The welcome snack — a potato soup — was especially memorable. It was refreshing yet full of taste, setting the tone perfectly for the rest of the meal. Each course that followed was well-paced and consistently impressive.

We also added the signature pasta, and it was absolutely worth it. The pasta was cooked perfectly and packed with flavour — definitely a standout addition.

On top of the wonderful food, the service and host team were great and very attentive throughout the evening. They made us feel welcomed and well taken care of, which made the whole experience even more enjoyable. Already looking forward to the next season menu.

Amazing dining experience, from entrance to table. We had the winter menu and you can feel the warmth and the effort that had gone into each dish, cheese pairing was also beautiful.
Staff were detailed and knowledgeable.
Will be back again to try the other seasons!

I came in not knowing what to expect and loved every bit of it. I won’t comment too much because I’d love for others to experience the charm and whimsy of the restaurant themselves, but what I admired most is that you can tell, from first welcome to final goodbye and everything in between, that it’s all extremely well thought out - the interplay of tradition and modernity, blending the history of Puglia, the warmth of Italian food and the elegance of fine dining. It was touching to see and hear the level of effort and detail that went into every dish, which made the experience that much more incredible. Thank you Chef Mirko, Jack and the rest of the Somma team for the surreal time.

We had the pleasure of celebrating our wedding anniversary at SOMMA on 7th February, and it was an wonderful evening! Chef Mirko Febbrile was absolutely charming, and every dish he created was inventive, beautifully presented and utterly delicious. The service was exceptional—Jeremy Chiam, Head of Service, and his team made us feel truly looked after, attending to every detail with warmth and professionalism.

A quick tip: be sure to book the “cheese experience” early, as we missed out because it was already sold out!

Overall, SOMMA is a fantastic spot for a memorable and delightful dinner. Highly recommended—go and treat yourself!
I really enjoy this place. Interesting food, very well presented and the fine dining is a true experience.

A truly unforgettable experience. The food is incredibly unique, thoughtful, creative, and full of surprises that makes every course memorable.

Beyond the cuisine, the entire experience is so special and warmhearted from start till end. The environment is just as impressive on how it’s designed, immersive and perfectly sets the mood for the meal. This dining experience will definitely stay with me long after it ends and will come back to try again for different season menu.

Honestly the best dinner I’ve ever had. Somma is such a unique spot and the experience was amazing from start to finish. The staff are so kind and really won my heart. Must get the signature Spaghettone, it was easily my favorite part of the night. Thank you to the Chef Mirko for an unforgettable evening!

if you are looking for a unique, world-class dining experience, Somma is the only answer. This wasn't just a meal, it was a symphony. The staff won my heart immediately with their flawless service and genuine passion, but the kitchen truly stole the show.

I was blown away by the creativity, especially the signature Spaghettone. The Spaghettone is a revelation—perfectly executed and a mandatory addition to your meal if you want the full Somma experience. Chef Mirko’s dedication to the craft is evident in every detail; the level of artistry here is definitely Michelin star worthy.

Thank you for making this the most amazing dinner of my life. We are already planning our return to see what magic you cook up next!

The food was exceptional and creative but homely, the ambience was so well thought of from the music, to the ceramics, to the cheese room (definitely add that on to your experience). I can't wait to go back and try it again when the menu changes! One of the best dining experiences I have ever had in Singapore. It was very special - thank you so much!

It’s not the first experiental restaurant I have been but unfortunately  not the best.

It was flavourful and delicious. However, I had to finish it before we could move on, keeping in mind there are others waiting downstairs for their turns. Food portions may be a bit on the smaller side for some.

Great service and impeccable atmosphere.

Lamb main and mussels with porridge was crazy good. Cocktails were great too.

Where I thought missed a mark - for a menu that was introduced as “designed to make you full”, it was a shame that our stomach were half-filled after the main course. For a $68 upgrade per pax for the mantis shrimp speghattone, we were expecting a full shrimp and pasta dish but were left disappointed as it came as a bisque-inspired course.

Good concept and menu. Value could be better.

I rarely leave reviews, but my dinner at Somma was disappointing enough to deserve one.

Food was decent but nowhere near Michelin level. Definitely not worth $500+ per pax (if you include their signature additional course of mantis shrimp, cheese course, and wine). Aesthetics were nice, and a few staff were friendly, but that’s where the positives end.

We waited 30 mins for our table, and then over an hour between the 2nd and 3rd course. I realised they had forgotten our course while two tables seated after us were already ahead. When I asked, staff claimed they couldn’t serve because my friend went to the toilet. (10 minutes tops). We sat there for another 20 minutes after he returned and we were still not served. I had to ask again before they finally went to check, and the course was brought out another 10 minutes later. Clearly, they had just forgotten about us. The first staff could easily have checked with the kitchen instead of giving such a weak excuse.

Once the error was noticed, everything was served in rushed succession as it was nearing midnight. The cheese course ($58++ per person), which we had looked forward to, became a 10-minute rush job. The staff in the cheese room was stern and glary, hurrying us through each cheese and wine pairing with little time to savour anything. Perhaps they were eager to close up for the night, but the delay was on their end, not ours. One drink was coffee-infused alcohol and drinking it at midnight left me awake till 5am.

The portion sizes were small; even with two supplements, it felt inadequate. The main lamb rib barely had meat, and the birthday cake was served by a visibly glum staff. At the end of the night, they handed us customised menus (nice touch in theory) but they even mixed up our names, which summed up the night perfectly.

Somma tries hard to be fancy but lacks the basics: timing, warmth, and attention to detail. I would strongly suggest having a more seasoned service lead to guide the younger team. The effort is there, but the basics (timeliness, attentiveness, hospitality) need serious work before trying to be “fancy.” I have dined at most of the restaurants under the Lo & Behold Group, and sadly, this was by far the worst experience I have had with them.

Had such a great dining experience at Somma recently that i’m already thinking of coming back for their next menu come December! Jack was our server and he managed to build rapport from the onset and that set the tone for the rest of the night which was personal, relaxing and comforting to say the least. Thanks Jack (and happy birthday once again!).

Chef Mirko came to introduce some dishes and also took the time to chat with us and told us more about his inspirations for Somma and gave us a hint to his upcoming Folklore menu (i must say i kept thinking about it every since). I appreciate his warm touch and genuinity which is not always the case at all fine dining establishments. I told Jack that i really love the tablewear items like the interesting bowls, plates and cups that were used in the courses and Chef Mirko said that he designed it together with a friend of his in Italy. What can this man not do?!

Thoroughly enjoyed the food and no regrets with adding on the cheese experience and red carrot spaghettone pasta which is something i’ll remember by for a long time to come. All in all, definitely worth coming to try Somma for their interesting dishes (first time being server scoby in a dish and one of the most delicious bread) and warm service!

- Sherrie & Oliver

it was the best experience of my entire life. initially i was slightly skeptical and scared of this, but to my surprise, the staff made us feel so welcomed and at ease, and they were extremely friendly as well. the food was chefs kiss, fantastic and delicious. every course had a story behind, and it made the dish tastes even more amazing!! the entire dinner was so memorable and perfect and was so worth the money. i would DEFINITELY come back soon!! if i could rate this a 100/10, i would!!
For when you’d like to have an authentic food journey

Somma bypasses the typical fine dining cliches, starting the course with a comforting, deeply savoury indigenous mushroom broth instead of the usual caviar or oyster.

The menu is a love letter to Puglia, clearly driven by a profound respect for its ingredients. Each course tells a story of its origin, sourced directly from known farmers in the region. The focus on fermentation adds an element of intrigue. I was especially curious knowing that the programme was led by a chef from Geranium in Copenhagen.

The highlight of the mains was undoubtedly the milk-fed lamb (and I’m usually not a fan of lamb); it was exceptionally tender and flavourful, a testament to the grilling and marination technique. My absolute favourite was the cheese soufflé. Perfectly light and airy, beautifully balanced by the sweetness of a Solliès fig. The optional “Somma cheese experience” ($56) is not to be missed: a masterclass in regional Italian cheese with interesting and thoughtful pairings. I enjoyed their eggplant, lardo di Colonnata (cured pork fat) ditali pasta too!

While the creativity is admirable across the board, a few dishes felt less impactful, which is the only reason this isn’t a 5 star review. Value for price is on the higher side - understandably so, considering the R&D that goes into the menu and the calibre of ingredients (including their 100-year-old balsamico). Oh and I love that the team is proud of their Italian wine - as fine dining restaurants tend to lean towards French wine as the go to.

I have deep respect for restaurants that dare to experiment and evolve rather than stay predictable and safe. For that alone, I’d recommend Somma.
