Reviews:
한국인이 더 좋아하는 바쿠테 맛집입니다
한국분들의 80%는 맛있다고 합니다

I was surprised no long queue as before, the one cooking is another person, so as the one doing the packing. The thin bee hoon is uncooked, very stiff. Soup is not thick and tasty as before. Likely change of owner.

Don’t get the hype around this. Had better fish soup at maxwell hawker/arcade fish soup. Think it’s overhyped. But still, the non fried fish slices were fresh and tasty! The fried fish though- super cold and hard. Not good at all- so disappointing! Think it used to taste better a few years back. Now it feels like it’s just hiding behind the Michelin guide stickers which it earned a long time back. Not recommended.

Finally tried the Michelin-recognised Song Fish Soup at Clementi hawker centre. Surprisingly, there was no queue today. I ordered the large bowl with mixed fish (fried fish and sliced fish). The broth was good — light, comforting, and not overly salty. Ingredients were generous, including fried egg and bitter gourd, which added nice texture and balance.

Do note that CDC vouchers aren’t accepted, but PayNow is available. The chilli comes pre-mixed with salted beans, which might not be for everyone. Personally, I found the bowl comforting and satisfying, though not something I’d consider a “must-eat” or “must-try.”

Michelin should revisit this shop again. Other than the generous amount of fish for just $6.50, its salty, nothing impressive. They didnt wash their spoons properly... whatelse not wash properly too? I dont know. Disappointed with Michelin being awarded to this stall

Ordered mixed fish. The slice fish is very tasty.
Healthy choice with vegetables & bitter-guard ..
love it
The soup is tasty and fish is tender. Queue is very long. The hawker centre is crowded because there are many stalls that sell delicious food at reasonable prices.

queued up at 7.30pm and was lucky enough to be the second last person to be served before they close for the day. a pity that at this point they have already ran out of most ingredients - fried fish, rice, ee mian.

settled for a bowl of fish soup. soup was light and refreshing, served with assorted vegetables like tofu and bitter gourd. they were also pretty generous with the fish slices, which were fresh with a firm bite.

it was overall a very hearty and comforting dish.

After a long day of work, this hearty, warming bowl of sliced fish soup helps to nourish the body. Boiled fish slices are fresh, firm, and mildly sweet, pairing well with the tangy orange chili sauce or soy sauce with chili padi. Options that include fried fish, fish head, fish maw, prawns, and clams can be ordered based on availability. Customers usually order a meal with a separate bowl of rice or rice noodles cooked in the soup. A larger bowl comes with thinly sliced, crunchy bitter gourd, tomatoes, lettuce leaves, and a satisfying piece of golden fried egg floss which soaks up the soup’s goodness as you eat it.

Adding a dash of evaporated milk to the soup is optional, though it makes the dish more fragrant according to the stall owner. On its own, the soup already has a depth of flavour that resembles those from charcoal steamboat stalls. It is enjoyable to the last drop. Ordering is smooth and easy, and at times two queues can be seen, the right one for ordering, and the left for collection. If unsure, simply ask those in the queue to check.
フィッシュスープのお店です。ミシュランを獲得しているので行列でした。15分ほど並んで買うことができました。味はとても薄く調味料で味付けが必要です。揚げた魚がたくさん入っていました。ビーフンは軟らかくてイマイチ。みんなビーフンではなくてライスを注文していました。
Fish was fresh and cooked just nice. Soup was just normal.

Saw that it was awarded the Michelin bib, so went to try out of curiosity. Ordered the mixed fish soup (fried and fresh sliced fish).

Soup tasted blander than I liked. The fried fish batter was also hard and unseasoned, but at least the fresh fish slices were good. Nothing else really stood out except for the egg floss. You rarely get egg floss in fish noodles so this was a pleasant surprise.

Probably would visit again if I'm craving that egg floss.

I never noticed this stall until I saw that they were on the Bib Gourmand list and gave it a shot though it was near their supposed closing time of 8pm. There was still a queue at that time (and some more after me) so it seems to be very popular.

Tried their fish soup + rice for $6. The fish was smooth, firm, and tasty (though the portion seems small) and the soup was tasty. It's nice but I wouldn't go for it if the queue was too long.
Soup was nice and tasty. Chose the clear version. Fish fresh. Chilli was the highlight. Love it. Brought out the taste of the soup and fish. Go early to avoid the queue

My grandparents once told me to keep my tummy warm after a morning heavy downpour, and that’s what I did this morning when I visited Song Fish Soup at the Clementi 448 Market & Food Centre. Overall the stall owner served the fish soup bee Hoon with generous portions of sliced fish, along with some fresh vegetables & even bitter gourds. Soup was clear and not too salty. It is no wonder the lunch queue gradually building up and I believe most if not all had been a regular patron to this Song  Fish Soup.  They were accorded Michelin Star in 2024 and offer a wide range of selection including fish maw & prawn combination.
Friendly stall owner and efficient in service. Perhaps I should experiment my taste buds with the rest of the menu such as that of with fish maw.

The taste of the fish soup has changed a lot. About a year ago when I tried it, the soup had a nice stroke of unami. Balance sweetness from the milk and stock. They used to have nice soft butter gourd and general amount of egg floss. Now everything just tasted so normal, just another fish soup down the block

soup was quite bland. i don’t see how this is michelin rated compared to other non-michelin stalls. fish slices were thin and very few (was very fishy, not fresh). got the large and small portions out of curiosity and figured out that both were about the same portion, the large just had more soup.
Ordered the big bowl and pic shown already half eaten...quite value for money and soup was nice. Above average food in general.

Used to be my family's favourite fish soup stall.  Previously, the soup was flavourful and fish slices were thick. But recently especially after they got e Michelin Bib Gourmand title, the standard dropped alot. They increased their price and the fish slices became thinner and soup tasted not as flavourful. You can easily get a better fish soup elsewhere.

Judging this based on its michelin bib gourmand, for its taste and affordability. Soup packed harmonious notes of seafood and garlic, tasted rather clean, but ingredients were not the best tasting. Fish batter rather clumpy and peels off the meat rather easily - without being soaked. Sliced fish cutting was not evenly sliced, questioning culinery skills relative to the award

Generally, I would say there would be people that love this if they do not care about the micro details, but generally, I would say you may get better if you were to spend 10-20 minutes queuing.
Very yummy fish soup. Highly recommend

If you’re in Clementi and craving a comforting bowl of fish soup, Song Fish Soup is a must-visit. Their sliced fish bee hoon is a standout—firm, fresh fish slices served in a light, subtly sweet broth. The addition of bitter gourd and cabbage adds a nice crunch and balances the flavors well. For something richer, the fried fish bee hoon in milky broth is equally satisfying, with crispy fish pieces that soak up the creamy soup beautifully. Don’t forget to try their unique chili sauce with fermented bean curd—it adds a delightful umami kick. The stall has earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand, and it’s easy to see why. Be prepared for a queue, but it’s well worth the wait!
Rich soup & good portion of sliced fish. Recommend to order the larger serving if one needs to queue for more than half hour. They are closed on Sundays.
Went there 1.15pm, queued for 30mins, ordered Yuanyang big with rice, nice soup, worth the wait n value

A long queue normally is a good sign of good food and this was worth the fifteen minute wait. The fried fish soup had a nice creamy fish broth that was flavourful and rich. The soup had bitter gourd which gave a nice firm texture to each bite. The noodles were firm and tasty. While the fried fish was fleshy and the batter a little crispy. Overall very enjoyable and worth the wait.
Very ordinary soup. Don't know how the Michelin come about. Very bland and normal. Beehoon too cooked and battered. Can find it better elsewhere.
Taste great! Got ingredients like bittergourd, bai cai, egg floss! Chilli is special !
Long queue and saw the michelin sign so decided to try. Definitely overrated and over hyped. As many comment here. Is just very normal fish soup and not flavourful.

Honestly, soup is quite bland and I had to add two large spoonful of the preserved soy bean sauce to make it platable.

On the bright side, the fish slices are fresh sweet.

Best fish soup ever
Been eating for more than 20 years!
My number 1 choice!
My favourite place for fish soup with noodles or rice for more than 20 years ago.

Fresh fish slices porridge. If u like something light this is for you. Springy tender no fishy fish. Simple but nice. Can order without porridge if want a even lighter meal. I ordered $8 as I want more fish! Came during off peak as usual. Service is helpful by the ladyboss. Served the bowl to my table. Simple hawker owners.
Taste clean no fishy smell. Porridge not bad but not really worth the queue

Been a long-time regular customer for years while working in the area, and great to see it recognised with the Michelin Bib Gourmand!

Uncle gives a good portion of fish, fish is fresh and good quality, soup is light and clear. I also like the soybean sauce. One of my favourite fish soup stalls in Singapore. It’s a one-man so there can be a queue especially around lunchtime, but he’s pretty fast.

MICHELIN but fish quality and fish slice thickness and porridge portion size has been dropping.

Sliced Fish Porridge ($6)
Fishhead Beehoon ($10, 12, 15)

No pork, no lard

Difficult to find parking after 6pm.

No playground nearby.

Wide aisles in the middle courtyard.
滿鮮的 好喝

Portions here are well worth the prices, soup was light and fish slices are fresh. Complementary condiments at the side would oomph up the soup based on one’s own preferences.

I’ve tried both Michelin bib fish soup stall and much prefer Song Kee’s for Uncle’s warm service. Thank you!
Love the Fish Soup 😋 so good, fresh & good price.
Prefer the Ee noodles to rice. Tasty fish slices. Still hot when i brought it back after 15 mins.

$15 fish soup. I dont think all the alices were fully cooked when served and the dish is very plain. I guess the fish is very tender but again I don't think all were fully cooked and it wasn't very tasty. Would not have again

I know I shouldn't expect too much from touristy hawker spots, but I'd eaten at Song Kee Fish Soup before, and it was okay. I happened to be in the area and saw the news about them making it into the Bib Gourmand list, so I thought of giving them another try. But this time, it was really bad.
I went with the $6 fish porridge, their smallest bowl. The portion is okay for the price, but the fish was really bad. The batang slices were so heavily marinated that I couldn't even recognise it as batang.

It was mushy, resembling a dory kind of soft texture, and the unique fishy profile of batang was completely gone. The only saving grace was that they were still generous with the condiments.
Portion is decent but fish is a bit bland.
Uncle is rude and has no manners at all.
Went for lunch, really pathetic serving of mushy thin fish slices and broken grain rice porridge

One of the last few rustic fish soup noodles that has tasted consistent for the past ten years of dining. Fresh fish is used, unlike other shops that use frozen fish. Wife array of noodle choices and rice is available.

Allergen Note: Gluten, Soy, No Pork, No Lard

Was a bit skeptical hearing fish porridge in a hawker centre, but when you see the fresh fish and uncle's techniques at making the porridge, you clearly understand what a treat you are in for. The dish itself was perfectly flavoured.

Starting from $6 for a bowl. Selected the thick bee Hoon option. Average bowl of fish soup one would expect.

Fish slices are small and thin.

I love fish soup in general, however, I was extremely disappointed with the serving size of this stall. The soup was not particularly fantastic, but, kudos for the exceedingly tender fish. What really took me by surprise was the meagre portion of rice that was in my fish PORRIDGE. I was looking forward to a healthy and filling meal (that’s why I chose porridge - for the rice) but was very much disappointed. Still, the Uncle running the stall was generally well-mannered. His chilli sauce concoction with beans was rather interesting though! $6-$8 for the fish porridge, slightly above average pricing.

Admittedly I was highly suspicious when I first ordered from the stall but as i watched the uncle’s technique, the confidence rose. There is something about the way he just flick the fish slices in, caresses the rice in the pot, pouring in more stock as the flame blazes… it’s mesmerizing and next thing you know, an excellent bowl of fish porridge is out - arguably, this is better than the Michelin (gourmand) brethren in the same hood.
Not a fan personally..
Fish is very fresh and nice

I only eat batang fish soup. This is the best clear, light tasting soup I have tried! With my favourite noodle mee sua; piping hot and perfect after some rain.

Only 2 dishes here: fish slice soup and fish head with choice of carb - porridge / rice / thick or thin bee hoon, mee sua, vermicelli (冬粉) and ee mian. And no garlic sauce here. Only chilli in soy sauce.

My fish slice mee sua soup was only $6, cheaper than the other stall with similar name behind selling fishball noodles. Fish soup $6, add carbs $0.50 there. Don't be confused like some other previous reviews.

Uncle was rearranging the fish slices on the ice. Not much left when I arrived for late lunch on Sat afternoon. Fried shallots, sour vegetables and coriander / parsley are self service (add as much as you like).

Dish is served in reusable bowl but still with disposable chopsticks and spoon.

Not much lunch options here on weekend as most stalls do dinner / supper crowd.

THIS is the real deal. Freshly sliced Batang, great mouthfeel, tasty broth. But due to renovations 15 years ago he had to give up the corner stall. Forget what Michelin thinks. This is the Teochew Fish Porridge worth queuing for. Only gripe is that it runs out too soon.

My uncle and aunt recommended my to this stall, stall owner was friendly, I ordered thru Foodpanda, delivery was very fast, fish soup was good as their fish was fresh, I like the bean sauce that they gave too. I'll reorder again soon:)
You will have a hard time finding better quality slice fish than Stall 37 at Newton. Both Bee Hoon & Mee Sua are divine.

One of the better classic no nonsense sliced fish and fish roe soup around downtown. I like that the perfectly balanced clear broth is not too salty and does not leave you with a dry throat like some other overly savory variety. Feel free to slurp the bowl dry. Consistently great year after year. Shiok.

ホーカー内のプラウンミー　prawn meeの大人気店。
2026年3月時点でドライの海老麺が4ドル。
安い！スープもついてきます。
外観は写真なども何も載ってなく分かりづらいけど1番の行列ができています。

味はほんのりハーブのような味もして、美味しいです！麺も選べるようでした。

Saw the queue because the elderly couple prepare the food quite slowly, so I thought it might be good. Decided to try it and queued for about half an hour. Ordered the $5 prawn mee, but was really disappointed. The prawn soup was underwhelming and honestly tasted quite bad. I barely took one mouth before feeling so put off that I had to stop and throw it away.

To be fair, the elderly couple were very generous with the portion of mee/mee goon so much that just looking at it, combined with the bad taste, completely killed my appetite 🤣 This is probably the first and only time I’ve taken one mouth and thrown the whole thing away.

Had this last Saturday. On the bright side, the dessert shop nearby selling bo bo cha cha was actually pretty good.
Soup is sweet with the briny prawn flavor. But it would probably had more oomph.

I like the layout of this hawker centre. It's airy,  spacious and the tables are well laid out. Unfortunately the prawn noodles were a disappointment. For $5 you get five half slices of small sized prawns and a few pieces of pork rib which is reasonable at this price point. But the prawns were not very fresh and there was a muddy taste. The pork ribs were meaty but tasted very "porky" like they weren't defrosted properly or kept for way too long. The soup base saved the dish. At least it's very drinkable as it's not laden with salt or msg. Don't get the queue or why it's so popular. I think better options can be found elsewhere.
Great old school prawn mee. Would say you get pretty much stuff from 5 dollar. The queue might be a bit slow as the couple is a old. Must try it you down here.

Atmosphere
This is one of the best hawker centres, centrally located with high ceilings & airy.  Overall a great place to dine at for hawker food.

Value
Generous portions with a variety of ingredients.  Went for the upsized version for $5 (&4 for normal).  Such a big bowl with plenty of ingredients.

Taste
Really the old school taste which I remembered eating during my growing up years, nostalgic yesteryears.

Conclusion
Always a que, but the line moves fast coz the aunty is a fast worker.  Definitely would eat again provided the que is not too long.
There is almost always a queue and for good reasons. Delicious and affordable pricing. Old school taste, generous fresh ingredients and good portion.
The Prawn Noodle here is absolutely delicious, and I thoroughly enjoyed my meal! Just a heads-up, as it's located in a food court, it can get a bit warm on hotter days.

This prawn noodles is really generous with the ingredients, just order the big one for five bucks, and you'll get a lot more. The soup is nice and rich, and the noodles are great too. Mix it all up, and the sauce will make it even tastier. It's one of the two best prawn noodles in the Lavender food court, for sure.

Popular with queues to match. Average. Lacks umami flavours. What’s good? Super generous (counted 11 half slices of prawns for my $6 bowl — I thought it wouldn’t end), larger than normal prawns and tender pork slices.

Tried Soon Huat Prawn Noodle recently.
For just $5, the portion is very generous — small eaters might want to stick to the smaller size. The taste is old-school and comforting — not overly rich, but smooth and satisfying.
The stall is run by a friendly elderly couple who go about their work meticulously.
Worth a try if you're in the area and appreciate traditional-style prawn noodles.
Good food goes to those who r patient. Aunty takes pride in her cooking, while uncle does his prep n PR. $4/$5 for a fulfilling bowl of prawn noodles. Both dry n soup versions r equally good.
Very traditional. Soup flavorful but not overpowering. Generous amount. Slow but the old couple kept queue moving steadily.
Cute stall with decent prawn mee. Not the best in capturing the essence of prawns but definitely gives a good value for money!
Queue is long because they spent lots of effort making the best prawn mee for you. Soup warms the soul and the generously big portion of noodle and meat fills your belly - for just $4.

I arrived around 11 am and found a long queue, mostly consisting of seniors. Given the elderly owners, there was a bit of a wait. I ordered and paid via QR code. The soup was decent but not mind-blowing. It had a light flavor and wasn't the best prawn noodle I've tried. It's understandable why the customer base skews older.
The best. Very flavourful, generous portion, cheap. Run by a humble old couple.

Popular noodle store.
Noodle and soup are good
The prawn and meat are pre cook and feel cold when served

Saw this stall with never ending queue even though it was a wet and rainy Monday morning and it piqued my curiosity.

Prices starts from $4 and comes with 2.5 prawns, fishcake and sliced pork. Chilli was good and I could taste the sweetness of the prawns in the soup, just that the soup was a lil too salty for me.

Aunty was very generous with the lard when I asked for more.

A very honest bowl of prawn noodles at $3.50. Soup tasted thin on my day of visit, but still flavourful. As someone with a huge appetite, this is a meal that managed to fill me up for $3.50. For that itself, I am grateful the chefs kept prices so affordable for their customers.
Fresh, Cheap and Quite A Good Portion. Ketchup chilli version. Soup thin yet very flavourful.$4 dry. $3.50 soup.

A very good bowl of prawn noodles, well deserving it’s Bib Gourmand. Soup is full with umami and the portion is so large. Certainly the largest portion of noodles for $3.50! See video. The chilli sauce is also very fragrant and adds extra dimension of flavour to the noodles.

Ingredient wise, I got three half prawns, tails on, a few slices of pork and fish cakes. The prawns were of the right size and fresh so they tasted sweet and flesh was crunchy. Lady boss gave me the last two pieces of pork skin at no extra charge😃Apparently you can also order pork rib noodles or add pork ribs and pork skin to your prawn noodles but they ran out.

Better come early for this delicious and cheap bowl of prawn mee, especially if you want to add extras. In my opinion, it’s not the best in Singapore but certainly Top 5. Much better than some of those stalls selling prawn noodles with large prawns at exorbitant prices.

Chanced upon this old-school prawn mee stall located at North Bridge Market. Very popular among the seniors, who ordered additional ingredients like pig skin and bak kut.

We decided to give it a try since the queue was not too long. The aunty was so generous in picking out the individual ingredients of sliced prawns, pork slices, fish cakes, etc. Large portion of noodles too. The soup was tasty, with a sweet fragrance from the prawns and not overly seasoned/salty. Really enjoyed this traditional, simple and authentic dish of goodness! Like a home-cooked dish at grandma's house. Even the sliced chilli was surprisingly spicy. Very affordable price starting from $3.50.

Do support the uncle and aunty who work tirelessly every single day. They are open from 830am to 2pm.

Expect to wait 20min for every 5 person infront of you in the queue. Most people would order for many takeaway and only 1 cook is making the orders so it can get long wait. It’s above average for its prawn noodle. (better than other local places). Ok to get if <5 people in queue. or else 30min++ is probably not worth it unless prawn noodle is your fav thing.
The waiting will be well rewarded…

I have always wanted to eat this much recommended prawn noodle, but I was always deterred by the queue. I decided to brave the queue on a Saturday close to lunch time. The queue was not that long - about 10 over people in the queue, but in the end the wait was over 45 minutes, due to some customers with multiple orders for takeaways. It is very flavourful and considering the price point, it is above average for sure.
The best prawn noodles I ever eaten.

The dining environment was beautiful, but the service needs a little attention. Our server, who was a trainee, struggled with basic requests. I hope the management can provide more hands-on training to help their new staff succeed, as it would greatly improve the overall guest experience.

I had a wonderful birthday lunch at Sospiri. The food (grilled wagyu, tiramisu, burrata) was great, and good ambience for an afternoon of chit chat. Jerryl came by our table for some entertaining magic, it was very engaging!
Had the weekend brunch here and highly recommend it! Service was excellent and they now have a weekend schedule of activities for kids and family. Excellent and would definitely be back!
The stars speaks for itself! The food is great, seasonings is on point and the dessert is marvellous ❤️ we will be back!!!

We ordered the weekend brunch and very pleased with the food. The serving size is generous.

Resturant engaged a magician and a kids area too. This is very interesting.

Grub
Dricka 🥂 🥂 🥂 🥂
Price 🔪 🔪 🔪🔪
Vibes 🏮 🏮 🏮 🏮 🏮
Look-out 🙇 🙇 🙇 🙇 🙇
Spot 🅿️ 🅿️ 🅿️ 🅿️
Overall 🏆 🏆 🏆 🏆

Here for after dinner drink. Alfresco. Full view of Marina Bay. Level 7 breezy and cooling. Night view splendid. Drinks starts from $16 I think. Great evening to wind down. Staffs are excellent and endearing.

A maiden experience at this beautiful location for a well-executed dinner service. The thoughtfully-curated menu presented a reflection of the wonderful flavors of southern Italy and its cuisine style, with seasonal ingredients that showcased the rich harvest of the land. A big thank you to Ivano and his fine team for the outstanding hospitality and personable service despite a busy evening!

분위기 맛 서비스 그 어떤것도 빠지지 않는 곳 💜
랑구스틴 파스타 꼭 드세요 생선요리도 추천받았던건데 단연코 최고의 맛을 경험하실 수 있을거에요 .. 잊지못할 식사였습니다

Loved the vibes, the foods, and hospitality.

But 1 thing that bothers me was, I felt I was rushed when I was having my meal because when my partner has finished the food, the staff was rushing to clean up my partner's plate and the empty plates despite that we didn't have any more order coming up

In a proper serving manner / etiquette, empty plates shouldn't be collected especially if the other person is still having meal.

Tried the Sunday brunch and simply enjoyed our time there and authentic Italian food. The menu is designed for sharing, which we love for family-style dining.

There's interactive magic entertainment by Singapore renowned Jerryl Tan whom come by to our table. There's balloon and face painting too.

Alcohol list is comprehensive with free flow option add on.

Overall It’s a beautiful, refined spot that manages to feel welcoming for a special family meal

Celebrated a family birthday here; great atomosphere. While one of the junior staff accidentally spilt wine on our of our family members, they had a fantastic service recovery.

Dishes were all great and well-cooked, and they paced their serving according to our family’s needs.

Would return again.

I would like to extend my special thanks to Das for delivering outstanding and exceptional service during our visit. Everything was perfect, and the experience truly exceeded our expectations.

This was one of the rare occasions where I can confidently say that both the food and service were simply amazing. The attention to detail and warm hospitality made our visit truly memorable.

Thank you to Das and the entire Sospiri team for creating such a wonderful and memorable experience. I look forward to visiting again soon.

We arrived a little earlier to enjoy the bar which we absolutely loved, beautifully breezy with natural air and a wonderful atmosphere. The restaurant itself felt a little too cold for us, which made it slightly less comfortable during dinner. As for the Valentine's Day menu, it was pleasant but didn't fully meet our expectations. That said, we truly enjoyed the truffle pasta and the main courses, both beef and fish were very well prepared and delicious. The starters & desserts were good, though not as memorable. What stood out most to us was the staff, incredibly efficient, warm and genuinely welcoming. Their service made the evening special. Thank you!
We enjoyed the food and ambience and most of all, the magic show!!!
Magician is very good

Second time here! This time we are celebrating early Vday dinner! Super awesome experience. Excellent service and excellent food. We particularly liked it that the staff made the effort to follow up on our special request :) - very thankful for that! Highly rec for meals for special moments!

Everything is nice.  Nothing to complain.
Will go back soon.

Great dining experience. Food was great, nice selection of wine, great cocktail and top notch service. The staff are well trained, very attentive and professional.

We ordered burrata salad, insalata Sospiri, spaghetti alle vongole, spaghettone alla puttanesca, branzino & cozze (seabass and mussels), and Sauvignon Blanc Vette 2023 San Leonardo. Brilliant. The best were the desserts (to die for) - Meringata & Torta Caprese (flourless choc cake) - great recommendations by Alan.

We had birthday celebration and it was memorable. Special thanks for Waran who greeted us at the bar and make me comfortable at the bar counter with a glass of aperitif. The Molin Superiore Zardetto prosecco was decent. Special thanks to Matt for his attentive service and chats. Special thanks to Alan who took care of us at our table during dinner, his attentiveness and professionalism. We are very pleased that the note during reservation on one of my guest’s diet requirements was taken care of.

++ Celebrating my birthday at Sospiri was a great choice.

A southern Italian menu demonstrating the culinary skills helmed by Michelin-starred chef Matteo Ponti. The food was exceptional and the dessert was the icing on the cake.

The service crew were on point and paid excellent attention to dietary restrictions (on par with Michelin restaurants). They constantly change plates after every course.

The ambience was chic, modern and had great selection of ambient lighting. Each table was laid with linen and a nicely curated set of Italian tableware.

Worth another visit!!

Excellent food, friendly service set in a nice ambience!
Will be back again!

We loved every moment in Sospiri.
My second time there and brought my husband for our wedding anniversary. We tried lunch this time and similarly, exceptional!

We ordered 2 appetizers, 2 mains, 2 drinks and 2 desserts - right portioning, right texture, flavorful and spot-on. The pasta noodles were aldente. That duck as a main is cooked perfectly. The meringue dessert was light that was a perfect ending to our lunch.

The service was impeccable. Our server truly helped us in the menu, very warm and welcoming and made sure we got the right menu that we wanted (we were seated at the same side as the door entrance/exit).

Definitely will be back to try out the other dishes.

$38++ for their set lunch. Leek soup was nice. Topped up $12 for steak. It was deliciousss but look at the portion :( 2 slices of meat for lunch is quite sad. Also, they did not ask for doneness. The meat portions and doneness were different for all of us at the same table.

Came at 12.15pm. Place was full. Food was served from 1.10pm. I suggest not to come if you have a hard stop to return to work. I had to leave at 1.30pm without eating my dessert.
staff are so slow to pour beers out the single tap they have. If you can't pour beers fast enough - why don't you come up with a solution like selling beers by the bottle

We had dinner here on New Year’s Eve, and it turned out to be a really lovely way to wrap up the year. The ambiance was honestly the highlight of the night — warm, lively without being chaotic, and with that special festive buzz you only get on the last evening of the year. The place was nicely lit, the music set the mood without being intrusive, and everything felt relaxed but still a bit special, which is exactly what you want on a night like that.

The food complemented the experience well. The menu had a good variety, and everything we ordered was nicely presented and enjoyable. Nothing felt rushed or careless, even though the restaurant was clearly busy. Portions were satisfying, flavors were balanced, and it all came together in a way that made the meal feel comforting and celebratory at the same time. It was the kind of food that lets you focus on the conversation and the moment, rather than overanalyzing every bite — which, on New Year’s Eve, is a good thing.

What really made the evening memorable was the timing. We finished dinner just before heading out for the fireworks, which felt perfect — full, happy, and already in a great mood as the year was about to change. The staff handled the crowd well and kept things moving smoothly, and the overall vibe made the night feel effortless and enjoyable. All in all, a very pleasant New Year’s Eve dinner and a great place to start the celebrations.

Cocktails fell short of the lofty claims on the website.

Antipasti (crab and tuna) were very nice. Caccio pepe with the black truffle was a miss. The truffle was totally unnecessary and the caccio e pepe lacked the punch and was a bit watery for my liking.

Lamb was nice. Well balanced. Portions were god overall. We shared t5 dishes along 3 adults.

Desert was fantastic. The meringue was delicious. The pistachio creme brulee also a hit.

We visited for lunch and were immediately struck by the bright, cheerful atmosphere. The weekend brunch course was an excellent value, allowing us to sample a variety of dishes—all of which were delicious. What truly set the experience apart, however, was the impeccable and friendly service. The staff played a huge role in making our afternoon so pleasant. We’re already planning our next visit and look forward to seeing some new seasonal items on the brunch menu
Great food and a lovely atmosphere. The Tagliolini Scampi was easily my favorite dish of the night! The Nduja was quite decent, and the clams were  fresh. Highly recommended for a solid Italian meal.

We headed up to the 57th floor to try our luck without a reservation. Even though the Lounge and Bar were fully booked, Stephen at the reception went above and beyond to accommodate us. He found a space for our group with a huge smile and personally walked us to our table—a fantastic first impression!
​Once seated, Rex Baniqued was a friendly and welcoming face. He did an amazing job explaining the set menu and giving us tailored suggestions. Our group of six ended up ordering a variety of dishes, and everything was a hit:
​Appetizers: I tried all the appetizers and they were wonderful. The Tuna Tartare in a cone was heavenly—the cone itself was so flavorful, and the fish was incredibly fresh.
​Tomato Soup: This was truly one of a kind. It was so delicious I had to use the bread to wipe the bowl clean!
​Main Courses: My Lamb was tender and perfectly done. I also tasted the Wagyu, which was packed with flavor, and the Sea Bass, which was beautifully prepared.
​Dessert: We finished with the Salted Caramel Soufflé, which was the perfect end to the meal.
​Overall, it was a stellar experience from the service to the last bite. I would absolutely come back and do it all over again. Highly recommended!

Celebrated our wedding anniversary here the past 2 years. Food and service as always was impeccable. Our server, Jude, was very warm, friendly, and quick to give us suggestions on the dishes we were considering. Service was great without being intrusive.

For starters, we had the burrata with conference pear which was light and refreshing. For mains, we ordered the wagyu ribeye for 2 and the portions were huge. Came with a dish of aligot potatoes that was very rich, and an excellent rendition of caramelized brussel sprouts. Jude was quick to let us know that we could always pack up anything we couldn't finish, and he was right coz we were very stuffed from the main alone and still had dessert coming! The Kaiserschamarrn was a lovely end to a fantastic meal. Fluffy and warm, it paired nicely with the cold strawberry sorbet and warm stewed strawberries. A complimentary hazelnut chocolate cake was presented to us for our anniversary, as well as a card with signatures from all the staff. Thanks to everyone at Spago for making it a night to remember.

The food here was fantastic. My wife had the lamb from the standard list and I had the veal. I think the lamb was better. But both were great. Staff were amazing and attentive as well.

One year later: Came back again….this time I wasn’t as impressed with the food. Not sure but steak was abit tough. The Brussels sprouts was a bit over caramelised.

The amazing restaurant really took excellent care of me!

我建議訂傍晚18:30的位置，可以待到20:15，你可以拍攝到不同時段不同面向的景色，非常值得，用完餐後悠哉地散步去看20:45的免費天空樹燈光秀表演。

The menu features premium ingredients, including steaks, seafood, and creative small plates. The ambiance is stylish and sophisticated, ideal for fine dining, business dinners, or special occasions. Service is professional and attentive, ensuring a smooth and memorable experience. Spago combines refined flavors, quality ingredients, and a polished atmosphere to deliver a top-tier dining experience in Singapore.
Beautiful place and view, with excellent service from Ivan and Joan which made us feel very well-taken care of. My wife and daughter enjoyed the food thoroughly; the Chilean sea bass was on point.
Great dining experience with free birthday cake! Great hospitality Jessy, Joan and Gobi!

From the food to the atmosphere to the impeccable service—everything was simply perfect. A truly memorable dining experience.
And the view from the balcony, it was mesmerizing. I’m still out of words.

PS: They have the best staffs, especially those in the reception area. I love their SMILES it made feel at ease and well taken care of.

Nice place~ nice foods~
We went on weekdays for their lunch set. $58 member and $68 without member. Everything is so yummy from starter to dessert. Highly recommended

Invited to a birthday celebration on Wednesday 4 February. Reservation was for a party of 4.  Really looked forward to the Wolfgang Puck dining experience. After we arrived we were quickly taken to a table with only 3 chairs. After standing at the window for 2 minutes being ignored in a busy dining room, a waitress who was repositioning a wine bucket stand to the exact spot where I was standing asked if she could help. She finally arranged for an additional chair to be pulled over from a nearby table. Why does reception confirm our reservation for 4 but ask us to sit at a table with 3 chairs. (Note: All the square tables only have 3 chairs. They use booths for seating 4 or 5.) After a meal which was really quite nice (except for the octopus which was served with a very sad looking lime that was far from fresh) we were abruptly informed by a waiter that we would have to leave for the second seating. There appears to be a disconnect in the Front of House as our host had  confirmed when making the reservation that we were welcome to stay at our table until closing. The waiter had to go check and by the time he returned to confirm that we could stay we were making ready to leave. A lack of service recovery reinforced our decision.
Overall, great view, good food, but service needs lots more polish.

The service at Spago was some of the best I’ve ever experienced. The staff were always present, without being invasive, and seemed to always be one step ahead of us, topping up our glasses, folding napkins and just being friendly while maintaining their professionalism.

At $88++ for the 3 course dinner set menu, it was great value for a special occasion meal with views overlooking both the city and Gardens by the Bay.

I’d recommend this for a special occasion. The staff really know how to make you feel cared for.

We decided to go to Spago for our double-birthday celebration this year. The staff were incredibly attentive. For birthdays you'll get a small chocolate mousse cake on a nicely-decorated plate and a card signed by the staff (very adorable). And of course, birthday wishes from every staff who passes by.

The lunch set menu has an extensive choice of appetisers and mains, and I liked that the menus were on their website with all prices indicated. With the variety of food, price point and great location, this is a great place for business lunches too. Currently they have a promo where you can get the lunch set for $58++ if you sign up for the free Sands Lifestyle membership.

Will definitely be back to try other things on the menu!

This was our family’s first time spending Christmas and New Year overseas. On Christmas Day afternoon, we enjoyed drinks at Spago Bar and Lounge, and it was truly a wonderful experience.

Located on Level 57 next to the Marina Bay Sands infinity pool, the venue offers stunning views and a sophisticated atmosphere. We thoroughly enjoyed our time there.

The only minor inconvenience was the lack of restrooms on Level 57, requiring a lift trip down to Level 55, which can take some time. Overall, however, it was a memorable and enjoyable visit.

An excellent value set lunch for 3 course at 68, and if you are a Sands member, you only need to pay $58. The selection for the 3 course is also very good with plenty of choices.
I was seated at the terrace which overlooks the swimming pool and the city skyline. Bread and sourdough was served with 2 types of butter.
These are my courses.

3pc Irish oysters with spinach, white wine and Parmesan. Very deliciously done. Loved to soak the bread into the white wine sauce.

Iberico pork loin with wheat beer, brandy mustard sauce,confit bacon, glazed Brussels sprouts and apple sauce. I had medium as recommended but I felt that the pork loin is not tender enough and slightly chewy.

Pistachio panna cotta with orange gelee, pistachio brittle and orange gelato. I enjoyed this dessert, the crunch of the pistachio brittle blended so well with the panna cotta.

Service was good and food delivered out in a good timely manner. A very satisfying delightful lunch.

If I could give 6 stars I would! From the very beginning all of my requests despite some being overwhelming and last minute, the team of Spago and MBS did not fail to make our anniversary unforgettable.

We often complain about the gst and service charge fees, but its my first for mentioning that I was so delighted in paying this without any grin because the whole team was spectacular.

Ms Gillian had assisted me with my requests, and the waiters and waitresses on my visit on the 28 of December 2025 at 6pm, every one of them who assisted us were fantastic.

Food was exceptionally excellent. You are dining for premium food, with premium prices came quality and professional services beyond excellence.

Genuinely, I will come back here with my partner as she was wowed with the service and we cant thank the entire team enough for making our anniversary perfect.

Thank you to the team, and I am looking forward to vouch and reference them whenever required for their exceptionally professional service and experience. Every restaurant in singapore should aim to provide such services as the benchmark.

Simply amazing!

nice views but gave me a really bad stomach ache after

We celebrated our Wedding Anniversary at Spago Dining Room and it was such a awesome experience. From the moment you were ushered to your seat, attentive staff will attend to you to show and recommend to you their specially curated menu and often come around to check on how you are doing through the dinner. All in all it is a great dish but is comparable to most spinach soup out there. I would say just go to the 4 stars spinach soup near your place.

Michelin Star but not a lot to shout about. It's quite hard to identify and mention anything outstanding about it. Just very standard, normal level of competency. Definitely won't travel just for this.

There are spinach soup stalls all over Singapore but this stall has the honor of listed by Michelin Guide for two years running. My order of just spinach century and salted eggs soup for $4.50 tells me why it’s listed. The soup is loaded with lots of spinach, salted and century egg pieces plus mushroom slices, wolf berries and minced pork! On top of that it’s very tasty.

My newfound favourite~ Visited this stall multiple times, and the spinach soup is consistently flavourful and ingredients are always fresh. Portion is huge as well. Very comforting meal and value for money!

The soup tastes very much like a comforting ban mian broth — light, clear & homely — but with spinach as the star. What makes it stand out are the variations, from the classic seafood version to the richer salted egg & century egg options, or even yong tau foo. A simple idea done well, hearty without being heavy & worthy of its Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition.

Absolutely fantastic broth and fresh ingredients.  I always go for their Signature Soup.  I was personally quite hesitant as I recall this brand is a franchise, but try it out once and got hooked and have been coming back frequently. This branch’s spinach soup is very tasty and feels almost like they are operating on their own recipe apart from the others - I tried the same in Toa Payoh, totally miss the mark.  There is often no queue so I can understand people may feel worried somewhat but trust the Michelin bib guide for this! 🤣🤣🤣

The spinach soup from Yuan Yang Spinach Soup is one of my absolute favourites at Geylang Bahru Market. The broth is not only flavourful but also rich and hearty, making it a comforting meal. What makes this stall stand out is the wide variety of options—from different noodle choices to add-ons and the type of spinach soup like seafood, meatballs, and yong tau foo, allowing you to customise your bowl to your liking.

A huge shoutout to the two hardworking ladies behind the stall, who have rightfully earned the Michelin Bib Gourmand award back-to-back in 2023 and 2024. Their dedication and consistency in serving top-quality spinach soup truly deserve recognition!

This spinach soup stall is definitely different from those under the same franchise. The soup is very tasty and not overly plain nor salty. The generous amount of ingredients help customers enjoy the soup better.
The spinach soup was tasty and value for money.  Will be back.
Delicious

Many michelin starred stalls in this hawker centre. Came here to try the dry ban mian but saw this and ordered a portion of its spinach soup. Excellent. Generous portion compared to others I have had.

The healthier choice in the Geylang Bahru hawker centre. The spinach soup is tasty but the yong tau fu are ordinary. Not deserving of a Bib Gourmand accolade though. Geylang Bahru Hawker Centre, a surprised gem for several Michelin awards stalls. I like this spinach soup here, as the soup base is very tasty. Importantly, you won't be thirsty after the soup meal..highly recommend..they have a Michelin awards too!

So. Yum.

Been wanting to try the Kingfish with Pickled Jambu and Green Chilli served with Pappadums, and it was a hit. I wish I can have this every day.

The BBQ Prawns with Fermented Mango and Roasted Chilli sauce was crazy. The mango and chilli sauce was beautiful with the char and sweetness of the prawn.

Is it okay to say I had the best Dahl here? Because damn, I never knew it could be this good. I can’t fathom the magic of making this, but we ordered so much roti to clean this and the Seeni Sambal. On that note, Roti could be better.

Enjoyed a great Sri Lankan dinner here with friends while visiting Singapore. very authentic and everybody was happy. The staff guided us through what their specials are, and how much we should order. Enjoyable and tasty!

The braised beef cheeks were also so tender and went very well with roti (in fact it would not be that good without the roti). As a non spice eater I would’ve enjoyed this a lot more if I liked spice perhaps? The banana blossom cutlets were a tad bit too spicy for me but i thought they were still nice.

Also got falooda as dessert, which was basically bandung chendol. The taste of the dessert felt cheap to me like I could make it on my own, and it was overly sweet with no other interesting elements.

Summer Palace continues to set the benchmark for what great Cantonese cuisine should be. From the moment you step in, the fantastic, spacious vibe creates a sense of calm luxury that lets the food and service truly shine.

The cuisine is outstanding — clean, crisp flavours executed with incredible precision. Every dish shows a deep respect for ingredients and technique, especially the beautifully balanced Cantonese wok-fried flavours that are both refined and deeply comforting. Nothing feels heavy or overworked; everything is confident, elegant, and perfectly judged.

What truly elevates the experience is the stellar, attentive service. It’s polished without being intrusive, warm without being overfamiliar — genuinely world-class service that makes you feel completely looked after.

I recently enjoyed an omakase lunch set and I found it quite amazing it was nothing short of remarkable. The chef’s artistry shines through, with a clear focus on balancing flavors, textures, and presentation to create a cohesive dining experience. Each course is thoughtfully paced, reflecting the chef’s deep consideration for the diner’s perspective.

**Highlights of the Meal:**

- **Yellowtail Sashimi with Raw Yam Purée**: The yellowtail is paired with a unique plum-marinated yam purée, its subtle sourness awakening the palate and complementing the fish’s delicate flavor.
- **Squid Sushi**: Fresh and delightfully chewy, the squid is elevated by lightly seasoned rice that enhances without overpowering. The rice feels almost ethereal, blending seamlessly with the fish.
- **Kama Toro**: This three-layered fatty tuna melts like ice cream, rich yet surprisingly light, leaving no greasy aftertaste.
- **Sanma**: A seasonal favorite, the sanma is expertly sliced to maximize its texture and flavor, delivering a full sensory experience.
- **Hokkigai Soup**: Served at the perfect moment, this refreshing soup with cabbage and radish slices highlights the natural sweetness of the surf clam, acting as a palate cleanser before bolder sushi courses.
- **Saba Sushi**: Saba can be challenging due to its fishy notes, but the chef’s skillful preparation eliminates any off-flavors. Once again, the light rice ensures the fish remains the star.
- **Foie Gras**: Marinated in sake with a touch of yuzu zest, this dish is rich yet approachable, striking a perfect balance of indulgence and freshness.

The only drawback from the tasty dishes is that  at the end of the meal, the richness of the dishes felt burdensome on my stomach, i was too full :)

**Final Thoughts**: With its premium sashimi, impeccable course progression, and harmonious balance of fish and accompaniments, this restaurant delivers an omakase experience that’s well worth revisiting. The chef’s attention to detail and innovative pairings make it a standout destination for sushi lovers.

We had dinner at Katori for omakase. While the food was decent for the price point (expected standard for the price we are paying), it wasn’t particularly outstanding or memorable for us. What affected our experience more was the atmosphere created by the chef.

I have had Sushi Katori on my radar for a while now but I had been prioritizing the bigger names. Decided to visit because they said they could serve shinko by pre-ordering 4 days in advance but unfortunately none was shipped from Japan on the day of my visit.

I went for their sushi omakase as I realised my preference is now going straight to trying sushi rather than going through a few different appetizers. I also got a bottle of their branded sake.

They use 2 different coloured shari here, seasoned with different vinegars for different types of neta. Admittedly, I couldn't really taste the difference, and I thought the vinegar could have been stronger for both types of rice.

There were a few standout pieces, such as the iwashi (sardine), in season clam, aji, negitoro with caviar and aburi-ed kamatoro. The iwashi was so good I added a second piece. I was also surprised by the lack of anago, as it is supposed to be a staple of edomae sushi as the last piece before the tamago. The home made mentaiko that Chef Katori served was also really good and went very well with the sake.

Service wise, I thought there could be improvements, especially if they want to try to get a Michelin star. I had to pull out my own chair when sitting down and the basket for my bag wasn't automatically offered. My cup of tea wasn't replaced entirely but topped up, so it wasn't hot at all times, which for me is really important to cleanse my palate before the next piece of sushi.

Every single piece of sushi was outstanding. You can truly taste the craftsmanship in every bite. I was completely blown away by the quality. I haven’t had many traditional sushi omakase meals, mostly because I’m not great with raw or cold foods, so I usually lean more towards kappou-style omakase. But from the very first bite at lunch yesterday, I could tell this had to be one of the top sushi restaurants in Singapore. I’m so glad I came across it while searching for Michelin recommended restaurants in SG. Will definitely be back!

문제점 1) 템포.
본래 싱가포르 스시야들이 일본, 한국 등과 비교해 템포가 느린 편이긴 하나, 이곳은 그를 넘어 아예 흐름이 끊기게 한다. 템포를 느리게 가져가는 것과 흐름이 뚝뚝 끊기는 것은 서로 다르다.
2) 온도감.
아부리를 하는 이유는 뭘까? 온도를 올려 네타 본연의 향을 살리고, 지방을 녹여 식감을 살리고, 은은한 토치향을 더하기 위해서다. 그렇다면 사와라와 가마스를 아부리 하고 다 식혀서 내놓을 것이라면 하는 의미가 있을까?
3) 향과 맛.
아예 이해를 못 할 것은 아니다. 싱가포르는 일본에서 대부분의 네타를 수입해오고, 입고-적재-대기-통관-수령까지 하다보면 못해도 20시간은 걸리니. 거기에 산진에서 한번 냉동, 싱가포르 도착 후 수입 업체에서 또 해동 후 손질, 다시 냉동, 그 후 가게에 도착해 재차 해동을 한다. 그러니 한국과 일본에 비해 향과 맛이 흐려도 이해는 된다. 본디 싱가포르 스시야는 그거 감안하고 가는 거니. 하지만 이곳은 그 싱가포르의 특수성을 감안해도 과하게 향이 옅다. 츄토로는 무슨 잘 갈은 생무를 씹는 줄 알았다.
4) 디저트.
식사의 꽃은 디저트다. 결국 우리의 기억은 최종장의 성대한 마무리을 제일 크게 보정해 기억한다. 그런 의미에서 이곳의 마무리는 대참사다. 편의점에서 한번 녹았다 다시 언 바닐라 향 아이스크림을 먹어본 적 있는가? 감히 단언컨데 이곳의 아이스크림은 식감과 맛이라는 측면에서 그것과 비슷하다.
5) 가격.
사실 이게 핵심이다. 그래도 가격이 적당하면 괜찮다. 근데, 정말 솔직히 말해 그냥 이 몸에 조금 더 보태 레자미를 가는 것을 추천한다.

총평: 흐린 향과 애처로운 맛.

前日の駆け込み予約で伺いました。
食前からテーブルに飾られてあるお花は全て日本から取り寄せているそうで、海外にいても日本の秋を感じられました。

The restaurant has great reviews online, which is partly why I decided to visit. But after this experience, I left feeling that the place may have become a bit too casual about the basics, and that, frankly, they didn’t seem too concerned about what a table or two might think.

I was served by the restaurant’s well-known chef that evening. Even before the meal began, he coughed several times near the counter — which I can understand; everyone has off days — but what followed was hard to overlook.

During preparation, a small piece of fish fell, and instead of discarding it, he simply placed it back between the fish and rice before serving it.

The meal stretched to over two hours, with three tables seated in a row. Throughout most of the evening, the chef focused his attention on chatting with one particular table, while the rest of us were left waiting and feeling rather awkward.
I understand wanting to make regular guests feel welcome, but when side dishes sat empty for quite some time until we had to ask for refills, it showed a clear lack of attentiveness.

What made it worse was that the chef continued chatting while holding half-made sushi in his hands. Once the conversation ended, he simply turned back, finished the sushi, and handed it straight to me. At that moment, I honestly thought, “If that sushi was part of the conversation, maybe it should go to that guest instead — or at least, wear a mask.”

I was invited to dinner here to try a nori (seaweed) that is supposedly legendary. I reached about 20 minutes before our reservation time and just chilled near the counter. We were ushered promptly to our seats at the reservation time.

Ambience of the place was nice, though it isn't really traditional Japanese. Chef was quite conversant in English and we were chatting quite a bit throughout the meal.

The nori lived up to its reputation. I really liked the negitoro, ankimo and unagi that utilized it. It's more crispy than any other nori that I have tried, and the flavour is more complex while being light too. Some of my other favourite dishes were the corn chawamushi (excluding the uni, I will get to that later) and the ice cream at the end.

The neta and shari for all the sushi were a letdown. There was no umami at all; I was just tasting dead fishes (no pun intended). I could taste the alum in all the uni, and the uni that was served is what I feel belongs at a lower priced point shop. I feel the shari could have been stronger; even though 3 types of vinegar were used, it didn't come out when I was eating it.

The service of the staff was great, but I think that's expected at a restaurant with this price point.

If I could just get the negitoro and ankimo as ala carte, I would definitely return and recommend it to other people. But if I want to eat sushi, this is not a place I would recommend or return to.

Chef Sakuta probably has the best mastery of flavors among all the michelin starred sushiyas in Singapore. For instance, he used the saltiness from caviar to balance the fried fish. The judicious drops of lime on the fish also accentuates the flavor as required.

Of all his dishes, the only area of improvement was the abalone with liver sauce. The sauce was a tad diluted for my liking and I prefer a much stronger and rich flavor like at Shinji or Kimura.

His sushi rice is also more acidic, which initially has a strong vinegar taste but does not linger on in your mouth (it is not bad, it's just different).

Also, because there is only 1 sitting which begins at 7pm. There is no rush to finish by a certain time. While we were done in 2 hours, it felt good-paced, unlike some places with 2 sittings and could feel rushed towards the end.

Now, given the number of options in SG, compared to Sushi Kimura and Shinji, Kimura's rice is much sweeter and if you like the vinegar taste to linger, Kimura's rice still takes the no. 1 spot, however, Kimura's ingredients are basic. While Shinji's rice is nothing to shout about, the more frequent use of premium ingredients is a differentiator. I wouldn't bother with the other options at a similar price point.

On parking, there is free parking at the hotel lobby, but you need to enter via hill street and park right outside the hotel entrance. Do NOT enter the basement carpark, there is no coupon provided.

Dining at Sushi Sato was always an extraordinary treat, from the intimate location hidden in Dempsey to the warm and welcoming demeanor of Chef Sato who made the meal feel personal. For someone who doesn’t usually like chawanmushi, the egg custard at Sato was a revelation—elevated by the subtle sweetness of chestnuts and creamy shirako, executed with such finesse that it became a highlight. The sushi, as expected of any high end sushi place, was of the highest quality. Sushi Sato sits comfortably in my top 5 omakase restaurant in Singapore.

Sushi Sato in Singapore is an absolute gem for anyone who appreciates high-quality sushi and precise Japanese craftsmanship. The meal was an experience from start to finish—every bite felt intentional, fresh, and beautifully balanced. The sashimi selection was stunning, with the perfectly seared tuna, sweet shrimp, and delicate white fish presented on kombu, enhancing the umami. The grilled fish was another standout—crispy, smoky skin with juicy, flavorful meat, paired with citrus and a bit of daikon for freshness. The sushi itself was on another level, with each piece melting in the mouth while still having that perfect bite of rice. Everything felt incredibly refined yet effortless. People often equate how much they pay with how good a restaurant should be. I won’t sugarcoat this.

It was our first visit, and we were recommended the Chef Picks for You menu at $78 per pax. As first-timers, we usually go with what the restaurant suggests, so we agreed. For two people, this brought our bill to over $200.

For context, I’ve had far better meals at lower price points. Just down the street at Pura Brasa, around $170 gets you a full rack of ribs, sliced beef, and a whole squid. Generous portions, clear flavours, and real value. That comparison matters, because what we received here fell short in both taste and substance.

We started with bread and a tomato-based sauce that was bland and unremarkable. This was followed by cheese. Cheddar, not an artisanal or curated selection. It was coated in sugar with a hint of truffle oil. Overly salty, oddly sweet, and frankly out of place for a restaurant charging this much.

Next was a falafel made with broccoli and chickpeas. It was dry and lacking flavour. The sour cream did most of the work. Good food should taste good on its own. Sauces should complement, not compensate.

The kebab that followed was fine. Not bad, not memorable. Just average. At this point, everything tasted so muted that we genuinely wondered if flavour was being intentionally compromised under the pretense of healthy food.

The mains confirmed this suspicion. We were served braised beef with spiced rice. Texture-wise, the beef was tender. Flavour-wise, it was flat. The rice was especially disappointing. Worse than what you would find at casual chains like Nando’s. You can get better braised beef at neighbourhood Italian osterias for much less.

After we mentioned that the rice was bland, the staff offered Brussels sprouts on the house, which was appreciated. However, they were extremely salty and overpowering, becoming unpleasant after a few bites.

Dessert was pistachio ice cream served on kunafa with chocolate drizzle. The elements did not come together. The kunafa was overly sweet. The pistachio flavour was barely present. The salted pistachio nuts clashed with the rest of the dish. It felt like each component was competing rather than working in harmony.

Now, about the “6-course” menu. In reality, we were served:
- Several small starters
- One main
- One dessert

That does not reasonably qualify as six courses.

On top of that, we were charged $3 per person for water, and $5 for an additional basket of pita bread that we did not ask for. These add-ons, combined with the overall pricing, pushed the bill past $200.

Service was mixed. Mohammad worked extremely hard and was attentive throughout. But when a waiter has to work this hard, it usually means the food isn’t speaking for itself. Another waitress repeatedly cleared plates despite us saying we weren’t done, spilled sour cream across our table, and walked away without cleaning it up. We had to call another staff member to help.

At this price point, the experience was deeply disappointing. The ambience is decent, but ambience alone does not justify bland food, misleading portions, and inconsistent service. Nothing we were served felt premium or worth what we paid.

If you’re dining in Tanjong and care about value and flavour, there are many better options nearby. This place simply does not make the cut.

Lovely place with beautiful aesthetics and décor. It was our first time here, recommended by Click who visited on a quieter night. We came for a team lunch and it was such a pleasant experience.

The food was freshly prepared and we loved every bit of it. Portions were on the smaller side, giving it a semi fine-dining feel, but still satisfying. The staff were friendly and attentive, which made the experience even better.

I’d definitely come back again! Perhaps with my husband for a date night, or with girlfriends just to chill and catch up. Overall, a lovely place and I’m sure we’ll be returning again.

Had a great time here celebrating a birthday. Great food but more importantly, top notch service by Eka and Mohammed. Mohammed learnt that it was our first time and gave us a thorough breakdown of the menu and friendly check ins throughout the whole night. Really loved dining here and will be back!

Rarely leave reviews but can’t recommend this place enough!!!

Special shoutout to Eika, Muhammad who served us and the chefs who crushed it!
- Falafel, cauliflower, branzino and beef skewers are a must — it’s incredible

Service is exceptional and they’re SO NICE!

Such good interior vibes too. DON’T HESITATE TO COME!

The ambiance was cozy, dimly lit, and private. The food was exceptional, and the service was outstanding. It was a wonderful dining experience, and I was fortunate to secure a seat as a walk-in. I would certainly recommend making a reservation. I eagerly anticipate returning to indulge once more.

Beautiful restaurant and nice workers. Wondered why it was empty- but food was really, really disappointing. Oyster mushroom sharing kebab turned out to be cold slices of hard shiitake mushrooms with a mild, weird sauce which had no association with any Middle Eastern food I have tried whilst travelling and 4 tiny wraps smaller than my palm. Literally two tiny snacks each. Halloumi was okay, but same quality as I could make myself at home.  Yeah won’t come again, some quality control needs to be looked into. Maybe due to eating vegetarian food, meat might be better.

Truly fantastic to pop across to the "mainland" and enjoy a wonderful dining experience with my oldest friends in Singapore, fellow naturalised Singaporean entrepreneur, Miguel Bernas, at the epic Fat Prince in Tanjong Pagar.

From the moment that I walked in early, (I'm always early thanks to my Grandad who taught me this as a young boy), and when I asked whether I could come in, (as they weren't open yet), was greeted with, "yes of course you can come in since I follow you on LInkedIn" uttered with a smile by Operations Manager Lukasz I felt at ease.

That was followed by "would you like a beer?" and if anyone has been following me on LinkedIn then a beer is most definitely the way to win me over!

Given how much I loved "The Fat Prince", bizarrely only my first visit here, although I have been to other Dandy Collection venues Neon Pigeon and Firangi Superstar (who's manager there is a fellow Toon Army fan!).

It was my friend Miguell's choice and a great one.

Simple Middle Eastern cuisine with every item a tantalising dish that stimulated my tastes buds and left me wanting more as they were so delicious and they all went well with the draught Asahi too!

The Fat Prince has a couple of excellent set lunches that provide amazing value for money.

Highly recommended and I will be back.
Amazing food, great and warm staff! The best way to enjoy Singapore evening ♥️

Came here for lunch with my boyfriend and we were spoiled with the chef's picks! Mr Mohammed was super attentive throughout and kept attending to us and ensured our plates were spotless before the food was served which was really awesome :) couldn't pick a favourite but the halloumi was solid 👌we polished off the chicken tagine as well (chicken was smooth and beautifully cooked, courgettes were so good) and rounded off the meal with a not too sweet Dubai chocolate kunafe dessert. Highly recommend coming here!

I had dinner with my boss, colleagues, and clients in this restaurant. We chose Fed by Chef, and the food came out was fantastic. On top of food, one of the waiter (Mohammed) also provided best service, delighted everyone and made our dining experience wonderful 👍. Thank you!

Only 1 suggestion, please make toilet light brighter ☺️
Great experience! Food was excellent and the service was fantastic.
Ordered from here for the first time. $100+ for this slop. Audacious.

The bartender was really nice and checked in on us frequently. He also did a great job explaining the bar bites clearly. However, the experience with another female staff member was disappointing. When I mentioned that the air-conditioning was dripping, she took the feedback poorly and responded defensively, saying she didn’t see any “waterfall” and that she was already aware of the situation (though she later changed her words). While I was offered another seat, I was honestly taken aback by her response and decided not to stay for dinner after happy hour. Food and drinks-wise, everything was good and enjoyable.

Mohammad explained the menu to us before our ordering and his recommendation of dishes and the quantity was great! Thank you Mohammad

The experience was superb. Our favorites is the dips and fish. Yum!
Meats, dips and bread were very good.

Flavours were fierce, punchy yet sophisticated. Absolutely floored by the food and attention to detail by the service staff as well.

A unique restaurant that truly stands out in Singapore's competitive fine dining scene. A must visit for sure!

A modern twist on Indian cuisine. Flavour and depth in the food was different with it's elavation. Some may like if you come in with an open concept minded. It's not like any other Indian food or traditional style.

I’ve been to plenty of fine dining restaurants in Singapore, and I can confidently say that Thevar has one of the best flavour combinations I’ve ever experienced. The dishes are bold and interesting — yet everything works beautifully together. Not a single dish tasted boring.

I requested a no-shellfish alternative, and it was just as delicious and thoughtfully prepared. My partner had the shellfish options, and they looked even better 😵‍💫 He even said it was the best lobster he has ever tasted!

The meal started strong and ended just as strong. The desserts were especially refreshing — not overly sweet, but perfectly balanced to round off the experience. Kudos to the pastry chef!

Normally, I don’t write reviews, but this place truly deserves to be praised.

A small suggestion — it would be even better if the background music featured some traditional Indian music to better match the restaurant’s vibe and ambience. Perhaps incorporating more Indian-inspired decorations, or even staff wearing Indian-inspired attire, would make the dining experience feel even more immersive and enhance the story telling behind the cuisines .

Will definitely be recommending this to friends and family!

The best of Singapore's Michelin 2-stars I tried — and I went in skeptical.
Cloudstreet got blacklisted. Meta was solid. Thevar genuinely surprised me.
Indian-influenced fusion that actually earns the label — the spice work is confident without being overwhelming, and it feels locally rooted without being a gimmick. About two-thirds of the menu was excellent. The shirako with Indian seasoning was an unexpected highlight — didn't think I'd see that combination work, but it did. The chicken naan taco with that filling? Really good.
Second half dropped off a bit — the grilled squid ran too salty (even for someone who’s drinking an entire bottle of wine alone 🧐) and the spiced lamb was too gamey for me. High opening, slightly uneven landing.
Practical tip: book the kitchen counter!! You're literally sitting inside the kitchen watching the pass — full Chef's Table experience, no surcharge.

The sommelier is also delightful, which helped smooth over the wobbles in the back half of the menu.
Already booked second return 🥰🥰

We decided to book a table to celebrate my mom’s birthday the other day — and it was an excellent choice!

The meal started off beautifully with three snacks, each one bursting with flavor and absolutely delicious. The fish course was fantastic — perfectly cooked with crispy scales and a delicious sauce that brought everything together. The lamb was just as impressive — tender, flavorful, and cooked to perfection.

But dessert… oh man, it was truly memorable! From the first dessert to the very last bite, every element hit the spot — sweet, sour, refreshing, and beautifully presented. You could really tell how much thought went into balancing the flavors.

We’ll definitely be back to try the new menu. Highly recommend!
Fancy but not approachable
Incredible modern indian dishes with all the range of flavors

Indian Fine Dining!  Not to be missed if you love Indian Cuisine. Those fine Indian spices used in new and different ways. Maybe the best rack of lamb I've ever had.  Great staff, very helpful with tourists, very fun evening.

Managed to secure an evening for private dining and the service from the staff was as impeccable as always. They helped to make the evening a very memorable one and every dish that was served was flawless as always. While the flavor profile might not be suitable for everyone, everyone that evening had an amazing time. One of the best Michelin starred restaurant in Singapore.

Had to literally eat the meal in pain.

Booked the restaurant for a birthday celebration but woke up the day before with severe neck pain, swallowing food was painful. Called the restaurant to reschedule the meal but was told a hard no and would lose the full fees.

The food is mediocre, more effort on the presentation than the actual taste. For the price point, the ingredients are disappointing. Duck, fish, lamb, really nothing out of the ordinary. Service was stuffy and cold.

This restaurant has no care for its customers. It’s more concerned about bottom lines and profits. How long will it last?
best piece of fish i ever had I’ll be thinking about it for a while.
This restaurant will certainly achieve 3-stars in the Michelin guide. The food is a fascinating fusion of cultures with only the very best ingredients.

Vegetarian set menu.
Exceptional food, bold flavours, and flawless execution. Thevar truly lives up to its Michelin star….
I spl loved dhokla bambooshoots white lshtu

Booked the private dining room for a corporate event and unfortunately a team member is down with influenza and yes the cancellation is within 72 hours.  But the restaurant should have looked into case to case basis.  It’s for a team of 6 members.  Called the restaurant but to no avail.  Sent a whatsapp message to urgently cancel the booking but no return call from any of the staff.  Only received a cancellation note to say that the cancellation is less than 72 hours therefore there will be a cancellation charge.  I find it totally ridiculous!  Cancellation charge is extremely expensive for a team member of 6 which amounts to SGD 2K plus.  That is easy money for them.

The least they could do is return my call and speak to me to explain or have some alternative method to see what can be done.

Anyway, will feeback to my boss about this.  So if you are planning on any function and utilise the function room, please think twice in case of any unforeseen circumstances that would come up.

Thevar deserves recognition beyond its current two Michelin stars. This fine dining establishment, under the leadership of Chef Mano Thevar and his exceptional team, offers an extraordinary culinary experience. Their passion for blending diverse spices with exquisite cuisine is truly palpable. Notably, Chef Thevar's generosity was evident when he honored his cleaner with a Michelin-level meal in their exclusive second-floor dining area. We were immensely impressed by the food, ambiance, and service, ranking Thevar among the top three Michelin restaurants we've experienced, surpassing even some three-star Michelin establishments in Singapore. We look forward to returning and thank Chef Thevar and his team for making our dinner and birthday celebration truly unforgettable.

Absolutely amazing experience.
We had a dinner here and I concluded that this was the best meal I had in very long time.
Loved the intricate menu, the humble & knowledgeable staff, the chef is very very talented and he deserves every star and more!
We will be back soon!

This is my second visit, and the snacks (appetizers) are just as tasty as my first visit. Decided to leave a review instantly because the Amadai dish was simply exceptional!🥺

I highly recommend Thevar. They should definitely be awarded a 3-star Michelin rating in future. Chef Mano Thevar was also very friendly and came over to check with us if everything was in order.
My husband and I have been here three times now and it never disappoints! Each dish was excellent and the service was flawless. The team are great and hospitable.

The meal was a whole new spin on Indian food and ingredients. Each course was exquisitely presented and brimming with flavour.

If you are celebrating a special occasion, the marsala chai tart is delightful. Rich in texture with hints of chai.

Superb dining experience at Thevar last night. The young chef himself joined us for a chat - proudly Malaysian, warm and so down to earth for someone holding two Michelin stars. Every course was delectable and faultless! P.S. The crispy bread was one of the best croissant-style pastries I've had.

Fabulous, just fabulous. Visited in November’25 for a dinner. Best dinner in whole Asia in this year. Perfect balance of spices with amazing texture and outstanding mixture of ingredients. Wine recommendation worked like magic with the food. Looking to revisit in 2026. Wow!

Came here for lunch. Very interesting blend of Japanese food items cooked with Indian spices in a French style with Penang influences. Weekday lunch meant lower traffic and very attentive service. Especially loved any dish with fish and the octopus tail. The recommendation is to have the wine pairing, but we declined as we were still nursing a hangover from the previous night. Good experience, delicious food, great service.

We had a lovely lunch at Thevar to celebrate my husband's birthday. The food was refined in presentation but bold in flavours and textures, with the "Chicken roti" a personal favourite. We opted for the king crab supplement and it was a good choice with the smokiness of the rice pairing well with the delicate king crab and broth.

Service was warm and attentive, with the sommelier Elgine taking wonderful care of us all afternoon. The rest of the front of house team was also excellent. If I had to give any suggestions for improvement, it would be that I thought desserts could be stronger (not that what was served was not good but rather the rest of the meal was so outstanding that dessert - a muskmelon payasam, felt a tad ordinary in comparison).

All in all a most enjoyable experience and we are already planning a return visit. Bravo!
Fresh ingredients delicate cuisine with great hospitality to details. We will def go back

Chef Mano never fails to surprise you despite the absolutely highest standards he maintains. Not a place to miss for a very special Indian dinner with a delightful blend of western and Japanese elements.

Thevar is elevated Indian cuisine. I changed my impression of Indian food completely. Every dish a delicately prepared and the Indian spices (which you can taste in every bite) does not overpower the freshness of the ingredients used. It was a great meal.

Flavorful, refined - elevated Indian cooking yet still so comforting and familiar. The chicken roti and lamb biryani were excellent and I’d go back even just for those 2 dishes alone.

Chef Mano was so nice and accommodating too
Simple flavorful and tender chicken. So good and balanced. Rice is great too!

I’ve tried chicken rice at several spots around Singapore, and while Tian Tian is good, I wouldn’t call it the best. The stall is clearly well‑established, professional, efficient, and run like a finely tuned operation but it doesn’t have the charm or character of a smaller setup.

If you’re eating at Maxwell, my recommendation would actually be Ai Tai rather than Tian Tian. Tian Tian’s flavors are solid, but Ai Tai offers a better balance and overall taste in my opinion. Their chicken has a slightly firmer texture in a really satisfying way and the seasoning feels more harmonious.

Of course, it’s worth trying both and forming your own opinion, but for me, Ai Tai is the standout.
