They definitely don’t maintain the taste and quality of the food. It’s getting worse.
Great quick meal with the locals. TTH is a must for good top rated chicken and rice.

Honestly, it was just above average. The chicken was tender and the rice was fragrant, but nothing really stood out as exceptional. The flavors felt a bit mild, and the chili sauce didn’t have the punch I was expecting given all the hype.

Considering its reputation and long queues, I expected something memorable. In comparison, the chicken rice at a Bishan coffee shop I frequent actually tastes better, more flavorful rice, juicier chicken, and a more balanced sauce. Overall, this felt overrated for what it is.

All the meat was tasted excellent, the shao rou skin was extremely crispy while the meat remained tender, the char siew was soft on the insides and just the right amount of crisp on the outer layer, the duck was moist and the skin just amazing to bite into, both textures and taste pairing to create something absolutely smashing.
The egg pairs well with the meal although it sells out fast I'd suggest going in the early morning, I find the yolk pairs with the rice well and the whites the meat.
While the sauce has a rich and in depth tasting flavor that can't be found anywhere else, believe me I've tried.
The owners are extremely nice people and get stuff done quickly and efficiently while maintaining excellent quality, theyre truly friendly people and it especially shows in how they interact with their regular customers.t
The environment gives a nostalgic childhood hawker experience and the flavors of the food take you there, especially for me.
Prices are as friendly as the people, truly a wonderful establishment as shown in their many achievements.

Duck was fantastic.

Generous portions and reasonable price of $5.30 for roast meat, char siew and an egg. So delicious! Crispy pork belly, sweet savoury charred char siew meat. Perfect with their chilli on the side.

Ordered duck, roast meat, char Siew and chicken for 3 person. $31+ for 3 person. Tasted ok but feel that it's slightly expensive. What takes away the stars is the service. I’m up early today to join the long snaking queue at Tien Lai Rice Stall which started forming way before lunch hour.
This stall serves an awesome roast duck with delightful glistening, crispy skin and succulent meat! And definitely one of my favourite picks for takeaway at Taman Jurong food centre. 🫶🏻
Char siew rice is superb

My usual go to for roast meat but today char siew was bit over cooked dried n tough, still otherwise still value for $ comfort food

Roast duck, meat was soft, tasty. Chili enhanced the flavour.

Definitely a place to come again.

Very nice decent plate of roasted pork belly and char siew. Portion size was good enough for me. Really liked the lean and nicely charred char siew and the crispy pork belly was very crispy! Skin is super crispy and tasty! Had way more meat than rice so it’s quite worth it. Added an egg and the total cost was $5.30. Price wise is also reasonable!

The queue never stops so make sure you come early!
Went early to queue up to try this stall for the first time. Otherwise, the queue and wait will be pretty long. Quite delicious and traditional but prefer to have more fats in the char siew.

One of the better roasts meat stalls in the west, there is always a queue but it moves quickly. My favorite is the char siew with roast duck combo, and the nice gravy. $5.50.  Even da bao home eat also taste great.

Excellent Cantonese-style roasted meats.

I tried their roast duck, char siew, and roast pork.

The roasted pork still had a crispy skin. It had a good ratio between meat and fats.

The roast duck was very good. The skin still had some crispiness. The meat was still moist and was tender.

The char siew was generally leaner - but it was tender and was nicely seasoned.

Do expect a bit of wait during peak lunch time.

Damn good siu mei at a damn good price; Tien Lai has always been on my bucket list and I finally got to try it one rainy weekday morning.

As I was really hungry, I went for a trifecta of roast duck, char siu and siu yuk, you know, the full works. And it was really amazing. The roast duck and siu yuk had a nice and crispy layer of skin, and the char siu was perfectly balanced between fatty and lean mean.

The perpetual queue here is a testament to how good they are, and they try to be really quick in dishing out each plate of rice. I would highly recommend this place for your siu mei fix.
First time tried the roast pork n char siew. Portion was ok. Tasty n nice.

Even at 9.30am on a weekday and raining to boot, there was already a queue all the way to the elevator. Bought mix of char siew, roast pork belly and roast duck. The char siew is more KL styled which is sweeter and more charred. Goes very well with the sour chicken rice chilli sauce. The roast pork was a bit too fatty for my liking but the crackling was very crispy. Roast duck was smoky and juicy. But I think the MVP must be their rice. Here you get chicken flavoured rice instead of plain rice. It goes so well with their chilli sauce that is so piquant and pack just the right amount of heat.

Pro tip: if you want duck drumsticks, you’d better come early or call ahead to reserve. These run out very quickly cause there are a lot of orders for half and whole ducks.

The duck is one of the best I have eaten!
Crispy skin, juicy meats, succulent all around and pairs will with the different chillis. Got fatty bits which some may or may not like...

Roast duck and char siew pale slightly sightly in comparison with the duck.
Rice is also not bad with the gravy.

Will come to eat again if the queue is not so long.
Was free enough to join in the queue. Maybe i had too high an expectation but it tasted pretty ordinary. Had better roasted pork and char siew less the queue so this isnt worth the wait for me.

Have alway wanted to try this stall for the longest of time. Finally managed to find a day on weekday to come Taman Jurong Food Centre. This stall is well known for their roast items like Charsiew, roast duck and roast meat. There was already a long queue when i reached, there was at least 15pax ahead of me. Queued for almost 25mins before it was my turn to order.

Ordered the charsiew rice which was SGD$4. The portion of the meat was quite generous to be honest. Charsiew was nicely roasted, there are bits of char and charsiew is more on the sweet side. Their chili also deserved a mention, it goes really well with the charsiew.

Overall, the food was fantastic. The roast duck looks equally fabalous, wouldnt mind trying the next time round. I would definitely recoomend this stall if you dont mind the long queue.
Famous at Taman Jurong, its always long queue. They sell from 9am, by 11am or before 12pm will sold out. Everything is tasty! Note they dun open on Fri or Sat.
Decent , chili could b abit spicer though

Restaurant Name: Tiong Bahru Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
Reviews: Very decent plate of chicken rice though it’s not something I would queue a long time for. Rice is flavourful. Chicken is tender. Chilli sauce and ginger sauce is very ordinary. The pickled veggies doesn’t add to the dish in anyway, doesn’t provide any interesting flavour. I would think they are a distraction and should be removed. Still not too shabby a dish overall.

Restaurant Name: Tiong Bahru Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
Reviews:
This stall always has a queue during lunch hours… weekends even longer. But service staff is fast, so I only waited about 20mins…
It’s been close to 6yrs since I last had this stall. Frankly, I personally felt the standard has dropped.  The rice is still flavorful, chilli sauce is now a tad sweeter (maybe to suit more tourists), and the ginger sauce is very watery.
The only plus point: they offers value for money. The meat portion is generous!  And they don’t flatten the meat with the cleaver. (Which is good!!)
The rice portion is also huge… so much so I have to ask for half portion of rice. (Pls see my pic)

I personally feel there are many stalls offers as good if not better than this stall. Eg.  ‘Stall 169’ at Chinatown Food Complex/ Mkt.
No right or wrong… but I prefer the latter.

Restaurant Name: Tiong Bahru Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
Reviews:
My hunt for Singapore’s top 5 Hainanese chicken rice continues…

- Proper crockeries and cutleries to eat from, not plastic nor plates made from paper
- reasonably priced, generous portion from seeing other’s orders. I bought a whole chicken - half for lunch and the other half to takeaway for dinner.
- chicken was tender and skin was lean, not fatty hence no feelings of guilt when I ate the skin 😁 it comes with a bowl of soup which is not oily nor salty.
- the queue moved quickly therefore not too long a wait
- staff (possibly the boss) was engaging and friendly unlike the other place I have frequented for over a decade and till date, still greets you with a long face

Family gave the thumbs up. Said this is better than the joint we used to go to 😄 Looks like we will return for more.

Restaurant Name: Tiong Bahru Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
Reviews: 3.8 for small, 4.8 for large portion. This is the large portion and I feel it's worth the money. Soup is not bad, chilli is the standard type of chilli where it's sweet and not that spicy. Rice is fragrant enough and chicken is tender and smooth. Worth a revisit !

Reviews: One of my most favorite chicken rice in Singapore. The tofu is good too

First visit to this kway chap stall in Old Airport Food Centre. Ordered myself a $8 portion and one bowl of kway for $1. This stall does not offer braised duck nor pig's head, but serves pig trotter instead.

Stall opens on Tues to Sat, operates between 10am to 2pm, long queue shows its popularity. Note CNY opening days will vary. Unit number 01-135.

Though Google maps says stall closed at 3pm, please don’t go before it closes as I was the lucky last customer the lady accepted and I arrived around 155pm. The customer behind me got turned away politely by the lady but the uncle cook gestured that he is good for one more but the lady disagreed but went ahead to accept him anyway. Ultra decent plate of braised pig innards and a comforting bowl of Kuay chap. The flavour to the ingredients on the plate were deep and filled with umami. Though there were hints of the usual acquired taste of innards, much more obvious on the intestines, the powerful chilli sauce did its job to mask it and bring the ingredients together. Good old school taste on a high level! These two couple running the show are very old and they are masters of their trade. Fortunate to have the opportunity to have a taste of that mastery. Price is on the high side though but I think it’s definitely worth it as I wouldn’t consider this an everyday kind of meal.

14 Jan 2026 Wednesday
11:35am queued till Noon

25 minute queue but not surprising since it’s only the one uncle doing the chopping and one aunty working as fast as she can, by taking orders and collecting money from those behind in the queue, plus a few customers with large orders for takeaway.

Food is braised well, the intestine head (they named it Bung, sounds unappealing in English, but do a direct translation, sounds better as “head”) was cleaned very well, no odour. Uncle gave me the fattier cuts as I requested, and he was amused that I specifically asked for them.  Good to banter with him, he said I know the best parts of the pig.  *Laugh gently*

Our order consisted of streaky pork, intestine head (they won’t sell you just large intestines as they have limited amounts, and they have to save it for those who order the sets), 2 braised eggs (nothing exceptional about those) and a tau pok (fried Beancurd puffs)

Also ordered a side of salted vegetables which was pretty good, boiled till incredibly soft, and slightly salty, perfect to cut through the fattiness.

Including 2 bowls of kway, our meal cost $23. Reasonable to me for having to clean intestines so well.  We were VERY full & tummies contented!

Uncle, I respect your work, but please also show some basic respect to your customers. Customers don’t owe you anything😅

To-Ricos Guo Shi is a popular kway chap stall located at Old Airport Road Food Centre in Singapore. Known for its Michelin Bib Gourmand award, it serves traditional Teochew-style kway chap—broad rice noodles in a light, savory broth, paired with tender braised pork belly, pig intestines, stomach, tofu, and eggs. Diners praise the clean taste of the offal and the richness of the soup. Open from Wednesday to Saturday, it draws long queues, especially during lunch. Just a short walk from Dakota MRT, To-Ricos is a must-visit for authentic, comforting Singaporean hawker food done with care and consistency.

We were greeted by a staff member named Khairul. No smile on the face though. As our children were hungry, I politely asked if we could view the menu and place our order while waiting for the table. I was told that the menu was only available outside and was asked to step out to check it.

However, after we were seated, I noticed that all menus were placed under the reception table where Khairul was standing. I asked him why we were previously asked to go outside to view the menu, but no clear or reasonable explanation was provided.

This interaction felt unnecessary and unaccommodating, particularly given that the restaurant was not busy and we were dining with young children. A little flexibility and clearer communication would have made a significant difference to our experience.

I am sharing this feedback in the hope that it will be taken constructively and help improve service standards going forward.

Restaurant Name: Tow Kwar Pop Tiong Bahru Market
Reviews:
Rojak in its truest, most glorious form! This plate is a beautiful chaos of textures and flavours that somehow come together in perfect harmony. The crunch of barbecued crispy cutterfish, fried dough (youtiao) and crispy fried bean curd (tow kua) meets the refreshing bite of cucumber, apple, and pineapple. Everything is generously coated in a rich prawn paste sauce, with a kick of chilli on the side if you’re feeling adventurous.

The crushed peanuts sprinkled on top add just the right nuttiness, while the shaved cuttlefish and fried crackers bring extra crunch. Every bite is sweet, savoury, tangy, and just a little spicy — a quintessential taste of Singapore that balances tradition with boldness.

If you’ve never had rojak, this Singaporean traditional dish is a must-try for the way it captures the soul of local street food: messy, vibrant, and unforgettable.

True Blue Peranakan is a restaurant where the ambience arguably plays a larger role than the food itself.
The setting in Central is undeniably beautiful, thoughtfully curated to showcase Peranakan culture. It’s an easy place to bring foreign friends or out-of-town guests if the goal is to impress visually and offer a cultural narrative alongside the meal.
That said, the overall dining experience felt slightly hurried. The flow of service moved at a brisk, almost transactional pace, which made it difficult to fully settle into the meal or linger over the dishes. There was a constant sense of being moved along rather than encouraged to dine at leisure.
Portion sizes were also noticeably modest. The staff checked in frequently on whether the dishes were “sufficient for four,” which subtly highlighted how restrained the servings were — and the restaurant appeared quite unapologetic about this. While the food itself was genuinely tasty and well-executed, the portions did not quite align with the premium pricing.
In terms of flavour, nothing was poorly done. The dishes were enjoyable and balanced, but not dramatically more refined than what you might find elsewhere. Given that prices are approximately 20% higher than comparable Peranakan establishments, the value proposition becomes harder to justify.
Overall, True Blue Peranakan works best as a destination for atmosphere and presentation rather than indulgence. If you’re dining to savour bold flavours and generous portions, there are more satisfying options, may want to check around.
A pleasant experience, certainly — just one that prioritises polish and pace over comfort and abundance.

Ushidoki offers an exceptional Wagyu omakase experience featuring the rare and exquisite Ozaki Beef, straight from the farm of Mr. Muneharu Ozaki in Miyazaki Prefecture. What sets Ozaki Beef apart is the meticulous care and unique approach Mr. Ozaki takes in raising his cattle. Unlike typical Wagyu, which is usually slaughtered around 28 months, Mr. Ozaki allows his cattle to mature up to 32-36 months, enhancing the beef’s depth and complexity.

The flavor profile of Ozaki Beef at Ushidoki is incredibly balanced. The beef is less fatty compared to other Wagyu varieties, thanks to a specialized feeding regimen in the final months of the cattle’s life. This careful preparation delivers a taste that’s rich and savory yet not overwhelming – a perfect harmony that lets you savor every bite without feeling heavy.

The omakase journey at Ushidoki is an absolute delight, guided by chefs who are both skilled and passionate about showcasing the uniqueness of Ozaki Beef. Each course felt like a masterpiece, highlighting the beef’s nuanced flavors with creativity and precision. Highly recommend Ushidoki for anyone looking to experience an unforgettable Wagyu adventure!

Welcoming the Year of the Fire Horse, Carlton Hotel Singapore presents a thoughtfully curated Lunar New Year experience centred on heartfelt reunions, auspicious flavours and timeless traditions. At the heart of the celebration is Wah Lok Cantonese Restaurant, where heritage Cantonese cuisine meets elegant festive dining.

A cornerstone of Lunar New Year celebrations, the reunion meal takes centre stage at Wah Lok. Known for its culinary legacy and refined Cantonese craftsmanship, the restaurant offers eight auspicious Lunar New Year set menus, starting from $88 per person, available from 9 February to 3 March 2026.

Each menu is meticulously designed to symbolise abundance, harmony, health and prosperity, making it ideal for multi-generational family gatherings and meaningful festive reunions. Set within a warm and elegant dining environment, Wah Lok continues to be a trusted choice for traditional celebrations elevated with finesse.

Debuting this season are two standout offerings:
Abalone Eight Treasure Duck ($208)
A luxurious centrepiece featuring slow-braised duck with abalone, sea cucumber, conpoy, pork, chestnut, mushroom and lotus seed. Rich in flavour and symbolism, the dish embodies unity and prosperity.
Sea Cucumber White Bait Lo Hei ($108 / $148)
A refined interpretation of the festive classic, bringing together auspicious ingredients and layered textures for joyful tossing and shared moments.

For celebrations beyond the restaurant, Carlton Hotel Singapore presents a refined range of Lunar New Year takeaways, thoughtfully crafted for home reunions and premium gifting. Pre-orders run from now to 10 February 2026, with collection and delivery available from 19 January to 16 February 2026.

With its well-curated menu, stylish ambience, and excellent service, Wakuda feels like an elevated izakaya.

Food was great all around. We had the Lobster Quinoa set, sukiyaki (ala carte), and Big Eye Tuna to start. Every dish felt thoughtfully done with high-quality, fresh ingredients.

The sukiyaki stood out—beautifully presented and made with Kagoshima wagyu that was very tender with minimal fat. The sauce was rich but well balanced by the egg yolk. A nice twist was the shishito peppers at the base, which added an unexpected but pleasant touch.

The Lobster Quinoa was also a highlight. Cooked in a style similar to Japanese garlic fried rice, but the quinoa gave it more texture and little bursts of bite. Lobster meat was generous and sweet.

Service deserves a special mention. The reception ladies were warm and cheerful, and the service staff were attentive, polite, and genuinely friendly without being intrusive.

I’d noted it was a birthday during reservation (didn’t expect anything), and was pleasantly surprised with a complimentary tiramisu. It looked great and tasted even better—honestly enjoyed it more than the banana cake from the set meal.

Overall, a great spot whether for a casual meal or a special occasion. Solid food, top service, and good value for money.

Wakuda, located in the lobby of Marina Bay Sands, conceptualized by Michelin star Chef Tetsuya Wakuda is more than just a restaurant; it’s a stunning architectural and culinary experience. I had their weekday set menu which included Appetizers, Main Course, and Dessert (definitely great value). For Appetizers, I had their Savory Egg Custard with Caviar, Egg Tofu, and Garden Salad. For Main Course, it was a Sushi platter. And dessert was chef special Mango Mascarpone Sorbet.
Stepping into Wakuda is immediately transporting. The award-winning design by Rockwell Group masterfully blends traditional Japanese craftsmanship—particularly the use of intricate kumiko wood joinery and natural stone—with a sleek, contemporary, and almost buzzing energy reminiscent of Shinjuku.
The menu at Wakuda is extensive, offering an à la carte selection spanning appetizers, sashimi, sushi, tempura, rice bowls, and grilled yakimono. While the price point is definitely premium (expect to spend S100–S200+ per person without drinks, and significantly more for the Omakase), the quality of the ingredients. Wakuda boasts an impressive bar and lounge area, making it a great place for pre- or post-dinner drinks. Best for: Special occasions, corporate dinners, or high-end date nights #Wakuda #MarinaBay #Michelin #Japanese #Omakase

A Wine Dinner brings me to Whitegrass! With so many choices of excellent restaurants, I set my sights on Whitegrass after a recommendation by a wine expert from Wine to Style. And the name of the restaurant does evoke the image of light yet vibrant cuisine, which really got me excited to try food here.

And the food is really light and vibrant as I have hoped. The French dishes here are unique in taste, being light on the palates while showcasing a myriad of well-balanced flavours. I’m totally impressed. In addition, the flavours reflect the mellow earthiness of autumn. Now I’m excited to see what Chef Takuya Yamashita has in store for winter.

The interior of the place also features this light and vibrant element. White walls and ceiling, white translucent curtains, a centrepiece of white chandelier suspended over a huge pot of floral arrangement and a vase of flowers and greenery on each table, all come together to create an elegant and modern space.

The service here is absolutely wonderful, immaculate and thoughful, taking note of little details. Winne and Wei Yi are such wonderful hosts. This is definitely a place that is worth a special visit.

For the first time, I’m trying lobster with Turnip sauce with Yuzu jelly, and it is oh-so-good. This is definitely the most refreshing tasting lobster dish. And the Canadian lobster actually gets sweeter with subsequent bites. The cool vegetal taste of turnip is match made in heaven with the lobster. The crunchiness of sliced turnip in the salad adds to the texture. Definitely my favourite dish of the night.

The quartet of appetisers exploring different faucets of taste, where:

The Braised Abalone here surprises me with how light and refreshing it tastes yet briny sweet at the same time. This is so great as starter to whet the appetite and anticipate the next dish with eagerness.

Next up is Foie gras puree with Shaoxing wine. This is so good too. The taste is creamy savoury umami that is surprisingly easy on the palates.

Red tomato with green tomato paste yields the taste of Italian tangy sweetness. So simulating yet well-balanced in taste.

Sweet potato topped with truffle has this rich vegetal nutty sweetness, which tastes a bit like meat, which is made even more exciting by earthy aroma of truffle.

Smoked salted butter goes perfectly with the served warm Foccacia, which is super airy, fluffy and crispy. The sweetness of wheat develops the more I chew on it. This is one excellent bread.

Hirame, usually known for clean briny sweetness, surprises me by how earthy good this dish is. The shaved cheese and beetroot sauce add complexity to the taste, where the aroma of nuts is balanced by the mild vegetal sweetness of beetroot.

Zucchini dish here demonstrates how to make zucchini taste exciting. A section of the zucchini is coated with a super thin coat of deep fried batter, yielding a refreshing crunchiness that is harmonised by the creaminess of cream cheese and briny sweetness of caviar.

Hokkaido scallop soaked in chicken mushroom sauce and topped with truffle has this deep complex earthy sweetness complex. Absolutely mesmerising taste.

Angel prawn dumpling is like the best dumpling I ever have. With citrusy, tangy, creamy yuzu kosyo, the Ebi wrapped in this thin smooth skin tastes so exciting and unique. Simply awesome.

Spanish mackerel paired with tomato and mushroom is juicy, firm and amazingly sweet. I love this too.

Shiga A4 Wagyu is so juicy and meaty. It also features a tender good bite. Tastes even sweeter when paired with the Japanese sauce and pickles.

Truffle pudding and pear work together so brilliantly. It is dessert perfection. The pudding is smooth in texture and has an intense earthy aroma balanced by a touch of floral tangy taste of the pear.

Thoughts: Exceptional, Well Thought-out Dining Experience

I've always wanted to try a proper Michelin star restaurant to see what it is all about. Got the opportunity to try it for a special occasion.

There are 2 set courses to choose from. Decided to try both. Service was exceptional as well, and the staff was mindful with the pacing of the dishes. Amazing experience. Damage was ~S$300++ per pax. Would I patronise it frequently? Probably not. But for special occasions, definitely a yes.

A big thank you to the whole crew especially Winnie and Wei Yi for their warm and attentive service throughout the evening, they made us feel so well taken care of. And of course, compliments to the chef for the amazing gastronomic journey, every dish was beautifully presented and full of flavor.

From the amuse bouche to the final dessert, everything was crafted with such finesse. It was truly an unforgettable dining experience. Thank you to the team of Whitegrass, for making my wife’s birthday celebration such a memorable one!!!

"<One Michelin Star>
*** White Grass @ CHIJMES ***
[minimum of $98++ per person]
•Set Lunch @ 1200 to 1430, Tuesday to Saturday
•Reservations require Credit Card deposit
•Restaurant does accept walk-ins though
•Empty for weekday lunch; busy on weekends
•WiFi available and free iced water
•Smart casual attire

[Directions] City Hall MRT, Exit A. Turn left and then turn right, alongside the perimeter of Raffles City. CHIJMES is across the road, directly to the left. White Grass is deep within the strip mall as part of a standalone building, directly to starboard of CHIJMES.

[Overall] The food is excellent, while the portions are fairly small, as is customary for fine dining. Service, atmosphere and deco are all similarly excellent.

It is quite expensive, even for the set lunch. But I think it is a worthwhile experience, just not an everyday meal. Their menu changes on the first Tuesday of every odd month.

-------------- $98++ Lunch Menu (Sep and Oct 2025) --------------

[Appetiser 1] The appetiser plate is good and looks quite cute. The complimentary white bread and its butter is good as well. Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. I hate the other complimentary brown bread that has nuts inside, but to be fair, I simply hate nuts. You may request for both bread to be the white bread.

[Appetiser 2] The tuna sashimi tastes decent, but is inferior to that at a dedicated Japanese sushi restaurant (obviously). I myself find the premium super-expensive tuna ($2 per tiny piece) at Donki to be better, actually. The sweet potato soup is good. It has foam on top and it looks kinda fun.

[Main Dish] The braised Wagyu beef is good, sorta like Chinese braised pork. The cabbage is arranged as if it is a flower; pretty. The Fish with Lobster was good, and the lobster itself was exceptional. I did not order the French Chicken, since it seems less expensive.

[Dessert] The first ice-cream is decent. Its topping is quite sour by itself, so you should eat it together with the rest of the ice-cream. The second ice-cream is Earl Grey flavour and tastes intriguing. The mochi, served alongside a pastry within a wooden box, is decent. I actually liked the pastry more.

-------------- $158++ Lunch Menu (Sep and Oct 2025) --------------

[Appetiser 1] The appetiser plate is pretty. The Sturgeon Caviar tastes good and is very expensive, accompanied by literal flakes of gold. The item on the spoon has a slighty meaty taste and is good. The bottom item is rather sweet, considering it is an appetiser. The top item has a crust with a strong meaty flavour and is good. Complimentary white bread was served.

[Appetiser 2] The raw salmon was excellent.

[Appetiser 3] The lobster was exceptional, nicely cooked with firm flesh. I rather disliked the spicy pumpkin-and-peanut sauce though; would rather have the traditional butter as condiment. Complimentary brown bread was served.

[Main Dish 1] The fish was excellent, despite its meh look. I rather disliked the mushroom though, which disintegrated as I ate it. Even though this softness was intended by the chef, I do not agree with this.

[Main Dish 2] The Wagyu beef steak was exceptional and its fat literally melted in my mouth. Correctly cooked as medium-rare. I rather disliked the condiment of green tomato paste with little seeds as it is quite weird.

[Dessert] The first ice-cream is decent and the same as for the $98++ menu. The second ice-cream is good and very pretty. The mochi and pastry are good, and the same as for the $98++ menu."

For a one-star restaurant, the Friday/Saturday lunch pricing is actually quite reasonable. Definitely a good way to experience Willow without committing to a full dinner tasting. I’d come back again, maybe to try the $138++ menu next time.

Michelin-starred Willow has recently reopened after a revamp of their beautiful space over at Hong Kong Street.

With a newly launched Spring menu that boasts innovative dishes with local flair, such as their Ebi - an interesting take on the rice noodle roll, also known as "Chee Cheong Fun" - you can surely be impressed by the intricate yet delicate flavours of each dish from Willow.

A culinary masterpiece where impeccable artistry meets the finest ingredients🍜👨‍🍳. Each dish offers a symphony of flavor, delivered with intuitive service🥂👨🏻‍💼. It is a truly memorable, transcendent experience worthy of a special journey.🍽🍷

Had such a lovely time at Willow! The menu was creative, unique, and every dish was well-executed. The staff and service were detailed and attentive and you can really tell there’s care behind each dish.

They just launched their new spring menu last month and we decided to drop by to try out their lunch menu on a Friday worth $98++ ! It’s amazing value for a one Michelin star restaurant and for the quality you’re getting.

Would highly recommend and come back again :)

I dropped by Willow with my partner on a Saturday to try their spring menu and it was honestly such a highlight!

We went with the $98++ lunch menu (they have a $138++ one too I believe) and I thought it was super worth it, especially for a one Michelin star resto.

Chose the ebi dish as my main course and it was so yummy. It’s served like a cheong fun - rice roll is incredibly soft and silky, and the ebi flavor was so well balanced.

The chefs was super knowledgeable and explained each dish with so much confidence, and the staff were all very attentive too. Such a great experience and definitely recommended! (It’s always a good idea to pamper yourself with good food 😬)
Great ambience. Food are amazing and very attentive service.
Wonderful new seasonal menu, newly renovated space with a lovely ambience.
Willow is unique in its own way, Had the wine pairing and i could say it was the best meal i had so far. Food and wine were so outstanding that every course was made to be paired beautifully.
Always enjoy visiting Willow, food is stellar and service is welcoming. Definitely worth a visit!
Visited for dinner, Attractive location, friendly staff's. foods served on time, very satisfactory dinner

Had a wonderful dining experience at Willow Restaurant. The food was beautifully presented and every dish was thoughtfully crafted with delicate flavours and great balance. We had counter service and it was attentive and knowledgeable. We went before they underwent renovations and the ambience was elegant yet comfortable.

A wonderful place where price is affordable  and the food is delicious, suitable for any occasion  a real delight for young and old. Service is really exceptional with its efficient and courteous staff. Highly recommended because of its impeccable service.

Service is amazing👌 with good quality food... 😋
Service and Atmosphere is very good...

Overall, it’s definitely worth the trip back. I’ll gladly return and recommend this place to friends and family. Great food, great service, great experience. 👍

I thoroughly enjoyed my experience at Willow. The presentation was excellent, and the interaction with the chefs made the meal especially engaging. The portions were generous—I actually felt pleasantly full, which is more than I can say for many other restaurants. The ambience and overall setup were also very well done. I will definitely be back.
food was great and the atmosphere was comfortable. The staff were friendly. Great place to enjoy a good meal and celebrate special moments.
Great food , like the ambience, worth trying!

definitely worth a visit. every course beautifully plated and makes my wife very happy on our date night. we had a counter seat and staff explains very well on every dish they serve. it was delicious.
celebrated my friend's birthday at Willow and we received a special curated birthday dessert! it was perfect and food was super good. worth spending your special dates there.

The beef hor fun here truly brings back the old-school Cantonese wok hei that’s hard to find nowadays. The noodles are perfectly stir-fried with that signature smoky aroma, nicely caramelised soy sauce, and tender slices of beef. You can really taste the skill behind the wok — fragrant, slightly charred, and full of depth.

At just $6, it’s incredible value for money. Generous portion, authentic flavour, and satisfying from the first bite to the last. Definitely worth the visit if you appreciate traditional Cantonese-style cooking. Highly recommended!

Pretty good beef horfun. Horfun full of wok-hei but the beef slice could do with lesser starch power coated on it. Portion was moderate with upsize option on both the horfun and beef separately. However, to upsize both the cost is pretty much like buying 2 plates.

Lukewarm food. Ordered the pork hor fan. Just separately cooked hor fan and gravy mix together and refried for a couple of minutes. No hint of wok hei flavour in the dish. Tasted bland to me. The pork lard was a nice touch and had texture to the food.

Congrats on being included in the Michelin Guide! We have been buying from this stall for many years but in our take out today, all the boxes had some black or burnt bits in the gravy. We hope the team can take more care in food preparation.

Came at 15mins to 8pm on a weekday and their famous hor fun was not available. Tried their bee hoon instead. The stock they used is good and so are their ingredients. Saw many customers walked away when informed no more hor fun. Need to come another round to try out.
Sharing a nice delicious ‘hor fun’ , this stall serve very delicious ’wok hei hor fun’, 😋😋😋 the beef was tender and the sticky gravy was tasty good, they do include crispy pork lard 👍👍👍

I like it!

4⭐️(can try if pass by) ok quality hor fun.
Ordered the beef hor fun. The portion of beef is generous, and while the beef isn’t exceptional, it’s decent overall. The hor fun and broth have an acceptable flavor. A solid, ok quality dish worth trying if you’re nearby.
The Sliced Fish Hor Fun was good and had a wok hei taste.

Restaurant Name: Xing Yun Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
Reviews:
I have been a regular and devoted customer of the Xing Yun Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice stall at Blk 347, Jurong East (Yuhua) for many years, and the quality has remained exceptionally high.

​The rice is truly top-tier, perfectly fragrant and flavorful. Combined with their legendary chilli—which is without a doubt, best-in-class—it reaches a level of perfection where I could happily finish the entire serving of rice with just the chilli alone.

Next, the boneless chicken is consistently soft, tender, and moist, complementing the robust flavors of the rice and chilli beautifully.
​
​This stall is always at the very top of my must-eat list whenever I return home from being overseas.

However the queue is long and need to wait quite some time. The portions are generous for the price. Whether you’re dining in or taking away, it’s consistently good.

I would like to commend Yan Ting restaurant manager Jiang Yong Zhe for his professional handling and sincere resolution to our complaint at Yanting.

Yanting completely missed our booking for 28 Feb 1pm and all tables were reserved for a private event.

After expressing our frustration, they initially recommended that we head over to the ground floor Italian restaurant. However as it is our family CNY celebration, we wanted a Chinese food menu. They then offered for us to dine at the Italian restaurant on their account.

What happened after this really demonstrated their sincere apologies for their mishandling of our reservation - They offered the Chinese menu, i.e. brought them down from Yanting kitchen the second floor, and even gave us their chef recommended lobster noodles.

Given that we managed to still have Chinese food menu albeit at a less than cosy Chinese restaurant environment, we wanted to pay for the meal but they insisted for our lunch to still be on their account to make amends, and even gave us a complementary box of Nian Gao.

Apart from the sincere way restaurant manager Jiang treated us, I also highly recommend the food at Yanting and the Italian restaurant. Good stuff ~

Dining at Chinese restaurant Yan Ting on a cold rainy Chinese New Year’s Day culminated in an unforgettable culinary experience for me  . With the fancy tableware set up , I found myself brimming with satisfaction having indulged  in a trio of irresistible robust flavours of the  hearty corn crab soup , pan fried crunchy radish cake ,exquisite roasted chicken , simmering spinach prawn ball broth and not forgetting the lusciously smooth yet texturally lively mango pudding with the tender sago pearls to finish off the meal . The Cantonese culinary art at Yan Ting is certainly one that titillates one’s tastebuds, treating one to an opulent spread of beautiful crafted Chinese cuisine abundant in flavour and finesse . Having said this ,the roast chicken is my perennial favourite as it deserves the accolades for my continued patronage of Yan Ting.

Every visit to Yan Ting is a top-notch Cantonese dining experience.

✨ An exceptional Cantonese culinary journey
Located at The St. Regis Singapore, Yan Ting is one of my top choices for upscale Cantonese cuisine. The ingredients are always fresh, the dishes exquisitely prepared, and every meal has been a thoroughly satisfying experience.

📌 Recommended dishes:
•	Yellow Wine Braised Chicken Claypot: Tender chicken in a rich, aromatic broth—an absolute must-try.
•	Crispy Roasted Pork Belly: Perfectly crispy on the outside and melt-in-your-mouth tender on the inside—truly exceptional.
•	Vinegar Pork Trotters: Especially loved by the elders in our family—well-balanced sweet and sour flavors, rich in collagen, and deeply flavorful.
•	Dim Sum Selections: The truffle mushroom dumplings and crystal shrimp dumplings are delicately crafted, both in flavor and presentation.
•	Coconut Pudding: Light and refreshing—an ideal way to conclude the meal.

🏛️ The restaurant boasts a refined, elegant ambiance—calm and perfect for family gatherings or festive celebrations. The staff are professional and attentive, making every dining experience a pleasure.

💰 While prices are on the higher side (approximately SGD 100+ per person), the quality absolutely justifies the cost. A place well worth revisiting!

We celebrated my dad’s birthday at Yan Ting, St. Regis, and it was a wonderful experience. As we came in a big group, we were given a semi-private room which made the evening feel extra special.

The service was excellent – attentive and professional throughout the night. Food was served promptly and every dish was delicious. A special mention to Weng Gor, who made sure everything was smooth and well taken care of.

To top it off, the team thoughtfully surprised my dad with complimentary 壽桃 (longevity buns), which made the celebration even more memorable.

Thank you to the Yan Ting team for making this occasion so enjoyable. Highly recommended for both family gatherings and special celebrations.

Yhingthai Palace is a great stop although I only tried their desserts so far. The red ruby ice is another highlight. The water chestnut rubies have a good crunch inside their soft, chewy exterior, and the coconut milk is smooth and lightly sweetened. Served with shaved ice, it’s refreshing without being diluted, making it a perfect finish to a rich meal.

Prices are on the higher side, but the quality of these two classic Thai desserts is reliably good, and the portions are decent. If you’re looking for a place that does mango sticky rice and red ruby ice with care and consistency, Yhingthai Palace is a solid pick. Our dining experience at Yhingthai Palace was deeply disappointing. We ordered several dishes, but unfortunately, none lived up to the restaurant’s reputation or its inclusion in the Michelin Guide. The food portion, quality, and execution were all far below expectations.
The Kuay Teow Phad See Eu Nur (rice noodles fried in black sauce with beef) was a letdown — the beef wasn’t fresh, and the noodles were mushy. The Kuay Teow Phad Thai was missing key ingredients like chives and preserved turnip, and despite my request for less sugar, it turned out overly sweet and unbalanced.
The Phad Prik Khing Thwa Yao (Thai string beans stir-fried with prawns and chilli paste) was undercooked, leaving the beans hard and unpleasant. The Phak Boong Fai Dang (spicy kang kong with shrimp paste chilli) was overcooked and far too salty.
The Thai Green Curry with Pork was watery and lacked the richness you would expect from a proper green curry. The pork wasn’t tender, and when I asked the server what cut of pork was used, she couldn’t even tell me.
The Pineapple Fried Rice was the biggest disappointment — it tasted like ordinary fried rice from a coffeeshop, with none of the aroma, balance, or authenticity of a true Thai dish.
Service was just as poor. The staff seemed clueless about the menu and the ingredients used, which further added to the frustration.
I truly cannot understand how Yhingthai Palace continues to hold a place in the Michelin Guide — it was a complete letdown from start to finish.

My previous dining experiences at Yi restaurant were particularly  memorable as I was not only impressed by the interior decor which exuded a genteel charm  aligning perfectly with the sophisticated  elegance of Raffles Hotel , but also with the unique gastronomic flavours of the fine Cantonese cuisine executed with such refined finesse .

However , my recent dining experience wavered somewhat between positive and negative impressions . Whilst the mushroom appetiser was artistically presented in a delicate composition with each element thoughtfully placed  , the fish maw soup on the contrary arrived only lukewarm rather than piping hot, thus diminishing the expected richness of the broth. A brief reheating to the ideal serving temperature is highly recommended as it would have fully restored  its delicate flavours and texture.
Though my request was accommodated promptly , Yi restaurant needs to place a greater emphasis on temperature control for food served and address any lapses to ensure a seamless culinary dining experience for the dining patron.

Acknowledging my dissatisfaction , I credit Yi restaurant for recovering the service well , presenting me with a fresh new piping hot soup bowl  a second time round .

The remaining  dishes such as the stone pot assorted vegetables bean curd dish and the Dong Gui duck were thoughtfully executed . The Dong Gui Duck arrived succulent  with its skin imbued with nuanced herbal undertones creating yet another harmonious pairing .  Especially commendable was the stone pot dish as the heated stone kept the mushroom and veggie aromatic flavours  deeply intact  in a simmering gravy while thoroughly enhancing  its flavours .

When the Pandan milk curd roll dessert  was finally served , it culminated as the epitome of the entire dining experience . Gently sweet with an ethereal lightness , the Pandan milk curd  was a delightful way to finish off the meal . Indeed it was a flawless execution , with exquisite well balanced flavours encased in a  baked golden crust.
I was pleasantly surprised too that the Nian Gao  served was on the house , probably to placate my initial disappointment for a less than satisfactory soup dining experience .

In sum, ultimately Yi restaurant is one fine dining venue that manages to delight the palate  , thanks to their  distinguished  cuisine coupled with their polish service and faultless hospitality in recognising the exacting standards of seasoned food critics .

前两次是在包房参加商务宴请，菜品质量很高，很满意。这一次是在大厅，没想到差距这么大，非常失望！上菜很慢，且菜品不尽人意。尤其是清蒸东星斑，口感很柴，不知是食材的原因还是烹饪的原因，简直难以下咽。在这个档次的中餐厅，把鱼做成这样，实属不应该！！

甬府有大堂和包厢，我担心大堂会像御宝那样吵，人吵碗碟噪音多，还是包厢吧，低消一人300，预约上12点后工作人员WhatsApp发来的菜单信息提及是以厨师配菜的形式呈现，再发消息询问可否单点，没等回复就打了通电话📞，确认可以就行，那我们12:20到。
🚖等车+司机停的地方不好，找店花费了点时间，12:40才到店。见两间包厢：宁波和成都。包厢内品茗区、大圆桌和洗手间，300在这吃不比板前高级日料强？ 过年过节漂亮饭还得是中餐👍

水晶冬瓜香油腌冬瓜，切成小块儿很精致。
蒋母手撕笋奉化羊尾笋，蒋介石老家。
🦀宁波十八斩吃着比三叔公的生腌蟹方便，嘬一口生蟹肉就出来了，新鲜舟山红膏梭子蟹。
没有醉虾但有花雕小龙虾🦞 🤵‍♂️（是经理吗？徐州的大哥）带下去剥好后送上来，轻轻一扯就行，个头大味美😋

全程服务的佩莹🇲🇾小姐姐💁‍♀️认真介绍餐厅不同菜系是由不同师傅掌勺👨‍🍳 介绍菜品… 狮子头，东海黄鱼鱼肉制成，💁‍♀️：汤里有只和尚蟹用于提味儿不可食用，会直着爬的螃蟹，可以捞上来放在狮子头上拍照🤳也很好玩。我一勺子捞上来，它左钳子抱着颗豆子，甚是可爱。
奉化芋艿羹，加了猪油渣，口味浓稠。送了碟伊朗开心果。
海鲜点了平鱼：东海白鳞鲳 (雪菜笋丝烧），鱼肉品质也棒👍

红烧肉看菜单得提前订，💁‍♀️还是帮我们去问了下厨房，很贴心。最初点单的时候好像问过了🤵‍♂️但是对象忘记了。

服务精神佳，观察食客用餐喜好调整桌面菜品位置、更换顶碟，看我们吃得慢，🐟趁热好吃哦🫶剩下的一半带下去加热再上。

🚻护手霜按压泵按不动+🧻用完了（倒是有补充装🧻摆在那）和💁‍♀️佩莹说了声，很快就去解决问题。

宁波年糕（荠菜 [季节性]无就经典的津白炒）师傅自己磨的纯手工年糕，不粘牙，切片厚度匀称，好吃😋

💁‍♀️听我们聊天💬“汤圆是三颗一例吗？刚才我担心吃不完就没点。”“不是，是一颗大汤圆。”后送了一例，这样一人一个嘛～也是师傅自己做的，皮薄馅儿多。个头大，溢出汤勺的大小还不破，超满足😌

最后上的甘肃香瓜🍈

结账送到门口🙋‍♀️🤵‍♂️情人节快乐～

这得是在坡县这么多年用餐整体体验最满意的一家，希望保持。还来多来，毕竟宁波和福州均位于东海之滨🌊 也想尝尝其它菜系师傅的手艺，期待！
Seriously one of the best chinese restaurants on sg.

Tastefully done interior and extensive menu predominantly featuring quality live seafood from Zhejiang, prepared in authentic Ningbo style. ‘Ningbo 18 cuts’ is raw crab marinated in spiced soy; each piece brims with orange roe that tastes gooey and buttery. Save space for deserts particularly Ningbo sticky rice balls filled with runny black sesame paste that are made to order.
The staff champ Ng & pei ling were friendly and professional, creating a welcoming atmosphere 👍👍👍 Jia you 🤗
the attentive and warm service  made me feel welcome right now. from the staff champ ng and pei ling

From the moment you step into the grand corridor, you are transported into a world of refined luxury. The floor-to-ceiling windows offer a breathtaking, panoramic view of the city skyline. It is the perfect spot for a celebratory lunch or a romantic place,
Definitely a top choice dining place if you want to impress your guests with good food and great views.

I love the overall food and service but I was kindof disturbed by the live fishes in one of the presentation of a dish. I don't think this is necessary and the fishes looks destress in the shallow water

Are you really serious about the price for the food they are serving. I made the mistake of asking them to recommend good dishes for lunch. It was over $300 per person! Must be one of the most expensive lunch I had anywhere especially in a windowless environment!

收到甬府的中秋小食,含有过期食品。中秋收到是1月19号生产，保质期120天的食品。而且还缺斤少两。
左边两包没有标示生产日期；
中间两包中，一包未标示生产日期，另一包已过保质期大半年；
其中同款产品出现两种不同的保质期标识（60天与120天）；重量也不同（100克和160克）

Fresh but so so. Too salty in fact. Ordered 6 dishes and only really ate the noodles and rice

Something very memorable is, we ordered a dish for less then 100, but after waiting for 30 mins or so, they suddenly inform us that it is out of stock, and have to change to another ingredient, and ask if we are okay. Being starved for 30 mins, we go with anything.
No price changes was informed. End up that one change of ingredients was nearly 480 dollars.

A very memorable sales tactic

Decent zhejiang/ningbo food, but nothing outstanding or particularly memorable, especially at the price they are charging. The Peking duck is kinda disappointing and seems rather small. 3 of us only had about 2 wraps and 2-3 pieces of very small pieces of skin. Didn't feel satisfying, given the very small pieces, to be honest. We love the yum soup and the veggie dish called "舍得”。 The signature cold crab is fine, but maybe just not the style of crab I usually like. If you like marinated, raw cold crab, maybe you will like it.

Presentation and services were great. Corkage at 50++ per bottle, seems standard for a restaurant of this caliber. Overall, I think it is a bit overpriced for the food they served, but compensated with nice ambiance and services. They said they are famous for their seafood, but then again zhejiang/ningbo area isn't really well known for their seafood cuisine, so we didn't ordered those.
Incredible quality ingredients!

Had lunch today there after confirmed with staff thru WhatsApp they have seasonal 薄壳米 in stock today although 海瓜子 was off season. My first time try 薄壳米金不换，really special than gold, the shell super thin, the meat soft and tender dip with soup taste like heaven, can’t stop to finish all, with 黄鱼狮子头，潮虾小葱炒 my both hands on and finger licking good! highly recommended!
Food is delicious and service is incredible

跟家人來新加坡旅遊，第一次試試寧波菜的天花板《甬府》啦！
環境嘛: 古色古香，吊頂很高，不會讓人覺得很壓抑。
味道: 點了AB各一套的晚市雙人套餐。我可太愛小龍蝦和生醃蟹了，非常鮮美，其他菜品都符合我們的口味。
服務: 工作人員多語種溝通都可，完全不用擔心點菜會語言不通，服務態度很好，時不時會問你菜品味道如何，時刻關注我們的用餐過程。
總體來講，還是非常推薦大家來試一下的，吃完還可以去旁邊的商場逛一下，很方便嘞。

I had a great dining experience at Yongfu Restaurant. The food was fresh, authentic, and full of flavor — especially the seafood, which was perfectly cooked. The service was warm and attentive, and the ambiance was elegant yet comfortable. A wonderful place to enjoy refined Chinese cuisine. Highly recommend! One of the Best Chinese restaurants in Singapore. Worth to try !

📍甬府｜麻辣东星斑🌶️🐟
近期最惊艳的一道鱼，毫不夸张！

东星斑本身肉质就很细嫩，这里处理得非常好，一点腥味都没有，鱼肉鲜美滑嫩，鱼皮Q弹带胶质，连不爱吃鱼的人都会喜欢！麻辣调味也拿捏得恰到好处，香麻不呛口，吃完还有微微回甘，越吃越上头🔥

每一口都很满足。而且服务特别贴心，服务员会适时帮忙分鱼、换盘，细节做到位。

店里环境也很好，装修典雅、氛围舒服，适合请客、约会或者家人聚餐。

新加坡甬府，一家坐落在Suntec City Tower 5，和周边商店格格不入的高级中餐厅。外观看似神秘，步入其中别有洞天。用餐区域分为大厅与包厢（有低消），装潢只能用“高大上”来形容。菜单涵盖了宁波、潮汕、川菜等融合菜系，选择有较大众化的两人、四人套餐，单点，甚至特别预订菜肴。

从氛围到味道以及服务，总体来说令人满意。甬府新加坡也登上了米其林推荐榜单，追求卓越用餐品质的各位不妨试试。推荐菜肴：宁式十八斩、鱼子酱西施贝海胆烩白玉珠、白辣椒炒黄金螺、宁波汤圆。

I had the pleasure of dining at a local high-end Chinese restaurant for the first time. Well I was blown away by the ambiance and decoation as it was so so so exquisite and luxurious! Meanwhile,  the waiters were so incredibly polite and their service were very very good! Thumbs up!!! 👍

Last but not least, I absolutely loved their stir-fried Ningbo sticky rice cake (It is dense, al dente rice cake that originated from Ningbo, China where it is still made by hand in some towns). It was incredibly delicious omg🤤! The rice cake was perfectly chewy and springy! As a rice cake lover, I strongly recommend it! 😍

Having dinner with my family for my birthday celebration in here today. All the food are quite delicious and very good service by the staff. Very satisfy with the dining experience for today. Definitely will come again next time.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: Good soup flavour, but pork ribs can be softer

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: 1st time trying and ordered the pig stomach and intestine herbal soup with rice and fried dough fritter for $7. Soup taste ok only, not piping hot even thou using claypot, you do not find the soup bubbling. Pig stomach was good but the intestine was overcooked and not very clean so only ate few pieces and skip the rest.  Amount of soup was quite little and not enough for the dough fritters, rice was abit lumpy and i only ate half bowl. Overall average and will be my last time patronising, stall owner was also putting a grumpy face.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: Tried their Dry BKT, not easy to find.  Very savoury, abit salty, so must pair with rice.  For $8.5 + rice at $0.5, the price seems a little high.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: 星期五和六休息，跟google map寫的營業時間有出路。點了藥材和胡椒口味。排骨有入味，也很嫩，輕輕一咬肉就撕開來了，湯頭是比較輕一點，不是重口味。整體不錯吃。豬腳也是有點肉骨茶味，較一般

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: They sell both peppery and herbal bak Kut teh. affordable and soup is refillable!

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: Yesterday, my friends and I checked out this amazing food stall for the first time. We sampled their recipe and were absolutely blown away by the authentic flavors and the exceptional customer service from the stall owners. They offer two delicious soup options: white pepper and herbal. I highly recommend both for anyone seeking an amazing culinary adventure.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: Nice herbal and pepper soup.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: Pork tenderloin soup (pepper) ($5) - Not bad. Good portion. Some slices were tender though some others were not so. The soup was a little too peppery.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: The 2 bowls in my photo…total $9.50 only! Can you get that at those in-mall Bak Kut Teh? Portions are fairly generous (for the price). & they do not close too early like the other Taman Jurong Food Center stalls. Accepts ShopBack payment. They often don’t on their signboard light, so don’t be mistaken that they are closed for the day.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: Tried the $4.5 pepper bkt - it’s decent. Will probably come back to try the rest.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: Both black and white are good.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: This stalls selling the rib pork herb soup are tasty and delicious. They also selling pork kidney and intestine herb soup.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: Not many bak kut teh in this area, this is not bad for the price, choice of either herbal or pepper soup base. Tried both, IMO herbal is better. Can't really taste the pepperish bkt taste for the pepper one.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews:
Seems to be a popular bak kut teh stall on this area. Always a constant queue when I was there.

Not exactly cooked in claypot but rather served in a claypot. Tasty and delicious, generous with the ingredients for a $6 bowl. A little more herbal would be great!

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: Portion big. Nice. But not as flavorful as some other bkt. Overall OK

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: Upon hearing my friends' suggestions for places I may have missed, I travelled all the way from Kallang to this place by GRAB to take away. Besides the side dishes, I ordered a LARGE ba ku keh and asked for extra soup. The male cook straight away rejected citing they do not give extra soup. Taste = NOT worth my time. This shall be my last time there and I will stop all my contacts from going there when ever possible.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: I would say it’s a decent bowl of Bak Kut Teh. Came on a rainy day and decided that a hot bowl of Bak Kut Teh won’t be very nice for this weather. Try the pepper version for $4.50. Portion is ok, just nice as I am not so hungry.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: Didn't manage to try the pepper base soup. Went at 7 and it was out of stock already. Herbal version of Bak Kut Teh was normal, meat was soft and rip off the bones easily. Would not recommend the you tiao 油条 cause there is a weird taste like the smell of other food and not heated up.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Reviews: Good value Bak Kut Teh. Both herbal and peppery varieties, both good tasting.

Very delicious food, reasonably priced ($6 as at Jan 2026). But only open 12-2pm, always long queue, don’t expect any service.

Queue clears up fast so don't worry, just join the queue!! 😊
Still as tasty $6 no need to choose jus say how many bowls you want.
Eat or take away 👍🏻

For the first time, I didn’t have to queue long for my bowl of YTF! This time I had it for lunch as opposed to tea time. All is still good except that I didn’t find it filling for a main course. Our family’s all time favourite to go for yong tau hu. Been in business for many decades. I am their regular since my kindy days 😂 And here I am bringing my family to indulge in a long and well established eatery. They operated their business from one stall and overtime took up the stall next door for food preparation. Have never seen them chat amongst themselves during their operating hours nor after. Men and woman of few words but genuinely nice folks as they take extra care to senior citizens.

Always patronise them on an empty stomach and never once did we leave disappointed. Just be prepared to join the long queue. Their operating hours are short as they get sold out under 4 - 5 hours (at most) every day.

Business too good head swell
Merely asked what time open,the lady just shoo me away ..I asked her again I just want to know what time open den she replied coldly 1200pm

Updated review Dec 2025: As a Hakka, I don't usually eat YTF outside unless it is handmade. This stall remains my favourite after so many years, despite the price hike (I have been a customer for at least 15 years). Their menu is simple, and every piece they make is perfect.

The tofu here is firmer than most out there, and I really like that unique texture and 'bean fragrance 豆香'. You may see mixed reviews because this is a simple, old-school taste, which many people these days don't appreciate as they seek stronger flavours and expects to choose items. Oh well, thats fine, because it means a shorter queue for me, haha.

Tip: Just note that the stall may open earlier or later than their listed time, depending on the completion of prep work. People usually start queuing at 11am and they are often sold out by 1:30 pm.

No noodles option YTF, first time trying. $6 standard bowl no choosing . Taste is good and worth eating once a while and if not super hungry. Like all the ingredients , can taste the freshness of the fish paste in the items . Soup is savoury good too.
A lot of people were queuing during lunch hour. Overall, I feel fine and think it's overrated.

Tasty and fresh. Nicely flavoured plain soup. Long but fast moving queue as there is only 1 dish, no rice/noodle and 1 price. They got their operation down to a T. Worth a try if you happened to be in the area. Lunch time only.

There are better ytf hawkers elsewhere in SG.
Ytf filling was minimal, could not taste much fish in the fish ball, one of the serving auntie’s attitude was terrible. Kept trying to sell me a pack that someone else rejected. Never coming back.
Standard serving.
I loved their yong tau fu!

The queue here can get quite long, especially during peak meal times, which shows how popular the place is. Service is generally decent — nothing overly fancy, but the staff are attentive enough to keep things moving smoothly despite the crowd. The real highlight is the food. Portions are generous, flavors are satisfying, and the overall quality is consistently good. What makes it even better is the pricing — very affordable for the standard you get. It’s the kind of spot where you don’t mind waiting a little because you know you’ll leave full and happy without overspending.
Truth is, overhyped and nothing special. Wasted 45 minutes queuing for something overpriced and mediocre. Not worth it and won't recommend it to anyone.

This genuine Hakka Yong Tau Foo stall has been around for decades. I believe this is the 2nd generation, currently the 3 brothers are in charge of the operation. They personally handmade the Yong Tau Foo everyday early in the morning despite only start selling at 12pm (it used to be 1pm). Personally, I have been eating Yong Tau Foo from this stall since I was a young child. The main difference is this stall's YTF comes without any noodles/rice. The soup is nicely done with taste of soyabean and probably sole fish. Each YTF was filled with delicious meat + fish fillings. Some pieces were deep-fried while some were steamed/boiled. Both versions were delicious! Highly recommended!

P/s: Even though the queue is always long, but it moves fast!
No frills bowl of old school YTF. They are incredibly fast and efficient. Cash only.

One of the best yong tau foo stalls on my list. I even make the walk here in the scorching heat during lunch just to have two bowls. Flavours are tasty without being too salty, and it feels healthier than most. Prices have gone up over the years, but the taste has stayed the same. I’ve been coming here since I was a boy, and it’s still as nostalgic as ever. Many close competitors in the area, but this stall still stands out

$6 for 10 items of YTH (no carbs). They are open from 12 noon. We went at 11:30am, thinking we should be in the front queue, we were number 22. Having said that the queue moved very fast upon opening.
If you are packing home, you will be told to join another queue and order. Each packet is for 2 serving (unless you said 1 pax). You need to tell the staff if you are eating soon or eating as dinner. The packing is different.

Worth the wait. Chill is good.

I’ve been patronizing this stall since I was a kid, and it has always delivered consistently great flavors. However, my recent visit fell a little short of expectations. The price has gone up from $4.50 to $6, which is understandable with inflation, but it did make me more aware of the quality.

The Yong tau foo ingredients are still fresh, but the soup lacked the rich, satisfying “oomph” it used to have. It also felt a bit oilier than before, which slightly affected the overall experience.

That said, it’s still a decent bowl of Yong tau foo. If I happen to be in the area, I’d likely drop by for a bowl—but I wouldn’t go out of my way just for it anymore.
Good bowl of yong tau fu here. Queue moves fast too.

People’s park food center is famous for yong tau foo. There’s at least 3 famous stalls here.

Saw there’s one with exceptionally long queue. So why would we not try? Actually end up i got my food within 10 mins. Queue is deceiving.

My advise is to let it cool down alittle before eating it. Best to buy some other food so you can have a complete meal too.

Tuo foo is v fresh and nice. Soup is not bad too. The key is to let it cool.

Been to this shop several times but realised that I never posted before. They used 1 dish to dominate. Their long queue for years explains everything.
Ok, would eat it again. The queue looks long but very fast because they only have 1 standard dish.

Yong tau foo soup ($6) - Not bad though too much pepper in soup. Not as good as before.

From earlier visits:
Yong tau foo soup ($6) - Good.
Yong tau foo soup ($6) - No rice or noodles in the dish, and there was no other dish and no choice of pieces. Long queue but it moved fast (10 minutes). Served to the table almost immediately. Best part was the soup and the delicate tofu.

Yummy Sarawak Kolo Mee is one of the few remaining historical landmarks of the Round Market. I think it could easily reclaim it's former glory by reverting a few changes made in recent years:

- Bring back the plastic bowls, because the new metal plates sap heat from the noodles and spin left and right when you're trying to eat

Zai Shun Fish Head Curry
A wildly popular kopitiam institution and Michelin Bib Gourmand regular, Zai Shun stays proudly local in crowd and character. It’s all about honest, comforting dishes served in a busy neighbourhood setting where the food does the talking. Come for the classics, stay for the familiarity, and don’t expect much hand-holding along the way.

Takeaways:
• Curry Fish Head remains a favourite. The broth leans tangy rather than overwhelmingly rich, which keeps it bright and easy to enjoy. The fish is fresh, meaty and acts as a clean backdrop for the lively sauce.
• Ngoh Hiang Prawn Rolls stand out for their chunkiness. The filling tastes fresh and leans toward whole pieces instead of minced paste, giving each bite more texture and heft.
• Long Beans arrive stir-fried and crunchy, with dried shrimp providing a strong umami lift and extra bite.
• The vibe is classic kopitiam: noisy, crowded and very local, especially during lunch when nearby residents pack the space. Service can be chaotic and you often need to flag someone down, but that’s simply part of the experience.

The Damage (no drinks): S$ 25-50 for two

The food? Absolutely world-class. Each dish is plated like a piece of art, and the flavors are perfectly balanced. The Omakase course is on another level — fresh ingredients, sophisticated techniques, and flavors that stay with you long after the meal.

What makes it even more memorable is how the chef personally comes out to explain the ingredients and cooking process, turning dinner into a cultural and educational journey rather than just a meal.

Yes, the price is premium, but the quality, service, and experience make it absolutely worth it. If you’re in Singapore and want a fine dining experience that truly stands out, Zen is a must-visit.

Restaurant Name: Zhang Ji Shanghai La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews:
[QUEENSTOWN, SINGAPORE] I feel like most people might know this stall in Alexandra Village Hawker, but I would like to highlight that after having their dumplings for at least 10 years, their quality is still really good.

The must orders are their Chilli Oil Dumplings 🥟 and Fried Dumplings 🥟, both at an affordable $8 per plate. Their chilli oil dumplings are quite spice friendly luckily, making it suitable for most to enjoy. If you need an extra kick, they have more chilli sauce available at the side! The dumplings were very slurp worthy, with quite a sizable amount of filling within. The fried dumplings may not be too crispy on the outside, but the filling inside is so generous. It was meaty and honestly really shiok with the sauce from the chilli oil style!

Their noodles are more sub-par actually, but I still got it anyway 😂 The Dan Dan Mian ($5) had quite alot of minced meat, but the sauce was missing some flavour and noodles were too soft.

Really recommend the dumplings here, you gotta have them as a side while you get mains from other stalls 😆

Reviews: It was truly a pleasant exploration of good food at the hawker center as I tried out the dumplings after observing a snake long queue right in front of this Zhang Ji Shanghai La Mian Xiao Long Bao. As the queue was too long and I have a time constraint this morning, I managed to take away these dumplings and hoping my taste buds would like these frozen dumplings.  True enough, as I boiled these dumplings, they were heavenly succulent with fillings and the skin was just perfectly at the right thickness to hold the fillings up until they were cooked. These must have been prepared by a seasoned chef who is skilful with not only  his rolling pin but also adept in squeezing all the well marinated fillings within a small diameter of the dumpling skin at such fine thickness. It is no wonder they were accorded with Michelin Star. Seeing is believing and now I believed why the queue was so long. In fact, despite the long queue. all members in the stall including the owner were expeditiously efficient in their service. Kudos to Zhang Ji Shanghai La Mian Xiao Long Bao, I am in love with the dumplings and ready to experiment the rest of your delicacy soon.

Restaurant Name: Zhang Ji Shanghai La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews:
Visit date: 2 Mar 2025
Actual rating: 4.0

Ever since that Chinese stall above Bishan bus interchange shuttered, it hasn't been easy to replace the lost 红油抄手 delicacy! :(

Few, if any, dumpling stalls can deliver similar quality, even if they have shifus hailing from the mainland...

So I was high in anticipation of this visit to AV hawker centre, as Yahoo gave top marks to this Chinese food stall 😆🤔

The score was quickly determined with an order of xiao long bao (XLB) and wontons in chilli oil (i.e. 抄手).

XLB was delicate and tasty enough to rival well known eateries. It wasn't served piping hot, so the experience of bursting soup had been watered (pun?!) down.

On the other hand, the chilli dumplings weren't as good! I was taken aback that they weren't the classic wrapped white skinned petite dumplings but huge wontons instead! :(

The problem with wontons is the skin is laden with gluten after cooking, so they did turn out very starchy and yucky!!

No can do, this isn't the replacement I've been looking high and low for.

Looks like #MHTamChiak has to keep searching for this delicacy, which has now entered #ElusiveFoods territory...

If you know where to get really good Chinese dumplings, do drop a comment. Much appreciated 👍

Restaurant Name: Zheng Zhi Wen Ji Pig Organ Soup
Reviews:
Zheng Zhi Wen Ji Pig Organ Soup is a hidden gem for anyone who loves traditional Teochew-style pig’s organ soup. The broth is clear, light, and incredibly flavorful with a nice peppery kick—comforting without being too heavy.

The ingredients are fresh and well-prepared. From tender pork slices to intestines, liver, and stomach, everything is cleaned properly and cooked to the right texture. Served with a bowl of white rice and a dash of soy sauce with chili—simple, classic, and so satisfying.

They also offer side dishes like braised tofu, eggs, and salted vegetables which complement the soup perfectly. Fast service, reasonable prices, and clean environment make it a great stop for a hearty, nostalgic meal.

Restaurant Name: Zhi Wei Xian Zion Road Big Prawn Noodle
Reviews:
It is flavour city with this one. The chewy,  thick bee hoon and yellow noodles are tossed in a savoury sauce with hints of ketchup and sambal. Prawns are fresh, succulent, and sweet with a satisfying bite, unlike the smaller ones commonly used. Dip them into a little soy sauce and chili powder for extra shiokness. At times, the combination of prawns with dry noodles even tasted like Singapore’s famous chili crab. Crab can also be ordered a la carte here.

The soup is the star here: full of depth and oomph, rich with the sweet essence of seafood and pork, and of course, umami. The pork ribs also deserve praise for its peppery aroma and tender texture. Bursts of fat come through when a piece of fried pork lard is bitten into - sinfully divine.

Reviews:
Kelantan Kway Chap 吉蘭丹粿汁 – Berseh Food Centre (Michelin Bib Gourmand)

Kelantan Kway Chap at Berseh Food Centre is a long-standing Michelin Bib Gourmand hawker favourite, celebrated for its honest, well-executed Teochew-style kway chap. The dish features smooth, wide rice sheets that are soft yet resilient, soaking up the flavours of the braising sauce beautifully. A generous assortment of soy-braised pork cuts is offered, including belly, skin, trotters and intestines, each prepared with care and braised until tender without losing texture.

The braising sauce is the heart of the dish — dark, aromatic and well-balanced, carrying notes of soy, spices and gentle sweetness without being overpowering. Every component feels thoughtfully cooked, allowing the natural flavours of the pork to shine while remaining deeply comforting. Portions are satisfying, and prices remain accessible, reflecting why the stall continues to earn Michelin recognition for quality and value.

What truly elevates the experience is their amazing homemade chilli. Fragrant, punchy and layered with heat, it adds an addictive kick that cuts through the richness of the braised meats and transforms each mouthful. A small spoonful goes a long way, but many regulars find themselves going back for more. Unpretentious yet full of character, Kelantan Kway Chap is a must-try for lovers of classic Singapore hawker fare. Look

and received a message at 1:35 pm saying: “Please note that we are releasing your table after 15 mins of no show from your booking reservation time. If you wish to hold the table, kindly response in this message before the due time.” The wording is grammatically incorrect and very confusing. When I first read it, I even thought I might have set my reservation at 1:20 pm by mistake and that my table was already being released because “15 mins of no show” had supposedly passed. “We are releasing your table…” sounds as if the table is already being released before my actual reservation time, and “kindly response” is also wrong English. A clearer and more professional version would be: “We will release your table 15 minutes after your reservation time if there is no show. If you would like us to hold the table, kindly reply to this message before that time.” Because of the poor wording and the timing of the message, it felt as though my confirmed booking was being threatened before the actual reservation time. I tried to clarify this with the staff over WhatsApp and even suggested the correct wording, but after their brief reply they stopped responding and did not acknowledge the clarification or the suggestion at all, which came across as unprofessional and dismissive of feedback.

Whether you're winding down after a game of golf or simply stopping in for an evening drink, the backdrop enhances the overall mood and elevates the experience.

In conclusion, 8 Degree Lounge at Orchid Country Club is a hidden gem for those seeking a refined yet approachable lounge experience. Whether for a quiet date night, after-work drinks, or a lively gathering with friends, 8 Degree Lounge consistently delivers on quality and atmosphere.

This is a good meepok fishball noodle. You will love the fishcake. I would say that they have a chance to be GREAT, with just 1 change.

The soup is great, it has a hint of Tang Chye (Preserved salted vegetable). IMHO, I think this is the key flavoring ingredient, started from the very beginning--50 years ago, eversince I was a kid.
I love the fishcake, it is firm with a nice tautness in the mouth, and a very normal fish flavour. Some fishcakes are... smell-less, yeah it sounds weird, but it is true, because it has not enough fish in it? Too much flour?
The chilli paste to noodle ratio is perfect. It has a nice flavourful mix where every bite is so satisfying. I would say it leans to the sweet side, because it lacks vinegar.
The biggest weakness is the fishball; it is too soft, it feels like it is made largely of flour, not enough firm fish meat. I think these fishballs are factory made, not handmade by them. When you bite into it, it feels light and soft. So this costs them 1 Star in this review.

Ah Meng Restaurant is a popular dining option located within the Singapore Zoo, offering a convenient place to enjoy meals without leaving the park. It’s named after the famous orangutan Ah Meng, which adds a fun and memorable connection to the zoo experience.

The restaurant provides a variety of food options, including local Singaporean dishes, Western meals, snacks, and beverages. It’s suitable for families, groups, and solo visitors who want a quick meal or a casual dining experience during their zoo visit. The menu is simple yet satisfying, catering to both adults and children with familiar flavors.

One of the highlights of Ah Meng Restaurant is its family-friendly atmosphere. The seating area is spacious, clean, and comfortable, with indoor and outdoor options available. The casual setup makes it easy to relax and enjoy a break between exploring the zoo.

The staff are generally friendly and helpful, managing orders efficiently even during peak hours. Food is served promptly, which is great for visitors with children or limited time in the park. While prices are slightly higher than outside options, the convenience of being inside the zoo makes it worthwhile.

Overall, Ah Meng Restaurant is a reliable and convenient dining spot during a Singapore Zoo visit. It provides decent food, friendly service, and a comfortable environment, making it an ideal place to refuel before continuing the wildlife adventure.

Convenience / location: Being in or near Tuas South Dormitory makes it very handy for residents. No need to travel far; quick access to a decent meal is a big plus.

Casual / friendly atmosphere: For many, these eating places are informal, relaxed, and feel familiar — kind of like home-style food rather than fancy restaurant meals.

Affordable pricing: Indian Muslim stalls generally try to keep prices within reach of workers; portion sizes are often reasonable.

---

⚠ Potential limitations (minor)

Mixed reviews on rating: On BipperMedia, Al-Rich has a rating around 2.3 out of 5 from a few reviews.  That suggests some people have had less good experiences, perhaps with food quality, service, or consistency.

Possible variation in service or food quality: Since many dorm-area food places serve many people, sometimes hygiene, food temperature, or serving speed can vary.

Limited upscale features: Probably not much in terms of fancy ambience, décor, or premium ingredients — it's more about basic, filling, home-style meals.

---

✅ Overall impression

Al-Rich Indian Muslim Foods seems like a reliable go-to option for many staying in the Tuas South dormitory area when they want hearty, familiar Indian Muslim food. It may not always be perfect (based on low average rating), but its convenience, flavour, and value make it worth trying, especially when you want something satisfying and accessible
