The wasabi provided is also from the actual wasabi plant, not from some packaged wasabi which tend to be too spicy.
We also tried the fish heart/ventricle, which is on their seasonal menu, it tastes exactly like what you would expect innards to taste like if you had tried innards from other animals such as chicken.
The maguro rib was a surprising one for me, the charred part didn't feel like fish but you could still tell it's still fish from the meat closer to the bones.
Their hot tea has free refills btw :)
This place can accommodate large groups, there was a large family dining here as well while we were here, counter seats are also available.

The food is great. Very fresh and grill just right. Highball can be more alcoholic. Service crew really professional, table is double wipe, hand written menu is really cute. But the place is really a bit cramp. I sat outside hence a little warm...
The manager is very friendly and attentive.

This is my first time dining after they move from the previous location.  The space is much bigger now. Food wise is usually good. Their sashimi were sliced after you ordered unlike other buffets were already prepared. Variety should be ok for jap buffet. Service is much better now compared in the past.
Great food and service
Great service and atmosphere, helpful staff!

Food was mediocre. Rice overcooked until it became soggy. Chicken is tasteless, dry and hard. Paid $9.90 per bowl. I think we can get better quality food from the foodcourt. Don't understand how it survives. We will not come again.
I always eat here for gyu don but I recently found out they sell ramen and it is delicious. There is many flavours such us tonkotsu and spicy.
good food

We had dinner at Kwee Zeen on Saturday night for their Seafood Buffet. We loved the Lobsters, Fresh Tiger Prawns, Clams and Scallops. Plus their Sushi & Sashimi.  It was worth the price we paid to dine there.
The Service was top-notch with friendly staffs and made our meals more enjoyable.
Thank you Kwee Zeen for an absolute night to remember.

Manager Albert very warm and lead well his team .I have been there for 3 years since 2023 for my birthday, first time try their dinner this year never fail to let me down with their food and service. Well done team Kwee Zeen!

It is a great space to dine with family. The service staff is attentive and kind. We were a mix of vegetarian and non vegetarian group but we opted for the Indian vegetarian dishes. They had several portion size was quite good and the rice n raita both exceeded expectations. The restaurant manager Peter (I hope I got the name right) was very kind in offering to make some of the non vegetarian dishes into vegetarian. The mango dessert was delicious and refreshing.

My family and I had the pleasure of dining for lunch at Kwee Zeen during our stay at Sofitel Sentosa Resort. The food was excellent and the ambiance was very calming and my son loved every dish that came out from the satay to the sides. Our server Ruby was particularly kind and accommodating to my family as the other servers were as well. They all made us feel very welcome and the service is top notch every time we come and stay at Sofitel. The variety and quality of dishes has us coming back again and again! Thank you Kwee Zeen for a lovely lunch as always!

Very nice place and staff are warm and friendly. Food is pretty good and fresh. Variety is sufficient. Outside sitting is cosy and comfortable and If you come at between 6 to 7 , you can see a nice sunset.

Ordered so many times and this time is horribly disappointed. Ordered 300 sticks for 3 families because we love the satay and just a simple request to split the gravy to 3 pack but was rejected reason being saving the environment for reduce plastic bag. However, asked me to cancel order and split the order to 3 different orders so each order have their own gravy, make no sense to waste paper to print additional invoice and make additional orders. They rather want me to cancel order and reorder again and not wanting the split the gravy for my current order. Seriously disappointed by the operator, hope that they can be more flexible else when people want to make group purchases have to order one by one which is not an ideal way of doing business.

Good price point and delicious satay especially the mutton and pork. Our choice of satay provider whenever we have BBQ at home. Their ketupat is good too, goes very well with the satay and sauce. The highlight is that they provide pineapple sauce with the satay sauce, this helps to cleanse the oil associated with BBQ.

Highly recommend for anyone looking for nice and affordable satay. The portal to order is easy to use and staff are prompt to response to your order.
Easy collection of satay here. The staffs are friendly. Satay is tasty, otah is better than average. Only drawback is that the Satay sauce/gravy is too watery.

Received miss call from the customer service at 8+am at every 3 min interval for 4-5 times. Called back and ask who called, that aunty who picked up the call is very very rude. First you did not tell me WHERE the call is from, second you straight ask for people’s name and a natural human reaction is provide own’s name. But the reply gotten was, “i call so many people how I know who are you?” Hinting what? Your business is so good until customer service is not important? I don’t know that aunty is an employee or the boss. But irregardless, hanging up a customer’s call is a bad move. Let alone trying to yell back at a paying customer. Suggest that aunty to go attend basic customer service training or else more and more bad reviews will bring the company down. Do not underestimate the internet reviews.
Very rude customer service who quarrel at customer
Tasty Halal food!! Thank you
Food so lousy, but still can tahan for so many years
请问这是你们公司的员工吗？麻烦叫他还钱！
The food quite so so and the fried lemon chicken more flour than the meat.
HAS ANYONE CHECKED THEIR HALAL STATUS?? I CAN'T FIND IT ON MUIS WEBSITE FOR ANY OF THEIR OUTLETS!! ARE THEY ON THE VERGE OF BECOMING LIKE BUEY TAHAN SEAPUUTTT??

There is an flying ant on my white prawn hokkien mee. When I confronted the staff, no apology and showed bad attitude as if the ant was put in by me. When my son went to collect the new order, she still warned my son to see carefully whether the order is free of insect.

Restaurant Name: L'entrecTe Singapore Duxton Hill, The Steak & Fries Bistro
Reviews: Attentive service and excellent value. The taste brings back wonderful memories of Parisian life. Staff speaks frankly about concept and ownership, and provides generous portion of fries and “secret sauce” upon request. Overall quite the experience for a night out in Singapore.

Restaurant Name: L'entrecTe Singapore Duxton Hill, The Steak & Fries Bistro
Reviews: Boring food. very 'unexceptional'. Service and location are good

Restaurant Name: L'entrecTe Singapore Duxton Hill, The Steak & Fries Bistro
Reviews: Service and food was amazing

Restaurant Name: L'entrecTe Singapore Duxton Hill, The Steak & Fries Bistro
Reviews: Sir Anthony had really good customer service! Great food! Steak was superb and the price was worth it. 😊

Restaurant Name: L'entrecTe Singapore Duxton Hill, The Steak & Fries Bistro
Reviews: As always never a disappointment with Entrecote ! Food, service and atmosphere are amazing.
Amazing

Kudos to the students running the place for the food and service. The place is done up well enough though some things can be refined a little.

My overall take is that they have done well but most things could use a little improvement.

1) The pasta I had was too firm. To note I love pasta al dente but this needed a bit more time.
2) The sauce tasted good but it was too dry. Just a tad more liquidy texture would elevate it.
3) The mango sticky rice didn’t really work as a reimagined version of the dish as I would have much preferred the original. Textures, taste and mashed up taken in altogether could be improved on.
4) They only had white or raw sugar and no equal or other type of non-sugar sweetener and it would be good to have that alternative for the hot tea/coffee.

Service wise it was excellent. So great job there 👏🏻

Saying all this they will be closed for reno for a year and after that not sure what the new form will be. All the best to the students there in their f&b journey 👍🏻🙂

Food is nice.
Was served by Yue Leng and Ardriana.
Adriana articulated well when introducing the dishes while Yue Leng is attentive and gentle.
Thanks Mr Clemence for the guidance provided to the students.

Very chill environment. Staff are very friendly and easy to approach. Food are delicious 😋
Highly recommended.

A hidden gem!! Everything was so good I can see why it’s packed even though the location is so uluu. The sea bass was too die for literally melted in my mouth. Burrata oh so creamy. Steak was good too. Sadly way too stuffed for dessert. Relatively affordable too. Will be back!!

La Braceria Pizza & Grill offers a refined take on Italian comfort, where the charcoal grill (the "braceria") takes center stage. The "Chef’s Specials" are the clear stars, featuring a succulent Wagyu Flank Steak with chimichurri ($38).
For a standout starter, the Portobello mushrooms—oven-baked and smothered in a silky parmesan cream sauce—are practically mandatory. It’s ambiance, it’s the kind of spot where a glass of red wine feels like a requirement, not an option.
Fantastic food with a cozy atmosphere and excellent service! Chef is friendly and kind!

This was my first time visit here to celebrate my friend’s birthday.

The valet service was excellent as we were assisted by a very friendly young indian parking attendant on where to park our car. He had also recommended us to must try the pizza and cheese cake. We ordered cooked ham & mushroom pizza, it was indeed very delicious and was well received by everyone. The cheesecake was nice and delicate. For the mains, l ordered lamb chop, it was tender and not dry though well done.

However, there was a point that I would like to share. As we were seated next to the door opening, the door had been opened/closed frequently which produced a little irritated sound when it repeatedly hit onto the door knob. I think by adding a small foam on the door knob can help to reduce the sound effect so that the whole dining experience can be improved.

Overall, the ambience, food and  service were great. Highly recommended!

Table for 3 for lunch during Hari Raya.
I used to be a regular, but it’s been years since I have been there and not sure what has happened. Was it a bad day in the kitchen or the standard has dropped overall?
The place has a dank smell to begin, with which does not make for a pleasant dining experience. Two people actually got seated and left without ordering.
The breads were bitter and the oil balsamic mix rancid, so too the bacon in the mushroom soup… I mean it’s mushroom soup, may be a Nonna recipe but you are not celebrating her.
Ordered the ‘Seasonal special’ lobster fettuccine all'arrabbiata. Perhaps the lobster was from last season cos it was so dry, tasteless and dead, it might as well have been eating a fossil.
Lasagne again.. how to go wrong. Too sweet, and just not nice?
Risotto al fungi - a watery mess with too much stale white wine.
Everything was just not fresh, rancid and the flavor profiles were just off.
I gave 2 stars because the front staff were really nice and tried their best, but I don’t think they are being supported in the backend.
It was a very sad experience.
‘Owner’ you can give me a rebuttal but this is my objective feedback and I hope real changes can be made, because you have weathered the times for 20 years, but now is the time for change.
Pizza ok but the cauliflower cheese dish was inedible. All the florets were brown and soggy. Would not go back.
Friends and I came for the one for one pasta and pizza. Amazing food and amazing service by our waiter Ryan. Will come again

Very good and fast service from the staffs here! Food was also delicious for most of the items! Recommend to try their pizza, it is good! Got the carnivora pizza and the crust and all was perfectly done!
Almost feels like I am in italy

cozy vibes, authentic Italian flavours.

Here’s what we tried:

🍟 Patatine Fritte al Profumo di Tartufo
Golden, crispy truffle fries loaded with Parmesan and fragrant black truffle. Savoury, aromatic, and honestly addictive from the first bite — perfect for sharing… or not.

🍍 Hawaiana Pizza
Thin, nicely charred crust topped with Italian tomato sauce and creamy fior di latte mozzarella. The salty ham and sweet pineapple combo hits just right — classic sweet-salty vibes done perfectly.

🍝 Fettuccine alla Carbonara
Homemade fettuccine tossed in a silky, rich sauce of egg, cream, and Parmesan. Smoky bacon adds that indulgent depth, making every bite comforting and deeply satisfying.

🍮 Crème Brûlée
The perfect sweet ending. Rich custard base with a layer of caramelized sugar on top — crack through the warm sugar to the chilled, creamy custard below. Absolute dessert goals.

My family and I tried once and we have been eating there often ever since! Food is delicious, service is awesome with all the staff being friendly. Thank you especially to Rajah, Albert and Fibi who are very attentive to customers' needs and check in with customers in between their meals to ensure all is well. Definitely would recommend Crema di Funghi, Quattro Formaggi & Honey (can customise half with blue cheese and half without), Brisket Stufato, Ravioli Truffle and Tiramisu! Kudos to the chefs for keeping such high standards every single time when we came to dine in (even on crowded days)!

Visited a few times so far, one of the better Italian restaurants in NE area. Food was good and fresh, prices were decent for the quality. Servers were attentive and friendly. Will continue to patronise.

Staff service was outstanding. That made the delicious food even better. My family, 2 young toddlers, my wife, and I were on an unusual adventure to the area and chanced upon this rustic Italian restaurant.

Warm friendly atmosphere and a very friendly crew that serves up quality Italian classics.

Would definitely visit and recommend👍🏻
We had a lovely brunch with family - food & service all amazing!
The food was delicious and I absolutely loved the pepperoni pizza

They are a good and reliable supplier of Italian produce and also run the famous 'la pizzaola' restaurant chain which has outlets at jalan riang, Kalidasa and dunearn. Service staff are friendly and attentive. They have been around a long time as well. I would recommend giving them a try

Absolutely love Ladda House! Every dish is crafted with so much care, and you can really taste the authenticity in each bite. It’s clear the cook goes the extra mile to source genuine Thai ingredients, which makes a huge difference in flavor.
The place itself feels like a cozy, welcoming home rather than just a restaurant. The warm and friendly couple who run it make the whole experience even more special, you feel genuinely taken care of from the moment you walk in.

I was so engrossed in eating that I forgot to take photos — which probably says everything you need to know. Highly recommended if you’re craving authentic Thai food made with heart!

There were 8 of us for dinner and we totally enjoyed ourselves! The cozy ambience, friendly hosts & superb delicious meal! I had “幸福感” when biting into every bit of the dishes! Must thank our friend, Will for the good recommendation!

My 2nd time at this private home Thai dining experience last night. Every dish was full of flavour, care and authenticity. The host and his wife made the evening extra special - welcoming, knowledgeable and clearly passionate about what they do. Highly recommended.

Cannot imagine a flat could house a literal restaurant serving amazing quality Thai dishes that you may not find on your trip to Bangkok. Loved the flavours and heartfelt dishes. Portion was huge, you will definitely leave stomach and heart full😋

Had the opportunity to dine at Laddas for a friends’ get-together. The private dining experience was fantastic.  The hosts were warm and friendly, above and beyond what you would get in a public restaurant setting. Somehow they were always around when you need their attention, while having our space+privacy for our chats and conversations.  The atmosphere+ambience were cosy and relaxed, super comfy.  The authentic Thai food is top notched.  Check out the king prawns! Thank you host-cum-chef Terrence and Laddas for the warm reception and gracious hospitality.  Highly recommended!  This is a must-try!
Found the Tim sum tasty. Fish porridge had decent amount of fish. Siew Mai was decently sized. Overall worth a return when around the area.
Have not tried for years. Decided to eat again on the first day of November 2025. It's terrible.. Food were lukewarm and hard. Standards have deteriorated so much.

This has to be the highest rated most lousy dimsum I have ever tried. The fried carrot cake, siew mai, har kau, and big pao all taste like crap compared to the famous every item 1.50 dim sum bar franchise. Total waste of time. Totally don't understand the palette of people who say it's good
Lai Kee Pau and Siew Mai is average. Nothing to rave about. It does cost a bit more than average. Service is so so.

Purchase their bun and there’s a nylon string?!

Fail.

Tucked in a corner, it can be rather packed during weekends.

Visited once in the afternoon for some drinks.

Would love to visit one day for the zi char.
Fyi
Noodles taste normal. Salt baked chicken w spaghetti also tastes very normal and not worth the price
The tofu no longer have minced meat and coriander inside. The half chicken we order is terrible. Served cold 🥶……..the food no longer as good as last time.

Great options to go with the salted baked chicken.
Do try the otah carrot cake. probably the most flavourful carrot cake in town.
Noodles are bouncy and goes well with the chilli / vinegar. Soup wasn’t so full flavour.

Restaurant Name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken (Causeway Point)
Reviews: Nice food

Restaurant Name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken (Causeway Point)
Reviews: Noodles is good. I always ate the watercress noodles. Like the taste & the soup texture.

Restaurant Name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken (Causeway Point)
Reviews: Salt baked chicken and chilli was excellent but quite pricey.

Restaurant Name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken (Causeway Point)
Reviews:
Recognized the name. We ordered 3 bowls of noodles - one signature, and two fisherman. Both types of dishes failed us...

I had the abalone noodle. The amount of abalone was so little, the extra money didn't seem worth it. The bowl looked like it had a lot of chilli but was really bland. The soup was somewhat better, and the fried fishball and chilli dip was best.

My parents had the fisherman dish. She felt the fried fish bean items would be better deep fried.

Restaurant Name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken (Toa Payoh 500)
Reviews: Long time eat the watercress soup noodle in Causeway point, overall still as good. Can add pork lards is plus point. Service also ok. Didn't know got yong toufu set. Better than kok kee i feel. Added abalone stick overall $10.40

Restaurant Name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken (Toa Payoh 500)
Reviews:
Everytime I come, they always say there's only 1 serving of the green sauce left. Interesting...

Edit: I usually come at 6

Restaurant Name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken (Toa Payoh 500)
Reviews: Went for dinner on 21/02/26 at 6.40pm at their outlet at Toa Payoh Cebtral foodcourt. Human hair spotted on the cutlery container. Chilli and cutlery running low and not refilled.

Restaurant Name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken (Toa Payoh 500)
Reviews: 4 cursed workers (1 female & 3 male) at the counter on 18 Feb at 1124hrs were extremely rude. They thought of themselves, delayed my takeaway order by 17mins without apologies. Poor owner Burnt salary to them to make them chase away regular customers.

Restaurant Name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken (Toa Payoh 500)
Reviews:
I’ve been a fan of Lam’s for years, especially their salt-baked chicken, but my visit today was extremely disappointing. For the first time in all my years of ordering Lam’s, the staff were rude and made me feel very uncomfortable.

Ordering was stressful, the lady cashier repeatedly questioned my a la carte chicken order. Then when I asked about the braised mushroom noodle (I always order this online but the menu in-store is tea flower mushroom noodle), the cashier just said “ok ok” without clarifying and cut me off to choose the noodle.

When I collected my order, the man with glasses handed it over in a dismissive manner. The cashier shook her head and then they both laughed in a way that made me very uncomfortable. When I asked for extra chili, the man responded with sarcastic-sounding “ok”s before finally giving it to me and then they laughed again. I’ve ordered here several times and know him as a polite and patient person based on my previous encounters.

Being treated this way was very upsetting and disappointing. I wouldn’t expect any customer to be treated like this.
High price, less portion

Not too bad.... Cant really say they deserve a 5 stars, but for a mixed vege rice, the only one Ard this area, I think it's good value (esp if U have the 10% for working there).
The food was above average for sure, but nothing fantastic. But as a daily meal, this is worth a thought.
Only issue, their selection of food is pretty limited.
So it's probably a 7.5 out of 10, and still I have come back here over and over again.
(No pics now, but will post the next time)
All 3 of my dishes were cold. Fish cold, tofu cold, steam egg cold, terrible. Will never eat from them again.

Restaurant Name: Lao Er Herbal Soup 2 (Ah Er Soup 2)
Reviews:
Decent soup and rice.

However, we were disappointed by what felt like a lack of transparency. The olive rice served appeared to be scraped from the bottom of the pot, with hard, chewy chunks, and it looked like plain white rice had been quietly mixed in to make up the portion. We only realised this after we got home.

We completely understand that it may have been the end of the day and supplies were running low — customers are usually very reasonable. But a simple heads-up would have been appreciated. Trying to pass it off without informing customers doesn’t feel honest.

Restaurant Name: Lao Er Herbal Soup 2 (Ah Er Soup 2)
Reviews: The soup used to be quite oily. It's better now. If F&B entities do not heed customers' feedbacks e.g. via this channel or others, it won't be long will close shop. The one near boon lay shopping centre just closed shop.

Restaurant Name: Lao Er Herbal Soup 2 (Ah Er Soup 2)
Reviews:
Tasty Soup. Good portion for the price. Not much qalams about it. Worth a try if u enjoy double boil soup!

Located inside FM Food Master.

Carpark (at a fee) and washroom available on site.

Place can be warm on a hot day.

Restaurant Name: Lao Er Herbal Soup 2 (Ah Er Soup 2)
Reviews: I bought lotus root soup and asked for no meat cos I want more lotus root. End up $7.10 soup + rice and only 3 pieces of lotus root. What a reap off!!!!!

Restaurant Name: Lao Er Herbal Soup 2 (Ah Er Soup 2)
Reviews: Probably one of the best soup in jurong west , soup had multiple layers along with ingredients. The pumpkin rice is to die for.
Curry fish head and salted egg pork ribs. 🤤 Must order!
Nice place to dine....
It is a small eating place with reasonabe good taste and good price. Cosy for family dinning oit

I had a fantastic experience at Lao Hero Kitchen. The food was absolutely delicious—everything tasted fresh and flavorful. What really stood out, though, was the service. The staff were incredibly friendly and made us feel right at home. I highly recommend checking this place out!
I'm feeling sick that's why I'm taking these. The boss are very friendly, I knew them very well.

If u want to have good quality soups but hate sweating out eating at hawker centres/ coffee shops… this is the plc.
It offers a variety of good, wholesome boiled soups in a spacious aircon seatings.
Ordered the lotus root peanut soup. The soup was good, and it’s not too salty. (For those want it more salty, can add to taste at your preference)
The pumpkin rice was soft and nice too.

Will be back to try their other soups in future.

Decent lunch at Star Vista with fuss free set lunches. About $17 per pax. The soups are warm and very nice, and allows for one time refill.

The dishes are really not their specialty.
Food was great. The service was quick and the place is well air conditioned

Lao Huo Tang. Franchise with 10 stores island-wide. Set lunch $69 and three tea, with total cost $89.81 (after GST & service charge). Soup was well boiled, with soft meat. Prawn was not as nice. 辣子鸡was good.

Plenty of tables in this restaurant. Arrived at 11.45 am and got a good table.

My favourite Mee Hoon kueh in the north area. Used to come on Saturdays for lunch and always order dried mee hoon kueh with extra vegetables and fried fish on the side.
Since July, they now open until 8pm.
The evening shift is managed by younger duo and I’ve been here for dinner 3 times since. All 3 times, I found the evening kueh to be a bit too thick and not cooked thoroughly, leaving this raw flour dough taste. Will try and see if I could request it to be thinner the next time, or maybe just stick to coming back on Saturday afternoons.

Atmosphere: Can be a bit stuffy at times, especially in the afternoon. There are 80s-90s songs being played in the evening sometimes, which is a vibe I enjoy.

Update: They're no longer open in the evening.
Fried fish soup was worth the price and delicious too. Nice and crispy. Not sure why the rating is so low. Def try the fried fish or the seafood soup. Cant comment on the ban mian tho!

Use to like their food very much. Always come with friend n family. But prices had gone up alot. I don't mind if the food is still good but disappointed. And their attitude and service is very bad especially their younger generation.
Overpriced fish soup... For a bowl of fish soup : $9
Bad attitude, uncooked dough, never buying again

Tried Lao San Dry Traditional Prawn Noodle with spice for the second time and I really like it! The noodles were cooked just right — not overly soft — and the flavour wasn’t too salty. The soup on the side was really good too, super rich and comforting. Definitely a satisfying bowl!
Terrible service by the lady preparing the noodles. I didn't have smaller change other than $50 and she berated me like she owes me a living. Do not patronise.
Bought prawn noodle soup. Their soup portion is very pathetic. I don’t know how that is considered as soup.

Super bad experience. I wanted to add some chilli padi. The guy told me they use sambal. So I told him about the chilli padi inside the soy sauce container. I was scooping here and there because there wasn’t much left. After I’m done, guess what, he opened the freaking fridge, took out a freaking container of chilli padi, and freaking refilled the soy sauce container with full of chilli padi. I told him that he could have put some in my container and he just brushed me off. When he was putting my container into a plastic bag, I told him it’s ok, he looked at me, continued whatever he was doing, I told him again it’s ok, he continued whatever he was doing, and handled it to me in plastic bag.

Also, they don’t give u any soup in plastic bag. You have to pay for container or bring your own container.

I swear I will NEVER return again.

Ordered intestine noodles add prawn. $2 for the prawns and just 1 min later, forget to add my prawns in. Came home to realize it’s prawn-less. Soup pic - paid a dollar for extra soup takeaway and only half a container. Cashier Msian, cook China here in Spore work but both can’t speak English at all.
Great place to find all type of good food for an affordable price. The vibe is also super nice.
Food not good

It's a very cool place to visit as a tourist, but honestly everything we tried was disgusting.
Special mention to Habib's Express, which also had terrible service

Great selection of food from multiple vendors.

We got there around 2:30 pm and just missed the lunch rush. It appeared that some of the vendors were already closed and others simply exhausted.

We had bites from two different vendors and both were very good.

We couldnt seem to find napkins and had to clean tables before we sat down. Some vendors did not sell drinks, but we did find Tiger beer.

Glad we stopped by!

Restaurant Name: Lau Phua Chay Authentic Roasted Delicacies
Reviews: In Alexandra Village Hawker. Next to the famous avocado drink stall. Decent plate of charsiew rice. The sauce is very different from most stores. Savory rather than sweet

Restaurant Name: Lau Phua Chay Authentic Roasted Delicacies
Reviews: One of the best roasted meats in the business, so don’t be deceived by the presentation. The sauce is savoury and not too sweet which is excellent.

Restaurant Name: Lau Phua Chay Authentic Roasted Delicacies
Reviews: チャーシューライスの認識が変わるほど美味い！オススメは叉焼焼肉飯、独特のタレがクセになる。チリを少し混ぜると旨さ倍増😇1人でもスモールサイズでは無く、中以上のサイズを頼んだほうが幸せになれる！皿の色が最近緑色からオレンジに変わった模様。ずっと緑色だったので、なんとなく違和感がある💦

(Update: This stall will permanently close by the end of June 2026 as there are not enough customers to keep the business going due to low footfall at the coffeeshop.
(The much-raved ‘Oh My Don’ Japanese stall at the same coffeeshop has already shut due to this)
So best enjoy the food before this stall shuts permanently!)

Unlike other zi char stalls, this stall sells a healthier and more wholesome selection of dishes that one doesn’t feel ‘jelak’ after eating.

Besides a choice of different styles of steam fish, it also sells a lot of other delicious healthy steamed dishes as well such as steamed prawns, steamed pork ribs in black bean sauce, black fungus steamed chicken, steamed egg, steamed otah.

There are plenty of other dishes too like Curry fish head, curry fish meat and some Zi Char dishes like prawn paste chicken, different styles of fried rice, San lor hor fun, stir fried Nai Bai with garlic, onion ginger fish slices, etc.

Although not on the menu, customers can ask for a smaller portion of a particular dish with rice, eg 姜葱鱼片饭 and they will charge accordingly like $7.

$3.50 Budget Meal is Egg Fried Rice.
Open for both lunch and dinner.
Close on Tuesday

The food.. wooo! The reason why I’m here.. unmatched. Must try! Uncle is very polite and brings warm not just in serving but the taste of the food. Price is reasonable. Place is peaceful and convenient with car park above the eatery. Had a hearty meal before another round of CNY reunion.

Food served were fresh and nice taste. Ordered the beancurb, slice steam fish, prawn paste chicken, nai Bai, steam otah. The dishes were prepared with less oil and salt with taste. I quite enjoyed the food.
Fish and prawns ingredients are fresh in the dishes sold by this store

San lau hor fan and steam fish really slaps, curry fish slice also slaps.
Idk why but onlu the egg fried cutlet rice is one of the most blend dish u can eat here. The rest of the menu is all good except for the egg fried cutlet rice. Cannot taste the egg fried and no msg

My recent excursion to Mad Charcoal during the sun-drenched lunch hour proved to be more than a mere meal; it was a masterclass in the delicate choreography between fire and freshness.

The plate arrived with an architectural grace that belied its rustic origins. Resting atop a dark, leaf-shaped vessel, the Pork Belly sat in a triumphant row of golden-brown tiles. Beside it, a verdant sprawl of romaine, punctuated by the ruby-red arc of tomato wedges and the golden shards of what appeared to be crisp beancurd skin, offered a vibrant visual counterpoint.

One does not simply eat this pork; one experiences the Maillard reaction in its most evolved state. The skin boasted a glass-like shatter, yielding to a layer of rendered fat that possessed a velvety mouthfeel, nearly liquifying upon contact. The meat itself remained impeccably succulent, whispering of a long, disciplined roast that preserved its structural integrity while infusing it with a deep, umami-rich soul. The subtle, char-kissed aroma lingering on the palate provided a haunting reminder of the charcoal’s transformative power.

To find such technical proficiency at a lunchtime special price point feels almost like a heist. While the evening service may offer a more lingering ambiance, the midday experience at Mad Charcoal is a streamlined, high-octane celebration of smoke and seasoning. It is proof that high-caliber culinary execution need not always come with a staggering premium.

Newly opened Mala stall. I decided to give it a try. Approached by a malay lady (surprised!  First time served mala stall by a malay! ). IT seems this stall is halal? (I did not check whether they has the logo)

Picked my ingredients (7) of them,  no pork so I chose chicken. Handed over for her to calculate price. Came up to $21... Costly for a medium portion, but I did add quite an amount of chicken meat.

They accept CDC voucher,  but was not ready and wifi connection was down when they tried using it to scan. No choice. Cash payment it is then. She then passed me change with electronic tab.

Cooking - the lady put the ingredients onto what look like automated cooking machine (interesting), after that I did not go kaypo further. It took around 6 minutes before my buzzer signalled me to collect.

Packaging - Good quality plastic container with good quality chopsticks and disposable wooden spoon. Packed nicely and no spill. Nice.  Good quality,  but bad for environment 😅

Taste - I ordered mild spicy. They put quite a lot of dried chilli and peppercorns. They also added some spices which I usually did not find in other mala. Star anise, bay leaf and somewhat olive lookalike but do not taste like it. (Google internet picture one similar is either it's nutmeg,  or another spice named "cashew ") They also added orange peel! Interesting!  Taste wise,  it did not have the wokhei, and I find it not as aromatic, but for those who wanted to try out the added spices you are welcome.

Conclusion:  taste and price should improve. Must remember this is hawker,  not restaurant.

Went there on a Sunday evening for dinner with friends. Place is relatively small and cozy, with the seating divided into a lower and upper floor area. We were seated upstairs as our reservation was for a bigger group, the lower area seemed to be packed as we were leaving so its probably best to make a reservation ahead of time if you're intending to come during peak dinner hours.

We ordered a selection of sides which included the Fried Calamari and Chilli Cheese Fries. Both were decent, although the fries felt like regular fries that you can find at NTUC.

Despite the relatively weak start, the pork ribs were a complete 180. They were quite literally "fall off the bone" tender and were simply delicious. I personally found the honey mustard flavour to be a tad too sweet to my liking and honestly preferred the Signature Original and Hickory flavours more. Nevertheless, if you're looking for a plate of excellent ribs, I can wholeheartedly recommend them.

Wanting to end off the meal with a dessert, we ordered a variety which included the Bro Bruce Browned Butter Brownie and the Belgian Waffles. The brownie was great, the waffle on the other hand was quite disappointing.

All in all, I would definitely still recommend this place just on the strength of the ribs alone.

A cute lil restaurant that intends to remind you that Abuelita always cooks best, this place serves a nice amount of Spanish dishes that does not vary. We ordered a few tapas and a main dish to fill our stomach for 2 during dinner over the weekend.

For tapas, we thought the portion was just right. Although I thought the price could be a lil much more reasonable.
We ordered oysters, oxtail stew, lobster bisque.

Oysters were fresh, I thought one of them is a lil too salty for some reason. But other than that, the size is reasonable. Simple food with hot sauce by the side. Nothing fancy & just direct.

The lobster bisque was served with a slice of garlic focaccia by the side. I thought that they could serve w much more bits of the crab meat inside or more focaccia slices to enjoy the sauce with. We thought the sauce is a bit wasteful seeing how much sauce left after dipping our slice in the plate. There was also only like 4 meat pieces in it. It will be great if provided more tho I understand that it’s suppose to be a small dish.

We thought the oxtail was tender and the mash potatoes were creamy light and smooth. This is by far one of our favourites from our order. The sauce was flavourful yet mild in a way that you could taste the mash potatoes after mixing it.

Last but not least, the seafood paella for 2 pas was good. Full of flavour, and it’s not too dry or wet. The only thing I’d like is that for someone who doesn’t like peeling seafood, you might find the clams is a bit too much as you will have to dig out rice from the shells. The prawns served were fresh, but and juicy.

I would love it that they would also offer service to refil water for us. I thought it was a bit weird considering that the time we went weren’t really a peak time yet. But overall, I would come again for some Abuealita’s food.

The Mountbatten Bar & Grill at the British Club is an excellent restaurant that combines refined dining, warm hospitality, and a peaceful atmosphere. It’s quiet and elegant, making it an ideal spot to enjoy a relaxing meal. The staff are exceptionally friendly and attentive, always serving with genuine smiles and ensuring every guest feels well taken care of.

The food is consistently outstanding, from starters to desserts. The MBT Signature Truffle Focaccia is soft, fragrant, and infused with the rich aroma of truffle — a perfect start to the meal. The Traditional French Onion Soup is another highlight, deeply flavorful with a rich, slow-cooked broth and topped with Emmentaler and Gruyère toast that adds just the right balance of saltiness and creaminess. The Grilled Ibérico Pork Neck is beautifully cooked — tender, juicy, and full of natural flavor, showing great attention to detail in preparation.

The true showstopper, however, is the Crêpe Suzette. This dessert is not only delicious but also a delightful performance. The staff prepare and cook it right in front of you on a rolling cart, explaining each step and ingredient along the way. The orange juice used is freshly squeezed from real oranges, giving the sauce a vibrant, natural sweetness and aroma. Combined with butter, sugar, and liqueur, it creates a thick, glossy orange sauce that coats the delicate crêpes perfectly. The result is fantastic — warm, fragrant, and bursting with citrus flavor.

Overall, the Mountbatten Bar & Grill offers an exceptional dining experience within the British Club — delicious food, attentive service, and a serene atmosphere. It’s a wonderful choice for both special occasions and quiet, indulgent dinners.

I have always visited Mountbatten Bar & Grill whenever they change their menu. Been here since a long long time, I think my earliest memory of dining here was in 2015-2016. Food & service never disappoints. I love their sourdough so much, it tastes really great with their butter. I have also always loved their lobster bisque, it is a must-try. Their latest menu is by far their greatest, yet. I enjoyed the scallop & my partner – their special’s for that day: the Foie Gras & Crab. The ambience is terrific for people who prefers a less rowdy environment.

The Mountbatten Room at the British Club Singapore exudes an air of refined elegance and historical significance. Named after Lord Louis Mountbatten, the last British Viceroy of India and a key figure in Singapore's post-war history, the room pays homage to its namesake with a tasteful blend of colonial charm and contemporary sophistication.

The upmarket restaurant serves as a versatile venue, hosting a myriad of events ranging from formal dinners and business gatherings to cultural celebrations. With its panoramic windows overlooking lush greenery, the Mountbatten Room seamlessly integrates the club's British legacy with Singapore's tropical landscape.

Whether savoring a traditional British high tea or engaging in lively conversations during social events, visitors to the Mountbatten Room experience a curated blend of nostalgia and contemporary luxury. It stands as a testament to the enduring connection between the British Club and Singapore's historical tapestry, providing a distinguished setting for both reflection and celebration.

Finally made it to Naked Finn, a seafood spot I first noticed more than a decade ago when it was just a humble roadside shack in Gillman Barracks. Since then, it has evolved into a sleeker, more polished space just a stone’s throw away, without losing its soul. The trek down was well worth it – the seafood here is all about pristine freshness and precise, respectful cooking - a nod to the "Naked" in its name.

A zesty chilled beehoon crowned with crisp sakura ebi set the tone: bright, refreshing, and perked up by a punchy sambal that made for a super additive starter; we had to have seconds. The sugarloaf cabbage arrived beautifully charred and naturally sweet, lavishly cloaked in rich anchovy butter.

The undisputed star of the evening was the Soon Hock – a whole marble goby, deep-fried with its scales on so the skin turned shatteringly crisp, the flesh beneath moist and delicately sweet, lounging in a pool of light soy sauce. It’s a dish that perfectly encapsulates the kitchen’s quiet mastery of seafood.

For something more substantial, the Donabe is a no-brainer: this evening’s version featured a fillet of Madara, a flaky Pacific cod, nestled atop fluffy Koshihikari rice that soaked up all the savoury juices. Desserts kept to the same thoughtful, unfussy spirit: a house-made chendol and Thai red ruby with coconut sorbet provided a cool, nostalgic finish.

All of this was wrapped in top-shelf service – warm, genuinely friendly, and backed by authoritative knowledge of where every ingredient comes from – making for a casual yet refined seafood dinner that feels special without ever trying too hard.

I recently visited Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang at Gardens by the Bay and left feeling quite disappointed, especially compared to my previous experiences at their other outlets like Plaza Singapura.

I ordered the Indomie Ayam Cabe Ijo, which I was initially excited about, but the dish fell short of expectations. The noodles and chicken both felt cold, as if they had been pre-prepared and left sitting for a while before serving. This really affected the overall enjoyment of the meal, as Indomie dishes are usually best enjoyed hot and freshly cooked.

Flavor-wise, it was decent, but nothing stood out enough to make up for the lack of freshness. The textures were also slightly off, with the noodles lacking that springy bite you would expect from a well-executed dish.

Given the location at Gardens by the Bay, I was hoping for a higher standard or at least consistency with their other branches. Unfortunately, this visit didn’t deliver. I would recommend the management review their food preparation and serving process to ensure dishes are served hot and fresh, as it makes a significant difference to the dining experience.

Newton Food Center is often touted as a 'must visit' for tourists in Singapore and, unfortunately, this results in high footfall despite the experience warranting it.

The food is quite okay-okay. Nothing spectacular, just run of the mill hawker food at above average prices.

The main issue is that the hawker uncles/aunties seem to be a bit more 'sales-y' and pushy than other hawkers. In most other hawker centers in Singapore, they would simply leave you be (unless you have questions to ask) and if you should wish to purchase, you may approach the stall. At Newton Food Center, the staff are constantly trying to sell to you when you are wandering around browsing. This is called 'touting' and its not part of the usual hawker experience but happens too often in Newton Food Center. This makes the experience far less pleasant as you have to ignore and avoid eye contact and reflects poorly on Singapore and our hawker culture to tourists who come to visit us and wish to experience our hawker culture first hand.

There was also an issue of some stalls trying to effectively 'monopolize' the tables near their stall. How it's supposed to work in Singapore hawker centers is that you simply sit at any available seat in the hawker center, purchase your food from any stall you choose, and enjoy your food. However, when me and my friends found a table near a stall, the stallowner came to us trying to 'sell' us drinks or food. Although he didn't persist, it was an uncomfortable experience and not what hawker culture in Singapore is about.

As a general rule of thumb, good food doesn't need to be 'pushed' or 'sold'- it sells itself! Tourists are recommended to go to other hawkers like Old Airport Hawker for a more true and authentic hawker experience.

If you’re in Singapore and want the classic chili crab experience with a postcard view of Marina Bay, this place will absolutely deliver. The chili crab itself was good. Rich sauce, fresh crab, plenty messy in the way chili crab should be. That said, the price made us blink a bit. It’s one of those meals where halfway through you look at the bill and think, “Well… I guess we’re paying for the view tonight.”

Beyond the crab, we actually found better value in the rest of the menu. The pork ribs were excellent and the fried rice was solid comfort food after wrestling with the crab. The bao buns were perfect for soaking up that chili sauce too. Owners and managers were warm and welcoming, though the rest of the service felt more assembly line than hospitality. Not rude, just very efficient and a bit impersonal.

Overall I’d call this a generous 4 out of 5. It leans touristy and very expensive, but that doesn’t automatically make it bad. If you want the chili crab “experience” with Marina Bay glowing in the background, it checks the box nicely. Time your reservation to the Marina Bay Sands light show and you’ll at least feel like the scenery helped justify the bill.

Would I rush back? Probably not. We tried chili crab a couple times in Singapore and this was the best version we had, but it’s still a $150–$200 per person novelty dinner. Fun to do once, great views, mediocre service, and a reminder that sometimes the sauce is cheaper than the scenery.

Poh Poh Roasted Chicken Rice sits quietly in the far reaches of Teban Gardens Food Centre, a place few would visit unless they live or work nearby. Yet this unassuming stall rewards anyone who makes the trip. Although Google Maps lists its hours as 7.30am to 8.30pm, the owners were still preparing when I first arrived and mentioned they would be ready at 10am. I returned later in the afternoon at 4pm, when only a small handful of stalls were open, and Poh Poh was among the few serving at that hour.

The steamed chicken had already sold out for the day, a good sign of its popularity, so I ordered the roasted chicken rice. Portions come in two sizes at $4 and $5, with an optional egg for an additional dollar. The owners were warm and generous, even encouraging me to come back for more rice if I was still hungry. A simple bowl of soup accompanied the dish.

The serving was hearty and satisfying. The roasted chicken was tender with a pleasant smokiness, the rice fragrant and well-seasoned, and the overall plate comforting in its simplicity. If anything could be improved, it would be the soup, which felt more functional than distinctive. Still, the meal was enjoyable and filling, and Poh Poh stands out as one of the better chicken rice options in the Teban Gardens area.

After trying the Western food and the Indonesian fried chicken at Rasa Rasa @ Yishun, I was quite satisfied with the food quality and service. However, that completely changed today after I tried the chicken rice stall there.
At lunchtime today, I went to the chicken rice stall and asked for a takeaway chicken rice with two chicken wings and chicken gizzard. Yes, it is really that simple and easy to understand. Yet the Chinese staff member taking the order took almost five minutes just to understand what I wanted. I am not new to ordering chicken rice — at other stalls, whether Halal or non-Halal, they understand immediately. I really don’t understand why communication at this stall was so difficult.
Even the Chinese staff member chopping the chicken beside him had already understood what I wanted, yet the one taking the order remained totally confused and only got more and more lost.
Then came the most unbelievable part. I was told that the price for my order had to be calculated as follows:
•	Chicken rice with one wing: $6
•	Extra chicken meat (because the second wing must be counted this way): $5
•	Chicken gizzard: $1.80
•	Two takeaway boxes: $0.60
Total: $13.40
For a simple request of two chicken wings, I was forced to pay an additional $5 for extra chicken meat, which felt like a form of forced upselling. I reluctantly accepted it.
But the shocking part came when the food was prepared. The “extra chicken” turned out to be dry, skinless chicken breast — completely white, with no fat and extremely tough in texture.
As for the chicken gizzard, the staff took out a box of pre-sliced gizzards from the refrigerator — clearly frozen leftovers from the previous day. Anyone who knows food safety understands that offal spoils very easily. Yet they were selling overnight frozen gizzards. In my decades of eating chicken rice in Singapore, this is the first time I have ever seen chicken offal that is not freshly sliced on the spot.
Compared to other chicken rice stalls that usually cost under $10, here I paid a much higher price while also having to worry about food safety risks.
This chicken rice stall has now moved straight to the top of my “never return” list. I will also make sure to alert nearby residents online about this experience.

If you’re visiting Bali and craving an authentic, high-quality seafood experience, Bali Nikmat in Kuta is an absolute must-visit. From the moment you pull up to the restaurant—easily recognizable by its iconic giant crab sign—you know you’re in for a treat. This establishment has been a staple since 2000, and it’s easy to see why it has maintained such a stellar reputation for over two decades.

The atmosphere is classic and bustling, perfectly capturing that "old-school" Chinese restaurant charm. It’s the kind of place that feels lively and welcoming, making it ideal for large family gatherings or a feast with friends. Despite how busy it gets, the service remains impressively efficient and attentive, ensuring that you’re never waiting too long for your next course.

Now, let’s talk about the food, which is the real star of the show. The seafood here is exceptionally fresh, likely because they specialize in live catches. We ordered the Creamy Salted Egg Crab, and it was life-changing. The sauce was rich, velvety, and perfectly seasoned, clinging to the succulent, sweet crab meat. It is arguably the best version of this dish on the entire island. We also tried the Fried Garlic Butter Prawns, which were crispy on the outside and incredibly juicy on the inside, packed with aromatic garlic flavor.

Another standout was the Steamed Live Fish with Soy Sauce. The fish was steamed to perfection—flaky and delicate—while the light soy dressing enhanced the natural sweetness of the seafood without overpowering it. Even the side dishes, like the stir-fried kailan with garlic, were executed with precision, providing a fresh and crunchy balance to the rich seafood mains.

While it is a Chinese-style restaurant, the flavors are elevated and distinctly premium. The portions are generous, and though it’s a "bustling spot," the quality of the ingredients justifies every bit of the price. Whether you are a local or a tourist, Bali Nikmat delivers a consistent, world-class dining experience. I’ve been to many seafood spots in Bali, but I keep coming back here because the flavors are simply unmatched. Five stars all the way—don’t leave Bali without eating here!

Reviews: On CNY Eve we prepared a feast for our family but was missing the butane fuel canister to cook the hotpot. I walked by this restaurant and asked to buy 2 canisters, and the 2 sweet Thai staff gave it to me without question and refused to take my money, effectively saving our reunion dinner. Seriously we need to see our migrant workers as the backbone of our society, and a blessing to all. Thank you!

Restaurant Name: Siam Square Mookata (Best Mookata Restaurant In Singapore) (Upper Thomson)
Reviews:
We planned to get a late-night mookata snack on a whim, just the two of us. We thought it’d be a cheap and cheerful meal—we were told the buffet was over $30 ➕➕
per person, but the final bill came to a whopping $130 total 🥲

We asked if they had an à la carte option when we walked in, and the staff said yes. Then my husband decided to switch to the buffet instead.

First, they handed us an à la carte bill for $112. I was shocked and pointed out we’d had the buffet, not à la carte. The staff looked dismissive, then reprinted a buffet bill—which was even more expensive at $130. And they refused to switch back to the $112 bill, claiming they’d printed too many receipts already.

To make it worse, the buffet didn’t include all dishes—some items were extra charge, and the staff never bothered to mention that. I even had to ask if water was included with the buffet because they didn’t say a word about it. The staff spent most of the time on their phones since it was quiet late at night, with zero proper communication.

And when I checked the receipt at home? They charged us for 3 bottles of Coke Zero when we only had 2. Seriously, what were they even doing at work?

This was our first time here, and it’ll definitely be the last. For $130, we could’ve had way better hot pot or BBQ with actual service. Lesson learned with buffets: ask every single detail before you order. Sure, we could’ve been more thorough—but the restaurant’s service and staff accountability need a massive upgrade.

Avoid this place at all costs:
SIAM SQUARE MOOKATA (UPPER THOMSON)

Another sore point is the cafe can get extremely and unbearable noisy to the point I have to use earbuds given that they now make the bread in-house here, and loud, noisy financial advisers (and even one religious preacher) like to talk shop with elderly customers. You will also occasionally see mynahs coming into the shop. One time I even saw a bird eating off a woman's plate and I tried to chase it away, and she turned around in horror and shrieked. I can only hope noise levels can be reduced or dealt with through better sound insulation and food portions restored to their former glory and service staff who actually enjoy the service industry work here.

Came to try porridge here. Ordered chicken porridge. It is very nice. So far, it is the best porridge that I have tried in Singapore. Nice to eat hot porridge in an air-conditioned place. Would not try this in a hot weather setting. Need to get yr own seats and seating is limited.

23 Sep 2024 Update: tried fish porridge. This is nice as well.

Ordered traditional set 1. Overall taste is ok. Eggs nicely cooked and already de shelled on behalf which is a plus point. However abit disappointed with amount of toasting and butter. Almost non-existent.
Nicely done eggs and toast. Beautiful as you can see from the photos. The Kopi o kosong is sweet itself without sugar.

here bright and early at 630am — overall great value for the quality

- tea c kosong was warm and rich with subtle sweetness
- half boiled eggs were perfect, not undercooked nor overcooked, imo better than Yakun
- bun was good (toasted for you)
- lady at store was polite and patient
- turnaround was quick, there were two folks infront of me but i got mine within 5 mins (needed to toast the bread and warm the eggs)

Was surprised to find out that the traditional set was sold out when I arrived at close to 10am on a Sunday.

Thus I had the thick peanut toast instead. It took a bit longer than the other sets, but came still pretty crispy, with decent amount of spread.

Eggs were too overcooked for my liking - the yolk while still viscous, remained stuck together.

Kopi-c kosong iced was pretty good. Coffee was what you'd expect, but they did not skimp on the evaporated milk.

came on a saturday morning around 9.30am and there was a snacking queue here! tried their traditional kaya toast set & taro toast. kaya toast was thin & crispy with the right amount of kaya. eggs and kopi were all right, appreciate if the egg yolks could be runnier. taro toast was a letdown - taro spread tasted like a blend of coconut & white chocolate..? not a huge fan. props to them for the innovative idea though!

Beef Stroganoff Pasta: Delicious and fragrant sauce with the moistest and softest steak cuts! There’s also mushrooms and bell pepper, although I wish there was more bell pepper 😋The amount of sauce and the portion size were just right 👍

Salmon Pink Pasta: The salmon was also very soft and moist! Probably the best salmon I have ever tasted, it was cooked really well 😋

Tiramisu Latte (Special): Not sure what the crunchy bites on top are, but they tasted like thin biscuits and added a really nice touch to the drink! Loved the cheese foam on top — it tasted amazing!! Definitely would order this again, only served cold ❄️

Chicken Floss Seaweed Tater Tots: Can’t go wrong if you love tater tots! Great for sharing and super crispy 👍

Homemade Nougats: Can't really tell what flavours they were though but they were soft and had an interesting texture!

The lady who served us was really nice and the whole place felt very homely, loved the music choice too! it sounded like songs from the old Disney movies
Okay. Compact, nice service. Food is good
Love the food, especially the tom yum pasta and crab meat pasta. Service is fantastic too!

Excellent service. Super sweet and nice owner. Love the tofu, perfect balance of flavours, half with a delicious egg sauce half with a sweet sesame.. the flavour of the tofu still comes through, and somehow becomes 10000x tastier....

I had the k style cream chicken pasta, my girlfriend had the bacon carb, beautiful al dente noddle that was warm and hearty but never gelat. Many flavours, i love the seaweed in the k style cream chicken

There are a few fish dishes to choose from.
I came for the Pig's Trotters!

When I sat, and started to eat, the meat was soft and tender and very delightfully tasty! Traditionally done to perfection. I savour ever drop of it. Yums!

Thank you for a wonderful experience. 😃👍🏽✨

The sausage was just gelatin and very little meat. Ngoh hiang had little taste. Only the chili was still good. Really do hope they can recover their original taste.

Restaurant Name: Sin Sin Ngo Hiang Prawn Cracker
Reviews: One of the best Wu Xiang I have tried so far. And items are homemade. Very underrated stall. Uncle & Aunty very friendly too

Restaurant Name: Sin Sin Ngo Hiang Prawn Cracker
Reviews: Been coming here for 18 years, food is not very oily and price point is just great. The prawn cracker has lots of prawn in it and has a crunch. The auntie remembers me and is always very welcoming, although I don't live near I love coming by and enjoying my childhood Ngo Hiang.

Restaurant Name: Sin Sin Ngo Hiang Prawn Cracker
Reviews: Ngo Hiang is not bad, the chili sauce could be stronger.
in this sin xiang kee teochew noodle stall,the foods and plain rice prices must be adjust downwards please.the plain rice must sell at 50 cent.the foods must be delivered to the customer table.

My favourite organ soup stall in Yew Tee. For a 4.50 portion, I think there are plenty of ingredients! I love the soup, brewed well and has strong 酸菜 taste. Using loin meat is great for texture, normally they would use small intestines.

Although at night if you purchase, it taste a little too concentrated. Might need to add water periodically!

The auntie’s son can be a little cranky, but he knows how to cook!

Paid $4.50 for a bowl of bak chor mee. The noodle was springy. The pork slices were tasty and tender. The pig liver and meat balls were also tender. The free pig organ soup was tasty too. Altough I asked not to add chilli sauce to the noodle, there was no ketchup or black vinegar added - very different from other bak chor mee stalls. Nevertheless, this was the best bak chor mee I have eaten in Yew Tee. Service was prompt as there was no queue.

Delicious foods 😍
Price is reasonable.
Mee Rebus is tasty. I added ladyfingers.
Food is tastless and expensive. Plus small opens whenever they feel like it. 1st and 15th day of the month also suka suka open and close. Terribly unreliable.

Sumptuous Vegetarian Lor Mee ($4.00)
Topped up an additional vegetarian Ngor Hiang (素五香) which cost another $1.50. Mom shared some green vegetables from her order w me.

Overall. It's filling. If you looking for Vegetarian food in this food centre, this is the place to patronise.

The most inedible vegetarian food ever .

The salted egg calamari was nice- flavourful and fried to golden crisp. Stingray was alright, the sambal lacked a punch. Portion of rice was good.

Overall, if you live nearby, this would be an option for family meals.
Food is great. Kids super love the chicken wings. The sea bass deal is worth it too.

Delightful dining at Siong BBQ Seafood. Their signature Hot Plate Stingray was delicious, with tender stingray cooked in a flavorful sambal sauce. I also enjoyed their fresh fried fish options, which were a great accompaniment to rice.

The classic Cai Po Beancurd and the flavorful Prawn Paste Fried Chicken were delicious additions to my meal.

Great!

Particular mention to the prawn paste and fish dumplings which blew my mind - totally unexpected quality of ingredients considering the price point 💯

Came here for the first time to celebrate my partner birthday, and it was definitely worth the visit!

The staffs were awesome and very friendly. The food was great and delicious. Paying a little extra for the special request was absolutely worth it, and the birthday cake was fantastic.

We would especially like to commend Mr Areon and Mr Kishore for their hospitality and service throughout the dinner. They were super friendly and professional. This is definitely one of the best restaurant service experiences we have ever had and make us want to return for sure. Truly appreciated! Please kindly convey the message to them. 💪🏻
Perfect place for a romantic birthday dinner! Thanks for the cake Skai!

Most of the staff were Filipino, which made the experience feel even more warm and welcoming. Special thanks to Sir Benj for taking great care of us. He was very attentive, friendly, and approachable. Overall, the staff were very nice and made our first visit memorable.” 🌅

Of course you pay for the absolutely stunning views over the republic but they are well worth it - do try the vodkatinis.
Book a table on a clear day and arrive at around 17.30 to watch the planes landing at Changi and then the Sun go down. When the lights come out you will enjoy a very different set of vistas.

Visually the most exciting bar in the World!! We shall be back.

Restaurant Name: Smiths Authentic British Fish And Chips (Balmoral Plaza)
Reviews: My wife and I went there last week to celebrate an early StPatrick's Day. The fish and chips were fantastic, the Guiness was great and tge service from the young lady from Manila was exellent. Will be going again 100%

Also they said outdoor space is available for pet friendly, but the outdoor space was so run down and at the edge, plus I saw two rats outside so we quickly finished our food and ran off. They advertised as rooftop bar but there is no rooftop spot lol. Felt like I wasted my money. I think if looking for keto desserts, Ketojiak is a better option and more reasonably priced. It was our first time at Sofra Turkish Restaurant. We sensed the staff's professionalism as soon as we entered.
The Ramadan semi-buffet dinner was well-prepared and had irresistible, dainty  desserts.  We ordered lamb shish kebab and Iskender kebab and they were deliciously made with quality meat. As a health-conscious family, we can say with confidence that this restaurant serves "real food".
The Turkish tea was served piping hot -- just as it should be --perfect for sipping slowly while enjoying the charming lighting and vibrant ambience contributed by other youthful and family diners.
Let's keep it short... excellent. Great food, kind service and Bay View.

Restaurant Name: Soi 19 Thai Wanton Mee (Ang Mo Kio)
Reviews: I love their pig Trotter rice! The meat and sauce are very flavorful, marinate till gao gao kind. The staff is also very nice to accommodate my request for lean meat only =)

Restaurant Name: Soi 19 Thai Wanton Mee (Ang Mo Kio)
Reviews: Taste nice, no queue, lots of tables available, parking lots also plenty.

Restaurant Name: Soi 19 Thai Wanton Mee Dairy Farm
Reviews: My wife and I were here today (21 March 2026) for an early lunch - we live nearby, in the Dairy Farm area. Whilst I had Soi 19's Wantan Mee before, but elsewhere, today was the first time for my wife at a Soi 19 outlet. We ordered the following here today: an Original Wanton Mee and a Black Wanton Mee - both with boiled wantans instead of deep-fried wantans. Overall, the Wanton Mee was very good - with the noodles nicely al dente, and with its add-ons pairing well with the noodles; especially the fish sausages. And the soup that came in a separate bowl, though clear, was flavourful. Service here was nice enough. The dining ambience here was also nice enough as the dining tables were adequately set apart and in air-conditioned comfort.

Restaurant Name: Soi 19 Thai Wanton Mee Dairy Farm
Reviews: This is actually very good. I tried the top rated wanton mee at honglim food center before and i can say this wanton mee can fight them and may win in some taste category.

Restaurant Name: Soi 19 Thai Wanton Mee Dairy Farm
Reviews: I was surprised to come across this stall at Dairy Farm mall. Ordered 1 signature Thai Wanton noodle at $6.90 and a chicken cutlet at $7.50. The chef is so generous with the pork lard and with the ingredients. I was surprised that the noodle is so delicious. The sausage is also very tasty, I have never tasted something like that before 😝. The service was fast too. I find the cutlet crispy but salty, so I may skip that the next round. Will be back again for the wanton noodles though. Recommend to try

Restaurant Name: Soi 19 Thai Wanton Mee Dairy Farm
Reviews: Wow surprised by the mee! Very fragrant! The ingredients are plentiful! Wanton has the traditional Thai taste coupled with the pork lard cubes! The pepperish soup gives that extra kick when eaten with the mee. Yummy! Worth a try!

Restaurant Name: Soi 19 Thai Wanton Mee Dairy Farm
Reviews: Standard has dropped compared to when it is newly open. Noodles are less tangy and seasoned

Eat at your own risk. Poor service. Food so so. For a super off peak timing.,had to wait 25 minutes, this is after asking twice as people who came later were served. The stall seems to prioritize grab food orders first. Should have read the 1 star reviews.

Ordered at 8.39pm where payment is made. Ordered failed but payment went through. People who came after me were served first. Had to go up and remind them twice of my order. Finally reached my phone after 25 minutes at 9.04pm.

It's an off peak timing on a lazy Sunday night. To add to insult,I wanted to eat in but the food came In a container.

Eat at your own risk. If you can't even get it right during off peak hours, goodness I wonder what will happen during peka orders.
Food is good but takes nearly one hour to come.

The food quality and standard has dropped a lot.

This review was 6 years ago: A place to go to when I have Thai Food craving. We always get a table as we visit on weekdays. Service staff are pleasant and friendly. Tasty Thai food which are reasonably priced with huge portion. Will be good for 4 pax or more if you would like to try more dishes.

Our all time favorite is their fried pork cheeks which is only $12.

Their pricing on the menu is nett price, so i personally it cheap for such authentic Thai food adapted to local taste buds.
A diner on the street. Sooo THAI, just like its name!
A nice place to spend time with friends.

Dined at this eatery with my family on a weekday evening, we enjoyed their ordering feature as it was using a QR code on the table that you scan and proceed to place your order, view the menu, etc. They are pretty advanced in technology in that sense, which is great.
I tried their Seafood Fried Rice, ordered a Coke, the fried rice was alright, taste was generally acceptable, but not something that I would miss/crave, they were not very generous with the ingredients. The canned Coke was fine, as it's just a regular can, but I personally didn't like that they crushed the ice cubes to smaller pieces, it dilutes my drink faster and I'm just not a fan of it. To be honest, I find the meal a little overpriced, we spent about $50-60 for 3 pax, considering its location at a HDB void deck as well, not in a shopping mall or near any MRT station. We only ordered one main each, 3 drinks and a vegetable dish to share. The waiters are not exactly very friendly either, but they are not rude, they just serve the food to your table, and walk away, reminds me a little bit of robots functioning as servers. Their seating space was sufficient, and pretty comfortable, not exactly very squeezy, which I love.
Ordered their Pad Thai and a Thai Milk Tea yesterday (25/1/2026) for my dinner, the waiting time was generally acceptable, granted it was a Sunday evening, and it was at about 7pm plus, a wait is expected. The Pad Thai tasted average, I've had nicer ones, without the chili flakes, there was barely any taste to the dish. The Thai Milk Tea was also average, kind of disappointing as I had high expectations of their Thai Milk Tea, considering that they are pretty hyped, and filled with diners most of the time when I happened to pass by.

Restaurant Name: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh Jem
Reviews:
For some reason, I actually prefer their cheaper bak kut teh option. Even though the pork ribs have less meat, I find it tastier, but that is just my personal preference.
The soup is still very good, and a big plus point is that the refills are not diluted at all. I really enjoy it because it is very peppery, which is exactly what I look for in bak kut teh.
The sliced pork soup is alright. The pork is super soft, though I personally do not enjoy it as much because it is a bit too soft for me. Again, just personal taste.
The other side dishes are pretty normal. The sesame chicken was slightly disappointing as the sauce was too watery. I think it would be better if the sauce were thicker, although flavour wise it is still okay.

Reviews:
Great place! It was darn bloody good that my family had to wait for 15 min to be seated. Can't be blamed since we went there during the peak hours. Lunch hour.

But I would like to take this opportunity to thank my wife for letting me choose lunch for the family.

The food was great! It was a shame that I didn't order more. Their kids meal was the right size for my 2 small kids. They loved their kids meal.

We we getting ourselves ready for the thinking that the seating area would be super warm since they were packed. But fortunatly the restaurant a/c held out well.

Their main dish, pork rib soup, oh~ the soup was flavourful, peppery taste, but yet, not that spicy. I was pleasantly surprised when we could ask for a refill for the soup with no additional charges. Thumbs up for that.

Usually, other restaurants/stall will reject your request and insist that you buy another serving just to taste the soup again.

The pig stomach soup is also a dish to die for! The tenderness of the meat, chewy, yet light on your jaw.

Paired with the steamy rice. O.M.G... I couldn't bear to leave the restaurant even after finishing my food. If not for my kids, I would have order another round just to stay and eat once more.

For the price we paid, it was a little expensive, but worth the taste.

Restaurant Name: Suki-Ya (All You Can Eat Shabu Shabu (Heartland Mall Kovan))
Reviews:
Suki-Ya at Heartland Mall Kovan is a Japanese all-you-can-eat shabu shabu restaurant that delivers generous portions, solid quality, and great value. Perfect for groups, families, or casual dinners, Suki-Ya lets you cook fresh ingredients at your table in simmering broth, choosing from two soup bases per pot to suit different tastes.

The buffet focuses on unlimited thinly sliced meats like pork and beef that cook quickly and stay tender. Orders are served fresh straight from the kitchen, keeping each serving hot and just right for tasting. Alongside the meats, there’s a self-service station with fresh vegetables, mushrooms, tofu, noodles, rice, and a variety of fish and meat balls — everything you need for a complete hotpot experience.

Sauces and condiments are easy to customise, letting you mix soy sauce, sesame, garlic, chilli, and more to match your preferred flavour profile. Most buffet packages also include unlimited soft drinks and simple desserts, offering a satisfying finish to a hearty meal.

Located inside Heartland Mall Kovan, the restaurant is easy to reach by public transport and fits well into a casual neighbourhood dining scene. The interior is straightforward and comfortable, designed to accommodate groups without fuss. Prices are affordable compared to premium hotpot spots, making this a go-to choice when you want a filling meal without overspending.

Overall, Suki-Ya at Heartland Mall Kovan is a reliable, well-priced shabu shabu buffet with fresh ingredients, friendly service, and a relaxed atmosphere.

The lack of variety of other basic sushi like kappa maki to clean the palate, endamame, yasai tempura, is dissapointing.

Another thing to note, the size of the sushi is almost half of the normal sushi I eat elsewhere. The price became not cheap plus the high ++.

Based on those reasons, I won’t be back anytime soon.

Booked for 3pm weekend hi-tea and when we arrived at 2.55pm, we were told that the lounge opens at 3pm. They could have let us take our seats first and come to get our drink orders at 3pm. The lounge was comfortable and they offer an interesting range of tea.

Tea Lounge at Conrad Singapore has long been one of my dependable weekend high tea spots, so when they introduced a special Chinese New Year themed edition, I was naturally curious to see how the experience would be reimagined.

The Spread: Comforting Familiarity with Festive Twists

The generous variety that regulars appreciate remains intact. The selection is extensive without feeling overwhelming, striking a nice balance between savoury classics and playful creations.

Highlights That Stood Out
•	Seafood Congee : Easily one of the stars of the afternoon. The broth was deeply flavourful, infused with the natural sweetness of seafood, and generously topped with prawns and fish. Comforting yet refined.
•	Kurobuta Pork Char Siew : Not part of the free-flow selection, but worth every bite. Exceptionally juicy and tender, with beautifully caramelised edges that delivered a delicate crispness and smoky sweetness.
•	Quiche : Above average, featuring an impressively thin, crisp crust that avoided the heaviness many hotel versions suffer from.
•	Chicken Satay : Juicy, tender, and paired with a rich homemade peanut sauce that tasted freshly ground rather than mass-produced.

Creative Touches That Keep It Interesting

Both the sandwiches and desserts continue to be where this high tea differentiates itself from others.
•	The sandwiches showcased unexpected ingredient pairings that somehow worked harmoniously, offering pleasant surprises rather than gimmicks.
•	Desserts were particularly strong, more imaginative than those at many other hotels. The combinations of flavours and textures felt thoughtfully composed, often unconventional but consistently enjoyable.

A Small Miss
•	Singapore Laksa : Slightly underwhelming compared to the rest of the spread. The coconut milk ratio leaned too heavy, resulting in a broth that felt diluted and lacked the punchy depth one would expect.

Value for Money

At $82++ per person, it sits on the pricier end of the high tea spectrum. However, considering the quality of ingredients, execution, and the creativity shown across the menu, it still offers solid value—especially for those who appreciate a high tea that goes beyond the predictable.

Final Thoughts

This festive edition proves why I keep returning. The experience stays true to its strengths—variety, quality, and creativity—while introducing seasonal elements that make it feel refreshed rather than repetitive. It’s a reliable indulgence that still knows how to surprise.

I stumbled upon this stall ("Teochew Fishball Minced Meat Noodle" at Food Hub) and ordered their dry Fishball Minced Meat Noodles with Mee Pok.

​The Verdict:
It is very good, but you need to know what you are eating. This is NOT Bak Chor Mee (BCM); it is a proper bowl of Teochew Fishball Noodles.

​The Difference: Don't come here expecting the vinegar-forward punch or the distinct savoury depth of tee poh (dried sole fish) that defines a classic BCM. The chilli is also different—it's not the typical BCM sambal style.

​Why it's still great: Despite not being BCM, it stands on its own merits. The Mee Pok was cooked perfectly al dente—springy with a great bite. The sauce mix was flavourful and savoury, coating the noodles well.

​The Ingredients: The toppings are generous—bouncy fishballs, sliced fish cake, minced meat, and fresh crispy lard croutons (you can add more on you own, there's a box of it next to the utensils) that add a wonderful texture.

​It was so satisfying that after finishing my bowl, I immediately ordered 4 more packets to take away for my family. If you appreciate a solid, traditional Teochew Fishball noodle, this gets my stamp of approval.
