Restaurant Name: The Embun Sg | Live Seafood • Ikan Bakar • Fresh Seafood (Halal)
Reviews:
I had dinner here with my family and spent almost $2,000. The food was good, but I honestly feel the price is a bit too expensive. At that price, I would expect the overall experience to better match the cost, including the service, amenities, and even the dining setup like the plates, forks, and spoons to feel more like hotel standard.

The food and drinks were okay, but to me, there was nothing very special compared to places like East Coast or other seafood restaurants. The main difference was the king crab, which stood out. Other than that, the rest felt quite normal.

I also felt that the prayer room was very small, wash basin not in working condition and not all areas were air-conditioned, which made the dining experience less comfortable.

For almost $2,000, I feel I could have gone for a buffet with a wider variety of food and desserts included. This is just my honest opinion based on the overall value and experience.

I would advise the shop to focus not only on profit, but also on making the dining experience feel worth it for families. Since many customers come with their family, it would be good to have more family set meals or value-for-money packages instead of charging separately for every single seafood item or by Kg. Of course, the business needs to make profit, but at the same time, customers should not leave feeling like they were being overcharged or ripped off. A better balance between pricing and value would make families more satisfied and more likely to return.

Seriously, I have been there once already, and I don’t think I will go back again. The price is just not worth the overall experience. I believe the shop should rethink its strategy, because customers may come once, but they may not return if they feel the value is not there.

Palm Restaurant Review

*Rating:* 2.5/5

I recently had the opportunity to dine at the Palm Restaurant, located within Singapore Swimming Club. While the setting is lovely, our experience was a bit of a mixed bag.

*Ambiance:* 4/5
The restaurant's ambiance is elegant and inviting, perfect for a special occasion or a night out with friends and family.

*Food:* 4/5
The menu is impressive, offering a wide variety of dishes from local cuisines to Western favorites like pasta. We were excited to try out different options, and the food was generally delicious.

*Service:* 2/5
Unfortunately, the service was a letdown. Because reservations are not allowed, we had to arrive early to secure a table for our large group. However, once seated, we had to wait quite a while for our orders to be taken and served. The waiters seemed overwhelmed and the service was not friendly.

*Value:* 3/5
Given the quality of food and service, the prices were reasonable. However, the lack of reservations and slow service might deter some diners.

*Overall:* 2.5/5
While the Palm Restaurant has potential, the service needs significant improvement. If you're planning to visit, arrive early to secure a table, and be patient with the staff.

For the oxtail soup however, the soup was not even hot…it was only mildly warm. I have to say that it was disappointing and it took quite long to be served i.e almost 20 minutes. Review for [Scrambled Egg Rice Stall] at Timbre+

I was really looking forward to trying this place, but the experience was disappointing from start to finish. Here’s why:

1. Ridiculous portion for add-ons
I paid an extra $0.90 for vegetables (cucumber) , but the portion was laughably small. It felt more like a garnish than an actual side. Definitely not worth the top-up.

2. Auntie actually scooped away the cucumber.
The server initially gave what seemed like a reasonable amount of cucumber, but the auntie (presumably the owner or supervisor) told him it was “too much” and proceeded to scoop some out right in front of me. If $0.90 can’t even get me a fair portion, that’s just stingy.

3. Served after people who ordered later.
I ordered first, yet multiple people who ordered after me received their food way earlier. The queue system felt completely disorganised, and there was no acknowledgment of the delay.

4. Odd and unprofessional interaction with another customer
I also witnessed the auntie being told off by another customer to stick her sticky note inside his takeaway container instead of outside. The whole interaction was awkward and showed a lack of basic service sense.

---

Verdict:
Overpriced, inconsistent service, and poor portion control. There are plenty of other stalls at Timbre+ that actually value their customers. I won’t be returning.

We used to patronise this Chinese restaurant frequently in the past as we stayed nearby, so we were quite disappointed with this recent visit. For a moment, I even thought the chef had changed, as the dishes tasted noticeably different. Unfortunately, not for the better. The standard seems to have dropped compared to what we remembered.

Some of the signature touches we used to enjoy were missing. For instance, the steamed prawns previously came with mung bean vermicelli, which added great texture and flavour, but this was no longer included. The crispy chicken used to be served with crackers on the side, but those were also absent this time. Likewise, the pork dish we had in the past came with fragrant fried ginger, which was missing from the version served to us.

We ordered the crispy spring chicken, stir-fried pork with spring onion, garlic steamed prawns, and beans with minced meat. During payment, I asked if there had been a change in chef, only to realise that the staff member who took our order had actually given us incorrect information, the fried ginger pork we expected was not what we were served.

Additionally, the service left much to be desired. The lady who took our order was very loud and came across as impatient, to the point that it was uncomfortable communicating with her.

Overall, the experience was not as enjoyable as before. It’s disappointing to see such a noticeable decline in both food quality and service standards.

The noodles were absolutely phenomenal, best bowl of beef noodles I've ever had. I got the sauerkraut beef noodles while my brother had the dry beef noodles(干捞牛肉面）
The soup of the sauerkraut beef noodles were so delicious and appetizing.
The chilli oil was absolutely fragrant, a must have when you're taking a bite of the beef slices. In my opinion the chili oil/crisp (found at each table in a small ceramic pot) is so good, it's better than lao gan ma. It's a must try!! It's not too spicy either, you can taste the flavour and fragrance rather than just numbing spicy chilli. Other than the noise of the dough sheeter machine and the sound of noodles slapping against the board while the chef is pulling the noodles (very cool by the way), it's still quite quiet. Please hire more chefs or decline orders if you’re overloaded. My baby ended up fussy due to the long wait time.

Restaurant Name: Tongue Tip Lanzhou Beef Noodles (The Woodgrove)
Reviews:
I went with the Signature Beef Noodles and was a bit stuck on which noodle type to pick, but the staff recommended the Erxi (thicker round noodles) as their most popular choice, so I went with that.

The soup was very clean-tasting and not gamey at all, which was great. I asked for less chili, which really let the natural beefy sweetness shine through. They are also quite generous when topping off the noodles with green onions, leeks, and coriander, which made the broth even more aromatic and refreshing. The daikon was also crunchy and had soaked up all that beefy goodness.

Since the Hui people are famous for their skewers, I had to try some on the side. The mutton skewers were juicy with a nice kick of cumin and chilli, while the beef tendon had good flavour and a melt-in-your-mouth texture.

Prices here are a bit on the steep side (about $3 for a single skewer), but the quality is definitely there.

Reviews:
I’ve been a loyal patron of this humble stall for over a decade. Back in the day, it was helmed by Uncle and his wife, whose Mee Hoon Kueh was nothing short of legendary in the neighbourhood — the kind of bowl that warms both the stomach and the soul. Even when their competitor, Fong Hup, opened right next door, they held their ground, retaining loyal customer and serving the superior Mee Hoon Kueh.

Today, the ownership has been passed to a spirited team of young men. While their enthusiasm is admirable and their marketing efforts earnest, the Mee Hoon Kueh I once adored has taken on a very different character — and not for the better. Sadly, the queues have thinned, and more of the regulars I used to see are now heading to Fong Hub next door for their cravings.

Restaurant Name: Trattoria Da Mimmo Restaurant And Pizzeria
Reviews:
Stepping into Trattoria Da Mimmo, one expects the warm, flour-dusted embrace of a traditional Italian kitchen. The atmosphere promises a rustic escape, yet the culinary journey that followed was a complex tapestry of artisanal brilliance marred by technical inconsistencies.

Burrata Pugliese - While the portion was undeniably generous—a gleaming orb of cheese that dominated the board—it was, alas, a masterclass in missed potential. The cheese lacked that essential, soul-warming milky sweetness, arriving somewhat muted and flavourless. It functioned more as a textural element than the star of the show.

Similarly, the Insalata Di Rucola offered an abundant mountain of greenery. However, the balance was skewed; the peppery arugula possessed an aggressive bitterness that overwhelmed the palate, lacking the necessary acidity or sweetness in the dressing to tame its wilder notes.

The Spaghetti Al Nero Di Seppia was a triumph. The jet-black strands were perfectly al dente, coated in a sauce that sang with the briny, umami-rich depths of the ocean. It was a dark, delicious embrace of coastal Italian tradition.

In stark contrast, the Fettuccine Al Salmone felt uninspired. The salmon lacked the vibrant, buttery flaking of a fresh catch, leaning towards a duller, "average" profile that failed to elevate the dish beyond standard trattoria fare.

However, the Strozapreti special (notably presented as beautifully cupped orecchiette in form) was an intriguing highlight. The texture was delightful, providing a nuanced chew that caught the sauce effectively—a truly enjoyable and creative diversion from the core menu.

Where Da Mimmo truly finds its rhythm is at the pizza station. Both the Pizza Hawaiian and the Pizza Prosciutto E Funghi were exceptionally well-crafted. The crusts bore the hallmark leopard-spotting of a well-stoked oven, providing a crisp foundation for the harmonious toppings. The Prosciutto E Funghi, in particular, displayed a wonderful earthiness, while the Hawaiian—often a point of contention—was handled with a refined balance of sweet and savoury.

The Cote De Boeuf was a heartbreaking encounter. Visually, the kitchen’s technique was evident; the doneness was a flawless, edge-to-edge ruby pink. Yet, the execution stumbled at the pass. The meat arrived at the table far too cold, which caused the fats to congeal and rendered the otherwise premium cut tough and laborious to chew. A dish that should have been a celebration of the Maillard reaction and succulent tenderness was instead dampened by poor temperature management.

Restaurant Name: Tsukada Nojo || Japanese Premium Hotpot || Collagen-Rich Chicken Stock || Thomson Plaza
Reviews:
Came here for their signature Bijin Nabe, and overall it was a satisfying and comforting hotpot experience.

The chicken collagen broth is the highlight — rich, silky and clean-tasting without being overly greasy. You can really tell it’s been simmered properly, and it becomes more flavourful as the ingredients cook. The white fish and prawns were fresh, sweet and cooked beautifully in the broth. The mushroom platter was generous and well-selected, adding natural umami depth to the soup.

I also liked the option to add beauty noodles at the end — light, springy, and a good way to soak up the remaining broth without feeling too heavy. Portions were adequate for sharing, and the meal felt balanced rather than indulgent.

The restaurant itself is bright and comfortable, though it can get quite busy during peak hours, which makes the space a bit noisy. Service was generally attentive, but timing between items could be smoother when the restaurant is full. Pricing is on the higher side for hotpot, but understandable given the quality of ingredients and concept.

Overall, a solid choice for Japanese-style collagen hotpot — comforting, well-executed, and ideal for a relaxed meal with friends or family. Would return, especially when craving a nourishing broth.

Very friendly security Indian lady, professional and courteous! Tricky entrance to the building for first-timers.  Should turn in on the first entrance you see near the security hut and not the one after if you're driving from the main road.
Very good service and provide wide variety of vegetarian food supplies. Highly recommend. 👍👍👍👍👍
Good services and responsive, fast delivery too
Helpful, food r nice they teach you how to cook

Food Taste was good, nice location inside Sentosa, this is an Indian Restaurant, but the food tase was good as everyone can enjoy, you can go as group of Friends enjoy food and drinks, good place to have Company get together more options to choose, the service was good a bit expensive as the location is within Sentosa you can walk from Imbiah Station to reach here.
Va ser el lloc on millor vem menjar de Sentosa. Restaurant indi boníssim, amb molta varietat, simpàtics, i realment bo. Vem anar a dinar i a sopar
Every thing I like ,Anup serves our so satisfied,I high recommend 👍

Delicious black pepper chicken chop. Chicken tastes good, nicely caramelised and crispy skin, sauce is nicer than most coffeeshop chicken chop and portion bigger too. Fries done very well, crispy outside and fluffy on the inside. Coleslaw flavour is a bit too sweet for me but tastes tangy cold and fresh and complements the chicken well. I have ordered this quite a few times, quality is consistent. Friendly service.
Bad attitude from middle age auntie. Very bad attitude, sound like I owe her a living.
Food is good portion

The medium Ribeye was nicely done and pretty value for money for it's thick cut. However, the soup was mediocre and was serve lukewarm, instead of consuming I mainly used it as dipping sauce for the garlic bread.
Middle aged cashier aunty was rude and condescending. Black pepper chicken chop was cold, dry and very little gravy. Standard dropped. Food and service were good in the past.

Thank you Alex for making our wedding a rousing success. My now husband and I really felt soooo at ease knowing you were at the helm. I really just sit there and chill the whole night knowing you're there jaga-ing. So impressed by the Chinese menu selection, didn't need to make any modifications and the venue size was perfect for our 120 guests. Still got space for march in, games and yamseng. Really covered everything needed for an unforgettable Chinese wedding.
Amazing food, great service from the staff. Even though we stayed till quite late on a weekday night, they did not rush us to leave and still asked if we wanted more drinks/dessert.
Been here a couple of times. Love the food, the ambience and the service here!
We celebrated a birthday dinner here and everything was perfect! Thank you Mr Clarence, Kabi, Chef Hansan, Chef Gumsan and the rest of the team for a great night out. ❤️
Food is excellent at very reasonable price. Service is good & nice conducive ambience both for family outing &/or business meetings

Had been ordering from them these years (though not regularly). Two weeks ago, due to schedule I had to cancel my order (only one dish) as it was taking too long and the food was not prepared yet.

The cashier was upset which I understand as she had to do a refund. I apologised to her a few times for the inconveniences.

Today I went back and before I told them my order, they immediately informed me if I cannot wait, this time they would not refund me. I asked about the waiting time and was told it was about 25mins. As I am not in a rush this time, I proceeded with the order. Eventually the wait was only less than 15mins.

I am not sure if the 25mins was to manage my expectations (due to what happened two weeks ago) or to discourage me from ordering. However, the front staff attitude was rather rude and hostile. Out of the many times over the years, that was the only time I had to cancel my order, and they "remember"!!

Definitely an unpleasant experience.
The zi char is very nice. Mee goreng is yummy

Food is awesome
Feels like home cook food
Great taste for all items she prepares 10/10
Highly recommend
Food options are good, especially Indian vegetarian. The preparation & taste is excellent. Nice ambience except that the food court is non-aircon.
Great experience , the steak are well cook and the beer are affordable .
Excellent service and fast response
Food is delicious and service is good. Nice atmosphere will be back again soon
Highly recommended!

Celebrated my birthday here with my family, food was awesome (even my picky eater son ate quite a fair bit!) and all the staff were very friendly! Husband requested for the staff to serve the cake with a candle and the staff went out of their way to sing me a birthday song, which really came as a surprise :) the lavender yuzu cake was really good, flavour was just nice and not overly sweet. Thumbs up for the wonderful service and keep up the good vibes!

As a dog owner who lives nearby, i'm a regular here and always looking to try their seasonal specials. Food is great and prices are reasonable. Their mee siam is v popular, and I also like their tomato soup, clams, aglio, chicken bowl, cakes and cinnamon bread. Their fizzy drinks are perfect for a lazy afternoon too.
Their staff are very sweet and attentive to dog owners. I rmb vividly that I was there alone with my dog on a public holiday, and not only were the staff (yes all of them) in good spirits, one of them took it upon himself to stand at my table and keep an eye on my dog while i went inside to settle the bill. (They can take the card reader to the table too, but I was in a hurry that day and thought to do a quick run to the till).
W39 has been around for years and I truly hope that there will be more to come. The food and the people here are deserving of our support.

Very nice people and if you have pets the sitting area is outside, with ceiling fans and despite us going at the  hot midday timing, it was nice with the fans,  and the awning definitely shields so  we could  enjoy the delicious food comfortably. There are water bowls and tap conveniently located and there’s a small but nice park just to the right of this place. The doggy received a free treat too.

The waiter bothered to swop a chair with a backing when he noticed my 90 year old mom.

I saw cars stopping by to do takeaways and people popping in to  buy bread too.
Regular haunt. Food is good but most of all staff are amazing.
Great vibes in a neighborhood that is thinning out in terms of crowd and consumption

I had a disappointing experience here due to the poor service and lack of transparency.

Despite ordering 1 mains, 1 side and drinks for 2, our server repeatedly pressured us to order more drinks, making us feel like we were not "justifying" our table. To top it off, she dropped the bill at our table without us asking and basically told us to leave because others were waiting. Incredibly rude and unprofessional.

Being hovered over and then pushed out the door is not hospitality. If there are house policies regarding spending or time, they should be clearly communicated upfront, not used to harass guests.

I recommend that you save your money and go somewhere that actually wants your business.

Came here one night with a friend, we wanted to come here as the place looked very lively. We wanted to sit inside as that’s where the live band is but sadly indoors were full :( , the staff told us if there’s a available table he’ll shift us so we were ok, moved inside probably after a pint and some starters, and I have the say the band was really great, it’s nice to have live music here in the neighbourhood, really beautiful and thank you in bringing something I didn’t know I would come to enjoy
The vibe is back in Holland V! Nice new fresh look! The live band adds so much to this institution! Congratulations to Team Wala Wala on such a wonderful revamp! Kudos.

This has been my fav place. Just when they announced they are closing, we went twice in very big group to support. Today we arrived at 630pm. Indoor is almost empty but all under reservation as claimed. I spoke to an Indian staff. He did not give us a table even after I asked 3 times. One of the table has 3 ladies on it but its joint by 3 tables. He told me that they reserved for 14 pax. However from 7 to 9, only the 3 were there. How can wala allow 3 pax to sit 14 pax long table for 2h and rejecting many customers who wanted to sit there? Ended up after 2h, they released the table to others but not to us. That particular staff is rude and did not keep his promise to release the table to us. It is very disappointing.

PLEASE close your shop and let other business come. What a stupid menu, we MUST buy cold drinks with ice cream and price difference almost $2 by itself. So lame and so dumb, no card payments. All payments must use cash or paywave only. Close your shop and let other kopitiam open in this location instead.

It was my first time visiting. There were seats available around 3 - 4 PM. I ordered milk tea, condensed milk Bun and crispy noodles with sliced beef and eggs. Out of these three items, I would say the noodles were worth the try. Maybe switching out with other noodles would taste better. For ordering and payment, you will have to mark it on the menu and head to the cashier to pay. There is no complimentary water and tissue provided.

2nd Visit - Beef Brisket Noodle, Polo Bun and Ice Lemon Tea. I liked the Ice Lemon Tea the most. As I was dining alone, midway into my noodles, the staff asked if I wanted chilli. I was surprised and appreciative of the gesture.

After the Covid19 hiatus, finally got the chance to dine here. The fried rice is really wonderful wif much wok hei....and so is the fried hor fun! (The bright yellowish egg yolk was so presentable!)
Worth reporting here wif no regrets after spending $49.80!

Enjoyed my experience here. Food has no gst, service charge. Everything is net. Do note they dont take credit card payment. Generous portions, decent taste, not too overly salty nor bland. Price reasonable for location. Been here for a long time and been through many rounds of renovations. Think even before daiso came around

Red bean dessert, fried carrot cake, prawn paste chicken wings and cheese baked rice are some of our favorite dishes at this cafe. Can be crowded during meal hours and they only accept cash and paynow.

Decent zichar food. Affordable in today's market. But the pork chop is quite dry, not the best.
Salted egg rice was decent too. But lesser sauce than I thought.

Nice simple tze char stall with friendly staff. Tried both the salted egg yolk chicken & fish on 2 separate occasions - both were good & very fragrant. Also can order ala carte veg / meat dishes ($6-8). Recently start serving spinach soup. Recommended.

Restaurant Name: Wan Yuan Vegetarian Stall Woodlands Spectrum 1
Reviews: Brown rice is not of good quality as looks dry and separated: no plump grains seen. Taukwa looks really processed and fried until have they hard edges. Happy that the peanuts are not burnt :) Chaipoh is oily and has a strong smell. Would skip it, if I would buy Leicha rice from this stall once more. Mani leaves are missing, substituted by Chye sim which brings a watery, bitter taste element into the dish. Shredded cabbage and finely cut longbeans are sweet.

Restaurant Name: Wan Yuan Vegetarian Stall Woodlands Spectrum 1
Reviews: Bad service from the aunty with short hair at this stall, bought thunder tea rice and is super oily. Bad service with bad food...

Reviews:
Vegetarian stall with vegan options, food contains no alliums. Good food at a reasonable price. The healthy vegan Lei Cha is good, highly recommended.

**Vegan Lei Cha ( not available on lunar New Moon Day and Full Moon Day )

** do help yourself with a nice bowl of free vegetables soup.

Restaurant Name: Wan Yuan Vegetarian Stall Woodlands Spectrum 1
Reviews: nothing to say.....almost finish...what can i say...

Restaurant Name: Wan Yuan Vegetarian Stall Woodlands Spectrum 1
Reviews: Very nice lei cha.. Big portion nad yummy.. Place is very spacious and windy.
There are 2x standard food selections. (Pork or Chicken) - Need to change the menu frequently

My go to Korean restaurant in SG to satisfy my Korean cuisine cravings, something that is hearty and value for money to me.

Have been coming back here many times and it never disappoints as the consistency is always there. I like that they have a fixed menu everyday and you just have to show up and have it served to you, without thinking much about what to eat.

My favourite dishes would be the Bulgogi (generous amount of meat) & seasoned fried chicken! Honourable mention goes to the homemade waffle for dessert 😋  Although it’s a very small piece, i really like the texture of it because it is the chewy kind, similar to mochi, served warm.

The friendly male boss is also very dedicated to his job & can give this place a try if you’re around the area! Can use CDC vouchers too ~

Wang Family Kitchen - this Korean family-run restaurant has been in operation for quite a number of years at Hillview Community Club, and its enduring presence thereat is testament to its no-fuss, no-nonsense, comfortingly delicious Korean meal sets served daily as a "Day Plate" and at a reasonable price. My wife and I have dined here on a number of occasions and we have always been satisfied with the place. As we sort of live "just across the road" in the Dairy Farm area, choosing this place for a Korean meal is a no-brainer. Service here is nice enough, and the dining ambience is comfortable. I recommend that you try this place for its home-cooked style Korean food, if you are in the Hillview area.

Home cooked taste and mostly only 1 set meal choice. Variety is limited and almost daily same dishes are served. Wish they would have 2 set choices with fish /seafood variety too. This store tends to serve chicken & pork as mains in 1 set meal. I rather have 1 main meat choice & more side dish varieties. Their samygetang [ginseng chicken] is popular too. Price is reasonable.

Highly recommend Uncle’s chicken feet noodles — a must order!
The chicken feet are braised until soft and full of collagen, rich and flavorful, and they go perfectly with the noodles. Definitely something you shouldn’t miss if it’s your first time here.

I give credit where credit is due. Honestly, this is one coffeeshop where mostly residents staying around here will visit and eat as the ever popular 505 Jurong west market & food centre is just a walking distance. I love this Bak Chor Mee and potion is good too. Keeps me full and satisfied with a happy smile. Do order the number 2. Uncle may look fierce or arrogant but he is not. He says thank you too. If you are around here, give this a try. If you look at the operating timing, sells till afternoon so it will be a disappointment if you are expecting to open late evening or night. If i come here. It will usually be in the morning so it’s alright.
The uncle owner attitude is worse act like he don't worry no customers come.after I buy from this stall one time I don't feel go eat again

Chanced upon this cosy eatery that serves scrumptious dim sim and other HK zichar dishes. Their century egg porridge is smooth and savoury; their braised pig ears are tasty and crunchy. Will definitely be back to try other dishes! What a precious find!

Confused staff poor management. Was told can use CDC voucher prior to ordering but was rejected when making payment. Was informed not allowed after 10pm cos collection of money by different boss.  Food first round was acceptable. When 2nd round of order, fish cake fried twice, dumpling very steamed till skin came off and char siew noodle was super sweet.  Not able to maintain food standard. Unpleasant experience.

chanced upon this place after taking a random bus from mandai bird paradise because no taxi wanted to pick us up - dropped down at this springleaf MRT area and walked past an entire street with empty stores, but this place was PACKED! curiosity got the better of us so we popped in and wah. no regrets. the fried rice there is bombastic, like primo wokhei, very fresh prawns used in the yang zhou fried rice, and my partner loved the beef fried rice!!! i would have ordered the dimsum if it wasnt so busy. highly recommended if you are in the area! Cash only or nets or paylah - no credit card, so be prepared!

Fantastic zhi char with wok hei
Dim sum is excellent. Char siew is KL style. Fish maw soup full of maw

First thought after dining at this place, "I NEED TO BRING MY MOM HERE COS SHE'S GONNA LOVE THIS"

Must try: pan fried dumpling, har kao.

The portions were generous, the seafood was fresh, and the pan fried dumplings were well fried, not oily! The steam pork ribs and San Lou Hor Fan were full of flavor. Pity it's a small place so it gets packed quite easily, but it's worth coming down to have a meal with your family if you're up for a good dim sum, Hong Kong food!!
The most horrible chicken and rice I have ever eaten.  As well got charged 8$ for this! Would never eat here again
Some of the best chicken rice and broth I have ever had. Rivals that of Beach Road in my opinion.

got food poisoning from the chicken rice and the uncle said it was my own problem but other review also mentioned getting food poisoning multiple times. attitude was bad and refused to let me speak to the owner
Very friendly and quick service. The chicken was soft and tender and the rice was the stand out, full of chicken flavour in the rice. The only complaint is the amount of meat is too little.

Charsiew Wonton Mee ($4) Charsiew was on the meaty side but still tender and delicious. Wonton was okay. Generous portion of noodles and the sauce they were tossed in (say yes to the chilli!) was quite delicious. Overall, for this price, wouldn't mind coming back regularly for a good and affordable meal. Minus points for atmosphere as there were a steady stream of birds terrorising the area.

Restaurant Name: Wang Xing Mixed Veg Rice • Porridge
Reviews:
Can't say for environment as I packed food for take away.
They anyhow charged for economic rice. One male staff told me $6 and wrote a "6" on the packet as usual. Then another staff took over. She open the packet open and took a look and said it's $6.60.  Not sure if she didn't see the number written on the packet or what. Even so, such anyhow charging is a bad experience for me as first time customer. I will not go back to the stall again.

My 2nd visit.  Order nasi brayani  with ayam merah as this is the only dish left as i came in late. Lady boss give me some curry vege to go with the rice. Over all the food is delicious. Worth my time to travel from east of sg to have this.
Wei Shan is a very helpful. Shes very patience in helping me in signing up membership.i like her services she is very cheerful always have a smile on her face.

I walked in around 1 o'clock and received my food after just 10 minutes. I would also like to praise Zong Huang for his thoughtfulness; he was very attentive and reminded us about the hot plate when it was served.
Zong Huang and Michael are very polite and courteous. They are so helpful with my order and request.
Zong Huang was very helpful in telling us which food was which, and he did so in a kind tone.
Michael and Zong Huang were very attentive throughout our visit. They were caring and kind, offering us menu recommendations when we weren't sure what to order.

Restaurant Name: Watami Japanese Dining (Mandai Wildlife East) (Free To Visit)
Reviews: Very bad dining experience. The staff were completely unbothered by children running around, making noise, and creating a mess in the restaurant while other diners were present. It was disruptive and uncomfortable, and the staff showed no responsibility in managing the situation. Proper control would have helped maintain a pleasant dining environment, ensure the safety of both the children and other guests, and show basic respect for customers who came to enjoy their meal peacefully.

Restaurant Name: Watami Japanese Dining (Mandai Wildlife East) (Free To Visit)
Reviews: Food is okay, 4 stars, but noise from children is  too excessive

Restaurant Name: Watami Japanese Dining (Mandai Wildlife East) (Free To Visit)
Reviews:
I would like to commend Guo Huang from Watami at Mandai for his excellent service. He was very friendly, attentive, and maintained a positive attitude throughout our visit.

Despite the restaurant being very busy over the weekend and many places around being full, the Watami team managed the situation very well and did their best to ensure that customers did not have to wait too long for their food.

It was truly appreciated to see such dedication and teamwork during a peak period. Thank you to Guo Huang and the team for providing a pleasant dining experience. 👍

Restaurant Name: Watami Japanese Dining (Mandai Wildlife East) (Free To Visit)
Reviews: Not bad. Considered fast service. Food was ok. Teristki chocen curry portion is big. Udon is tad salty but the ikan broth was tasty. My red spicy ramen was spicy. But i like the al dente noodles. I like it hard. Not a bad choice if the Sushiro beside it gets packed.

Restaurant Name: Watami Japanese Dining (Mandai Wildlife East) (Free To Visit)
Reviews: Beautiful meal and fabulous service.

Wanted a quick bite for lunch as was super hungry.Waitress Kathleen Simpson is patient to serve and recommend.
Good job , keep it up.

I recently dined at Watami Japanese Dining at Star Vista and unfortunately the experience was quite disappointing. The staff were not very attentive, and it was difficult to get their attention throughout the meal. Service overall felt lacking and unengaged.

As for the food, it was just average and didn’t stand out, especially considering the price point. There wasn’t anything particularly memorable about the dishes.

Overall, the combination of poor service and mediocre food made the visit underwhelming. I hope the restaurant can improve on both fronts.

I would like to applaud this young female staff (should be a student) whom I was seated at the upper level. As it was dinner time it was full house and she is the only server. She was really patient, courteous & very hardworking despite restaurant being very busy. I hope management sees this msg and kindly reward her or compliment her. Food wise my family loved it as we dine at least twice a month hope as a regular member can provide more discount or voucher!
Fantastic food n thank you En Kee for exceptional service

stood at entrance waiting for 20mins

Restaurant Name: Wee Nam Kee Hainanese Chicken Rice Restaurant
Reviews: 曜日の関係か7時ぐらいでも空いていました。Steamed Chicken Set 水餃子と野菜付きで14ドル。Hokkien Noodles Sで6.5ドル。ビールは缶ビールですがジョッキも出してくれて6.5ドル。
A hidden Gem selling bestest braised duck, pork belly and big intestine head with yam rice or noodle. It's very much better than those top brand claimed. Come and try it and you wouldn't regret.

We rushed down here and manage to be the last customer today before they closed. We were not able to try the braised duck as it was already sold out. However, we managed to get the braised duck wings which was excellent. The braised pig intestines were very tender and flavourful. My favorite was the duck gizzard. It was so tender and full of flavours. The mui chai was also very good.
Service is friendly and the lady is very patient with all our questions.

The hor fun, preserved vegetables, braised pork, and intestines are all very tender and flavorful 👍
The duck meat is above average, though there are many Teochew braised duck stalls that do it better. That said, the overall experience is still worth queueing for — and the stall usually has a long queue and sells out early.
This is e legend duck rice from senoko loop, e duck meat is tender, braise pork literally melts in ur mouth and most best part is e portion is damn value for money !

This braised duck rice is pure shiok! The duck is super tender and soaked through with that rich, savoury dark sauce — every bite just melts and bursts with flavour. The gravy is thick and slightly sweet, coating everything from the egg to the intestines perfectly.

Simply said — solid comfort food, confirm worth the calories.

If you’re not a rice person, they do serve braised duck noodles as well!

West Co'z Cafe @ West Coast Plaza
👍😋

Staffs were friendly n efficient. Ambient were good. Only food i felt so so. Some prawn i felt were not fresh. As the prawn come out green paste. Pandan chicken not really nice. But curry fish was good.

A Halal restaurant which is always full during meal times and is famous for their curry fish head.

Their signature curry fish head is really reasonable for the price and great to the taste buds and has sufficient meat. Proportion  is also just nice so that you won't overeat.

Service is fast and for an air-conditioned place, definitely a
thumbs up!

A regular customer at the shop. Food is nice but the level of service has declined. Only friendly staff is the Chinese lady who never fails to remember what I like. The serving staff is OK but the staff managing the cashier, Krystal, has serious attitude. Not only she gave wrong bill and charged me (ended asking the Chinese lady to chase after me when I left and not informing her why need me to come back), she presented an attitude that customer owing her.  While I informed her I needed to check fave app, she simply not patience with attitude like asking me to quickly pay and move on. Not a single smile. Suggest not to put her at a front line position.  Rethinking whether I should continue to patronise.
Though food is nice, I don't think diners deserve such service.
Post review
I realised I was charged twice as Krystal voided the other table customer's payment instead of the wrong charge to my card. Only I reviewed the credit card statement, I realised I am being charged twice. While the manager swiftly refunded me when I called, I would thought that the counter closing would realise Krystal done the wrong thing, instead of me calling to inform.
食物很好,鱼头新鲜,服务员态度很好..会再来试别的菜肴..

The new Ubin seafood restaurant used to be here and it was packed. We visited WLSR on a Sunday night and it was almost empty. The food is good/decent zichar but generally the vibe is really, really off, decor wise. It's strange and hollow. Not a nice place to dine in. Dabao better. But kudos to the staff working here for having to tank the strange env and weirded out customers and serving up decent fare. Pls change the chairs!! The carpet is a little funky smelling too
The worst crab I ever had. No meat.

Food was serve hot and the flavour just nice. They were short handed due to 15th day of Chinese New Year. Room has very nice porcelain paintings and ancient feel. Would come back again. They have CRAB PROMO 2 FOR $68. Air-conditioned Restaurant you will never find such price.

Apart from the really bling decor, f is surprisingly good. There’s yummy wok hey taste. Dishes were also quite affordable. Normal Zhi char pricing but got aircon. Though there’s a slightly musty smell but you forget about it when the food comes. Would recommend this place for a weekend family dinner. When we were there on a Sunday dinner, we were the only customers so we had our doubts at first. But I’m really surprised this place hasn’t gotten much publicity cos the food was good. I’d rather eat here than the nearby Ga Hock or Jiak.

Chinese new year food too cold , 1 yu sheng no style,2 shark fin like water 3 chicken very cold 4 猪脚 cold 5 lotus with Holland bean , no style and colour 6 Hong Kong Steam fish cold ,7 lotus rice still ok , 8 steam prawn not fresh silk and leg black, 9 yam paste no oil give a bit coconut to put.
They used to operate at NTU Hall Two Canteen at some point before moving here to Old Airport Road. The food is on the oilier side but definitely give the garlic sauce a try if you are here!

My visit to Whampoa Keng Fish Head Steamboat was a standout dining experience that truly showcased the depth and comfort of traditional Singaporean cuisine. Known for its signature charcoal-cooked steamboat, the restaurant delivered both flavour and authenticity from the moment the dish arrived.

The highlight was, without a doubt, the fish head steamboat. Served bubbling in a claypot over charcoal, the broth was rich, slightly milky, and deeply infused with the sweetness of fresh seafood. The fish head itself was tender and flaky, absorbing the soup beautifully. Accompanied by napa cabbage, tofu, yam, and other ingredients, the dish felt hearty and well-balanced.

What made the experience even more enjoyable was the nostalgic cooking method. The use of charcoal added a subtle smokiness that elevated the overall flavour, setting it apart from more modern steamboat styles. It also created a warm, communal dining atmosphere.

Service was efficient and no-nonsense, typical of many well-loved local establishments. Despite the busy environment, dishes arrived promptly and staff were attentive when needed.

Overall, Whampoa Keng Fish Head Steamboat offered an authentic and satisfying meal. It’s a must-visit for anyone seeking a traditional, flavour-rich dining experience in Singapore. Highly recommended!!!

I’m extremely disappointed with my repeated experiences at Xin Yuan Ji at Lentor Modern. This is not a one-time issue, it has happened three times, and enough is enough.
Residents at Lentor Modern are supposed to receive a 10% discount. We even confirmed this with the staff beforehand, and she acknowledged that the discount applies. However, when it came to payment, she keyed in the full amount and asked us to pay immediately. It is our negligence that we didn’t double-check on the spot as it felt stressful to hold up the person and trusted that the discount had already been applied.
A major red flag was that she didn’t even offer a receipt. It was only after I confronted her that she printed it, which then revealed that the discount had not been applied at all. Her explanation? She “forgot” to key it in. But this exact same situation has happened three separate times, which makes it very hard to believe it’s accidental.
When we requested a refund for the missed discount, we were told it couldn’t be done because it was already keyed into the system. Instead, the staff tried to compensate by offering to “add more ingredients.” This is not an acceptable solution. The added items were either not what we wanted (e.g., tofu), or in previous cases, there was no noticeable difference at all especially for takeaway orders where they claimed to add more vegetables.
This pattern of behaviour feels dishonest and misleading. Customers should not have to repeatedly check whether they are being charged correctly, especially after confirming a promotion with staff.
Overall, this experience has been extremely frustrating. I hope the management takes this seriously, as it reflects poorly on the integrity of the business.

This stall is run by a very friendly middle-age couple previously from China.
Their ban mian/u mian noodle which the husband painstakingly kneads by hand every morning (no machine is used) is consistently very good.
What sets this stall apart from other ban mian stalls is that they have fried u mian and fried bee hoon which is very Heng Hwa style on their menu.
What’s more, they are flexible to tweet the ingredients depending on customer’s dietary restrictions.
For instance, as I am a pescatarian, the ingredients for my order of fried u mian or fried bee hoon can be changed to fish slices instead of the usual la la, etc  .
The owner is even very readily willing to fry ban mian when requested…
It is something customers never get to taste anywhere else in Singapore.
The stall’s dumplings are big and delicious too - value for money.
Plus, they give fresh green vegetables instead of the usual cabbage and the fish they use is fresh batang instead of the cheap tilapia…
Highly recommended…

Reviews:
Went to YAYOI @ 100AM for a weekday lunch during the CNY period. The restaurant was relatively quiet around noon, which made it a comfortable spot for a group lunch (we had 6 pax).

We ordered several teishoku sets - Amazu Chicken Steak, Hakata Mizutaki, Namban & Ebi Fry, Tori Katsu Toji, and Sukiyaki, along with their Salmon Yu Sheng for the festive season (it was repeatedly recommended by their staff).

The portions of their mains were generous, but my Amazu Chicken Steak had too much sauce, which overpowered the entire dish. A few of my colleagues felt the same about their dishes - meat was nicely cooked, but way too saucy overall.

That said, the value of their lunch meals is pretty good. Each teishoku set comes with rice, miso soup, and access to the free refill counter. The salad bar was a nice touch as it had cherry tomatoes, corn, pickled ginger and other small sides that you can help yourself to. The unlimited rice and miso soup definitely made it more satisfying, especially for bigger eaters. The hojicha (both hot and iced) was also included in the lunch set :)

The highlight for us was actually the Salmon Yu Sheng. The ingredients were fresh, the salmon sashimi slices were thick, and the overall mix was well-balanced. Really yummy!

Overall, mains were slightly underwhelming due to the saltiness, but the free refills and seasonal offerings helped balance out the experience. A decent option for a casual weekday lunch, especially if you value set meals with unlimited sides :)

这次来悦私宴用餐整体体验很好，很适合家庭聚会或者公司晚宴。

餐厅走的是比较高端的粤菜私宴路线，环境安静私密，大多是包间设计，装修也很精致典雅，很适合正式一点的宴请场合。包间空间宽敞、氛围很好，坐下来吃饭会感觉很舒服，不会嘈杂。

菜品方面主打经典粤菜和海鲜，食材非常新鲜，做法也比较讲究，基本都是突出食材本身的味道，没有过多复杂的调味，吃起来很清爽。作为广东人来说，这种原汁原味的做法会觉得特别亲切，也更能吃出海鲜本身的鲜甜。

整体来说，无论是环境、私密性还是菜品品质都很在线，如果是想找一个 比较体面、高端一点的粤菜宴请餐厅，悦私宴确实是一个很不错的选择。

PREVIOUS REVIEW (4 Stars):
I decided to try Zi Jia Yong Tau Foo at Timbre+ Hillview, and my experience was a mix of highs and lows. The quality of the yong tau foo itself is fantastic and definitely a highlight.

Let's start with the best part: the ingredients. Each piece of yong tau foo I selected was fresh, flavourful, and expertly cooked. The fried items had a wonderful savoury taste, and the stuffed pieces were delicious. In terms of the core product, the quality is easily comparable to other top-tier YTF stalls I've enjoyed.

Unfortunately, there was a mix-up with my order which affected the final dish. I had ordered the dry version with kway teow, but I was initially served the soup version with the YTF pieces on the side. To their credit, they were quick to rectify it. However, the method of correction—simply pouring the soup away from the noodles and then combining everything into a dry bowl—seemed to have an unfortunate side effect.

I'm not sure if this was the direct cause, but the kway teow ended up being overcooked, soft, and mushy, lacking that smooth, springy texture that makes the dish enjoyable.

Despite the disappointing noodles, the meal was saved by the sheer quality of the yong tau foo pieces. For that reason, I'm giving it a solid 4 stars. I would definitely be willing to return, as the ingredients are clearly top-notch. Next time, I'll be sure to double-check my order and perhaps try a different noodle option.

I've now visited Danlao twice, and it's clear that the choice of topping makes all the difference. This is a solid spot for a comforting scrambled egg rice bowl, especially if you know what to order.

On both my visits, the two constants were the egg and the rice. As the name suggests, their scrambled egg good—cooked just right, soft and creamy, blanketing the rice underneath. While it's good and competently made, I wouldn't call it spectacular. The rice was also consistently well-cooked, with distinct grains (粒粒分明) and not mushy at all.

My first visit was a bit of a letdown. I had the Cheesy Char Siew bowl. The char siew was unfortunately on the dry side, and the "cheesy" element was simply a slice of processed cheese laid on top that hadn't fully melted. It felt like an afterthought and didn't add much to the dish.

However, my second visit was a significant improvement and the reason for the 4-star rating. I ordered the Classic Luncheon Meat and added on a Chicken Cutlet. The chicken cutlet was the undeniable highlight of the meal—perfectly crispy, juicy, and flavourful. It provided a fantastic textural contrast to the soft eggs and rice. The luncheon meat was standard fare, good but not memorable.

In conclusion, Danlao offers a satisfying meal, but the experience can be hit-or-miss depending on your protein choice. Based on my visits, I'd highly recommend skipping the char siew and going straight for the fried items, especially the excellent chicken cutlet.
